# openshop.uz — REST POST, full-catalogue sweep

Client: [`narxnoma/sources/openshop.py`](../../narxnoma-crawler/narxnoma/sources/openshop.py)
Fixture: `tests/fixtures/sources/openshop.json` · Tests: `tests/sources/test_openshop.py`

Single-seller shop (OpenShop, stores in Tashkent). Next.js front end over a Laravel
JSON API. **The whole catalogue — 5,723 products on 2026-10-14 — comes down in ~120
requests (~2.5 min)**, so it is swept and matched locally, never searched per product.

Verified live 2026-10-14 and 2026-10-22: full sweep, 191 matched links each re-read
from the product API and the public page, six opened in a browser; `cli fetch` for
all seven categories; live contract test.

---

## 1. Transport

```
Base: https://web.openshop.uz/api/v1
Every call is POST. Filters go in the QUERY STRING, not the body.
```

```http
Accept: application/json, text/plain, */*
Accept-Language: ru
language: ru            # custom header; without it names come back in Uzbek
Origin: https://openshop.uz
Referer: https://openshop.uz/
```

No auth, no token, no cookies needed. The API advertises `x-ratelimit-limit: 120`
(per minute); the client enforces ≥ 0.55 s between requests on its own
(`MIN_INTERVAL`), independent of `NARXNOMA_MIN_DELAY`.

## 2. Endpoints

| Endpoint | What it is | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /shop/product/get_products?category_id=&page=&per_page=48&sort_by=latest` | the catalogue browse the category pages call | **the sweep** |
| `POST /shop/category/categories_tree`, body `{}` | 3-level category tree with `products_count` | sweep plan, product type |
| `POST /shop/product/get_product?slug=<slug>`, body `{"with_variants": true}` | one product + its variant group | verification |
| `POST /shop/product/search_product?q=<text>` | header search box | humans only — §4 |

`get_products` also accepts `subcategory_id`, `subsubcategory_id`, `brand_id`,
`search`, `price_min`, `price_max`, and `*_slug` forms. They were read out of the
front-end bundle (`buildShopFilterQueryParams` → `/shop/product/get_products?…`),
which is only loaded on a category page — the homepage bundles do not contain it.

Response:

```json
{"data": [ {"id": 133328, "name": "Смартфон Samsung Galaxy A27 5G 8/256GB Синий",
            "slug": "133328-samsung-galaxy-a27-5g-8-256gb-moviy-smartfoni",
            "brand_name": "Samsung", "category_id": 11, "subcategory_id": 4,
            "subsubcategory_id": 20, "is_stock": true,
            "price": {"total": 4268000, "old_price": 4268000, "discount": 0, "currency": "UZS"},
            "link": "https://web.openshop.uz/shop/product/133328-…", "group": {"id": 98, "variants_count": 6},
            "tags": "…", "installment": {…}, … } ],
 "meta": {"current_page": 1, "last_page": 36, "per_page": 12, "total": 432}}
```

> **`/shop/category/<slug>` in the bundle is a front-end ROUTE, not an API path.**
> POSTing it to the API host returns HTTP 200 with an empty `data` — a "success"
> that is really a miss.

## 3. TRAPS in the sweep

1. **`per_page` is capped at 48.** Asking for 100 or 500 silently returns 48 and
   `meta.per_page` says 48. Smaller values are honoured.
2. **Deep paging stops at ~2,400 results per query.** An unfiltered walk reported
   `meta.total = 5731` but repeated earlier products from page 51 on. Walk each of
   the 11 **top-level categories** separately (largest ~1,577) and every product
   comes back. `iter_catalogue()` does this; `iter_raw()` logs a warning whenever a
   query's `total` exceeds the cap.
3. **Only in-stock goods are browsable** (`is_stock: true` on all 5,723). "Not found"
   can mean "sold out".
4. Sweep categories map to `subcategory_id` plus a third-level filter
   (`CATEGORY_SUBSUBCATEGORY_IDS`): TVs 30, ACs 31, fridges 33+34, washers 44+1411,
   ovens 32+1215+1403. **Countertop mini-ovens** sit in 1215 ("Духовые шкафы") and
   are dropped by title — no other source files them under `ovens`.

## 4. Why not the search endpoint

`search_product?q=` is fuzzy over the SEO `tags` field and capped at **60**
results: `q=Honor X9d` returns every Honor phone, tablet, watch and earbud.
`get_products?search=` is paginated but equally fuzzy (the full name of one phone
matches ~500 products). `search()` uses the latter and returns raw listings — pick
the variant by name.

## 5. How openshop tags goods

- **Every colour × memory combination is its own product** (own `id`, `slug`,
  `price`), tied together by `group.id`.
- `get_product` → `variants.axes` lists the attribute chips (`Оперативная память`,
  `Встроенная память`, `Цвет`); `variants.matrix` lists every sibling with its own
  price and stock.
- The category tree has 3 levels; **the third level is the product type**
  (`Беспроводные наушники`, `Утюги`, `Микроволновые печи`), and for phones and
  tablets it is the brand (`1213 Honor`). Restricting candidates to the right
  third-level ids is what keeps "Galaxy Buds 2" off a *case for* the Galaxy Buds 2.
- iPhones come in three SIM variants at different prices — `(SIM + eSIM)`,
  `(eSIM + eSIM)`, `(SIM + SIM)` — plus `Apple Certified Refurbished` listings.
- `badge.supplier` and `badge.edited_at` are **internal** fields (`"public": false`)
  the API leaks: the supplier is sometimes a person's name, `edited_at` a
  days-since-edit counter. Not catalogue data — never surface, store or match on them.

## 6. Price

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `price.total` | **what the customer pays now**, after any discount — the listing price |
| `price.old_price` | struck-through price; equals `total` when not discounted |

Integer UZS. No tiyin, no pre-discount trap (unlike mediapark and radius): confirmed
in a browser on a discounted listing (2 963 000 shown, 3 282 000 struck through).

## 7. Product URL

```
https://openshop.uz/shop/product/<slug>?lang=ru
```

- The item's `link` field points at `web.openshop.uz` — the **API host**, not the shop.
- Without `?lang=ru` the page renders in Uzbek (`Narx: … so'm`).
- The page is server-rendered and its `<title>` states price and memory:
  `Смартфон Honor X9d 5G 8/256GB Midnight Black | Цвет: Чёрный | Память: 8 ГБ / 256 ГБ | Цена: 4 899 000 сум`.
  `page_title(slug)` returns it with the parsed price — an independent second copy
  of the price for verification.
- The page server answers the occasional **502**; retry before calling a link dead.

## 8. Matcher gaps its names exposed

Found by matching a 2,619-name, 118-type assortment against the openshop catalogue
and reading every pair. These are gaps in how `matching/` handles names it was not
measured on; they are **not fixed in `matching/`** (the golden corpus pins phone
behaviour) and were worked around in the caller by rewriting names before
`extract_features`:

| Name | What went wrong | Caller workaround |
|---|---|---|
| `iPhone 17 Pro 256GB … (SIM + eSIM)` | `normalize()` turns `+` followed by a space into a `plus` model token → **every iPhone rejected** | collapse to `SIM+eSIM` |
| `Redmi Note 17 Pro Max 5Г` | Cyrillic `Г` survives homoglyph folding → token `5г` | `5Г` → `5G` |
| `Galaxy Watch 4` vs `Watch 8` | non-phone path drops 1-char tokens, the model digit included → **Watch 4 matched Watch 8** | glue the digit to the word: `watch4` |
| `PRM-20MW/LA1` vs `/LA2` | `head_for_model` cuts at `/` → **LA1/LA3/LA4 all matched LA2** | split `/` into a space instead of cutting |
| `Galaxy Buds 2 Оқ` | Uzbek `қ ў ғ ҳ` escape the `[а-я]+` Cyrillic-word filter → `оқ` became identity | drop words containing any Cyrillic letter (non-phones) |
| `Honor X7e … Lite Blue` | colour "Lite Blue" read as the model word `lite` | `Lite <colour>` → `light` |
| `Galaxy Tab A11+ (WiFi)` vs `(SIM)` | same name, different good, ~22 % apart | treat tablet connectivity as identity |
| `Samsung Buds 3 Pro` | openshop drops `Galaxy` on accessories | `galaxy` is not identity off-phone |

Each is a candidate fix for `matching/`, to be measured against the golden corpus
before it lands.

# radius.uz — Saleor GraphQL, public and introspectable

Client: [`narxnoma/sources/radius.py`](../../narxnoma-crawler/narxnoma/sources/radius.py)

The ninth source, added 2026-08-11. Technically the cleanest of the nine and
the smallest by volume — and those two facts are unrelated to its value, which
is that it puts a **second price on 212 products**.

radius.uz runs [Saleor](https://saleor.io/). Its own front end talks to
`https://new.api.radius.uz/graphql/` anonymously: no token, no signing, no
per-brand search, and **introspection is enabled**, so the schema documents
itself. Every field we need is a typed column rather than a string to be
parsed.

---

## 1. Endpoint

```
POST https://new.api.radius.uz/graphql/
```

No auth.

```http
Accept: application/json
Content-Type: application/json
Accept-Language: ru
Origin: https://radius.uz
Referer: https://radius.uz/
User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/150.0.0.0 Safari/537.36
```

Found by reading their own JS bundles (`/_next/static/chunks/*.js`) for a
`radius.uz` host — the front end is server-rendered, so the call never appears
in the browser's network tab. `api.radius.uz` does not resolve; `new.api.` is
the live one. `GET` on the endpoint serves a GraphQL Playground.

The schema is Saleor's, so the [Saleor API
reference](https://docs.saleor.io/api-reference) applies to anything not
covered here.

## 2. The query

```graphql
query CategoryProducts($slug: String!, $first: Int!, $after: String) {
  category(slug: $slug) {
    slug
    products(first: $first, after: $after) {
      totalCount
      pageInfo { hasNextPage endCursor }
      edges { node {
        id name slug isAvailable
        brand { name }
        category { slug }
        defaultVariant { id }
        variants { id name sku priceAmount currency
                   isAvailable quantityAvailable thumbnail(size: 512) { url } }
        pricing { priceRange { start { amount currency } } }
        thumbnail(size: 512) { url }
      } }
    }
  }
}
```

`Category.products` **already includes descendant categories** — verified:
`konditsionery` reports `totalCount: 17`, which is exactly the sum of its five
brand children. So the sweep asks the parent and gets the brands for free.

Pagination is Saleor's cursor connection: pass `pageInfo.endCursor` back as
`after` while `hasNextPage` is true. There is no page number.

**`Money` here is flat.** `{ amount currency }`, not Saleor's usual
`{ gross { amount } }`. Querying `gross` fails the whole request with
`Cannot query field "gross" on type "Money"`.

## 3. The variant is the offer, not the product

**This is the one decision that matters on this source, and getting it wrong
costs almost the whole phone catalogue.**

radius keeps the product name generic and the identity on the variant:

| | |
|---|---|
| `Product.name` | `Samsung Galaxy A26` |
| `Variant.name` | `Смартфон Samsung Galaxy A26 5G 8/256GB Black (Черный)` |

A phone key needs the memory pair and the colour, and the product name has
neither. Measured: emitting one listing per `Product` attached **1 of 80
phones (1.3%)**. Emitting one per `ProductVariant` attached **168 of 169
(99.4%)**.

Non-phones attached at 100% either way — which is exactly why this had to be
read per category rather than trusted as an average. A single headline
attachment rate would have hidden it.

Each variant also carries its own `priceAmount`, its own stock and its own
working URL, so this is not a modelling preference — a per-product parser
publishes one of "HUAWEI Nova Y61"'s three prices (1,397,000 … 1,959,000) as
the price of all three.

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `variant.id` | **the source key** (decoded, see §4) |
| `variant.name` | **use this for the product name** — carries memory and colour |
| `variant.priceAmount` | **use this** — plain UZS as a float |
| `variant.isAvailable` | stock; falls back to `product.isAvailable` |
| `variant.sku` | the manufacturer code, e.g. `ARTSID2CW12BE` |
| `product.slug` | the URL slug (see §5) |

## 4. Ids are base64 global ids

Saleor returns `id` as base64 `"<Type>:<number>"`:

```
UHJvZHVjdDo1MTk1              -> Product:5195
UHJvZHVjdFZhcmlhbnQ6ODA0Ng==  -> ProductVariant:8046
```

Decode to the number. A malformed id must cost one listing, not the sweep, so
the decoder returns `None` rather than raising.

## 5. The product URL uses the DEFAULT VARIANT id — not the product id

```
https://radius.uz/ru/product/<variant-id>-<product-slug>
```

This is the trap [README rule 1](README.md) exists for. Both ids sit next to
the slug in the payload and both are plausible integers, but:

```
/ru/product/5195-konditsioner-artel-artsid2cw12be-iceberg-inv   404   (product id)
/ru/product/8046-konditsioner-artel-artsid2cw12be-iceberg-inv   200   (variant id)
```

Checked on six products: **every product-id URL 404s.** Verified further that
a *non-default* variant's id also resolves and renders that specific colour,
which is what makes the per-variant URL in §3 legitimate rather than a guess.

## 6. Category slugs — and the Apple trap

Verified live 2026-08-11 by walking the whole tree through
`categories(first: 100, level: 0)` and reading every `totalCount`.

| Our category | radius slugs | Products |
|---|---|---:|
| `smartphones` | `smartfony`, `iphone-17-17-pro-17-pro-max-air`, `iphone-air-3` | 84 |
| `fridges` | `kholodilniki` | 22 |
| `televisions` | `televizory` | 18 |
| `acs` | `konditsionery` | 17 |
| `washers` | `stiralnye-mashiny` | 17 |
| `laptops` | `noutbuki`, `noutbuki-apple` | 16 |
| `ovens` | `gazovye-plity`, `dukhovoi-shkaf` | 13 |

**Not every category hangs where its name suggests.** `noutbuki` holds 9
laptops and not one is an Apple: the 7 MacBooks sit under a top-level **Apple**
category, as do the iPhones, which are absent from `smartfony` entirely.
Sweeping the obvious slug alone silently loses every Apple product — including
the iPhones, the most-compared phones in the catalogue — and the loss looks
exactly like a retailer that stopped stocking them.

The Apple entries are the fragile ones: they are marketing buckets
(`🆕 iPhone 17 | 17 Pro | 17 Pro Max`), renamed as lines launch. There is no
stable "Смартфоны Apple" node. `test_radius_categories.py` pins this map.

Deliberately not swept: `mikrovolnovye-pechi` (9) and `mini-pechi` (8) — the
same decision as [asaxiy](asaxiy.md#5-category-leaves), for the same measured
reason: all 540 `ovens` offers the other sources contribute contain no
microwave, so these could never price-compare.

## 7. GraphQL reports failure with HTTP 200

Same trap as [uzum](uzum.md): an `errors` key beside a `null` `data`, under a
200 status. The client raises on `errors` and on a null `category`, because
swallowing either would record a half-swept category as a successful harvest
of nothing — the one failure mode `EXPECTED_MIN_OFFERS` and `harvest_run.ok`
exist to catch.

## 8. Measured result

274 offers, **98.9% of them attached** to a canonical product.

| Category | Offers | Attached |
|---|---:|---:|
| smartphones | 169 | 99.4% |
| fridges | 22 | 100% |
| televisions | 18 | 100% |
| washers | 17 | 100% |
| acs | 17 | 100% |
| laptops | 17 | 88.2% |
| ovens | 14 | 100% |

**212 of its products are carried by at least one other store, and 54 of them
had only one price before radius arrived.** That is the number a small source
is worth judging on: radius adds 2.2% of the catalogue's offers and 4.8% of
its comparisons.

Its prices sit consistently at the top of the range (it sells on instalment
terms), which is itself useful — a comparison needs both ends.

All 212 multi-store variants were read offer by offer. Every merge is correct,
matched on catalogue codes: `ARTSIQ3BW12BE`, `ARTSID3AW12BE`, `AVLSIQ1AW12BE`.

---

## 9. TRAP — a thumbnail URL for a thumbnail that was never rendered

Saleor returns a `thumbnail(size: N) { url }` for every image, and the field is
non-null and well-formed regardless of whether the file exists. radius's
thumbnailer does not render `.avif` sources: the URL 404s with
`application/xml`.

Sampled across all 274 live radius offers:

| extension | count | thumbnail status |
|---|---|---|
| `.webp` | 218 | 200 |
| `.jpg` | 31 | 200 |
| `.png` | 23 | 200 |
| `.avif` | 2 | **404** |

The original **does** exist — the same path with `/thumbnails/<N>/` replaced by
`/media/` returns `200 image/avif` — so that is what we publish for those two.
Only for avif: `/thumbnails/` is the right thing to hotlink into a grid
everywhere it works, and swapping wholesale would serve full-size originals for
272 products to fix 2.

Worth stating plainly because no upstream check can catch it: "the field is
present" and "the file exists" are different questions, and only the second one
matters to a page that renders the URL.

# texnomart

## Product-type denylist (sweep-time crawl policy)

texnomart items carry **no category field** — verified against the recorded
fixture, unlike idea (`category_id`) and beemarket (a category endpoint).
The only usable signal is the product-type noun in the name, which is weaker
evidence, so the filter is a **denylist of things that are not phones** (see
`narxnoma/sources/not_a_phone.py`), never an allowlist of phone words: an
allowlist would silently drop any phone whose name lacks the expected noun,
and losing a real phone is worse than admitting an accessory the price fence
and the matcher still get a chance to reject.

Measured on 467 live offers (2026-08-02): **142 (30.4%) are not phones**, and
15 of them had already become canonical products — a tablet carries a brand,
a memory pair and a colour, so it forms a full key exactly as a phone does.
Two false-positive classes were caught and fixed before this rule shipped:

- `Черное стекло` — "стекло" is a screen protector AND a colour; only the
  qualified protector sense counts.
- `USB-адаптер` in a phone's marketing title — "Samsung Galaxy A37 5G: …
  USB-адаптер 8/128+ …" is a real phone with the charger in the box.
  "adapter" is therefore NOT in the denylist: a standalone charger carries
  no memory pair, cannot form a variant key, and can only ever land in
  unresolved_offer. (The previous doc's mitigation belonged to the
  target-driven matcher and does not apply at harvest time.)

# uzum.uz — GraphQL, multi-seller

Reference implementation: [`fill_uzum_prices.py`](../../fill_uzum_prices.py)

The largest marketplace in Uzbekistan and the richest data source here — it is the
only one that exposes **per-variant (SKU) price, stock and characteristics**, rather
than a single price attached to a name string.

It is also the only one with auth, and the only one where a naive implementation
returns **plausible but wrong numbers**. Read the two trap sections before writing code.

---

## 1. Auth — anonymous, self-minting

`graphql.uzum.uz` returns a bare **401 with an empty body** without a Bearer token.
The token requires no account:

```
POST https://id.uzum.uz/api/auth/token
Accept-Language: ru-RU
Referer: https://uzum.uz/
Body: {}
```

Response is **`204 No Content`** — the token is **not in the body**, it arrives as a
`Set-Cookie: access_token=<JWT>` header (a `refresh_token` is also set, on
`.id.uzum.uz`). This is why an early probe looked like it returned nothing.

TTL **6 hours** (`exp` in the JWT payload), no login, no captcha. Mint a fresh one
per run and refresh ~5 min before `exp`.

### Exactly two headers are required (measured by ablation)

| Header | Required | Omitting it gives |
|---|---|---|
| `Accept-Language` | **yes** (any value: `ru-RU`, `ru`, `en-US` all work) | `400 {"baseError":{"code":"insufficient_headers"}}` |
| `Referer` | **yes**, must be on the `uzum.uz` origin (any path) | `400 {"baseError":{"code":"unallowed_app"}}` |
| `Origin` | no — mints fine without it | — |
| `Accept`, `Content-Type`, `User-Agent`, `x-iid` | no | — |

A foreign `Referer` (e.g. `https://example.com/`) is rejected with `unallowed_app`,
so this is a soft origin check keyed on Referer rather than Origin. Send both plus a
real UA anyway to stay indistinguishable from the site's own traffic.

```python
import uuid, json, base64, requests

UA = ("Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 "
      "(KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/150.0.0.0 Safari/537.36")

def mint():
    iid = str(uuid.uuid4())
    s = requests.Session()
    s.post("https://id.uzum.uz/api/auth/token",
           headers={"Accept": "*/*", "Accept-Language": "ru-RU",   # required
                    "Content-Type": "application/json",
                    "Origin": "https://uzum.uz",
                    "Referer": "https://uzum.uz/",                 # required
                    "User-Agent": UA, "x-iid": iid},
           json={}, timeout=25)
    token = next(c.value for c in s.cookies if c.name == "access_token")
    p = token.split(".")[1]; p += "=" * (-len(p) % 4)
    exp = json.loads(base64.urlsafe_b64decode(p))["exp"]
    return s, token, iid, exp
```

## 2. The endpoint

```
POST https://graphql.uzum.uz/
```

Required set, measured by ablation — **four headers**, and two of them are
non-obvious:

| Header | Value | Required |
|---|---|---|
| `Authorization` | `Bearer <token>` | **yes** — bare `401` without |
| `Content-Type` | `application/json` | **yes** |
| `apollographql-client-name` | `web-customers` | **yes** — see below |
| `x-iid` | any UUID (install id) | **yes** — see below |
| `apollographql-client-version` | `1.63.2` | no |
| `city-id` | `1` (Tashkent) | no, but affects stock/delivery |
| `city-latitude` / `city-longitude` | `41.379112` / `69.29944` | no |
| `Origin` / `Referer` / `Accept` / `Accept-Language` / `User-Agent` | — | no |

> **Failure mode you must handle: it does not fail with an HTTP error.**
> Drop `apollographql-client-name` or `x-iid` and the request still returns
> **`200 OK`**, with `data: null` and:
> ```json
> {"errors": [{"message": "HTTP fetch failed from 'search-gateway': 4.."}]}
> ```
> Checking `response.status_code` alone will report success on a request that
> returned nothing. **Always inspect the `errors` key.** This is also true of the
> valid-query-but-null case:
> `{"extensions":{"valueCompletion":[{"message":"Cannot return null for non-nullable field Query.makeSearch"}]}}`
> — which is what a stale variables shape looks like.

Minimal working request: `Authorization` + `Content-Type` +
`apollographql-client-name` + `x-iid`. Send the full browser-like set anyway.

### Persisted queries are NOT enforced

The browser sends an Apollo **persisted query** — a `sha256Hash` instead of query
text, which is why the captured request body is only ~322 bytes. That normally
implies a server-side safelist. **It is not enforced here**: sending full query text
works fine. You do not need to extract hashes.

### Introspection is ON — use it, don't copy old scrapers

```graphql
{ __schema { queryType { name fields { name } } } }
```

works and returns 49 root queries / 428 types. **The query shape used by every
public uzum scraper is stale** — `SortType`, `SearchFilterInput`, and the old
`MakeSearchQueryInput` fields no longer exist. If the schema changes again,
re-introspect rather than guessing:

```graphql
{ __type(name: "MakeSearchQueryInput") {
    inputFields { name type { kind name ofType { kind name } } } } }
```

Note: this server rejects `__type(name: $var)` with a **variable** — inline the
string literal.

## 3. The search query (current, verified)

```graphql
query getMakeSearch($q: MakeSearchQueryInput!) {
  makeSearch(query: $q) {
    total
    items {
      catalogCard {
        __typename
        productId
        title
        category { id title }
        ... on SkuGroupCard {
          skuList {
            id
            sellPrice
            fullPrice
            availableAmount
            characteristicValues { title characteristic { title } }
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Variables:

```json
{"q": {
  "text": "Samsung Galaxy A17 6 128",
  "showAdultContent": "TRUE",
  "filters": [],
  "sort": "BY_RELEVANCE_DESC",
  "pagination": {"offset": 0, "limit": 72}
}}
```

`MakeSearchQueryInput` — required: `showAdultContent`, `filters`, `sort`,
`pagination`. Optional and useful: `categoryId`, `correctQuery`, `getFastCategories`,
`getFastFacets`, `showOnlyOriginalSKUs`.

- `Sort` enum: `BY_RELEVANCE_DESC`, `BY_PRICE_ASC`, `BY_PRICE_DESC`,
  `BY_RATING_*`, `BY_DATE_ADDED_*`, `BY_ORDERS_NUMBER_*`
- `ShowAdultContent` enum: `NONE`, `FALSE`, `TRUE`
- `CatalogCard` is an **interface** implemented by `ProductCard`, `SkuGroupCard`,
  `SkuCard` — `skuList` only exists on the concrete types, hence the inline fragment.

**Pagination caps at `offset` ≈ 1000** (beyond that `items` comes back empty).
`limit` is honoured generously — 72 is a good value, giving ~100 phone SKUs per call.
Per-query search is the right approach; a full-catalogue pull like olcha's is
infeasible because the Android smartphone category runs to thousands of multi-seller
listings.

### Category filter

Relevance search mixes in cases, chargers and (genuinely) vacuum cleaners. Filter
client-side on the card's `category.id`:

| id | title | our category |
|---|---|---|
| `15271` | Смартфоны Android | smartphones |
| `15272` | Смартфоны Apple iPhone (iOS) | smartphones |
| `12601` | Телевизоры | televisions |
| `12520` | Ноутбуки | laptops |
| `14373` | Сплит-системы | acs |
| `82` | Холодильники | fridges |
| `83` | Морозильники | fridges |
| `15291` | Полуавтоматические стиральные машины | washers |
| `15296` | Автоматические стиральные машины | washers |
| `11` | Духовые шкафы | ovens |
| `13` | Газовые плиты | ovens |

`showOnlyOriginalSKUs: "TRUE"` narrows 262 → 60 results but does **not** cleanly
strip grey-market resellers (the "IMEI зарегистрированы" cards survive it). Not a
useful lever — skip it.

### The query frontier is per CATEGORY, not per brand

**Verified live 2026-08-10.** Phones sweep by brand. Nothing else can, and using
the brand list for a category sweep is why uzum held 2,381 phones and **zero**
air conditioners, fridges, washers and ovens:

- the brands that sell white goods here — Artel, Premier, Shivaki, LG, Hisense —
  sell no phones, so they were never in the brand list to be queried;
- and for Samsung, which sells both, relevance ranks phones first while
  pagination caps at `offset` ≈ 1000, so a fridge never surfaces.

Measured, one page of 72 each:

| query | in-category | what else came back |
|---|---|---|
| `televizor` | 72/72 | — |
| `noutbuk` | 72/72 | — |
| `konditsioner` | 72/72 | — |
| `kir yuvish mashinasi` | 72/72 | — |
| `duxovka` | 45/45 | — |
| `холодильник` | 72/72 | — |
| `artel` | **0/72** | remote controls, vacuum filters, electric kettles |

So the noun does the work and brand queries are a supplement, not the frontier.
See `narxnoma/sources/brand_queries.py`.

**Two traps this measurement caught, both of which had silently cost a whole
product type:**

1. `газовая плита` is category **13**, not 11. Gas cookers were being fetched
   and then filtered out, because the config listed only `11` for ovens.
2. `muzlatgich` — the Uzbek for "refrigerator" — resolves to **83
   Морозильники** (freezers) on uzum, not to 82. `холодильник` and `sovutgich`
   are the words that reach 82. Other retailers do use "Muzlatgichi" for a
   fridge, so the word stays in the frontier; it simply must not lead it.

## 4. Response shape

```jsonc
{"data": {"makeSearch": {
  "total": 262,
  "items": [
    {"catalogCard": {
      "__typename": "SkuGroupCard",
      "productId": 1983388,
      "title": "IPhone 17 Pro/Pro Max, 256, 512 , 1 ТБ , 2 ТБ / Оба IMEI зарегистрированы",
      "category": {"id": 15272, "title": "Смартфоны Apple iPhone (iOS)"},
      "skuList": [
        {"id": 7028608, "sellPrice": 20789010, "fullPrice": 31000000,
         "availableAmount": 27,
         "characteristicValues": [
           {"title": "17 Pro Max 256 GB", "characteristic": {"title": "Модель"}},
           {"title": "Серебряный",        "characteristic": {"title": "Цвет"}}]}
      ]}}
  ]}}}
```

- **Price field: `skuList[].sellPrice`** — plain SUM integer, discount already applied.
  `fullPrice` is the struck-through pre-discount price and is often fantasy
  (`31,000,000` above) — never use it.
- `availableAmount` — filter to `> 0`; zero-stock SKUs are phantom listings.
- Card-level `minSellPrice` / `minFullPrice` also exist. **Do not use them** — see below.

> **V1 crawler note (`narxnoma/sources/uzum.py`).** The `availableAmount > 0`
> filter above is matcher-era guidance: it was written for a target-driven
> matcher hunting one specific phone, where a zero-stock SKU is noise to
> screen out. The V1 aggregator crawler is cataloguing every real offer, so
> it deliberately keeps zero-stock SKUs rather than dropping them — recorded
> with `availability="OUT_OF_STOCK"` (derived from `availableAmount`).
> Hiding an out-of-stock offer is a presentation decision that belongs
> downstream, not a reason to lose the observation. See the module
> docstring in `uzum.py` and `test_zero_stock_sku_is_kept_as_out_of_stock`
> in `tests/sources/test_uzum.py`.

## 5. TRAP 1 — card price ≠ product price

Uzum resellers bundle **several models and every storage tier under one card**:

```
"IPhone 17 Pro/Pro Max, 256, 512, 1 ТБ, 2 ТБ"    minSellPrice = 16,985,000
    ├ 17 Pro 256 GB          19,106,010
    ├ 17 Pro Max 256 GB      20,789,010   ← the one we actually sell
    ├ 17 Pro Max 512 GB      24,483,000
    └ 17 Pro Max 1 TB        39,999,000
```

`minSellPrice` — the obvious field, and the one every naive scraper reads — is the
cheapest variant *on the card*. For a 17 Pro Max 256 it understates by **~3.8 M**.

**Match at SKU level.** Build the candidate string from the SKU's own
`characteristicValues`, and use the card title only for brand context.

### 5a. Card titles are marketing blurbs

`"Смартфон Samsung Galaxy A17, 6.7\" Super AMOLED 90Гц экран, камера 50Мп, 5000 мАч"`
— those stray numbers become model tokens and reject every real match. Take the card
title only **up to its first comma**, and let the SKU's `Модель` characteristic
override it entirely when present.

### 5b. The same trap for memory — subtle and costly

```
card title:  "…Samsung Galaxy A17 4G 8/256GB"   ← the card's overall range
sku Память:  "6/128GB"                          ← what THIS sku actually is
```

Concatenating both lets the title's `8/256` satisfy an 8/256 target while the SKU is
really a 6/128 — it reported **2,672,010** for a phone whose true price was
**3,068,010**. When the SKU states its own memory, strip memory figures from the
title before concatenating:

```python
if mem_v:  # sku stated its own memory → it wins outright
    spec = re.sub(r"(?<![a-zа-я])\d{1,4}\s*(?:gb|гб|tb|тб)?\s*[/\\+|]\s*"
                  r"\d{1,4}\s*(?:gb|гб|tb|тб)?", " ", spec, flags=re.I)
    spec = re.sub(r"(?<![a-zа-я\d])\d{1,4}\s*(?:gb|гб|tb|тб)\b", " ", spec, flags=re.I)
```

> **V1 crawler note (`narxnoma/sources/uzum.py`).** The strip above applies
> to the **card title only**. Never run it over the SKU's own `Модель` or
> memory value: those are the trustworthy figures this section exists to
> protect, and stripping them turns `"A16 8/256"` into `"A16"` — a name
> with no storage tier, which the clustering stage cannot key at all.
> `_strip_memory` in the crawler is documented as card-derived-text-only for
> exactly this reason.

> **Measured 2026-08-02 — the `if mem_v:` gate above is not enough.** The
> sample code asks "did the SKU state its own memory?" by testing whether a
> memory *pair* or a *unit-bearing* figure is present. uzum's most common
> shape is neither: `Память: "128"`, `Модель: "17 Pro 256"` — a **bare
> figure**. Both read as *no memory stated*, so the protection in this
> section never engaged and the card's range won anyway, on 130 of 2,376
> live offers. Two separate symptoms, one blind spot:
>
> ```
> card 'Смартфон "Apple iPhone" 12, 64/128/256 ГБ' + Память "128"
>   -> 'Смартфон "Apple iPhone" 12 128 64/128 Алый'   ← 64 becomes a MODEL token
> card 'IPhone 17 Pro / Max 256/512 GB' + Модель "17 Pro 256"
>   -> 'IPhone / Max 256/512 GB 17 Pro 256 Оранжевый' ← keys as 512 GB
> ```
>
> The second merged a 17 Pro 256, a 17 Pro Max 256 and a 17 Pro 512 into one
> variant with one headline price of 18,349,000 against a median of
> 31,000,000 — the incumbent's own defect, different products behind one
> price, reproduced in our data. `_states_memory` now answers the question in
> every shape, and the last-resort card-title recovery is switched off
> entirely whenever the SKU stated anything. **A failure to recognise a
> stated figure is not a licence to substitute the card's range for it.**

### 5c. A RANGE is not a spec

A pair of figures means two different things depending on the figures:

| shape | reading | example |
|---|---|---|
| small + capacity | this SKU's RAM and storage | `4/128`, `12/256` |
| capacity + capacity | the **card's range** across bundled SKUs | `128/256`, `256/512` |

The rule that separates them is whether the smaller figure is a plausible
**RAM** size. A range identifies nothing, so recovering one puts a coin-toss
capacity on a real product; the crawler refuses it and lets the clustering
stage park the offer instead. The single-figure fallback is suppressed in the
same case, or it simply takes one half of the range it just declined.

Two further shapes were leaking figures into identity, both now handled:

- **chained ranges.** `12/256/512` had exactly two figures consumed, leaving
  `512` standing in the head — where the bare-pair scan read the card's 512 as
  the capacity and demoted the SKU's own 256 to a model token. The strip is
  greedy across the whole chain.
- **hyphen separators.** Sellers also write the RAM-ROM pair with a hyphen:
  `POCO C81 Pro (4-64/4-128)` matched no memory pattern at all and was chewed
  into `POCO C81 Pro (4- -128) 4/64`. Catalogue codes stay safe — the `0` of
  `SM-A075F` is preceded by a letter, so no chain can begin inside one.

### 5d. A card lends a SKU the model it is NOT

uzum bundles siblings on one card. `IPhone 17 Pro / Max 256/512 GB` carries
both the Pro and the Pro Max, and the head must supply only the **brand** the
bare `Модель` value lacks. Filtering out the head words the `Модель` repeats
is not sufficient: for the plain `17 Pro 256` SKU the word `Max` was not
repeated, so it survived into the prefix and the offer keyed as a Pro Max.

The head is kept only **up to** the first word the `Модель` value already
states. Once a head word belongs to the model, everything after it is model
territory and the per-SKU `Модель` field owns it — the head is the shared one.

## 6. TRAP 2 — eSIM-only variants

> **V1 crawler note (`narxnoma/sources/uzum.py`).** This whole section is
> matcher-era guidance, written for a target-driven matcher where an
> eSIM-only variant was the wrong answer to a specific query and had to be
> screened out. The V1 aggregator crawler keeps eSIM-only variants — they
> are a legitimate, separate product at a genuinely different price, and
> dropping them loses real offers. Whatever SIM characteristic exists (any
> of the three encodings below) survives verbatim into
> `Listing.raw["characteristic_values"]` for a later clustering stage to
> classify; `is_esim_only`/`sim_kind` (`narxnoma.matching.sim`) are not
> called from the crawler at all. See `test_esim_only_variant_is_kept` in
> `tests/sources/test_uzum.py`.

Our iPhones are **nanoSIM + eSIM**. Uzum lists eSIM-only variants side by side at a
materially lower price:

| variant | price |
|---|---|
| 17 Pro Max 256 GB (dual) | 20,789,010 |
| 17 Pro Max 256 (e-Sim) | 19,453,000 |
| 17 Pro Max 256GB (eSIM) | 18,099,000 |

Encoded **three different ways** — all must be screened:

1. `Модель: "17 Pro Max 256 (e-Sim)"` or `"iPhone 17 Pro Max 256GB (eSIM)"`
2. a SIM characteristic (`Сим-карта`, `SIM карта`, ` SIM карта`) with value
   `e-SIM` / `ESIM` — the physical variant reads `SIM`
3. the **card title** itself, e.g. `"Apple смартфон iPhone 17 Air 256GB, 512GB, 1TB, eSIM"`

Explicit dual markers (`SIM+eSIM`, `nanoSIM+eSIM`, `2 SIM`, `dual`) must **not** be
rejected — check them first. The dual marker appears with `+`, `/` and `-`
separators (`SIM+eSIM` in the raw characteristic value, `nano-SIM/eSIM` on the
rendered spec sheet), so all of them — plus whitespace, `_` and `.` — are
stripped before matching, collapsing every spelling onto one canonical form:

```python
_SEPARATORS = re.compile(r"[\s_.\-/+]")
_DUAL = re.compile(r"simesim|dual|2sim|двесим")
_ESIM = re.compile(r"esim")

def is_esim_only(text):
    low = _SEPARATORS.sub("", str(text).lower())
    if _DUAL.search(low):
        return False
    return bool(_ESIM.search(low))
```

`_DUAL` matches a **bare `dual`**, not just `dualsim`. The marker list above names
`dual` on its own, but the pattern used to require the compound spelling, so
`sim_kind("dual")` returned `"unknown"` — a phone explicitly documented as dual came
back unclassified. The bare alternative subsumes `dualsim`, so that spelling no longer
needs its own branch.

Verify on the rendered page: the product spec sheet shows
`Тип SIM карты : nano-SIM/eSIM` for the dual variant.

### An unmarked phone is dual, not unknown

Because eSIM-only variants are **always** explicitly marked — in all three encodings
above — silence carries information: an unmarked phone is the ordinary dual-SIM one.
`variant_key` therefore normalises `sim_kind="unknown"` to `"dual"` before building the
key.

This is also what keeps `slug()` injective. `slug()` only appends a suffix for
`esim_only`, so `"unknown"` and `"dual"` built two *different* `VariantKey`s that
rendered to the *identical* slug — two canonical products claiming one URL, with
whichever wrote last silently winning. Normalising at key construction collapses them
into the one product they always were. `esim_only` keeps its distinguishing `-esim`
suffix.

`SIM_KINDS` is enforced, not merely declared: `variant_key` raises `ValueError` on
anything outside `("dual", "esim_only", "unknown")`. Without the check a typo such as
`"Dual"` or `"dual_sim"` became part of a canonical identity and minted a second
product for a phone that already had one.

Note the normalisation is deliberately **not** applied to `partial_key`: there,
`"unknown"` still means "not yet known" and is what lets `resolve_partial` match a
partial offer against either SIM variant before refusing on ambiguity.

## 7. Characteristic keys are a typo minefield

Never match characteristic keys exactly. Observed across 66 queries:

`Цвет` · `Память` · `память` · `ПАМЯТЬ` · `Памят:` · `Память:` · `Памяьт:` ·
`памяять` · `Память ` · `Объем памяти` · `Xotirasi` (Uzbek) · `RAM/ROM` · `Модель` ·
`модел` · `Сим-карта` · `SIM карта` · ` SIM карта` (leading space) · `Тип` ·
`16 PRO MAX` (a value used as a key)

Added from the 2026-08-01 live "Samsung" recording: `Xotira` · `Xotira:`
(trailing colon) · `XOTIRA` · **`xotra`** (a typo missing the final `i`) ·
`Rang` (Uzbek for colour).

Classify loosely by prefix:

```python
def char_kind(key):
    k = normalize(key)
    if k.startswith("памя") or k.startswith("xotira") or "объем памяти" in k:
        return "memory"
    if k.startswith("модел"):           return "model"
    if "sim" in k or "сим" in k:        return "sim"
    if k.startswith("цвет") or k.startswith("rang"): return "color"
    return "other"
```

> **Corrected 2026-08-01 (V1 crawler, live "Samsung" recording).** Add
> `Xotira:` (trailing colon — already handled fine by `normalize`, which
> strips punctuation) and, more importantly, **`xotra`** — a typo missing
> the final `i` — to the observed-keys list above. `xotra` does **not**
> match this section's own `startswith("xotira")` sample: `"xotra"` is
> shorter than `"xotira"` and Python's `str.startswith` requires the full
> prefix to be present, so a key that reads `xotra` falls through to
> `"other"` and its memory value is silently lost. `narxnoma/sources/uzum.py`
> uses the shorter `k.startswith("xot")` instead, which catches `Xotirasi`,
> `Xotira`, `Xotira:` and `xotra` alike. If you copy this section's sample
> code elsewhere, use `"xot"`, not `"xotira"`.
>
> **`RAM/ROM` has the same defect, and it is in this section's own list
> above.** `normalize` folds the slash to a space, so the key arrives as
> `ram rom`, which none of the prefix tests in the sample recognise — it
> falls through to `"other"` and the SKU's memory value is silently
> dropped. `narxnoma/sources/uzum.py` additionally treats a bare `ram` or
> `rom` *token* as memory. Match on tokens, not as a substring: a plain
> `"ram" in k` also fires on the Uzbek colour key `Rang`.
> `test_char_kind_classifies_every_observed_key` in
> `tests/sources/test_uzum.py` runs every key named in this section through
> the classifier, so a key added here without a matching rule fails a test
> rather than losing data in production.

## 8. Colours are Russian — and, in card/model strings, Uzbek

> **Corrected 2026-07-26.** The heading used to read "Russian only". That holds for the
> **`Цвет` characteristic**, but *not* for card titles and `Модель` values, which are
> frequently Uzbek: `Smartfon HONOR X7d 6/128GB Tilla`, `Honor X7d 6/128GB Kumush rang`,
> `HONOR X6c smartfoni 6/128 GB Muz`. Because §5 builds the candidate string from the
> card title when the SKU states no `Цвет`, those Uzbek words reach the matcher — and an
> unresolvable colour **rejects** (see below), so every one of them was a silent miss.
> Adding the Uzbek vocabulary took a 20-target benchmark from **5/20 to 15/20 matched**.

```python
UZ_COLORS = {
    "qora": "black", "oq": "white", "kumush": "silver", "kulrang": "gray",
    "tilla": "gold", "oltin": "gold", "sariq": "yellow", "yashil": "green",
    "kok": "blue", "ko'k": "blue", "moviy": "blue", "muz": "blue",
    "binafsha": "purple", "pushti": "pink", "qizil": "red",
    "jigarrang": "brown", "bej": "beige",
}
```

`rang` means "colour", not a colour — put it in `NON_MODEL_TOKENS` or `Kumush rang`
leaves a stray `rang` model token. Same for the listing filler `smartfoni`, `telefon`,
`zarbaga`, `chidamli`. Uzbek qualifiers `to'q` (dark) and `och` (light) must stay
**unmapped**, exactly like `тёмно` / `светло`.

### The `Цвет` characteristic itself

`Цвет` values are always Russian, so an English colour map is useless. All 33 values
observed: Черный, Серый, Тёмно-серый, Серый металлик, Серый меланж, Угольный,
Темно-синий, Синий, Синий меланж, Светло-синий, Голубой, Небесно-голубой, Ледяной,
Бирюзовый, Фиолетовый, Лавандовый, Сиреневый, Серебряный, Зеленый, Тёмно-зелёный,
Мятный, Оранжевый, Манго, Золотой, Песочный, Бежевый, Белый, Молочный, Кремовый,
Бордовый, Коричневый, Алый, Черное стекло.

Map at **token** level after normalising `ё → е` and stripping punctuation, so
`Тёмно-серый` → `{темно, серый}` → gray. Leave qualifier tokens (`тёмно`, `светло`,
`небесно`, `металлик`, `меланж`) unmapped — the base colour word is always present.

**An unmapped colour must reject, not pass.** If a candidate has a `Цвет` value you
cannot resolve, drop it for any colour-bearing target. Treating it as a wildcard let
`Конфетный` (candy) and `Хром` match *both* the Awesome Gray and Awesome Navy targets
simultaneously.

## 9. Product URL

```
https://uzum.uz/ru/product/<productId>?skuId=<skuId>
```

`302`-redirects to the canonical slug URL, so **no slug construction is needed** —
`/ru/product/2996442` lands on `/ru/product/smartfon-samsung-galaxy-2996442`.
`?skuId=` pre-selects the exact variant, which is what makes the link verifiable.

## 10. Query building

Uzum's search is strict AND. Drop colour words **and `5G`/`4G`** from the query —
many seller titles omit the band (`"Samsung Galaxy A37 8/256GB Gray Green"`), so
keeping it silently excludes real listings. Restore precision in the matcher, which
treats `5g`/`4g` as reserved and never scores on them.

Two-shot strategy: broad query first (no colour, no band), then the verbatim name as
a fallback; dedupe candidates by `skuId`.

## 11. Metrics produced

Multi-seller, so a single number hides the spread. Two columns:

- **`uzum min`** — cheapest matching in-stock SKU
- **`uzum median (IQR)`** — median of matching SKUs after IQR stripping

Links sheet gets both URLs (median link = the SKU whose price is nearest the median).
A large min↔median gap is genuine grey-market spread, not an error — Redmi A5 3/64
had sellers at 1.45 M and 3.0 M.

## 12. Result

**61/66 (92 %)** — best of all seven sources. The 5 misses were each verified as
genuine absence: Honor 400 12/256 (uzum stocks only 8/256 and 12/512) and Vivo Y31d
×4 (not listed at all).

---

## 10. Product photos — the field nobody asked for

uzum published **no image at all** for 5,461 offers — the largest source in the
catalogue, every row imageless — for the simple reason that `SEARCH_QUERY` never
requested `photos`. The site's placeholder-heavy look traced back to this one
missing selection.

```graphql
catalogCard {
  ...
  photos { link(trans: PRODUCT_540) { high } }
}
```

Two things about the field are not guessable and were read off the live schema:

1. **`photos.link` requires a `trans:` argument** of type `Transformation!`.
   A bare `link { high }` is a *validation error* — HTTP 400 — not a null.
   Valid values: `ORIGINAL`, `PRODUCT_60`, `PRODUCT_80`, `PRODUCT_120`,
   `PRODUCT_240`, `PRODUCT_24034`, `PRODUCT_480`, `PRODUCT_540`, `PRODUCT_720`,
   `PRODUCT_800`. `PRODUCT_540` is a card-sized render; `ORIGINAL` is a
   full-resolution original and the wrong thing to hotlink into a grid.
2. **`PhotoLink.high` / `.low` are plain URL strings**, not objects.

Yielding e.g.
`https://images.uzum.uz/d9kvjoa1146g73i19b0g/t_product_540_high.jpg`.

**makeSearch returns one card per COLOUR.** A single `productId` comes back as
several cards (16 of 72 items in the recorded fixture) whose `skuList`s differ
only in storage tier. So the photo is accurate to the *colour*, not merely to
the model — which matters here, because colour is part of a phone's identity in
this catalogue and showing the black handset under the green variant would be a
substitution. The first test written for this asserted the opposite ("all SKUs
of one productId share one photo") and failed, which is how the structure was
found.

```
    export NARXNOMA_TEST_DSN="postgresql://narxnoma@127.0.0.1:55432/narxnoma_test"
    python -m pytest tests/ -q

NARXNOMA_TEST_DSN is the TEST variable. NARXNOMA_DSN is the PRODUCTION one and must
never be used for tests — the db fixture truncates its database on every db-marked test,
and doing that on the server would destroy live crawler data. A guard refuses any
database whose name lacks "test". Details in docs/deployment/local-postgres.md.
A green run with NARXNOMA_TEST_DSN unset proves nothing: the db tests silently skip.

HOW TO WORK
Use the superpowers:subagent-driven-development skill and follow it properly:
- Pre-flight the plan first. Every pre-flight so far has found real defects in the plan
  itself — a test that asserted nothing, a NOT NULL that could not hold, offers parked
  forever with no retry. Scan Tasks 2-8 for the same before dispatching anything.
- One implementer subagent per task, then a reviewer subagent, then fix, then re-review.
- Generate each task brief with:
    bash "C:/Users/ASUS/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/superpowers/6.1.1/skills/subagent-driven-development/scripts/task-brief" \
      "docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-01-narxnoma-clustering.md" <N>
- Generate each review package with the sibling script review-package BASE HEAD.
- Append one line per completed task to .superpowers/sdd/progress.md, and record every
  open finding there. Conversation memory does not survive; that file does.
- Verify claims yourself with small throwaway scripts against the real corpus and the
  real database. Nearly every serious bug in this project was found that way, not by
  reading. Delete the scripts afterwards.

THE TWO TASKS THAT MATTER MOST

Task 2 — _SKU_MIN_LEN. narxnoma/matching/features.py drops mixed letter+digit tokens of
length >= 5 as SKU codes, so "reno15" (7 chars) is discarded and every OPPO Reno yields
empty model_tokens: unkeyable, and score_match(Reno15, Reno14) = 45, above the accept
threshold of 30. MEASURE candidate boundaries against the 14,860-row golden corpus at
narxnoma-crawler/tests/fixtures/golden/ and report the table BEFORE choosing a value.
Do not pick a number and justify it afterwards. This comes before clustering on purpose:
clustering writes permanent canonical identities, so a model token wrongly discarded then
becomes a permanently wrong catalogue rather than a transient error.

Task 4 — clustering. This is where the platform's entire competitive claim becomes code.
The incumbent (uzprice.uz) pools colour variants, so on 23% of its multi-store pages the
headline price belongs to a different colour than the page title — worst measured case
9.3% understated. Our answer is: never guess. An offer whose partial key matches two
canonical variants goes to unresolved_offer with a reason; it does not get attached.
Getting that refusal right matters more than coverage.

RULES THAT ARE NOT NEGOTIABLE
- Colour is a hard identity field. Unknown colour never equals any colour.
- RAM is identity only for brands that publish it; Apple does not.
- Never guess an ambiguous offer. Park it with a reason and count it.
- docs/parsers/ is the source of truth for retailer behaviour. If code and doc disagree,
  verify live, then fix BOTH in the same commit.
- Every price is an integer in SUM, inside 100,000-100,000,000.
- Do not weaken a test to make it pass. Do not lower a floor to silence an alert.

Start by reading the ledger, then pre-flight the plan, then begin Task 2.
```

---

## Why the ledger matters more than this prompt

`.superpowers/sdd/progress.md` is ~370 lines and records not just what was built but what
was *found* — including the defects that a green test suite could not see. Some of those
are still open and will bite the next person who touches that area:

- `_SKU_MIN_LEN` making OPPO Reno models unkeyable (Task 2 fixes this).
- `brand_queries.py` doubles as the crawl frontier for three sources, so a brand missing
  from it means zero offers, not one degraded name.
- texnomart has no category filter at all, so any accessory over 100,000 SUM enters
  `offer` as a phone.
- The same pagination shape is duplicated across six clients; six `TODO(plan-3)` markers
  point at hoisting it.
- Recorded fixtures are single snapshots — they cannot catch category renumbering or a
  pagination-semantics change. The `live` contract tests are the counterweight and are
  currently unscheduled.

Before the first unattended full sweep: record an Apple-query uzum fixture, schedule the
`live` tests weekly, and add a `pg_try_advisory_lock` single-instance guard.

# Narxnoma — electronics price comparison for Uzbekistan

**Status:** approved design, ready for implementation planning
**Date:** 2026-07-27
**Scope of this spec:** V1 — smartphones, Russian, mobile-first web

---

## 1. Purpose

Build the highest-quality electronics price-comparison platform in Uzbekistan. Aggregator
only — we never sell, we send traffic to retailers.

The competitive thesis is **data quality, not catalogue size**. The incumbent
(uzprice.uz) already has scale; it does not have correctness. Every architectural
decision below exists to make one promise true:

> The price we show belongs to the exact phone you are looking at, and we can show you
> which listing it came from.

### Why this is winnable — measured, not assumed

Findings from the 2026-07-26 audit of uzprice.uz. Treated as validated; do not
re-investigate without new evidence.

| Finding | Measurement |
|---|---|
| Colour pooling | 30 of 40 sampled multi-store pages pool >1 colour; **23% of all multi-store pages** show a headline price sourced from a different colour than the page title (49/210) |
| Worst observed error | Honor X7D 6/128 silver advertised at 2,149,000 — a Desert Gold price. **+200,000 sum (9.3%)** |
| Duplicate canonicals | 26 groups / 52 products differing only by case or punctuation (`Cosmic orange` vs `Cosmic Orange`) — splits the offer pool so *both* pages are wrong |
| Unstable pagination | 735-product category returns 744 rows / 720 unique ids — 24 duplicated, 15 unreachable |
| Thin comparison | 72% of smartphones are single-store (86% smartwatches, 84% tablets, 83% laptops) |
| Source concentration | alifshop supplies **76%** of smartphone offers, 31% overall — and is itself a multi-seller marketplace, so store counts overstate depth |
| Missing sources | No **uzum** (largest marketplace in UZ) and no **beemarket** |

What they do well, and we must match: 2–4 hour refresh, normalized per-category specs,
stored price history, programmatic SEO.

### Our validation of the thesis

Independently fetching all 7 sources and matching variant-exact against 20 of their most
comparison-rich pages: **17 exact agreements, 3 within 2%, 0 differing by more than 2%**
versus their own offer data re-filtered to the correct colour. uzum+beemarket produced a
cheaper legitimate price on 3/20, best case 722,000 sum (8.2%).

Honest read: *"we are cheaper"* is weak. *"our number is attributable"* is strong.

---

## 2. V1 scope

**In:**

- Smartphones only
- Russian only (Uzbek later; keep strings in one catalogue so adding a locale is a
  routing change, not a rewrite)
- Mobile-first, per the `Narxnoma Mobile.dc.html` design
- Search, category browse with brand/price/colour/RAM facets, product page
- Uzum multi-seller spread panel (min / median / seller count / range)
- Variant picker showing a separate price per colour

**Out of V1** — present in the design canvas, implemented later:

- Price-history UI (`showOldPrice = false`)
- Store trust badge (`showTrust = false`)
- Favourites / Profile (bottom nav ships Главная + Поиск only)
- UZ/RU language toggle
- Categories beyond smartphones

**Consequence to note:** screen 01's «Реальные снижения» feed is driven by price history.
In V1 that block shows *cheapest multi-store offers* instead. We deliberately do **not**
substitute retailer-supplied "old prices" — 19 of uzprice's smartphones carry ≥50%
"discounts" sourced from `oldPrice` fields our parser docs already identify as fantasy
(`uzum.fullPrice`, `texnomart.old_price = 0`, `beemarket.price`).

`showFreshness` stays **true** — `offer.last_seen` is real data from day one.

---

## 3. Sources

Supported: **uzum, alifshop, beemarket, idea, mediapark, olcha, texnomart**.
Excluded by decision: ishonchsavdo, ishonchsale (our own systems; we are an aggregator).

`parsers/*.md` is the source of truth for each client — exact request, response shape,
price field and unit, URL construction, and the traps. Contradict it only with verified
live testing, and when you do, **update the doc in the same change**.

### Sweepability — measured 2026-07-26

This determines the architecture. Six of seven can be browsed; only mediapark cannot.

| Source | Sweepable | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| beemarket | yes, fully | empty query → 233 pages |
| alifshop | yes, per brand | `Samsung` → 50 pages (1,000 listings) |
| uzum | yes, per brand | `Samsung` → 577 total, under the ~1000 offset cap |
| texnomart | yes, generic query | `smartfon` → 25 pages (~500) |
| olcha | yes, catalogue | 22 calls, ~440 phones |
| idea | partly | `quantity=100` honoured → 94 in one call |
| **mediapark** | **no** | autocomplete, no pagination — target-driven only |

---

## 4. Architecture

Source-driven discovery, not target-driven. The current parsers assume a curated list of
phones; production must discover products itself.

```
Source APIs
   ↓  harvest      (network — the only stage that does I/O)
Raw offers
   ↓  extract      (pure function — no I/O, fully unit-testable)
Features
   ↓  cluster      (assign canonical identity, or park as unresolved)
Canonical variants
   ↓  aggregate    (min / median / IQR / spread rollups)
variant_price
   ↓  publish      (ISR revalidate for changed variants only)
Frontend
```

Every stage is independently testable. Only `harvest` touches the network; only
`publish` touches the web tier.

### Harvest has two phases, because mediapark cannot be swept

`harvest` runs in two passes:

- **Pass A — sweep.** The six browsable sources, independent of any product list.
- **Pass B — targeted.** mediapark only, searching for variants that already exist in
  the catalogue.

Pass B deliberately reads the variant list produced by the **previous** cycle rather than
the current one. Feeding it the current cycle's clustering output would make the pipeline
cyclic (harvest → cluster → harvest → cluster) for one source's benefit. The cost is that
a genuinely new phone gets its mediapark offer one cycle late — 4 hours. That is an
acceptable trade for keeping the pipeline a straight line, and mediapark is our weakest
source anyway (46/66 coverage, no pagination).

**Chosen over two alternatives.** *Target-driven scaled up* was rejected: ~4,200 requests
per cycle for 700 phones and structurally blind to any product not already on the list.
*Seeding from uzprice's open API* was rejected on three grounds — it inherits the exact
duplicate-canonical and colour-pooling defects we differentiate against, it breaks
silently when they change schema, and building a competing commercial product on a
competitor's aggregated database is avoidable legal exposure. It is retained as a **test
fixture** (see §9), not a data source.

Measured cost of the chosen approach: **~1,100–1,900 requests, 8–13 minutes** per full
cycle — cheaper than target-driven despite far wider coverage, because sweep cost scales
with catalogue size rather than product count.

### Two deployables, one database

```
narxnoma-crawler/   Python, systemd timer, VPS in Uzbekistan
narxnoma-web/       Next.js App Router, same VPS
                    └── shared PostgreSQL
```

The parsers are verified Python and stay Python. Porting them to TypeScript for language
uniformity would mean re-deriving every trap in `parsers/*.md` — the classic source of
port drift. Hosting is a UZ VPS so the crawler egresses from a local IP (source blocking
is a real risk: ishonchsale already 403s our current IP at the Cloudflare edge) and page
latency stays low for UZ users.

---

## 5. Canonical model

**Canonical products are permanent identities. Offers are temporary observations.**
Specifications belong to canonical products; prices belong to offers. Every offer retains
its originating retailer, its raw name and its URL. Nothing is inferred that cannot later
be audited.

### The variant key

```
key = (brand, model_tokens, ram_gb, storage_gb, colour, sim_kind)
```

All six derive from `extract_features` in `parsers/_matching-engine.md`. `sim_kind` is
`dual | esim_only | unknown` — an eSIM-only iPhone is a different product at a materially
different price, not a colour variant (uzum lists them side by side, 18,099,000 vs
20,789,010 for the same nominal phone).

### Identity rules — non-negotiable

- **Colour is a hard identity field.** Unknown colour never equals any colour.
- **Model numbers are sacred.** Storage/RAM extraction must never consume a model
  identifier. See the phantom-RAM trap below.
- **Model modifiers must never disappear** during parsing (`Pro`, `Max`, `Air`, `FE`).
- **Every rejection must be explainable** — `why()` returns the specific reason.

### Never guess a missing field

Sources routinely omit RAM (beemarket) or state an unresolvable colour.

1. Build full-key clusters from listings that state everything.
2. A listing with a missing field forms a *partial* key.
3. Exactly one full cluster matches → attach.
4. More than one matches → `unresolved_offer`, with reason. **Never attach.**

A `Redmi Note 15 256GB Black` with no RAM, where both 8/256 and 12/256 exist, is
genuinely ambiguous. uzprice attaches it anyway and lets it set the headline price. We
exclude it and count it. `unresolved_offer` is a **quality metric we watch**, not a
dumping ground — a rising rate means the matcher needs work.

### Display names are generated, never copied

Canonical name is built *from the key*: `Смартфон {Brand} {Model} {ram}/{storage} ГБ, {Colour}`.
Copying a store's name is exactly how uzprice produced `Cosmic orange` and `Cosmic Orange`
as two products. Generating it makes name and slug deterministic functions of the key, so
duplicates are structurally impossible.

### Matcher corrections already back-ported (2026-07-26)

Found by benchmarking, now fixed in `parsers/*.md`:

1. **Phantom-RAM collapse** — `"iPhone 16 256 GB"` has the same shape as `"12/256 GB"`,
   so the bare-pair heuristic read 16 as RAM, moving it into `reserved_nums` and deleting
   the model number from `model_tokens`. iPhone 16, 17 and Air became mutually
   interchangeable (an iPhone 16 at 12,000,000 matched an iPhone Air target, 1.44M low).
   Fixed by testing the **raw** string for a `/` separator — `normalize()` has already
   erased it — and never inferring RAM for Apple. `air`/`fe`/`se` added to
   `MODEL_MODIFIERS`.
2. **Uzum serves Uzbek colour names** in card/model strings (`Kumush`, `Tilla`, `Yashil`,
   `Muz`), though `Цвет` values are Russian. Unresolvable colours reject, so every one was
   a silent miss. Adding the vocabulary took uzum from **5/20 to 15/20**.
3. **alifshop needs broad query stripping** — a `Glacier Blue` query never reaches the
   listing alifshop stores as `Синий`. Now two-shot: colour-stripped, then verbatim,
   deduped by slug.

Generalised lesson, recorded in `parsers/README.md`: **a transport check cannot validate a
matcher.** Wrong matches look exactly like right ones until diffed against an independent
source.

---

## 6. Schema

```
store             slug, name, website_url, trust_score, is_active
raw_offer         store_id, source_key, name_raw, price, url, availability,
                  observed_at, payload jsonb            -- append-only
offer             store_id, source_key UNIQUE, variant_id?, price, availability,
                  url, first_seen, last_seen            -- current state
variant           brand, model_tokens[], ram_gb, storage_gb, colour, sim_kind,
                  display_name, slug, category          -- permanent identity
variant_price     variant_id, min, min_store_id, median, offer_count,
                  store_count, computed_at              -- render-ready rollup
unresolved_offer  offer_id, partial_key, reason, candidate_variant_ids[]
```

`raw_offer` is append-only and is where price history comes from **free** — the crawl
needs it to know what changed, so the time series accumulates whether or not the chart
ships in V1. `variant_price` is a materialised rollup so a product page is one indexed
read, not a request-time aggregation.

Index `(brand, model_tokens, ram_gb, storage_gb, sim_kind)` — this makes the colour-sibling
lookup powering the variant picker cheap.

> **`display_name` must be injective over the key (measured 2026-08-02).** It is generated
> from the key so that duplicates are structurally impossible — but it omitted `sim_kind`
> while `slug` encoded it, so an eSIM-only phone and its dual-SIM sibling, genuinely
> different products at different prices, rendered byte-identical. 42 live pairs were
> indistinguishable, including *Смартфон Apple iPhone 17 Pro 256 ГБ, Оранжевый* twice, at
> 16,985,000 and 17,690,000. **Every field of the key must reach the name.** A generator
> that drops one reintroduces exactly the confusion it exists to prevent, so the test
> asserts the invariant directly rather than pinning this one field.
>
> `display_name` is also *stored*, and `upsert_variant` uses `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`, so a
> name is written once at creation and never revisited. A correction to the generator would
> otherwise apply only to products first seen afterwards — the same shape as the
> `schema.sql` header rule. `refresh_display_names` regenerates them every cycle.

> **Attachments need reconciling, not just creating (measured 2026-08-02).** Clustering
> loads only offers with `variant_id IS NULL`, so an offer attached in an earlier cycle is
> never reconsidered. That is right while `name_raw` is stable and wrong the moment a
> parser fix changes it — which is precisely when the catalogue is most likely to be wrong.
> The uzum card-range repair rewrote 217 stored names; without a reconcile step every offer
> behind them would have stayed on the variant the old, incorrect name produced, and no
> report would have said so. `detach_drifted_offers` only *detaches*: the offer is then
> re-attached, or refused, by the ordinary rules, so a fix can never invent a new outcome.

---

## 7. Web layer

Next.js App Router, SSR + ISR. Routes: `/`, `/c/[category]`, `/c/[category]/[brand]`,
`/p/[slug]`, `/search`, `/stores`, `/about`, plus `/api/revalidate` (crawler webhook) and
`/api/out/[offerId]` (302 to retailer, logs the outbound click).

SEO from day one: sitemap index, per-category and category×brand landing pages, and
`robots.txt` disallowing faceted query strings with `Clean-param` hygiene.

### Design tokens

From `Narxnoma Mobile.dc.html`, so the build cannot drift:

| Token | Value |
|---|---|
| paper / card | `#EDE6D8` / `#FAF6EC` |
| ink / muted | `#211C16` / `#6B6154`, `#8A7E6C` |
| terracotta (action) | `#B0472B` |
| savings green | `#3E6B47` |
| uzum amber | `#C4881F` |
| highlight | `#F2E7CF` |
| borders | `#DED3BF`, `#EBE1CE` |

Archivo for text; **JetBrains Mono for every number** — prices, dates, counts.
`border-radius: 0` throughout, flat, no glow. Touch targets ≥44px. 390×844 baseline.

### Every design element maps to a column

| Design element | Source |
|---|---|
| `2 723 000` headline | `variant_price.min` |
| `3 магазина · до 2 811 000` | `store_count`, max offer price |
| `«Смартфон Xiaomi Redmi Note 15 8/256 ГБ, Синий»` | `offer.name_raw`, verbatim |
| `проверено 2 ч назад · в наличии` | `offer.last_seen`, `availability` |
| `Uzum · медиана 7 продавцов · разброс 2 569 000 – 2 940 000` | uzum offers → min/median/IQR |
| Variant picker per-colour price + `−154 000` | sibling variants, `variant_price.min` delta |
| `нет в продаже` | sibling with no in-stock offers |
| `2+ магазина` (default-on filter) | `store_count >= 2` |

**Counts in the design canvas are illustrative, not literal.** The mockup reads
`744 модели · 9 магазинов` — those are uzprice's numbers, carried over from the audit.
Ours are 7 sources and a catalogue size not yet known until the first full sweep runs.
Every such figure must be rendered from the database, never hardcoded from the design.

Two design decisions carrying real product weight:

**Quoting the retailer's own product name on every offer row** is the honesty mechanism —
it lets a user verify our match themselves, and it is exactly what would expose colour
pooling if a competitor did it.

**`2+ магазина` default-on** handles the 72%-single-store reality: the catalogue leads
with pages that have something to compare, and single-store pages say
`1 магазин · сравнить нечего` rather than pretending.

---

## 8. Failure handling

- **Source isolation.** Each source harvests in its own transaction. One failure degrades
  coverage; it never aborts the cycle or corrupts other sources.
- **Staleness is visible.** `last_seen` > 24h → hidden from pages. > 7d → dropped from the
  index. Store pages show the real last successful crawl. This is the direct fix for
  uzprice's joybox — dead since 2026-04-01, still flagged `HEALTHY`.
- **No price without provenance.** An offer missing `url`, `name_raw` or `last_seen` is
  rejected at write time.
- **Ambiguity is counted, not guessed.** `unresolved_offer` rate crossing ~5% raises an
  alert.
- **Sanity fences.** Price must land in 100k–100M sum, catching the whole unit-bug class
  (alifshop's tiyin divisor, a source switching currency).
- **Documented traps become assertions.** uzum token refreshes 5 min before `exp`; a
  GraphQL `200` carrying an `errors` key is a failure, not a success.
- **Idempotent crawls.** Unique on `(store_id, source_key)`; a re-run never duplicates.

---

## 9. Testing

- **Matcher unit tests** seeded from the existing `audit_*.json` files — thousands of real
  candidate names with scores and rejection reasons, free golden data. Pins all three
  regressions: iPhone Air vs 16/17, Uzbek colours, Pro vs Pro Max.
- **Clustering tests** on fixtures, asserting the ambiguous-RAM case lands in `unresolved`
  rather than attaching.
- **Source contract tests** — one live smoke test per source per day, asserting documented
  field names and units still exist. This catches silent API changes before they become
  wrong prices.
- **uzprice as an external oracle** — their API is open; a scheduled job compares our
  variant-exact minimum against their offers re-filtered to the correct colour and alerts
  if agreement falls below the ~95% measured.
- **Price-link consistency** — every filled price has a link and vice versa, per source.

---

## 10. Crawl schedule

Full sweep every 4 hours (measured 8–13 min, ample headroom). Sequential per source,
0.3–0.6s between requests, real User-Agent and the `Origin`/`Referer` each SPA sends.
Sources staggered so we never hit two hard simultaneously.

---

## 11. Pending review — decisions requiring the owner

1. **Repository location.** Spec currently written into `DerCompact/docs/`, which also
   holds unrelated pricing spreadsheets. Recommend a dedicated `narxnoma/` repo.
2. **Domain and brand registration** for Narxnoma.
3. **VPS provider and provisioning** in Uzbekistan.
4. **Monetization.** uzprice currently sends raw outbound links with no affiliate
   parameter. Whether we pursue CPC/affiliate deals affects `/api/out/` design.
5. **Legal pages** — privacy policy and PD-processing consent are required for a UZ
   consumer site; uzprice publishes both.
6. **Robots/ToS posture** toward sources — we use documented public JSON APIs politely,
   but this deserves an explicit decision.

---

## 12. Deferred, in priority order

1. Price-history UI (data accumulates from day one)
2. Uzbek locale
3. Favourites, profile, price-drop alerts
4. Categories beyond smartphones — laptops, TVs next by value
5. asaxiy, castore, radius (uzprice indexes them; asaxiy carries 12% of their offers)
