================================================
"""Command line entry point:
    python -m narxnoma.cli fetch --source SLUG [--category C | --query Q]
    python -m narxnoma.cli harvest [--source SLUG]
    python -m narxnoma.cli report
    python -m narxnoma.cli research run|workbook|check ...   (see narxnoma/research/cli.py)
"""
import argparse
import dataclasses
import json
import logging
import sys

from narxnoma.db import repository
from narxnoma.db.connection import connect
from narxnoma.matching.keys import CATEGORIES
from narxnoma.db.migrate import migrate
from narxnoma.pipeline.aggregate import recompute_variant_prices
from narxnoma.pipeline.backfill import DEFAULT_MAX_QUERIES, backfill_search_only_sources
from narxnoma.pipeline import cluster
from narxnoma.pipeline.cluster import cluster_offers
from narxnoma.pipeline.extract import identify
from narxnoma.pipeline.quality import quality_report
from narxnoma.pipeline.quality import render as render_quality
from narxnoma.pipeline.harvest import HarvestResult, harvest_all
from narxnoma.pipeline.report import SourceCoverage, coverage_report
from narxnoma.sources import SOURCES

# A cycle makes 400+ requests at up to a 90-second read timeout; two of them
# overlapping double our request rate at every retailer at once. The advisory
# lock is session-scoped, so Postgres releases it automatically if the
# process dies however it dies -- no cleanup logic to get wrong.
CYCLE_LOCK_KEY = 20260802


def render_report(rows: list[SourceCoverage]) -> str:
    """Readable coverage table. Suspicious rows get a `*** SUSPICIOUS ***`
    marker so they cannot be skimmed past -- a source that quietly lost most
    of its catalogue is the one failure mode nothing else in this system
    would otherwise surface.

    The marker NAMES the rules that fired, because the three of them call for
    three different responses: "never fetched" means the source has never
    stored anything, "stale" means it stored rows once and stopped refreshing
    them (the upsert-only trap -- the count still looks healthy), and
    "last run failed" means the harvest itself errored. A bare SUSPICIOUS
    would leave an operator to guess which.
    """
    header = (f"{'slug':<10} {'offers':>7} {'floor':>7} {'median':>10} "
              f"{'oldest_seen':<20} {'newest_seen':<20} {'age_h':>7} "
              f"{'last_run_ok':<12} flag")
    lines = [header, "-" * len(header)]
    for r in rows:
        oldest = r.oldest_seen.isoformat(timespec="seconds") if r.oldest_seen else "-"
        newest = r.newest_seen.isoformat(timespec="seconds") if r.newest_seen else "-"
        median = str(r.median_price) if r.median_price is not None else "-"
        age = f"{r.age_hours:.1f}" if r.age_hours is not None else "-"
        last_run_ok = "-" if r.last_run_ok is None else str(r.last_run_ok)
        flag = f"*** SUSPICIOUS: {', '.join(r.reasons)} ***" if r.is_suspicious else ""
        lines.append(f"{r.slug:<10} {r.offers:>7} {r.expected_min:>7} {median:>10} "
                     f"{oldest:<20} {newest:<20} {age:>7} "
                     f"{last_run_ok:<12} {flag}")
    return "\n".join(lines)


def report_exit_code(rows: list[SourceCoverage]) -> int:
    """Non-zero the moment any source is suspicious -- a crawl that
    "succeeded" while losing most of a catalogue is not a success."""
    return 1 if any(r.is_suspicious for r in rows) else 0


def render_status(result: HarvestResult) -> str:
    """Render one of three visibly distinct states for a harvest result.

    `skipped` is checked before `ok` on purpose: a skipped source currently
    also carries ok=True (it isn't a failure), so checking `ok` first would
    render it as plain "ok" -- indistinguishable from a source that
    genuinely swept its whole catalogue. That was the bug: mediapark's
    skip looked identical to a real, successful, zero-listing run.
    """
    if result.skipped:
        return f"SKIPPED ({result.error})"
    if not result.ok:
        return f"FAILED: {result.error}"
    return "ok"


def run_clustering(conn) -> tuple[int, int, int]:
    """reconcile -> extract -> cluster -> aggregate. Returns (attached, created,
    unresolved).

    The reconcile step runs first so that an offer whose name has changed since
    it was attached is back in the unattached pool before clustering loads it.
    Without it a source fix can correct `name_raw` and still leave every
    affected offer sitting on the variant the old, wrong name produced.
    """
    detached = cluster.detach_drifted_offers(conn)
    if detached:
        logging.info("reconciled: detached %d offers whose name no longer matches "
                     "their variant", detached)
    renamed = repository.refresh_display_names(conn)
    if renamed:
        logging.info("reconciled: regenerated %d display names", renamed)
    rows = repository.load_unattached_offers(conn)
    result = cluster_offers(conn, (identify(row) for row in rows))
    # After re-attachment, not before: a variant emptied by the reconcile above
    # is often refilled by the clustering that follows, and deleting it first
    # would churn its id (and its URL) for no reason.
    orphaned = repository.delete_orphan_variants(conn)
    if orphaned:
        logging.info("removed %d variants no offer references any more", orphaned)
    recompute_variant_prices(conn)
    return result.attached, result.created_variants, result.unresolved


def run_backfill(conn) -> int:
    """Query every search-only source for variants the catalogue already has."""
    ids = repository.store_ids(conn)
    written = 0
    with conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute("""
            SELECT v.id, v.display_name
              FROM variant v JOIN variant_price vp ON vp.variant_id = v.id
             ORDER BY vp.store_count DESC, vp.computed_at
             LIMIT %s
        """, (DEFAULT_MAX_QUERIES,))
        variants = cur.fetchall()

    for source in SOURCES.values():
        if source.can_sweep or source.slug not in ids:
            continue
        result = backfill_search_only_sources(conn, source, ids[source.slug], variants)
        logging.info("backfill %-10s queried=%d matched=%d offers=%d",
                     source.slug, result.queried, result.variants_matched,
                     result.offers_written)
        written += result.offers_written
    return written


def _stage(name: str, fn, outcomes: dict) -> None:
    """Run one stage, recording its outcome without letting it kill the rest.

    A clustering failure must not lose the harvest that preceded it: the
    offers are already durably written, and re-running the cycle would just
    re-fetch several thousand listings from retailers for nothing.
    """
    try:
        fn()
        outcomes[name] = True
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - stage isolation is the point
        logging.exception("stage %s failed", name)
        outcomes[name] = False
        logging.error("%-10s FAILED: %s", name, exc)


def run_fetch(source, category: str, query: str | None, limit: int | None,
              raw: bool, out) -> int:
    """Stream one source's listings as JSON lines, one Listing per line.

    This is the whole engine with the database removed: no Postgres, no
    matcher, no clustering -- exactly what the retailer said, in the shape
    `Listing` guarantees. A search-only source asked to sweep is refused
    here, before any request is made, for the same reason `Source.sweep`
    raises: an empty stream that exits 0 is indistinguishable from an
    empty shop.
    """
    if query is None and not source.can_sweep:
        logging.error("%s cannot be swept (search-only); pass --query", source.slug)
        return 1
    listings = source.search(query) if query is not None else source.sweep(category)
    written = 0
    for listing in listings:
        row = dataclasses.asdict(listing)
        if not raw:
            row.pop("raw")
        out.write(json.dumps(row, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
        written += 1
        if limit is not None and written >= limit:
            break
    logging.info("%-10s wrote %d listings", source.slug, written)
    return 0


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    argv = sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else argv
    if argv and argv[0] == "research":
        # database-free, and kept out of the parser below so its options stay in one place
        from narxnoma.research.cli import main as research_main
        return research_main(argv[1:])
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="narxnoma")
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
    fetch = sub.add_parser("fetch", help="print one source's listings as JSON lines; "
                                        "needs no database")
    fetch.add_argument("--source", required=True, choices=sorted(SOURCES))
    fetch.add_argument("--category", default="smartphones", choices=sorted(CATEGORIES),
                       help="catalogue sweep to run (default: smartphones)")
    fetch.add_argument("--query", help="search instead of sweeping; the only way "
                                       "into a search-only source such as mediapark")
    fetch.add_argument("--limit", type=int, help="stop after this many listings")
    fetch.add_argument("--raw", action="store_true",
                       help="include the retailer's untouched payload per row")
    harvest = sub.add_parser("harvest", help="sweep retailers into the database")
    harvest.add_argument("--source", action="append", choices=sorted(SOURCES),
                         help="limit to these sources (repeatable)")
    # One category at a time is how a stalled or newly-configured category gets
    # re-run without re-fetching the other six -- a full sweep is 400+ requests
    # and 8-13 minutes, so re-running everything to fix ovens is wasteful and
    # discourages fixing ovens.
    harvest.add_argument("--category", action="append", choices=sorted(CATEGORIES),
                         help="limit to these categories (repeatable; "
                              "default: every category)")
    sub.add_parser("report", help="print per-source coverage and freshness; "
                                  "exits non-zero if any source is suspicious")
    sub.add_parser("cluster", help="identify offers and attach them to canonical "
                                   "products, refusing anything ambiguous")
    sub.add_parser("aggregate", help="recompute each variant's price rollup")
    sub.add_parser("quality", help="matcher health; exits non-zero if the "
                                   "unresolved rate is above the threshold")
    sub.add_parser("cycle", help="harvest, then cluster, aggregate and report "
                                 "quality, isolating each stage")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(asctime)s %(levelname)s %(message)s")

    if args.command == "fetch":
        # JSON lines are meant to be piped into a file; a Windows console
        # defaulting to cp1251 would otherwise raise on the first Uzbek name.
        if hasattr(sys.stdout, "reconfigure"):
            sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8")
        return run_fetch(SOURCES[args.source], args.category, args.query,
                         args.limit, args.raw, sys.stdout)

    if args.command == "report":
        with connect() as conn:
            migrate(conn)
            rows = coverage_report(conn)
        print(render_report(rows))
        return report_exit_code(rows)

    if args.command == "cluster":
        with connect() as conn:
            migrate(conn)
            attached, created, unresolved = run_clustering(conn)
        logging.info("attached=%d new_variants=%d unresolved=%d",
                     attached, created, unresolved)
        return 0

    if args.command == "aggregate":
        with connect() as conn:
            migrate(conn)
            written = recompute_variant_prices(conn)
        logging.info("variant_price rows written: %d", written)
        return 0

    if args.command == "quality":
        with connect() as conn:
            migrate(conn)
            report = quality_report(conn)
        print(render_quality(report))
        return 1 if report.is_alerting else 0

    if args.command == "cycle":
        outcomes: dict[str, bool] = {}
        with connect() as conn:
            migrate(conn)
            if not repository.try_advisory_lock(conn, CYCLE_LOCK_KEY):
                logging.error(
                    "another cycle is already running; refusing to start a "
                    "second one. Two concurrent cycles double our request rate "
                    "at every retailer at once.")
                return 1
            results: list = []
            _stage("harvest", lambda: results.extend(
                harvest_all(conn, [SOURCES[s] for s in sorted(SOURCES)])), outcomes)
            _stage("cluster", lambda: run_clustering(conn), outcomes)
            # Pass B: the sources that cannot be swept are reached by asking
            # about products the catalogue now knows exist. It runs after
            # clustering for that reason, and its results are clustered on the
            # NEXT cycle -- a search hit is a suggestion, not evidence.
            _stage("backfill", lambda: run_backfill(conn), outcomes)
            rows = coverage_report(conn)
            report = quality_report(conn)

        for r in results:
            logging.info("%-10s seen=%-6d kept=%-6d %s",
                         r.slug, r.seen, r.kept, render_status(r))
        print(render_report(rows))
        print()
        print(render_quality(report))

        # The exit code reflects the worst outcome across the whole cycle.
        failed_stage = not all(outcomes.values())
        failed_source = any(not r.ok and not r.skipped for r in results)
        return 1 if (failed_stage or failed_source
                     or report_exit_code(rows) or report.is_alerting) else 0

    # harvest
    chosen = [SOURCES[s] for s in (args.source or sorted(SOURCES))]

    with connect() as conn:
        migrate(conn)
        results = harvest_all(conn, chosen, categories=args.category)
        rows = coverage_report(conn)

    for r in results:
        logging.info("%-10s seen=%-6d kept=%-6d %s", r.slug, r.seen, r.kept, render_status(r))
    print(render_report(rows))
    return 0 if all(r.ok for r in results) and report_exit_code(rows) == 0 else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

"""Environment-driven settings. Import this, never os.environ directly."""
import os
from dataclasses import dataclass

USER_AGENT = (
    "Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 "
    "(KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/150.0.0.0 Safari/537.36"
)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Settings:
    dsn: str
    user_agent: str = USER_AGENT
    min_delay: float = 0.3
    max_delay: float = 0.6
    connect_timeout: int = 15
    read_timeout: int = 90


def load_settings() -> Settings:
    return Settings(
        dsn=os.environ.get("NARXNOMA_DSN", "postgresql://narxnoma:narxnoma@localhost:5432/narxnoma"),
        min_delay=float(os.environ.get("NARXNOMA_MIN_DELAY", "0.3")),
        max_delay=float(os.environ.get("NARXNOMA_MAX_DELAY", "0.6")),
    )

FILE: narxnoma-crawler/narxnoma/daily.py

"""Unattended daily jobs: nightly price refresh, morning market report to Telegram.

Runs on the owner's own machine from the OS scheduler, with no Claude session involved.

    python -m narxnoma.daily refresh            03:00  re-sweep every store into the cache
    python -m narxnoma.daily report             09:00  catalogue -> research workbook -> Telegram
    python -m narxnoma.daily probe              show the shape of the catalogue response (no values)
    python -m narxnoma.daily report --no-send   build the file, do not send

Everything private lives in an env file OUTSIDE the repo (default `~/.narxnoma-daily.env`,
override with `--env-file` or `NARXNOMA_DAILY_ENV`); see docs/daily-report.md. Nothing about
the catalogue API (URL, token, field names) is hard-coded here.
"""

import argparse
import csv
import json
import logging
import os
import shutil
import sys
import tempfile
import time
from datetime import date
from pathlib import Path

import requests

logger = logging.getLogger("narxnoma.daily")

DEFAULT_ENV = Path.home() / ".narxnoma-daily.env"
LIST_KEYS = ("items", "results", "data", "products", "rows")
NAME_FIELDS = ("name", "title", "product_name")
PRICE_FIELDS = ("price", "sale_price", "retail_price", "current_price")
CATEGORY_FIELDS = ("category", "category_name", "category.name", "category_title")
ACTIVE_FIELDS = ("is_active", "active", "published", "is_published")
MAX_PAGES = 500


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- config


def load_env(path: str | Path | None) -> dict:
    """KEY=VALUE lines (quotes and `#` comments allowed) layered under the process env."""
    cfg: dict = {}
    p = Path(path) if path else DEFAULT_ENV
    if p.exists():
        for line in p.read_text(encoding="utf-8-sig").splitlines():
            line = line.strip()
            if not line or line.startswith("#") or "=" not in line:
                continue
            k, v = line.split("=", 1)
            cfg[k.strip()] = _env_value(v)
    for k, v in os.environ.items():
        if k.startswith(("ECOM_", "TG_", "NARXNOMA_")):
            cfg[k] = v
    return cfg


def _env_value(v: str) -> str:
    """A quoted value is taken as is; an unquoted one ends at ` #` (an inline comment), so
    `TG_SESSION=C:\\x\\s   # note` is the path, not the path plus the note."""
    v = v.strip()
    if v[:1] in ("'", '"') and v.count(v[0]) >= 2:
        return v[1 : v.index(v[0], 1)]
    for sep in (" #", "\t#"):
        if sep in v:
            v = v[: v.index(sep)]
    return v.strip()


def telegram_problem(cfg: dict) -> str | None:
    """Why a send cannot work, or None. Checked before the report does any work: a bad session
    path also breaks the failure notice, so without this check nothing would arrive and the
    only trace would be report.log."""
    missing = [k for k in ("TG_SESSION", "TG_API_ID", "TG_API_HASH") if not cfg.get(k)]
    if missing:
        return f"missing in the env file: {', '.join(missing)}"
    if not str(cfg["TG_API_ID"]).isdigit():
        return "TG_API_ID must be a number"
    if not _session_path(cfg).exists():
        return f"Telegram session file not found: {_session_path(cfg)}"
    try:
        import telethon  # noqa: F401
    except ImportError:
        return "telethon is not installed (pip install telethon)"
    return None


def _session_path(cfg: dict) -> Path:
    s = Path(cfg["TG_SESSION"])  # Telethon takes it with or without ".session"
    return s if s.suffix == ".session" else s.with_suffix(".session")


def read_token(cfg: dict) -> str:
    """The bearer token is rotated by another job, so it is read fresh at every run.
    `ECOM_TOKEN_FILE` may be plain text, a JSON object, or a KEY=VALUE env file."""
    if cfg.get("ECOM_TOKEN_FILE"):
        raw = Path(cfg["ECOM_TOKEN_FILE"]).read_text(encoding="utf-8-sig").strip()
        if raw.startswith("{"):
            obj = json.loads(raw)
            for k in ("access_token", "token", "bearer", "ECOM_TOKEN"):
                if obj.get(k):
                    return str(obj[k]).strip()
            raise ValueError("token file is JSON but has no access_token/token key")
        if "=" in raw.splitlines()[0]:
            for line in raw.splitlines():
                k, _, v = line.partition("=")
                if k.strip() in ("ECOM_TOKEN", "TOKEN", "ACCESS_TOKEN"):
                    return v.strip().strip("'\"")
            raise ValueError("token file has no ECOM_TOKEN= line")
        return raw.removeprefix("Bearer ").strip()
    if cfg.get("ECOM_TOKEN"):
        return cfg["ECOM_TOKEN"].removeprefix("Bearer ").strip()
    raise ValueError("set ECOM_TOKEN_FILE (preferred) or ECOM_TOKEN")


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- catalogue


def dig(obj, path: str):
    """`a.b.c` lookup through dicts; None when any step is missing."""
    for part in path.split("."):
        if not isinstance(obj, dict) or part not in obj:
            return None
        obj = obj[part]
    return obj


def first_field(obj: dict, candidates) -> object:
    for c in candidates:
        v = dig(obj, c)
        if v not in (None, ""):
            return v
    return None


def extract_items(payload) -> list:
    """The product list inside one page, whatever envelope it comes in."""
    if isinstance(payload, list):
        return payload
    if isinstance(payload, dict):
        for k in LIST_KEYS:
            if isinstance(payload.get(k), list):
                return payload[k]
        for v in payload.values():  # {"data": {"items": [...]}}
            if isinstance(v, dict):
                got = extract_items(v)
                if got:
                    return got
    return []


def fetch_catalogue(cfg: dict, session: requests.Session | None = None) -> list[dict]:
    """Walk the paginated admin endpoint and return every raw product dict."""
    url = cfg.get("ECOM_PRODUCTS_URL")
    if not url:
        raise ValueError("set ECOM_PRODUCTS_URL")
    size = int(cfg.get("ECOM_PAGE_SIZE", 100))
    params = dict(p.split("=", 1) for p in cfg.get("ECOM_EXTRA_PARAMS", "").split("&") if "=" in p)
    sess = session or requests.Session()
    headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {read_token(cfg)}", "Accept": "application/json"}
    pause = float(cfg.get("ECOM_PAUSE_S", 0.3))
    out: list[dict] = []
    seen_first = None
    for page in range(1, MAX_PAGES + 1):
        r = sess.get(
            url, params={**params, "page": page, "page_size": size}, headers=headers, timeout=60
        )
        if r.status_code in (401, 403):
            raise PermissionError(
                f"catalogue API said {r.status_code}: the bearer token is expired or wrong"
            )
        r.raise_for_status()
        items = extract_items(r.json())
        if not items:
            break
        marker = json.dumps(items[0], sort_keys=True, default=str)
        if marker == seen_first:  # a server that ignores `page` would loop forever
            break
        seen_first = seen_first or marker
        out.extend(items)
        if len(items) < size:
            break
        time.sleep(pause)
    else:
        raise RuntimeError(f"more than {MAX_PAGES} pages; refusing to continue")
    return out


def to_targets(items: list[dict], cfg: dict) -> tuple[list[dict], dict]:
    """-> (rows for the research input file, stats). Rows without a name or a price are dropped
    and counted; inactive ones too when ECOM_ONLY_ACTIVE (default on)."""
    f_name = [cfg["ECOM_FIELD_NAME"]] if cfg.get("ECOM_FIELD_NAME") else NAME_FIELDS
    f_price = [cfg["ECOM_FIELD_PRICE"]] if cfg.get("ECOM_FIELD_PRICE") else PRICE_FIELDS
    f_cat = [cfg["ECOM_FIELD_CATEGORY"]] if cfg.get("ECOM_FIELD_CATEGORY") else CATEGORY_FIELDS
    f_act = [cfg["ECOM_FIELD_ACTIVE"]] if cfg.get("ECOM_FIELD_ACTIVE") else ACTIVE_FIELDS
    only_active = cfg.get("ECOM_ONLY_ACTIVE", "1") not in ("0", "false", "no")
    stats = {"seen": len(items), "inactive": 0, "no_name": 0, "no_price": 0, "no_category": 0}
    rows = []
    for it in items:
        if only_active:
            flag = first_field(it, f_act)
            if flag is not None and not _truthy(flag):
                stats["inactive"] += 1
                continue
        name = first_field(it, f_name)
        if not name:
            stats["no_name"] += 1
            continue
        price = _num(first_field(it, f_price))
        if not price:
            stats["no_price"] += 1
            continue
        cat = first_field(it, f_cat)
        cat = cat.get("name") if isinstance(cat, dict) else cat
        if not cat:
            stats["no_category"] += 1
        rows.append({"name": str(name).strip(), "our price": price, "category": cat or ""})
    stats["kept"] = len(rows)
    return rows, stats


def _truthy(v) -> bool:
    if isinstance(v, str):
        return v.strip().lower() not in ("0", "false", "no", "inactive", "")
    return bool(v)


def _num(v) -> float | None:
    if v is None or isinstance(v, bool):
        return None
    try:
        return float(str(v).replace(" ", "").replace(",", "."))
    except ValueError:
        return None


def write_targets(rows: list[dict], path: Path) -> None:
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with path.open("w", newline="", encoding="utf-8-sig") as fh:
        w = csv.DictWriter(fh, fieldnames=["name", "our price", "category"])
        w.writeheader()
        w.writerows(rows)


def shape(items: list[dict]) -> dict:
    """Field names and value types of the first product, never the values (safe to paste)."""
    if not items:
        return {}

    def walk(o, prefix=""):
        out = {}
        for k, v in o.items():
            if isinstance(v, dict):
                out.update(walk(v, f"{prefix}{k}."))
            else:
                out[f"{prefix}{k}"] = type(v).__name__
        return out

    return walk(items[0])


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- locking


class Lock:
    """One job at a time: `refresh` (03:00) and `report` (09:00) never run on the same cache
    together. A lock older than `stale_h` is taken over (a crashed run must not block forever)."""

    def __init__(self, path: Path, stale_h: float = 6):
        self.path, self.stale_h = path, stale_h

    def acquire(self, wait_s: float = 0) -> bool:
        deadline = time.time() + wait_s
        while True:
            try:
                self.path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
                fd = os.open(self.path, os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL | os.O_WRONLY)
                os.write(fd, str(os.getpid()).encode())
                os.close(fd)
                return True
            except FileExistsError:
                if time.time() - self.path.stat().st_mtime > self.stale_h * 3600:
                    logger.warning("taking over a stale lock %s", self.path)
                    self.path.unlink(missing_ok=True)
                    continue
                if time.time() >= deadline:
                    return False
                time.sleep(15)

    def release(self) -> None:
        self.path.unlink(missing_ok=True)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- telegram


def send_telegram(cfg: dict, path: Path, caption: str) -> None:
    """Send a file to Saved Messages through the owner's existing Telegram user session.

    The listener that owns the session keeps it open, so the send works on a temporary COPY of
    the session file, deletes it afterwards, and never logs in (a login would invalidate the
    listener's authorization). API id/hash come from the env file only at send time."""
    try:
        from telethon.sync import TelegramClient
    except ImportError as exc:  # pragma: no cover - environment dependent
        raise RuntimeError("pip install telethon to send to Telegram") from exc
    src = _session_path(cfg)
    if not src.exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"Telegram session file not found: {src}")
    tmpdir = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="narxnoma_tg_"))
    try:
        copy = tmpdir / "send.session"
        shutil.copyfile(src, copy)
        client = TelegramClient(
            str(copy.with_suffix("")), int(cfg["TG_API_ID"]), cfg["TG_API_HASH"]
        )
        client.connect()
        try:
            if not client.is_user_authorized():
                raise RuntimeError("Telegram session is not authorised; log it in once by hand")
            client.send_file("me", str(path), caption=caption)
        finally:
            client.disconnect()
    finally:
        shutil.rmtree(tmpdir, ignore_errors=True)


def send_text(cfg: dict, text: str) -> None:
    """Failure notices go to the same place; a silent failure is worse than a noisy one."""
    try:
        from telethon.sync import TelegramClient
    except ImportError:  # pragma: no cover
        return
    tmpdir = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="narxnoma_tg_"))
    try:
        shutil.copyfile(_session_path(cfg), tmpdir / "send.session")
        client = TelegramClient(str(tmpdir / "send"), int(cfg["TG_API_ID"]), cfg["TG_API_HASH"])
        client.connect()
        try:
            if client.is_user_authorized():
                client.send_message("me", text)
        finally:
            client.disconnect()
    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 -- a failed notice must not mask the original error
        logger.exception("could not send the failure notice")
    finally:
        shutil.rmtree(tmpdir, ignore_errors=True)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- jobs


def work_dir(cfg: dict) -> Path:
    return Path(cfg.get("NARXNOMA_DAILY_DIR", Path.home() / "narxnoma-daily"))


def cache_dir(cfg: dict) -> Path:
    return work_dir(cfg) / "research_cache"


def job_refresh(cfg: dict) -> int:
    from narxnoma.matching.keys import CATEGORIES
    from narxnoma.research.collect import default_markets, refresh_cache

    lock = Lock(work_dir(cfg) / "daily.lock")
    if not lock.acquire(wait_s=0):
        logger.error("another daily job holds the lock; refresh skipped")
        return 2
    try:
        res = refresh_cache(default_markets(), sorted(CATEGORIES), cache_dir(cfg))
    finally:
        lock.release()
    logger.info("refresh: %d sweeps ok, %d failed", len(res["ok"]), len(res["failed"]))
    if res["failed"] and cfg.get("TG_SESSION"):
        lines = [f"{s}/{c}: {why[:80]}" for s, c, why in res["failed"][:12]]
        send_text(cfg, "narxnoma 03:00 refresh: failures\n" + "\n".join(lines))
    return 1 if res["failed"] and not res["ok"] else 0


def job_report(cfg: dict, send: bool = True, wait_lock_min: float = 90) -> int:
    from narxnoma.research.build import make_workbook
    from narxnoma.research.run import run_research
    from narxnoma.research.targets import load_targets

    out_dir = work_dir(cfg) / "reports"
    stamp = date.today().isoformat()
    if send and (why := telegram_problem(cfg)):
        logger.error("report not started, Telegram cannot send: %s", why)
        return 1
    lock = Lock(work_dir(cfg) / "daily.lock")
    # the nightly refresh may still be running on a slow night: wait for it, do not race it
    if not lock.acquire(wait_s=wait_lock_min * 60):
        logger.error("the refresh is still running after %s min; report skipped", wait_lock_min)
        if send and cfg.get("TG_SESSION"):
            send_text(
                cfg, f"narxnoma {stamp}: the 03:00 refresh was still running, no report today"
            )
        return 2
    try:
        items = fetch_catalogue(cfg)
        rows, stats = to_targets(items, cfg)
        logger.info("catalogue: %s", stats)
        if not rows:
            raise RuntimeError(f"no usable products in the catalogue response ({stats})")
        targets_path = out_dir / f"products_{stamp}.csv"
        write_targets(rows, targets_path)
        targets = load_targets(targets_path)
        research = run_research(
            targets,
            None,
            cache_dir=cache_dir(cfg),
            max_age_h=float(cfg.get("NARXNOMA_MAX_AGE_H", 30)),
            force=False,
            title=f"Market analysis {stamp}",
        )
        xlsx = out_dir / f"market_analysis_{stamp}.xlsx"
        research.to_json(xlsx.with_suffix(".json"))
        info = make_workbook(research, xlsx, pivots="auto", model="auto", verify=False)
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 -- always tell the owner, then fail loudly
        logger.exception("report failed")
        if send and cfg.get("TG_SESSION"):
            send_text(
                cfg, f"narxnoma {stamp}: report FAILED - {type(exc).__name__}: {str(exc)[:300]}"
            )
        return 1
    finally:
        lock.release()

    caption = (
        f"Market analysis {stamp}: {stats['kept']} products, "
        f"{info['layout']['n_offers']} offers"
        + (
            f"; {stats['no_category']} without a category were not matched"
            if stats["no_category"]
            else ""
        )
    )
    logger.info("wrote %s", xlsx)
    if send:
        # the cube-status job also sends around 09:00 from a copy of the same session; if the
        # two collide Telegram may refuse one of them, so wait and try again instead of failing
        for attempt in range(1, 5):
            try:
                send_telegram(cfg, xlsx, caption)
                break
            except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
                logger.exception("Telegram send failed (attempt %d/4)", attempt)
                if attempt == 4:
                    return 1
                time.sleep(90)
        logger.info("sent to Telegram Saved Messages")
    return 0


def job_probe(cfg: dict) -> int:
    items = fetch_catalogue({**cfg, "ECOM_PAGE_SIZE": "5"})
    print(json.dumps(shape(items), indent=2, ensure_ascii=False))
    rows, stats = to_targets(items[:5], cfg)
    print("with the current field mapping:", stats)
    return 0


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        prog="narxnoma.daily",
        description=__doc__,
        formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter,
    )
    p.add_argument("job", choices=["refresh", "report", "probe"])
    p.add_argument("--env-file", default=os.environ.get("NARXNOMA_DAILY_ENV"))
    p.add_argument("--no-send", action="store_true", help="report: build the file, skip Telegram")
    args = p.parse_args(argv)
    cfg = load_env(args.env_file)
    wd = work_dir(cfg)
    wd.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    logging.basicConfig(
        level=logging.INFO,
        format="%(asctime)s %(levelname)s %(message)s",
        handlers=[
            logging.StreamHandler(),
            logging.FileHandler(wd / f"{args.job}.log", encoding="utf-8"),
        ],
    )
    if hasattr(sys.stdout, "reconfigure"):
        sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8")
    if args.job == "refresh":
        return job_refresh(cfg)
    if args.job == "probe":
        return job_probe(cfg)
    return job_report(cfg, send=not args.no_send)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

FILE: narxnoma-crawler/narxnoma/db/connection.py

import contextlib
from typing import Iterator

import psycopg

from narxnoma.config import load_settings


@contextlib.contextmanager
def connect(dsn: str | None = None) -> Iterator[psycopg.Connection]:
    """Open a connection that COMMITS on clean exit and rolls back on error.

    The commit is not optional and its absence was a real, silent bug. psycopg
    opens an implicit transaction on the first statement -- including a plain
    read, such as the catalogue load every pipeline stage begins with. Once
    that transaction is open, the repository's own `with conn.transaction()`
    blocks nest inside it as savepoints, which release without committing. So
    a `close()` with no commit rolled back everything the process had done.

    The symptom was as quiet as it gets: `recompute_variant_prices` reported
    "recomputed prices for 1380 variants", every log line looked healthy, the
    exit code was whatever the reports said -- and the database was untouched.
    """
    target = dsn or load_settings().dsn
    conn = psycopg.connect(target)
    try:
        yield conn
        conn.commit()
    except BaseException:
        conn.rollback()
        raise
    finally:
        conn.close()

import pathlib

import psycopg

SCHEMA = pathlib.Path(__file__).with_name("schema.sql")


def migrate(conn: psycopg.Connection) -> None:
    """Apply schema.sql. Idempotent by construction."""
    with conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute(SCHEMA.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    conn.commit()



================================================
FILE: narxnoma-crawler/narxnoma/db/repository.py

"""The only place that writes offers. Keeps SQL out of the pipeline.

Commit boundary: each function below commits its own transaction
independently. start_run, the data writes (record_raw_offers /
upsert_offers) and finish_run are deliberately *not* one unit of work.
For a long-running crawl that is the right choice -- if a source dies half
way through a sweep, the listings already written should stay written
rather than being rolled back along with everything else, and start_run,
finish_run and the upsert are all idempotent enough that re-running a
failed step is safe.
"""
import functools
import json
from typing import Any, Iterable
from uuid import UUID

import psycopg
from psycopg.types.json import Jsonb

from narxnoma.matching import VariantKey, display_name, slug
from narxnoma.sources.base import Listing


def _scrub_nuls(value: Any) -> Any:
    """Recursively strip NUL (\\u0000) characters from strings nested in
    dicts, lists and scalars. \\u0000 is valid JSON but PostgreSQL's jsonb
    type rejects it outright with error 22P05, and retailer payloads --
    parsed straight from their API JSON -- occasionally contain it."""
    if isinstance(value, str):
        return value.replace("\x00", "")
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        return {k: _scrub_nuls(v) for k, v in value.items()}
    if isinstance(value, list):
        return [_scrub_nuls(v) for v in value]
    return value


# default=str: a retailer payload can contain a value json.dumps cannot
# serialise on its own (e.g. something that survived parsing as a non-JSON
# type). Rather than raising a TypeError mid-batch and aborting every row,
# such a value is degraded to its str() form.
_dump_json = functools.partial(json.dumps, ensure_ascii=False, default=str)


def store_ids(conn: psycopg.Connection) -> dict[str, UUID]:
    # Every function in this module wraps its body in conn.transaction(),
    # which commits on success and rolls back on error. Without this, a
    # failed statement leaves the connection in psycopg's "aborted
    # transaction" state, and every subsequent call on that connection
    # raises InFailedSqlTransaction -- including the finish_run(ok=False,
    # ...) call a caller makes to record the very failure that just
    # happened. The rollback here is what keeps the connection usable for
    # that call.
    with conn.transaction():
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute("SELECT slug, id FROM store WHERE is_active")
            return {slug: sid for slug, sid in cur.fetchall()}


def record_raw_offers(conn: psycopg.Connection, store_id: UUID,
                      listings: Iterable[Listing]) -> int:
    """Append one row per observation. Never updates -- this is the permanent
    log price history is later derived from, not a cache of current state."""
    rows = [
        (store_id, listing.source_key, listing.name_raw, listing.price, listing.url,
         listing.availability, listing.image_url, listing.category,
         Jsonb(_scrub_nuls(listing.raw), dumps=_dump_json))
        for listing in listings
    ]
    if not rows:
        return 0
    with conn.transaction():
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            cur.executemany(
                "INSERT INTO raw_offer"
                " (store_id, source_key, name_raw, price, url, availability, image_url, category, payload)"
                " VALUES (%s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s)", rows)
    return len(rows)


def upsert_offers(conn: psycopg.Connection, store_id: UUID,
                  listings: Iterable[Listing]) -> tuple[int, int]:
    """Insert new listings, refresh existing ones. first_seen never moves.

    RETURNING always yields the *new* row version, whether the INSERT or the
    ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE branch fired. Its xmax is 0 (true) when INSERT
    fired -- a brand-new row has never been locked by anyone. It is
    non-zero (false) when DO UPDATE fired instead: Postgres locks the
    conflicting row first while evaluating ON CONFLICT, and that locker's
    transaction id is carried forward onto the new row version's xmax. This
    is an undocumented detail of how ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE is implemented,
    not a guarantee made by the PostgreSQL documentation -- re-verify it
    against the release notes before relying on it across a major version
    upgrade. first_seen is omitted from the DO UPDATE SET list entirely, so
    on conflict it keeps its original DEFAULT now() value from the first
    insert.

    Deliberately not batched into a single multi-row VALUES statement: with
    ON CONFLICT, one statement touching the same conflict key twice raises
    "cannot affect row a second time", which a buggy client sweep could
    trigger. The per-row loop tolerates that; a batched statement would not.
    """
    inserted = updated = 0
    with conn.transaction():
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            for listing in listings:
                cur.execute(
                                    "INSERT INTO offer"
                                    " (store_id, source_key, name_raw, price, url, availability, image_url, category)"
                                    " VALUES (%s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s)"
                                    " ON CONFLICT (store_id, source_key) DO UPDATE SET"
                                    "   name_raw = EXCLUDED.name_raw,"
                                    "   price = EXCLUDED.price,"
                                    "   url = EXCLUDED.url,"
                                    "   availability = EXCLUDED.availability,"
                                    "   image_url = EXCLUDED.image_url,"
                                    "   category = EXCLUDED.category,"
                                    "   last_seen = now()"
                                    " RETURNING (xmax = 0) AS was_inserted",
                                    (store_id, listing.source_key, listing.name_raw, listing.price,
                                     listing.url, listing.availability, listing.image_url, listing.category))
                if cur.fetchone()[0]:
                    inserted += 1
                else:
                    updated += 1
    return inserted, updated


def start_run(conn: psycopg.Connection, store_id: UUID) -> int:
    with conn.transaction():
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute("INSERT INTO harvest_run (store_id) VALUES (%s) RETURNING id", (store_id,))
            run_id = cur.fetchone()[0]
    return run_id


def finish_run(conn: psycopg.Connection, run_id: int, ok: bool,
               seen: int, kept: int, error: str | None = None) -> None:
    with conn.transaction():
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute(
                "UPDATE harvest_run SET finished_at = now(), ok = %s,"
                " listings_seen = %s, listings_kept = %s, error = %s WHERE id = %s",
                (ok, seen, kept, error, run_id))


# --------------------------------------------------------------- clustering
# Canonical products. These are permanent identities; offers are temporary
# observations of them.

def load_variant_keys(conn: psycopg.Connection) -> dict[VariantKey, UUID]:
    """Every canonical variant that exists, as keys the matcher can compare.

    Clustering needs the whole set in memory because resolving a partial key
    means asking "how many existing variants is this compatible with?" -- and
    the answer must be exact. One is an attachment; two is a refusal.
    """
    with conn.cursor() as cur:
        # `category` is part of the key and MUST be read back. Omitting it made
        # every stored variant claim to be a smartphone, which is silent and
        # expensive: display_name took the phone branch and dereferenced a NULL
        # colour, is_wellformed applied the phone capacity guard to television
        # diagonals, and the `known` map in cluster_offers could never match a
        # freshly-built non-phone key -- so every TV, fridge and laptop was a
        # candidate for being created a second time on every cycle.
        # The write side of this was fixed earlier (upsert_variant omitted the
        # column); the read side was missed.
        cur.execute(
            "SELECT id, brand, model_tokens, ram_gb, storage_gb, color, sim_kind,"
            " coalesce(category, 'smartphones')"
            " FROM variant")
        return {
            VariantKey(brand=brand, model_tokens=frozenset(tokens), ram_gb=ram,
                       storage_gb=storage, color=color, sim_kind=sim,
                       category=category): vid
            for vid, brand, tokens, ram, storage, color, sim, category
            in cur.fetchall()
        }


def upsert_variant(conn: psycopg.Connection, key: VariantKey) -> UUID:
    """Find or create the canonical variant for this identity.

    The slug is a deterministic function of the key, so ON CONFLICT on it makes
    creation idempotent and race-free -- and makes duplicate canonical products
    structurally impossible, which is the defect this platform exists to fix.
    """
    with conn.transaction():
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute(
                            "INSERT INTO variant (brand, model_tokens, ram_gb, storage_gb,"
                            " color, sim_kind, category, display_name, slug)"
                            " VALUES (%s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s)"
                            " ON CONFLICT (slug) DO NOTHING RETURNING id",
                            (key.brand, sorted(key.model_tokens), key.ram_gb, key.storage_gb,
                             key.color, key.sim_kind, key.category, display_name(key), slug(key)))
            row = cur.fetchone()
            if row is not None:
                return row[0]
            # Already existed -- another offer in this same run created it.
            cur.execute("SELECT id FROM variant WHERE slug = %s", (slug(key),))
            return cur.fetchone()[0]


def attach_offer_to_variant(conn: psycopg.Connection, offer_id: UUID,
                            variant_id: UUID) -> None:
    """Attach, and clear any previous refusal.

    An offer parked as ambiguous in one cycle is often resolvable in a later
    one, once some other retailer's listing has created the variant it needed.
    Leaving the unresolved row behind would make that count a permanently
    rising number nobody can act on.
    """
    with conn.transaction():
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute("UPDATE offer SET variant_id = %s WHERE id = %s",
                        (variant_id, offer_id))
            cur.execute("DELETE FROM unresolved_offer WHERE offer_id = %s", (offer_id,))


def record_unresolved(conn: psycopg.Connection, offer_id: UUID, reason: str,
                      candidate_ids: list[UUID] | None = None) -> None:
    """Refuse to guess, and say why.

    unresolved_offer is a quality metric we watch, not a dumping ground: a
    rising rate means the matcher needs work, so the reason must be specific.
    """
    with conn.transaction():
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute("UPDATE offer SET variant_id = NULL WHERE id = %s", (offer_id,))
            cur.execute(
                "INSERT INTO unresolved_offer (offer_id, reason, candidate_ids)"
                " VALUES (%s, %s, %s)"
                " ON CONFLICT (offer_id) DO UPDATE SET"
                "   reason = EXCLUDED.reason,"
                "   candidate_ids = EXCLUDED.candidate_ids,"
                "   recorded_at = now()",
                (offer_id, reason, candidate_ids or []))


def delete_empty_malformed_variants(conn: psycopg.Connection, is_wellformed) -> int:
    """Remove variants that hold no offers and could never hold one.

    Deliberately narrow. A variant whose offers have merely gone out of stock
    is KEPT -- schema.sql makes min_price nullable precisely so we neither
    publish an unbuyable price nor lose the product's history. This deletes
    only variants the clustering guard would refuse outright, which can never
    be attached to again, and which would otherwise serve a product page with
    no price for a phone that does not exist.
    """
    removed = 0
    with conn.transaction():
        for key, variant_id in load_variant_keys(conn).items():
            if is_wellformed(key):
                continue
            with conn.cursor() as cur:
                cur.execute(
                    "DELETE FROM variant WHERE id = %s"
                    " AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM offer o WHERE o.variant_id = %s)",
                    (variant_id, variant_id))
                removed += cur.rowcount
    return removed


def delete_orphan_variants(conn: psycopg.Connection) -> int:
    """Remove variants that no offer references at all.

    NOT the same as a variant whose offers are out of stock. An offer row is
    never deleted -- the tables are append-and-upsert -- so a variant with zero
    offers can only be the residue of RE-KEYING: a parser or vocabulary change
    moved every offer to a differently-named variant and left the old row
    behind. schema.sql's decision to keep a real variant with a NULL price
    covers out-of-stock, which still has offers pointing at it; this covers a
    row that can never be reached again.

    Measured after the category-identity change: 928 of 1,263 laptop variants
    held no offers. They do not render -- every listing query inner-joins
    variant_price, which aggregate deletes alongside them -- but they make the
    variant count meaningless as a health signal, and the quality report's
    "no offers at all" line is meant to be a small number worth reading.

    Safe to run every cycle: upsert_variant recreates any of these on demand
    from its deterministic slug, so deleting one is at worst undone next run.
    """
    with conn.transaction():
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute(
                "DELETE FROM variant v"
                " WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM offer o WHERE o.variant_id = v.id)")
            return cur.rowcount


def refresh_display_names(conn: psycopg.Connection) -> int:
    """Regenerate every variant's display_name from its key. Returns rows changed.

    display_name is a pure function of the key, but it is STORED, and
    `upsert_variant` uses ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING -- so a variant's name is
    written once, at creation, and never revisited. A correction to the
    generator would then apply only to products first seen afterwards, leaving
    the existing catalogue on the old wording indefinitely. That is the same
    shape as the schema.sql header rule: a change that silently applies to
    fresh data and not to production.

    Adding the eSIM marker was exactly such a correction, and it had 52 live
    variants to repair.
    """
    changed = 0
    with conn.transaction():
        for key, variant_id in load_variant_keys(conn).items():
            with conn.cursor() as cur:
                cur.execute(
                    "UPDATE variant SET display_name = %s"
                    " WHERE id = %s AND display_name IS DISTINCT FROM %s",
                    (display_name(key), variant_id, display_name(key)))
                changed += cur.rowcount
    return changed


def load_attached_offers(conn: psycopg.Connection) -> list[dict]:
    """Offers currently attached to a variant, with their latest raw payload.

    The mirror of `load_unattached_offers`, and the input to the drift check:
    an attachment written in an earlier cycle is only trustworthy while the
    name it was derived from is unchanged. See `cluster.detach_drifted_offers`.
    """
    with conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute("""
            SELECT o.id, o.name_raw, o.variant_id, o.category,
                   (SELECT r.payload FROM raw_offer r
                     WHERE r.store_id = o.store_id AND r.source_key = o.source_key
                     ORDER BY r.observed_at DESC LIMIT 1)
              FROM offer o
             WHERE o.variant_id IS NOT NULL
        """)
        return [{"id": oid, "name_raw": name, "variant_id": vid, "category": cat, "raw": payload}
                for oid, name, vid, cat, payload in cur.fetchall()]


def detach_offer(conn: psycopg.Connection, offer_id: UUID) -> None:
    """Return an offer to the unattached pool so clustering reconsiders it."""
    with conn.transaction():
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute("UPDATE offer SET variant_id = NULL WHERE id = %s", (offer_id,))


def load_unattached_offers(conn: psycopg.Connection) -> list[dict]:
    """Offers not currently attached to a variant, with their latest raw payload.

    Deliberately includes offers already sitting in unresolved_offer: they must
    be reconsidered every run, not parked forever.
    """
    with conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute("""
            SELECT o.id, o.name_raw, o.category,
                   (SELECT r.payload FROM raw_offer r
                     WHERE r.store_id = o.store_id AND r.source_key = o.source_key
                     ORDER BY r.observed_at DESC LIMIT 1)
              FROM offer o
             WHERE o.variant_id IS NULL
        """)
        return [{"id": oid, "name_raw": name, "category": cat, "raw": payload}
                for oid, name, cat, payload in cur.fetchall()]



def try_advisory_lock(conn: psycopg.Connection, key: int) -> bool:
    """Take a session-scoped advisory lock, or return False immediately.

    Session-scoped rather than transaction-scoped on purpose: the lock must
    outlive every transaction a cycle runs, and must be released even if the
    process is killed. Postgres drops it when the connection closes, however
    that happens -- a lock TABLE would need explicit crash cleanup, and that
    cleanup is where this kind of guard usually fails.
    """
    with conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute("SELECT pg_try_advisory_lock(%s)", (key,))
        return bool(cur.fetchone()[0])

FILE: narxnoma-crawler/narxnoma/db/schema.sql

-- Idempotent. Executed on every application start.
--
-- HOW TO CHANGE THIS FILE. Never edit an existing CREATE TABLE to add or alter a
-- column: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS is a no-op on a database that already has the
-- table, so the change would apply on a fresh database and silently not apply in
-- production. Instead append an explicit migration at the bottom of the file --
-- ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS ... -- and bump the schema_version row.

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS schema_version (
    version     integer PRIMARY KEY,
    applied_at  timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
INSERT INTO schema_version (version) VALUES (1) ON CONFLICT (version) DO NOTHING;

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS store (
    id           uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    slug         text UNIQUE NOT NULL,
    name         text NOT NULL,
    website_url  text NOT NULL,
    is_active    boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT true,
    created_at   timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

-- Append-only observation log. Price history falls out of this for free.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS raw_offer (
    id           bigserial PRIMARY KEY,
    store_id     uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES store(id),
    source_key   text NOT NULL,
    name_raw     text NOT NULL,
    price        bigint NOT NULL CHECK (price BETWEEN 100000 AND 100000000),
    url          text NOT NULL,
    availability text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'UNKNOWN'
        CHECK (availability IN ('IN_STOCK', 'OUT_OF_STOCK', 'UNKNOWN')),
    image_url    text,
        payload      jsonb,
        observed_at  timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
    );
    -- Plan 5: which category sweep produced this observation (defaults smartphones).
    ALTER TABLE raw_offer ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS category text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'smartphones';
    CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS raw_offer_store_key_time
        ON raw_offer (store_id, source_key, observed_at DESC);

-- Current state, one row per retailer listing. variant_id is filled in Plan 3.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS offer (
    id           uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    store_id     uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES store(id),
    source_key   text NOT NULL,
    variant_id   uuid,
    name_raw     text NOT NULL,
    price        bigint NOT NULL CHECK (price BETWEEN 100000 AND 100000000),
    url          text NOT NULL,
    availability text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'UNKNOWN'
        CHECK (availability IN ('IN_STOCK', 'OUT_OF_STOCK', 'UNKNOWN')),
    image_url    text,
        first_seen   timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
        last_seen    timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
        UNIQUE (store_id, source_key)
    );
    -- Plan 5: which category sweep produced this offer (defaults smartphones).
    ALTER TABLE offer ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS category text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'smartphones';
    CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS offer_last_seen ON offer (last_seen DESC);
    CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS offer_variant ON offer (variant_id) WHERE variant_id IS NOT NULL;

-- One row per source per cycle. Makes a silently-dead source visible.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS harvest_run (
    id            bigserial PRIMARY KEY,
    store_id      uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES store(id),
    started_at    timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    finished_at   timestamptz,
    ok            boolean,
    listings_seen integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    listings_kept integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    error         text
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS harvest_run_store_started
    ON harvest_run (store_id, started_at DESC);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS variant (
    id            uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    brand         text NOT NULL,
    model_tokens  text[] NOT NULL,

        storage_gb    integer NOT NULL,        -- NOT NULL for phones (see Plan 5 note)

    );
    CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS variant_identity
        ON variant (brand, ram_gb, storage_gb, sim_kind);
    CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS variant_siblings
        ON variant (brand, storage_gb, ram_gb, sim_kind);   -- colour-sibling lookup

    -- Plan 5 (categories, 2026-08-10): non-phone categories (televisions,
    -- laptops, ACs, fridges, washers, ovens) carry no colour/SIM identity, so
    -- both hard identity fields become nullable. Idempotent by construction:
    -- DROP NOT NULL on an already-nullable column is a no-op, and the sim_kind
    -- CHECK passes for NULL (UNKNOWN). Existing phone rows are untouched.
    ALTER TABLE variant ALTER COLUMN color DROP NOT NULL;
    ALTER TABLE variant ALTER COLUMN sim_kind DROP NOT NULL;
    -- storage_gb is also relaxed: a TV or fridge has no memory figure, and
    -- requiring one would make most appliances unkeyable.
    ALTER TABLE variant ALTER COLUMN storage_gb DROP NOT NULL;

-- min_price is NULLABLE on purpose. Only IN_STOCK offers may set a headline
-- price, and a variant can legitimately have offers where every one of them is
-- out of stock. NOT NULL would force us either to publish an out-of-stock price
-- as if it were buyable, or to delete the row and lose the variant's history.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS variant_price (
    variant_id            uuid PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES variant(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    min_price             bigint,
    min_store_id          uuid REFERENCES store(id),
    min_offer_id          uuid REFERENCES offer(id),
    median_price          bigint,
    max_price             bigint,
    offer_count           integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    in_stock_offer_count  integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    store_count           integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    computed_at           timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    CHECK ((min_price IS NULL) = (in_stock_offer_count = 0))
);

    reason         text NOT NULL CHECK (reason <> ''),
    candidate_ids  uuid[] NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
    recorded_at    timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS unresolved_reason ON unresolved_offer (reason);

"""Brand vocabulary and per-brand policy.

Single home for anything brand-specific, because three modules need it:
memory.py (who publishes RAM), features.py (alias resolution) and keys.py
(key completeness + display label).
"""

# TWO ROLES, WITH OPPOSITE FAILURE MODES -- read this before removing an entry.
#
# 1. RECOGNITION vocabulary for extract_features. A brand missing here degrades
#    ONE listing's identity.
# 2. CRAWL FRONTIER, via narxnoma.sources.brand_queries. idea, alifshop and
#    uzum have no browsable catalogue endpoint, so this list is their ENTIRE
#    reach. A brand missing here is not a degraded name -- it is ZERO OFFERS,
#    permanently, from three of seven sources, and nothing in the system
#    reports the absence of something never looked for.
#
# So this list is cheap to extend and expensive to trim. Adding a brand nobody
# sells costs one wasted query per cycle; omitting one costs its whole catalogue.

# Order matters: matched as substrings, so sub-brands come before parents.
BRANDS: list[str] = [

def canonical_brand(token: str) -> str:
    """Collapse a sub-brand to its parent ('redmi' -> 'xiaomi')."""
    return BRAND_ALIASES.get(token, token)


def canonical_non_phone_brand(token: str) -> str:
    """Collapse an appliance sub-brand or code prefix ('prm' -> 'premier').

    Separate from canonical_brand rather than a category flag on it, so the
    phone path -- a plain substring scan pinned by 14,860 golden rows -- keeps
    resolving through BRAND_ALIASES and nothing else.
    """
    return NON_PHONE_ALIASES.get(token, token)


def brand_label(brand: str, category: str = "smartphones") -> str:
    """Display label for a brand, in the context of a category.

    Category matters for exactly one entry, and getting it wrong is visible to
    every user: BRAND_LABELS maps "apple" to "Apple iPhone", because for phones
    the word "iPhone" is stripped as a NON_MODEL_TOKEN and has to be put back.
    A MacBook is also brand "apple", so the phone label would render
    "Ноутбук Apple iPhone MacBook Air" on a laptop page.
    """
    if category != "smartphones":
        if brand in APPLIANCE_BRAND_LABELS:
            return APPLIANCE_BRAND_LABELS[brand]
        if brand == "apple":
            return "Apple"
        return BRAND_LABELS.get(brand, brand.capitalize())
    return BRAND_LABELS.get(brand, brand.capitalize())

FILE: narxnoma-crawler/narxnoma/matching/categories.py

"""Non-phone identity vocabulary.

A phone's identity is a signature: brand + model + RAM + storage + colour + SIM.
A television's is not. A TV, fridge, oven or air conditioner is identified by
its **catalogue code** -- "UE55DU7100UXUZ", "RT47CG6442B1WT", "NV68A1145RS" --
optionally preceded by a model NAME ("Predator Helios Neo", "Serie 6", "Alba").
Everything else in the title is marketing.

That inverts two rules the phone matcher depends on, which is why this module
exists instead of a flag inside features.py:

1. **The SKU-code rule must not fire.** features.py discards mixed letter+digit
   tokens of five or more characters, because for a phone "sm-a175f" is a
   catalogue code and "a17" is the identity. For a TV there IS no friendlier
   name: the code *is* the product. Measured on the live catalogue, that single
   rule made 100% of ovens, and the great majority of TVs and fridges,
   permanently unkeyable.

2. **Alphabetic tokens must be kept.** features.py keeps a word only if it is a
   known MODEL_MODIFIER ("pro", "max", "note"), because for phones any other
   word is noise. Appliance model names are made of exactly such words --
   "Vostro", "ThinkPad", "Aspire", "Predator" -- and dropping them merges every
   Acer laptop of the same memory tier into one product.

Both relaxations WIDEN what counts as identity, so the risk they introduce is
splitting one product into several, never merging two into one. That is the
safe direction for this project: a duplicate page is a coverage bug, a merged
page is the exact defect the platform exists to prevent.

The instrument that keeps splitting under control is the stopword vocabulary
below. "Телевизор Artel UA43H3502 Android TV" and "Телевизор Artel UA43H3502"
are one product, so "android", "tv" and "smart" must never reach the key.
"""
import re

# Product-type nouns, Russian and Uzbek (Latin), across all six non-phone
# categories. These lead almost every title in the live catalogue and identify
# the CATEGORY, which is already an axis of the key -- so repeating them inside
# model_tokens adds nothing and splits "Смарт-телевизор X" from "Телевизор X".
CATEGORY_NOUNS: frozenset[str] = frozenset({
    # televisions
    "телевизор", "телевизоры", "телевизора", "televizor", "televizori",
    "telewizor", "тв", "tv",
    # laptops
    "ноутбук", "ноутбуки", "ноутбука", "noutbuk", "noutbuki", "laptop",
    "netbuk", "нетбук",
    # air conditioners
    "кондиционер", "кондиционеры", "кондиционера", "konditsioner",
    "konditsioneri", "kondisioner", "сплит", "система", "системы",
    # fridges
    "холодильник", "холодильники", "холодильника", "автохолодильник",
    "автохолодильники", "muzlatgich", "muzlatgichi", "sovutgich",
    "sovutgichi", "морозильник", "морозильники",
    # washers
    "стиральная", "стиральные", "стиральной", "машина", "машины", "машинка",
    "mashina", "mashinasi", "kir", "yuvish", "стирально", "сушильная",
    # ovens / hobs
    "духовой", "духовка", "духовки", "шкаф", "духовых", "духовые",
    "плита", "плиты", "плитка", "duxovka", "duxovkasi", "pech",
    "варочная", "панель", "вытяжка", "печь",
})

# Words that describe HOW the appliance works or is installed. Real words, real
# information -- and not identity: "Двухкамерный холодильник Artel HD455" and
# "Холодильник Artel HD455" are one fridge. Measured as head tokens on the live
# catalogue ("полуавтомат" 28, "автомат" 10, "бытовой" 5, "двухкамерный" 3).
DESCRIPTORS: frozenset[str] = frozenset({
    "полуавтомат", "полуавтоматическая", "автомат", "автоматическая",
    "двухкамерный", "двухкамерная", "однокамерный", "трехкамерный",
    "встраиваемый", "встраиваемая", "встраиваемые", "встроенный",
    "напольный", "настольная", "настенный", "колонный", "кассетный",
    "витринный", "бытовой", "бытовая", "промышленный",
    "газовая", "газовые", "газовый", "электрическая", "электрический",
    "комбинированная", "комбинированный", "индукционная", "индукционный",
    "безрамочный", "игровой", "игровая", "портативный", "переносной",
    "вертикальная", "горизонтальная", "фронтальная",
    "новый", "новая", "оригинал", "оригинальный",
})

# Marketing and platform words. These vary between listings of the SAME
# product, so any one of them reaching the key splits a real product in two.
# "Телевизор Artel UA43H3502 Android TV" vs "Телевизор Artel UA43H3502" is the
# measured case that motivates the list.
MARKETING: frozenset[str] = frozenset({
    "smart", "смарт", "android", "андроид", "google", "assistant", "webos",
    "tizen", "yandex", "алиса", "ai", "wifi", "wi", "fi", "bluetooth",
    "inverter", "invertor", "инвертор", "инверторный", "инверторная",
    # Inverter-type markers on air conditioners, stated by some listings of a
    # unit and not by others: "Artel Dc Full Shahrisabz 12" and "Artel
    # Shahrisabz 12" are one air conditioner, as are "Artel Marvarid Inv 18"
    # and "Artel Marvarid 18". "art" is Artel's own product-line prefix
    # ("Artel ART HDG Iceberg 12"), not a model.
    # Series letters ("12BE", "12HE", "HS") are deliberately NOT here: those
    # ride inside the figure token and may distinguish real units, and merging
    # two real products is the failure this module must not have.
    "inv", "dc", "full", "art",
    "led", "qled", "oled", "nanocell", "frameless",
    "uhd", "fhd", "hd", "ultrahd", "fullhd", "4k", "8k", "2k",
    "dyuym", "дюйм", "дюйма", "дюймов",
    "eco", "premium", "series", "serie", "серия", "gen",
    # NOTE: "pro", "air", "max", "plus", "ultra", "lite", "mini" and "neo" are
    # deliberately ABSENT. They read as marketing on a phone, but outside
    # phones they are the model name itself -- a MacBook Air is not a MacBook
    # Pro, and "Predator Helios Neo" is not "Predator Helios". Stripping them
    # would merge genuinely different products, which is the one failure this
    # module must not have. features.py keeps them for phones for the same
    # reason (MODEL_MODIFIERS).
    "new", "новинка", "хит", "акция", "скидка", "подарок", "гарантия",
    "доставка", "бесплатно", "рассрочка", "кредит",
    "official", "официальный", "оригинальный",
    "energy", "class", "класс",
})

# Measurement units and their figures' companions. A capacity in litres or
# kilograms is a SPEC, and the same product is listed with and without it.
UNITS: frozenset[str] = frozenset({
    "кг", "kg", "л", "лт", "литр", "литров", "l", "см", "cm", "мм", "mm",
    "вт", "w", "квт", "kw", "в", "v", "гц", "hz", "об", "мин", "rpm",
    "btu", "btuh", "м", "m", "м2", "m2", "м3",
    "гб", "gb", "тб", "tb", "мб", "mb", "ram", "ssd", "hdd", "emmc",
    "ddr", "ddr3", "ddr4", "ddr5", "lpddr4", "lpddr5",
    "ips", "va", "tn",
})

# Processors and graphics. A laptop's CPU is a specification, not its name --
# and it only reaches the tokens when the retailer omits the "/" delimiter that
# usually fences the spec off. Measured: "Ноутбук Acer Aspire Snapdragon X1
# 26100" became a different product from "Ноутбук Acer Aspire".
#
# Bare part numbers ("1334U", "26100", "N4405") are deliberately NOT listed:
# they are indistinguishable from real model codes by shape, and the vendor
# words below are enough to catch the titles that carry them.
# "apple" is a BRAND, and "m1".."m4" are the identity of a MacBook -- an Air M4
# is not an Air M2. Both are deliberately absent for the same reason "pro" and
# "air" are absent from MARKETING.
PROCESSORS: frozenset[str] = frozenset({
    "intel", "amd", "qualcomm", "mediatek", "nvidia",
    "snapdragon", "ryzen", "core", "celeron", "pentium", "athlon", "atom",
    "i3", "i5", "i7", "i9", "u5", "u7", "u9",
    "rtx", "gtx", "geforce", "radeon", "iris", "arc", "vega", "graphics",
    "processor", "процессор", "видеокарта", "graphic",
})

#: Everything a non-phone model token must not be.
NON_MODEL: frozenset[str] = (
    CATEGORY_NOUNS | DESCRIPTORS | MARKETING | UNITS | PROCESSORS
)

#: The same, for a category that has no processor. See CATEGORIES_WITH_CPU.
NON_MODEL_WITHOUT_CPU: frozenset[str] = (
    CATEGORY_NOUNS | DESCRIPTORS | MARKETING | UNITS
)

# Categories where a PROCESSORS word is a specification rather than a name.
# Only a computer has a CPU; on an air conditioner the same words are the
# model. Measured 2026-08-10 across all 5,132 non-laptop non-phone offers:
# exactly 8 (0.16%) contain a PROCESSORS word, and every one is an air
# conditioner whose LINE NAME collides with a chip --
#     "Кондиционер Rulls ARC 12 Inverter"     (Intel Arc)     6 offers, 2 stores
#     "Кондиционер Sitronic Vega Inverter 18" (Radeon Vega)   2 offers
# -- and all 8 were unresolved, so scoping this re-keys nothing that already
# clustered. cut_at_processor made it worse than a plain stopword would: it
# truncates positionally, so "Rulls ARC 12" lost its capacity as well as its
# name and could not form a key at all.
CATEGORIES_WITH_CPU: frozenset[str] = frozenset({"laptops"})

# Categories where a RAM/storage figure is a real specification. A laptop has
# 16 GB and a 512 GB SSD; a television, fridge, oven, washer or air conditioner
# has neither.
#
# This matters because the phone extractor reads a LONE plausible capacity as
# storage, and the plausible-storage set (32, 64, 128, 256, 512) overlaps
# exactly with television diagonals and fridge capacities. Measured: "Телевизор
# Premier 32PRM840FSV" was keyed with storage_gb = 32 and rendered as
# "Телевизор Premier 32PRM840FSV 32 ГБ" -- a spec the product does not have,
# printed on the page, and worse, a key that SPLITS from the same television
# listed without its diagonal.
CATEGORIES_WITH_MEMORY: frozenset[str] = frozenset({"laptops"})

# A laptop listing's identity ends where its specification begins. Retailers
# delimit that boundary explicitly and consistently:
#     "Ноутбук Acer Predator Helios Neo 16S AI / U9-275HX / DDR5 32GB / ..."
# Everything after the first "/" is CPU, GPU, memory and panel -- specification,
# not name. Keeping it would key the laptop on its graphics card.
#
# This is the same instrument uzum.md section 5a already applies to uzum card
# titles (truncate at the first comma); the delimiter set is wider here because
# these are seven retailers' free-text titles rather than one API's field.
#
# Applied to model TOKENS only. Memory and colour are still read from the WHOLE
# title, so "Acer Aspire 8/512" keeps storage 512 and stays distinct from the
# 8/256 -- truncating those away would merge two real products.
_SPEC_DELIMITERS = re.compile(r"[/|(\[]")


def head_for_model(name: str) -> str:
    """The part of a title that names the product, before its specification."""
    if not name:
        return ""
    return _SPEC_DELIMITERS.split(name, 1)[0]


def cut_at_processor(tokens: list[str], category: str = "laptops") -> list[str]:
    """Drop everything from the first processor word onward.

    The "/" fence catches most laptop specifications, but retailers that omit
    it run the spec straight on from the name:

        "Ноутбук Acer Aspire Snapdragon X1 26100"
        "Ноутбук ASUS Vivobook 17 X1704VA Core 5-120U 16GB 512GB"

    A vendor word is a reliable marker that the name has ended, whereas the
    part numbers after it ("x1", "26100", "5") are indistinguishable from real
    model codes by shape -- which is why PROCESSORS lists only the words and
    this function handles the rest positionally.

    Positional truncation is only right where the word really is a spec
    boundary. On a category with no processor it is a name, and cutting there
    discards the rest of the name too -- see CATEGORIES_WITH_CPU.
    """
    if category not in CATEGORIES_WITH_CPU:
        return tokens
    for i, t in enumerate(tokens):
        if t in PROCESSORS:
            return tokens[:i]
    return tokens


# Product-line names. Identity treats every model token alike, but a NAME has
# to read the way the product is sold: "Vivobook Go 15", not "15 Go Vivobook".
# model_tokens is a frozenset, so display order has to be reconstructed, and
# alphabetical order puts the screen size first on almost every laptop.
FAMILY_WORDS: frozenset[str] = frozenset({
    # laptops
    "vivobook", "zenbook", "expertbook", "chromebook", "macbook", "thinkpad",
    "thinkbook", "ideapad", "yoga", "legion", "loq", "aspire", "swift",
    "predator", "nitro", "travelmate", "extensa", "pavilion", "envy",
    "elitebook", "probook", "omen", "victus", "vostro", "inspiron",
    "latitude", "precision", "xps", "modern", "prestige", "katana",
    "cyborg", "bravo", "sword", "raider", "stealth", "tuf", "rog", "gaming",
    # televisions / appliances product lines
    "bravia", "crystal", "frame", "serif", "neoqled", "smarttv",
    "alba", "naomi", "marvarid", "milagro", "apetito", "shaxrisabz",
    "grand", "forever", "city", "tashkent",
})


def ordered_non_phone_tokens(tokens: frozenset[str] | set[str]) -> list[str]:
    """Model tokens in the order a person writes them.

    Family name first ("Vivobook"), then the remaining words alphabetically,
    then catalogue codes, then bare figures such as a diagonal or a BTU class.
    Ordering is DISPLAY ONLY -- identity is the unordered set, so two listings
    that name the same tokens in different orders remain one product.
    """
    families, words, codes, figures = [], [], [], []
    for t in sorted(tokens):
        if t in FAMILY_WORDS:
            families.append(t)
        elif t.isdigit():
            figures.append(t)
        elif any(c.isdigit() for c in t):
            codes.append(t)
        else:
            words.append(t)
    figures.sort(key=lambda x: (len(x), x))
    return families + words + codes + figures


# Things sold ALONGSIDE the product, in the product's own category feed. A
# laptop bag is returned by a laptop sweep, carries a brand and a code, and so
# forms a perfectly valid key -- "Rivacase 7531" became a laptop. Unlike the
# phone case, nothing downstream rejects it: the price fence passes it and the
# key system accepts it, so it reaches the catalogue as a product.
_ACCESSORY = re.compile(
    r"\b("
    r"sumka\w*|сумк\w*|chexol\w*|чехол\w*|"
    r"kronshteyn\w*|кронштейн\w*|подставк\w*|крепление|крепление\w*|"
    r"pult\w*|пульт\w*|kabel\w*|кабел\w*|переходник\w*|удлинител\w*|"
    r"filtr\w*|фильтр\w*|мешок|мешк\w*|шланг\w*|картридж\w*|"
    r"lampa\w*|лампочк\w*|щетк\w*|щётк\w*|насадк\w*|"
    r"аксессуар\w*|aksessuar\w*|салфетк\w*|чистящ\w*|"
    r"стабилизатор\w*|подключение|установка|монтаж"
    r")\b",
    re.I,
)

# The same shape the phone denylist uses (sources/not_a_phone.py): a title that
# LEADS with the product noun is the product, and an accessory word inside it
# describes what is in the box. "Телевизор ... с пультом" is a television.
_LEADS_WITH_CATEGORY_NOUN = re.compile(
    r"^\s*(" + "|".join(sorted(CATEGORY_NOUNS, key=len, reverse=True)) + r")\b",
    re.I,
)


def is_accessory(name: str | None, category: str = "smartphones") -> bool:
    """True when a title in a category feed is an accessory, not the product.

    Conservative in the direction this project always chooses: a title that
    names its own category first is never an accessory, so the failure mode is
    admitting a bag rather than losing a laptop.
    """
    if category == "smartphones" or not name:
        return False
    if _LEADS_WITH_CATEGORY_NOUN.match(name.strip()):
        return False
    return bool(_ACCESSORY.search(name))


def is_model_token(token: str, category: str = "laptops") -> bool:
    """True when a token may stand as part of a non-phone product's identity.

    Deliberately permissive about SHAPE and strict about VOCABULARY: any word
    or code survives unless it is a known category noun, descriptor, marketing
    word or unit. Shape cannot separate "wgk264zxme" (identity) from "ddr5"
    (specification) -- both are letters plus digits -- so the vocabulary does
    the work, and every entry in it was measured against live titles.

    `category` decides one thing: whether the PROCESSORS words are part of
    that vocabulary. They are a specification on a computer and a model name
    on everything else -- see CATEGORIES_WITH_CPU. The default keeps the
    stricter laptop vocabulary, so a caller that does not pass a category
    gets exactly the behaviour this function always had.
    """
    stoplist = NON_MODEL if category in CATEGORIES_WITH_CPU else NON_MODEL_WITHOUT_CPU
    if not token or token in stoplist:
        return False
    # A bare unit-suffixed figure is a spec: "43дюйма", "512gb", "1200об".
    if re.fullmatch(r"\d+(?:gb|гб|tb|тб|кг|kg|л|lt|см|cm|вт|w|hz|гц|об|rpm|дюйм\w*)", token):
        return False
    # A lone letter is never identity; it is a stray initial from a split code.
    return len(token) > 1
