"""uzum.uz client: anonymous-token GraphQL, per-brand sweep.

uzum is the largest marketplace in Uzbekistan and the only source here with
auth, per-variant (SKU) pricing, and a failure mode that looks like success.
Read docs/parsers/uzum.md in full before touching this file -- every trap
below has a section there with the live evidence behind it.

Auth (docs/parsers/uzum.md section 1): `graphql.uzum.uz` returns a bare 401
without a Bearer token. The token is minted anonymously via
`POST id.uzum.uz/api/auth/token` with an empty JSON body -- no account, no
captcha. The response is **204 No Content**: the token is not in the body,
it arrives as a `Set-Cookie: access_token=<JWT>` header, which is why
`_mint_token` talks to `requests` directly instead of `get_json`/`post_json`
(those call `response.json()` unconditionally and would raise
`NonJsonResponse` on the empty 204 body). Exactly two headers are required
to mint -- `Accept-Language` (any value) and `Referer` (must be on the
uzum.uz origin); `Origin` is NOT required, the opposite of what you would
guess. TTL is 6 hours (`exp` in the JWT payload); `_get_token` caches the
token at module (process) level and refreshes ~5 minutes before `exp`.

The GraphQL endpoint itself (docs/parsers/uzum.md section 2) needs four
headers -- `Authorization`, `Content-Type`, `apollographql-client-name:
web-customers`, `x-iid: <any UUID>` -- or it returns a bare 401. Drop only
`apollographql-client-name` or `x-iid` and it instead returns **200 OK**
with `data: null` and an `errors` array: checking `response.status_code`
alone reports success on a request that returned nothing.
`UzumSource._fetch_payload` inspects `payload.get("errors")` explicitly and
raises `UzumGraphQLError` when present, so a broken sweep call is loud
rather than silently looking like "no more items for this brand." `parse()`
itself never raises for this -- it logs and returns `[]`, so a caller handed
one already-fetched payload gets an empty result rather than a crash.
`_fetch_payload` also survives a **server-side token revocation**: the cache
refreshes only when the locally decoded `exp` passes, so a token revoked
early arrives as a bare 401 the cache cannot predict. That 401 re-mints once
and retries; a second 401 is a real auth failure and raises.

**Card price is not product price** (section 5): a card bundles several
models and every storage tier under one `minSellPrice`. Every listing here
is built from a `skuList[]` entry using `sellPrice` -- never `minSellPrice`,
never `fullPrice` (a struck-through pre-discount figure, often fantasy).

**Off-category noise** (section 3): relevance search mixes in cases,
chargers and vacuum cleaners. `parse()` filters client-side on
`catalogCard.category.id` in `PHONE_CATEGORY_IDS` (15271 Android, 15272
iPhone) -- folded into `parse()` itself, not left to a separate crawl-policy
step, because `search()` hits the exact same noisy relevance endpoint as
`sweep()` and both need it.

**Pagination caps at offset ~= 1000** (section 3): beyond that `items` comes
back empty regardless of `limit`, so `sweep()` goes brand by brand (see
`narxnoma.sources.brand_queries.BRAND_QUERIES`) rather than attempting one
unbounded query -- the Android smartphone category alone runs to thousands
of multi-seller listings.

**name_raw** (sections 5a/5b/7): uzum hands back no single product-name
field. `name_raw` is the *only* handle the clustering stage gets on a
product's identity -- a name that loses the brand or the storage figure
cannot be keyed at all, and the offer drops out of the catalogue silently.
`_build_name_raw` therefore has three jobs, and each of them has already
been got wrong once:

- take the card title only up to its first comma (marketing blurb after
  that), and let the SKU's own `Модель` characteristic override it;
- when the head is reduced to a prefix in front of a `Модель` value, keep
  the whole brand-bearing head rather than its first word, after dropping
  a leading `Smartfon`/`Смартфон`/`Telefon`/`Телефон` product-type noun.
  Keeping only the first word turned
  `("Smartfon Samsung Galaxy A16, ...", "A16 8/256")` into
  `"Smartfon A16 Qora"` -- brand, RAM and storage all unrecoverable -- and
  10 of this recording's 20 cards lead with that noun, so it was the common
  case rather than an edge;
- when the SKU states its own memory, strip memory figures out of the
  *card-derived* text before combining, so the card's overall storage
  *range* never masquerades as this SKU's specific tier (the exact bug that
  once reported 2,672,010 for a phone whose true price was 3,068,010; see
  `test_known_product_name_raw_strips_the_cards_other_memory_tiers`).
  Memory stripping is **never** applied to the `Модель` value itself --
  that value is the trustworthy one, and stripping it deleted the very
  figure section 5b exists to preserve.

When neither the SKU's characteristics nor the truncated head yields any
memory at all, the *full* card title is searched for a memory pattern and
the match appended: cards that state memory after the first comma
("Smartfon Samsung Galaxy A16, 4/128 GB, 2 SIM, ...") otherwise produced a
storage-less, unkeyable name from information we were already holding in
`raw["card_title"]`.

Characteristic keys are a typo minefield (`Память`, `памяять`, `Памяьт:`,
`Xotirasi`, `RAM/ROM`, and -- observed live in this recording -- `xotra`, a
typo the doc's own `startswith("xotira")` sample does not catch;
`_char_kind` here classifies by the shorter `startswith("xot")` prefix
instead, and treats a bare `ram`/`rom` token as memory because `normalize`
folds `RAM/ROM` to `ram rom`), so keys are classified loosely, never matched
exactly. `_parse_sku` also puts the untouched card title and the SKU's full
`characteristicValues` list into `Listing.raw`, so a later clustering stage
can redo this name-building better without re-crawling.

**Two deliberate inversions of docs/parsers/uzum.md** (project decision, not
a doc bug -- see the task-10 brief): that document was written for a
target-driven matcher hunting one specific phone, where an eSIM-only
variant or a zero-stock SKU is noise to screen out. This client is an
*aggregator* cataloguing every real offer, so both instructions invert:

- eSIM-only variants (section 6) are **kept**, not dropped -- they are a
  legitimate, separate product at a genuinely different price. Whatever SIM
  characteristic exists survives into `raw["characteristic_values"]`
  verbatim for a later clustering stage to classify.
- Zero-stock SKUs (`availableAmount <= 0`, section 4) are **kept**, not
  dropped -- recorded with `availability="OUT_OF_STOCK"` rather than
  discarded. Hiding an out-of-stock offer is a presentation decision that
  belongs downstream, not a reason to lose the observation.
"""
import base64
import json
import logging
import re
import time
import uuid
from dataclasses import replace
from typing import Iterator

import requests

from narxnoma.config import load_settings
from narxnoma.matching.normalize import normalize
from narxnoma.sources.base import Listing, coerce_price, paginate, try_build_listing
from narxnoma.sources.brand_queries import queries_for
from narxnoma.sources.http import pause, polite_session, post_json

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

AUTH_URL = "https://id.uzum.uz/api/auth/token"
GRAPHQL_URL = "https://graphql.uzum.uz/"
# Canonical product URL WITHOUT skuId. uzum's own 302 meta-refresh builds
# id.uzum.uz/api/auth/redirect?redirectUrl=<product>?skuId=<id> with the
# nested query raw (never encoded), and the auth endpoint answers that
# malformed parameter with a conflict JSON -- the broken-link bug reported
# against the site. The clean URL produces a clean redirect + access_token
# cookie and lands on the product page (all SKUs listed there). SKU identity
# lives in source_key, not in the human-facing URL.
PRODUCT_URL = "https://uzum.uz/ru/product/{product_id}"

# 15271 = Смартфоны Android, 15272 = Смартфоны Apple iPhone (iOS) -- see
# docs/parsers/uzum.md section 3. Relevance search mixes in cases, chargers
# and (genuinely) vacuum cleaners; this is the only usable signal to drop them.
PHONE_CATEGORY_IDS = frozenset({15271, 15272})

# Plan 5: category -> uzum category.id set, verified live 2026-08-10 by
# querying makeSearch per product type and reading catalogCard.category.id.
#
# Re-verified live 2026-08-10 while fixing the category frontier. Two
# corrections, both found by reading catalogCard.category off a real response:
#   - ovens held only 11 (Духовые шкафы). "газовая плита" is category 13
#     (Газовые плиты) and is a different id, so every gas cooker uzum sells was
#     filtered out of a sweep that had gone and fetched it. The other sources
#     already harvest gas cookers into `ovens`.
#   - fridges gains 83 (Морозильники). The Uzbek "muzlatgich" resolves to
#     FREEZERS on uzum, not refrigerators -- "холодильник"/"sovutgich" are the
#     words that reach id 82 -- and freezers belong with fridges here for the
#     same reason cookers belong with ovens.
CATEGORY_IDS = {
    "smartphones": PHONE_CATEGORY_IDS,
    "televisions": {12601},
    "laptops": {12520},
    "acs": {14373},
    "fridges": {82, 83},
    "washers": {15291, 15296},
    "ovens": {11, 13},
}

PAGE_LIMIT = 72
# Pagination caps at offset ~= 1000 -- beyond that `items` is always empty
# regardless of limit (docs/parsers/uzum.md section 3). sweep() stops each
# brand here even if the response claims a larger `total`.
OFFSET_CAP = 1000

# Refresh the cached token 5 minutes before its 6-hour JWT `exp`, per
# docs/parsers/uzum.md section 1.
_TOKEN_REFRESH_MARGIN_SECONDS = 300

# Assumed TTL when the access_token cookie is not a decodable JWT. uzum can
# change the cookie format at any time; a crash inside _decode_jwt_exp would
# kill the entire sweep over a value that is only a refresh optimisation, so
# an undecodable token is treated as short-lived instead.
_TOKEN_FALLBACK_TTL_SECONDS = 3600

# Cached at module (process) level -- "mint a token once (cached for the
# process, refreshed ~5 minutes before its 6-hour exp)" per the task brief.
# Every UzumSource instance in this process shares one token.
_token_cache: dict = {"token": None, "iid": None, "exp": 0}

SEARCH_QUERY = """
query getMakeSearch($q: MakeSearchQueryInput!) {
  makeSearch(query: $q) {
    total
    items {
      catalogCard {
        __typename
        productId
        title
        category { id title }
        photos { link(trans: PRODUCT_540) { high } }
        ... on SkuGroupCard {
          skuList {
            id
            sellPrice
            fullPrice
            availableAmount
            characteristicValues { title characteristic { title } }
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
"""


class UzumGraphQLError(RuntimeError):
    """Raised by the live fetch path (never by parse()) when a 200 OK
    GraphQL response carries an `errors` key -- docs/parsers/uzum.md
    section 2's headline trap: this looks like success by status code alone.
    """


def _decode_jwt_exp(token: str) -> int:
    """The `exp` claim of the access_token cookie, or a conservative
    fallback expiry if the cookie is not a decodable JWT.

    The expiry is only used to decide *when to refresh*, so it must never be
    able to raise: an opaque or reformatted cookie would otherwise crash
    _get_token and take the whole sweep with it, even though the token
    itself may be perfectly usable.
    """
    try:
        payload_b64 = token.split(".")[1]
        payload_b64 += "=" * (-len(payload_b64) % 4)
        claims = json.loads(base64.urlsafe_b64decode(payload_b64))
        return int(claims["exp"])
    except (AttributeError, IndexError, KeyError, TypeError, ValueError):
        logger.warning(
            "uzum: access_token is not a decodable JWT; assuming a %ds TTL",
            _TOKEN_FALLBACK_TTL_SECONDS,
        )
        return int(time.time()) + _TOKEN_FALLBACK_TTL_SECONDS


def _mint_token() -> tuple[str, str]:
    """POST id.uzum.uz/api/auth/token and pull the bearer token out of the
    Set-Cookie header (the 204 response body is empty -- see module
    docstring). Bypasses get_json/post_json on purpose: both call
    response.json() unconditionally and would raise NonJsonResponse on this
    endpoint's empty body.
    """
    settings = load_settings()
    iid = str(uuid.uuid4())
    session = requests.Session()
    try:
        response = session.post(
            AUTH_URL,
            headers={
                "Accept": "*/*",
                "Accept-Language": "ru-RU",       # required
                "Content-Type": "application/json",
                "Referer": "https://uzum.uz/",    # required, must be uzum.uz origin
                "User-Agent": settings.user_agent,
                "x-iid": iid,
            },
            json={},
            timeout=(settings.connect_timeout, settings.read_timeout),
        )
        response.raise_for_status()
    finally:
        pause()  # a real retailer call either way -- see http.get_json/post_json
    token = next((c.value for c in session.cookies if c.name == "access_token"), None)
    if not token:
        raise RuntimeError("uzum auth: no access_token cookie in the mint response")
    return token, iid


def _get_token() -> tuple[str, str]:
    """The process-cached bearer token and install id, minting or refreshing
    as needed. See module docstring for the caching contract.
    """
    if _token_cache["token"] and time.time() < _token_cache["exp"] - _TOKEN_REFRESH_MARGIN_SECONDS:
        return _token_cache["token"], _token_cache["iid"]
    token, iid = _mint_token()
    exp = _decode_jwt_exp(token)
    _token_cache.update(token=token, iid=iid, exp=exp)
    return token, iid


def _invalidate_token() -> None:
    """Force the next _get_token() to mint a fresh token.

    The cache refreshes on the locally decoded `exp`, which cannot see a
    *server-side* revocation: uzum can invalidate a token before its stated
    expiry, and the only signal is a 401 on the next graphql call. See
    UzumSource._fetch_payload.
    """
    _token_cache.update(token=None, iid=None, exp=0)


# `RAM/ROM` is in docs/parsers/uzum.md section 7's own observed-key list, but
# `normalize` folds the slash to a space and hands back `ram rom`, which no
# prefix test in this function recognised -- so the key classified as "other"
# and its memory value was dropped without a trace. Same class of bug as the
# `xotra` typo below. Matched on tokens, not as a substring: `rang` (colour)
# must not be caught by a bare `"ram" in k`.
_MEMORY_KEY_TOKENS = frozenset({"ram", "rom"})


def _char_kind(key: str) -> str:
    """Classify a characteristic key loosely -- never match exactly.
    docs/parsers/uzum.md section 7 catalogues the typo minefield
    (`Память`, `память`, `ПАМЯТЬ`, `Памят:`, `Память:`, `Памяьт:`,
    `памяять`, `Объем памяти`, `Xotirasi`, `RAM/ROM`); this recording
    additionally turned up `xotra` (missing the final `i`) and `Xotira:`
    (trailing colon, stripped by `normalize` anyway) -- neither matches the
    doc's own `startswith("xotira")` sample, which is why this uses the
    shorter `startswith("xot")` instead. Every key in section 7's list is
    exercised by test_char_kind_classifies_every_observed_key.
    """
    k = normalize(key)
    if (
        k.startswith("памя")
        or k.startswith("xot")
        or "объем памяти" in k
        or _MEMORY_KEY_TOKENS & set(k.split())
    ):
        return "memory"
    if k.startswith("модел") or k.startswith("model"):
        return "model"
    if "sim" in k or "сим" in k:
        return "sim"
    if k.startswith("цвет") or k.startswith("rang"):
        return "color"
    return "other"


def _characteristics(sku: dict) -> dict[str, str]:
    """First model/memory/color value seen for this SKU, classified via
    _char_kind. SIM values are not extracted here -- name_raw never carries
    them (see module docstring); they survive into Listing.raw verbatim as
    part of the full characteristicValues list instead.
    """
    found = {"model": "", "memory": "", "color": ""}
    for cv in sku.get("characteristicValues") or []:
        if not isinstance(cv, dict):
            continue
        key = ((cv.get("characteristic") or {}).get("title")) or ""
        kind = _char_kind(key)
        if kind in found and not found[kind]:
            value = cv.get("title")
            if value:
                found[kind] = str(value)
    return found


# docs/parsers/uzum.md section 5b, verbatim: when a SKU states its own
# memory, strip memory figures out of the card-derived spec before
# combining, or the card's overall storage range masquerades as this SKU's
# specific tier.
# The trailing `+` makes the chain greedy across MORE than two figures. A
# card offering three tiers ("Galaxy S25 Edge 12/256/512") otherwise had
# exactly two of them consumed, leaving "512" standing in the head -- where
# the bare-pair scan then read the card's 512 as the capacity and demoted
# the SKU's own 256 to a model token. That is the leak inverted, not fixed.
#
# `-` is a separator too, because uzum sellers write the RAM-ROM pair with a
# hyphen ("POCO C81 Pro (4-64/4-128)", "4GB-128GB") -- but ONLY when it is
# TIGHT, with no space on either side. A SPACED hyphen is prose, and treating
# it as a separator ate the model number: "REALME NOTE 70 - 2 дня работы"
# matched "70 - 2", so the strip deleted the 70 and left the battery figure
# standing in for the model ("realme note 6300 /128"). The capacity guard
# cannot catch that -- 6300 is not a capacity, so the variant looks perfectly
# well-formed -- and another retailer's Realme Note 70 keys correctly, so the
# two never merge and the offer pool splits. Slash and plus keep their
# optional spaces; only the hyphen is restricted, because only the hyphen
# appears in ordinary prose.
#
# The leading `(?<![a-zа-я])` still protects catalogue codes: the "0" of
# "SM-A075F" is preceded by a letter, so no chain can start inside one.
_MEMORY_PAIR_RE = re.compile(
    r"(?<![a-zа-я])\d{1,4}\s*(?:gb|гб|tb|тб)?"
    r"(?:(?:\s*[/\\+|]\s*|-)\d{1,4}\s*(?:gb|гб|tb|тб)?)+",
    re.I,
)
_MEMORY_SINGLE_RE = re.compile(
    r"(?<![a-zа-я\d])\d{1,4}\s*(?:gb|гб|tb|тб)\b",
    re.I,
)


# Residue left behind by the two substitutions above. Stripping "(8+8)/128
# GB" out of "Smartfon Oppo A5i Pro (8+8)/128 GB" leaves "( )/" hanging off
# the end -- SKU 6931382 in the recorded fixture parsed to
# "Smartfon Oppo A5i Pro ( )/ 8/128 Binafsha".
_EMPTY_BRACKETS_RE = re.compile(r"[(\[{]\s*[)\]}]")
# A separator with no word character immediately to its left is orphaned.
# Deliberately one-sided: a separator that IS preceded by a word character
# may be a real model marker ("Note 14 Pro+"), and must survive.
_ORPHAN_SEPARATOR_RE = re.compile(r"(?<!\w)[/\\|+]+")

# Anything smaller is a RAM figure or a screen size, not a storage tier --
# used to reject "4/6" out of "4/6/128Gb" and "2 SIM" when recovering memory
# from a full card title.
_MIN_PLAUSIBLE_STORAGE_GB = 32

# RAM sizes retailers actually sell. Used to tell a RAM/storage SPEC from a
# storage RANGE: "4/128" and "12/256" pair a RAM figure with a capacity and
# identify one product, while "128/256" and "256/512" pair two capacities
# and are the card's range across the SKUs it bundles -- they identify
# nothing, and recovering one puts a coin-toss capacity on a real product.
_PLAUSIBLE_RAM_GB = frozenset({1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 16, 18, 24})


def _is_storage_range(figures: list[int]) -> bool:
    """True when every figure is a capacity, so this states a range."""
    return len(figures) > 2 or (
        len(figures) == 2 and min(figures) not in _PLAUSIBLE_RAM_GB
    )


def _collapse(text: str) -> str:
    return re.sub(r"\s+", " ", text).strip(" ,;:-/\\|")


def _strip_memory(text: str) -> str:
    """Remove memory figures from CARD-DERIVED text only.

    Never call this on a SKU's own `Модель` or memory value:
    docs/parsers/uzum.md section 5b strips memory from the *card title*
    precisely because the SKU's own value is the trustworthy one. Applying
    it to `Модель` deleted the figure the whole section exists to preserve
    ("A16 8/256" -> "A16").
    """
    text = _MEMORY_PAIR_RE.sub(" ", text)
    text = _MEMORY_SINGLE_RE.sub(" ", text)
    text = _EMPTY_BRACKETS_RE.sub(" ", text)
    text = _ORPHAN_SEPARATOR_RE.sub(" ", text)
    return _collapse(text)


def _has_memory(text: str) -> bool:
    return bool(_MEMORY_PAIR_RE.search(text) or _MEMORY_SINGLE_RE.search(text))


# A bare capacity, with neither a unit nor a partner figure: `Память: "128"`,
# `Модель: "17 Pro 256"`. Restricted to real capacities so a model number
# ("17", "Note 14") is never mistaken for one.
_BARE_MEMORY_RE = re.compile(r"(?<![a-zа-я\d])(?:32|64|128|256|512|1024|2048)(?!\d)", re.I)


def _states_memory(text: str) -> bool:
    """Does this text state a memory figure IN ANY SHAPE?

    Distinct from `_has_memory`, which only recognises a separated pair or a
    unit-bearing figure. Both of this module's section-5b decisions ask
    "did the SKU tell us its own memory?", and for a bare figure `_has_memory`
    answered no -- so the card's overall RANGE was substituted for a figure
    the SKU had stated perfectly clearly:

    - the recovery gate appended the range beside the SKU's own capacity,
      turning `Память: "128"` on a "64/128/256 ГБ" card into
      `... 12 128 64/128 Алый`, where 64 becomes a MODEL token;
    - section 5b's strip gate never fired, so `Модель: "17 Pro 256"` on an
      "IPhone 17 Pro / Max 256/512 GB" card kept the card's range and keyed
      as 512 GB, merging three different SKUs onto one variant.

    A failure to RECOGNISE a stated figure is not a licence to substitute
    the card's range for it.
    """
    return bool(_has_memory(text) or _BARE_MEMORY_RE.search(text))


def _memory_from_title(title: str) -> str:
    """First plausible memory figure anywhere in the FULL card title.

    Last resort for cards that state memory after the first comma
    ("Smartfon Samsung Galaxy A16, 4/128 GB, 2 SIM, ...") while the SKU has
    no memory characteristic of its own. Without it those SKUs produce a
    name with neither RAM nor storage, which the clustering stage cannot
    key -- and the figure was sitting in raw["card_title"] all along.
    """
    saw_range = False
    for match in _MEMORY_PAIR_RE.finditer(title):
        figures = [int(f) for f in re.findall(r"\d{1,4}", match.group(0))]
        if not figures or max(figures) < _MIN_PLAUSIBLE_STORAGE_GB:
            continue
        # A range identifies nothing -- see _is_storage_range. Taking one
        # would put a coin-toss capacity on a real product, which is the
        # single defect this project exists to avoid; a name with no
        # capacity is refused by the clustering stage instead.
        if _is_storage_range(figures):
            saw_range = True
            continue
        return _collapse(match.group(0))
    if saw_range:
        # The single-figure fallback below would otherwise pick one HALF of
        # the range it just refused -- "128/256GB" yields "256GB" -- which is
        # the same coin toss with the evidence hidden.
        return ""
    match = _MEMORY_SINGLE_RE.search(title)
    return _collapse(match.group(0)) if match else ""


# "Smartfon Samsung Galaxy A16", "Смартфон Samsung ...", "Telefon ...".
# Harmless while the whole head is the name (it is what the retailer wrote),
# but fatal once the head is cut down to a prefix: it is a product-type noun
# carrying no identity, and keeping it in place of the brand is what made
# ("Smartfon Samsung Galaxy A16, ...", "A16 8/256") parse to
# "Smartfon A16 Qora".
_LEAD_NOUN_RE = re.compile(r"^(?:smartfon|смартфон|telefon|телефон)\w*\b[\s:,-]*", re.I)

_SUBTOKEN_RE = re.compile(r"[^0-9A-Za-zЀ-ӿ]+")


def _prefix_for_model(head: str, model_v: str) -> str:
    """The brand-bearing part of the card head, to sit in front of a Модель.

    A bare Модель value ("17 Pro Max 256 GB", "A16 8/256") carries no brand
    of its own, so the head has to supply it. The head is kept only UP TO
    the first word the Модель value already states, so
    "IPhone 17 Pro/Pro Max" + "17 Pro Max 256 GB" yields "IPhone" while
    "Samsung Galaxy A16" + "A16 8/256" keeps "Samsung Galaxy".

    Truncating rather than filtering is what stops a card lending a SKU the
    model it is NOT. uzum bundles siblings on one card -- "IPhone 17 Pro /
    Max 256/512 GB" carries both the Pro and the Pro Max -- and dropping
    only the words the Модель repeats left "Max" standing in the prefix of
    the plain "17 Pro 256" SKU, which then keyed as a Pro Max. Once a head
    word belongs to the model, everything after it is model territory and
    the Модель value owns it: it is the per-SKU field, and the head is the
    shared one.
    """
    model_tokens = {t for t in _SUBTOKEN_RE.split(model_v.lower()) if t}
    kept = []
    for word in _LEAD_NOUN_RE.sub("", head).split():
        subtokens = [t for t in _SUBTOKEN_RE.split(word.lower()) if t]
        if subtokens and all(t in model_tokens for t in subtokens):
            break
        kept.append(word)
    return " ".join(kept)


def _build_name_raw(card_title: str | None, model_v: str, mem_v: str, color_v: str) -> str:
    """Best-effort faithful name -- and the clustering stage's ONLY handle on
    this product's identity. See the module docstring for the three rules
    and the bug each of them fixes.
    """
    full_title = (card_title or "").strip()
    head = full_title.split(",")[0].strip()

    if model_v:
        # The SKU's own Модель wins outright and is never rewritten.
        spec = model_v
        prefix = _prefix_for_model(head, model_v)
        if mem_v or _states_memory(model_v):
            # ...but the card head in front of it must not smuggle the
            # card's overall storage RANGE in beside it (section 5b).
            prefix = _strip_memory(prefix)
    else:
        prefix = ""
        spec = _strip_memory(head) if mem_v else head

    name = _collapse(" ".join(p for p in (prefix, spec, mem_v) if p))

    # Last resort, and ONLY when this SKU stated no memory of its own. The
    # card title past the first comma is shared across every SKU the card
    # bundles, so reaching into it for a capacity the SKU already supplied
    # replaces a specific figure with a range -- see _states_memory.
    if not _states_memory(name) and not (mem_v or _states_memory(model_v)):
        recovered = _memory_from_title(full_title)
        if recovered:
            name = _collapse(f"{name} {recovered}")
    return _collapse(f"{name} {color_v}" if color_v else name)


def _items(payload: dict) -> list[dict]:
    return (((payload or {}).get("data") or {}).get("makeSearch") or {}).get("items") or []


def _card_image(card: dict) -> str | None:
    """The card's first photo, or None.

    uzum was the only source publishing no picture at all -- 5,461 offers,
    the largest source in the catalogue, every one of them imageless, because
    `photos` was simply never asked for. The site's placeholder-heavy look
    traced back to this one missing field.

    Two things about the field are not guessable and were read off the live
    schema: `photos.link` REQUIRES a `trans:` argument (`Transformation!`), so
    a bare `link { high }` is a validation error and a 400, not a null; and
    PhotoLink's `high`/`low` are plain URL strings, not objects. PRODUCT_540
    is a card-sized render -- ORIGINAL exists but is a full-resolution
    original, which is the wrong thing to hotlink into a grid.

    The photo belongs to the CARD, and a card is finer-grained than a
    product: makeSearch returns ONE CARD PER COLOUR, so a single productId
    comes back as several cards (16 of 72 items in the recorded fixture) whose
    skuLists differ only in storage tier. The picture is therefore accurate to
    the colour, not merely to the model -- which matters here, because colour
    is part of a phone's identity in this catalogue and a card showing the
    black handset under the green variant would be a substitution.
    """
    photos = card.get("photos")
    if not isinstance(photos, list):
        return None
    for photo in photos:
        if not isinstance(photo, dict):
            continue
        link = photo.get("link")
        url = link.get("high") if isinstance(link, dict) else None
        if isinstance(url, str) and url.startswith("http"):
            return url
    return None


def _parse_sku(card: dict, sku: dict) -> Listing | None:
    if not isinstance(sku, dict):
        return None
    sku_id = sku.get("id")
    if sku_id is None:
        return None
    product_id = card.get("productId")
    if product_id is None:
        return None

    price = coerce_price(sku.get("sellPrice"))  # never fullPrice -- see module docstring
    chars = _characteristics(sku)
    name_raw = _build_name_raw(card.get("title"), chars["model"], chars["memory"], chars["color"])

    try:
        amount = int(sku.get("availableAmount") or 0)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        amount = 0
    # Deliberate inversion of docs/parsers/uzum.md section 4 -- see module
    # docstring. Kept, not dropped; OUT_OF_STOCK rather than discarded.
    availability = "IN_STOCK" if amount > 0 else "OUT_OF_STOCK"

    return try_build_listing(
        store_slug="uzum",
        source_key=str(sku_id),
        name_raw=name_raw,
        price=price,
        url=PRODUCT_URL.format(product_id=product_id, sku_id=sku_id),
        availability=availability,
        image_url=_card_image(card),
        raw={
            "card_title": card.get("title"),      # untouched, for re-derivation downstream
            "category_id": (card.get("category") or {}).get("id"),
            "product_id": product_id,
            "sku_id": sku_id,
            "characteristic_values": sku.get("characteristicValues") or [],
            "available_amount": sku.get("availableAmount"),
            "full_price": sku.get("fullPrice"),
        },
    )


def parse(payload: dict, category: str = "smartphones") -> list[Listing]:
    """Turn one raw makeSearch response into Listings. Pure function, no I/O.

    Unlike idea/beemarket, category filtering happens inside parse() itself
    rather than as a separate crawl-policy step in sweep() -- search() hits
    the same noisy relevance endpoint sweep() does, so both need the filter
    and there is no separate category-scoped endpoint to lean on instead.

    Handles the `errors`-key failure mode (docs/parsers/uzum.md section 2)
    by returning [] rather than raising -- the live fetch path
    (UzumSource._fetch_payload) is what raises on this, so a broken sweep
    call is loud instead of silently looking like an empty brand.
    """
    if (payload or {}).get("errors"):
        logger.warning("uzum: graphql payload carries an errors key, returning no listings: %s",
                        payload.get("errors"))
        return []

    ids = CATEGORY_IDS.get(category)
    if ids is None:
        raise ValueError(f"unknown category {category!r}")
    listings: list[Listing] = []
    for item in _items(payload):
        card = (item or {}).get("catalogCard") or {}
        category_id = (card.get("category") or {}).get("id")
        if category_id not in ids:
            continue
        for sku in card.get("skuList") or []:
            lst = _parse_sku(card, sku)
            if lst is not None:
                if lst.category != category:
                    lst = replace(lst, category=category)
                listings.append(lst)
    return listings


def _search_variables(text: str, offset: int) -> dict:
    return {
        "q": {
            "text": text,
            "showAdultContent": "TRUE",
            "filters": [],
            "sort": "BY_RELEVANCE_DESC",
            "pagination": {"offset": offset, "limit": PAGE_LIMIT},
        }
    }


class UzumSource:
    slug = "uzum"
    can_sweep = True

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self._session = None

    def _get_session(self):
        if self._session is None:
            self._session = polite_session(
                referer="https://uzum.uz/",
                origin="https://uzum.uz",
                extra_headers={
                    "Accept-Language": "ru-RU",
                    "apollographql-client-name": "web-customers",  # required
                    "apollographql-client-version": "1.63.2",
                    "city-id": "1",
                },
            )
        return self._session

    def _post_page(self, text: str, offset: int) -> dict:
        session = self._get_session()
        token, iid = _get_token()
        return post_json(
            session,
            GRAPHQL_URL,
            headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}", "x-iid": iid},
            json={"query": SEARCH_QUERY, "variables": _search_variables(text, offset)},
        )

    def _fetch_payload(self, text: str, offset: int) -> dict:
        """POST one makeSearch page, raising on the errors-key failure mode
        (docs/parsers/uzum.md section 2) rather than treating it as an
        empty/end-of-results page -- see module docstring for why.

        A 401 re-mints the token once and retries. The cached token is only
        refreshed when its locally decoded `exp` passes, which cannot see a
        server-side revocation: without this, a token revoked in the middle
        of a brand sweep propagated an HTTPError all the way out of sweep()
        and ended the run, even though minting a new one takes one request.
        A second 401 is a genuine auth failure and is left to raise.
        """
        try:
            payload = self._post_page(text, offset)
        except requests.HTTPError as exc:
            if getattr(exc.response, "status_code", None) != 401:
                raise
            logger.warning(
                "uzum: 401 for %r@%d -- re-minting the token and retrying once", text, offset
            )
            _invalidate_token()
            payload = self._post_page(text, offset)
        errors = (payload or {}).get("errors")
        if errors:
            raise UzumGraphQLError(f"uzum graphql errors for {text!r}@{offset}: {errors!r}")
        return payload

    def _walk(self, text: str, category: str = "smartphones") -> Iterator[Listing]:
        def fetch(offset):
            return self._fetch_payload(text, offset)

        def following(payload, offset):
            # Two end signals: the offset cap (docs say results run out
            # before it for most brands) and the items running out -- uzum
            # has no last_page, so an empty payload IS its end marker
            # (base.paginate's rule: the client whose end signal is an
            # empty payload expresses that in its own next_page).
            nxt = offset + PAGE_LIMIT
            if nxt > OFFSET_CAP:
                return None
            return nxt if _items(payload) else None

        yield from paginate(fetch, lambda payload: parse(payload, category), following, first_page=0)

    def sweep(self, category: str = "smartphones") -> Iterator[Listing]:
        """Every item uzum returns across this category's query frontier,
        paginating each until its items run out or offset hits OFFSET_CAP
        (see module docstring for why offset can't just run unbounded).
        Deduplicated by source_key (SKU id) across queries, since the same SKU
        can surface under more than one query.

        Phones sweep by BRAND; everything else sweeps by the product NOUN.
        Using the brand frontier for a category left uzum holding zero air
        conditioners, fridges, washers and ovens: the brands that sell white
        goods here sell no phones and so were never queried, and for Samsung,
        which sells both, relevance ranks phones first and pagination caps at
        offset 1000 so a fridge never surfaced. Measured live, "konditsioner"
        returns 72 of 72 in-category while "artel" returns remote controls,
        vacuum filters and electric kettles. See sources/brand_queries.py.
        """
        seen: set[str] = set()
        for query in queries_for(category):
            # Per-page retries live in base.paginate() via _walk.
            for listing in self._walk(query, category):
                if listing.source_key in seen:
                    continue
                seen.add(listing.source_key)
                yield listing

    def search(self, query: str) -> Iterator[Listing]:
        payload = self._fetch_payload(query, 0)
        yield from parse(payload)

import os

import pytest
from psycopg.conninfo import conninfo_to_dict


def require_disposable_test_database(dsn: str) -> None:
    """Belt-and-braces guard, independent of the NARXNOMA_TEST_DSN /
    NARXNOMA_DSN split above: refuse to truncate any database whose name
    does not mark it as disposable.

    The primary guard against wiping production is that the test suite
    reads NARXNOMA_TEST_DSN, a variable distinct from NARXNOMA_DSN (the
    setting narxnoma/config.py hands the deployed crawler and web app).
    This function is the second line of defense, for the case where
    NARXNOMA_TEST_DSN itself gets pointed at the wrong database.
    """
    dbname = conninfo_to_dict(dsn).get("dbname") or ""
    if "test" not in dbname:
        raise RuntimeError(
            f"refusing to truncate database {dbname!r}: the test suite only "
            "runs against a database whose name contains 'test', so that a "
            "human can see at a glance it is disposable. Point "
            "NARXNOMA_TEST_DSN at a database like 'narxnoma_test', not "
            f"{dbname!r}."
        )


@pytest.fixture(scope="session")
def dsn():
    value = os.environ.get("NARXNOMA_TEST_DSN")
    if not value:
        pytest.skip("NARXNOMA_TEST_DSN not set; start postgres and export it")
    return value


@pytest.fixture()
def db_conn(dsn):
    from narxnoma.db.connection import connect
    from narxnoma.db.migrate import migrate

    require_disposable_test_database(dsn)

    with connect(dsn) as conn:
        migrate(conn)
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            # variant must be here too: its slug is UNIQUE, so a test that
            # commits a variant would collide with the next test inserting the
            # same identity. CASCADE clears variant_price and unresolved_offer,
            # which reference it.
            cur.execute(
                "TRUNCATE raw_offer, offer, harvest_run, variant"
                " RESTART IDENTITY CASCADE"
            )
        conn.commit()
        try:
            yield conn
        finally:
            conn.rollback()

import pytest

from narxnoma.cli import main, render_report, render_status, report_exit_code
from narxnoma.pipeline.harvest import HarvestResult
from narxnoma.pipeline.report import BELOW_FLOOR, LAST_RUN_FAILED, STALE, SourceCoverage


def _row(slug, offers, expected_min, reasons=()):
    return SourceCoverage(slug=slug, offers=offers, median_price=None,
                          oldest_seen=None, newest_seen=None, last_run_ok=None,
                          expected_min=expected_min, reasons=tuple(reasons),
                          age_hours=1.0)


def test_render_report_marks_suspicious_rows_distinctly():
    rows = [_row("olcha", 3, 300, [BELOW_FLOOR]), _row("texnomart", 500, 300)]
    out = render_report(rows)
    olcha_line = next(line for line in out.splitlines() if line.startswith("olcha"))
    texnomart_line = next(line for line in out.splitlines() if line.startswith("texnomart"))
    assert "SUSPICIOUS" in olcha_line
    assert "SUSPICIOUS" not in texnomart_line


def test_render_report_names_the_rule_that_fired():
    """A bare SUSPICIOUS cannot be acted on. "stale" and "last run failed"
    have different causes and different fixes from "below floor", and the
    stale case is invisible in the count column -- offers clears its floor.
    """
    rows = [_row("olcha", 448, 300, [STALE]),
            _row("idea", 3, 100, [BELOW_FLOOR, LAST_RUN_FAILED])]
    out = render_report(rows)
    olcha_line = next(line for line in out.splitlines() if line.startswith("olcha"))
    idea_line = next(line for line in out.splitlines() if line.startswith("idea"))
    assert STALE in olcha_line
    assert BELOW_FLOOR not in olcha_line
    assert BELOW_FLOOR in idea_line and LAST_RUN_FAILED in idea_line


def test_report_exit_code_nonzero_when_any_source_suspicious():
    assert report_exit_code([_row("olcha", 3, 300, [BELOW_FLOOR]),
                             _row("idea", 200, 100)]) == 1


def test_report_exit_code_zero_when_none_suspicious():
    assert report_exit_code([_row("idea", 200, 100)]) == 0


@pytest.mark.db
def test_cli_report_exits_nonzero_when_a_source_is_suspicious(db_conn, dsn, monkeypatch):
    # Reuses the `dsn` fixture (NARXNOMA_TEST_DSN) rather than reading
    # NARXNOMA_DSN directly, so the connection main() ends up using is
    # guaranteed to be the same disposable database db_conn just truncated.
    import narxnoma.cli as cli_module
    from narxnoma.db.connection import connect as real_connect

    monkeypatch.setattr(cli_module, "connect", lambda: real_connect(dsn))

    # db_conn's fixture already truncated offer/raw_offer/harvest_run, so
    # every source sits at zero offers -- below every non-zero floor.
    exit_code = main(["report"])
    assert exit_code != 0


def test_render_status_ok():
    result = HarvestResult("olcha", ok=True, seen=448, kept=448)
    assert render_status(result) == "ok"


def test_render_status_failed():
    result = HarvestResult("idea", ok=False, error="upstream 503")
    assert render_status(result) == "FAILED: upstream 503"


def test_render_status_skipped_is_not_reported_as_ok():
    # Fix 1: a skipped source (mediapark, search-only) must render visibly
    # differently from a source that actually swept its catalogue -- the
    # original bug was that both printed as plain "ok".
    result = HarvestResult("mediapark", ok=True, skipped=True,
                           error="search-only, skipped")
    status = render_status(result)
    assert status != "ok"
    assert status == "SKIPPED (search-only, skipped)"
    assert result.skipped is True

def test_new_subcommands_are_registered():
    """A typo in a subcommand name should fail here, not in a cron job."""

    from narxnoma import cli

    for command in ("cluster", "aggregate", "quality", "cycle"):
        with pytest.raises(SystemExit) as exc:
            cli.main([command, "--nonsense"])
        assert exc.value.code == 2, f"{command} is not a registered subcommand"


def test_cycle_isolates_a_failing_stage(monkeypatch):
    """A clustering failure must not lose the harvest that preceded it.

    Those offers are already durably written; re-running the whole cycle would
    re-fetch several thousand listings from retailers for nothing.
    """
    from narxnoma import cli

    calls = []

    def boom(conn):
        calls.append("cluster")
        raise RuntimeError("clustering blew up")

    monkeypatch.setattr(cli, "run_clustering", boom)
    monkeypatch.setattr(cli, "harvest_all", lambda conn, sources: calls.append("harvest") or [])
    monkeypatch.setattr(cli, "migrate", lambda conn: None)
    monkeypatch.setattr(cli.repository, "try_advisory_lock", lambda conn, key: True)
    monkeypatch.setattr(cli, "coverage_report", lambda conn: [])
    monkeypatch.setattr(cli, "quality_report", lambda conn: _FakeQuality())

    class _NullConn:
        def __enter__(self):
            return self

        def __exit__(self, *a):
            return False

    monkeypatch.setattr(cli, "connect", lambda: _NullConn())

    monkeypatch.setattr(cli, "render_quality", lambda r: "")
    monkeypatch.setattr(cli, "render_report", lambda rows: "")

    code = cli.main(["cycle"])

    assert "harvest" in calls, "harvest must still have run"
    assert "cluster" in calls, "clustering must have been attempted"
    assert code == 1, "a failed stage must make the cycle exit non-zero"


class _FakeQuality:
    is_alerting = False
    total_offers = 0
    attached = 0
    unresolved = 0
    variants = 0
    single_offer_variants = 0
    diverging_variants = 0
    reasons: list = []
    unresolved_by_store: list = []
    unresolved_rate = 0.0


def test_cycle_refuses_to_run_twice_at_once(db_conn, dsn, monkeypatch):
    import psycopg
    from narxnoma.cli import CYCLE_LOCK_KEY, main
    from narxnoma.db.repository import try_advisory_lock

    holder = psycopg.connect(dsn)
    try:
        assert try_advisory_lock(holder, CYCLE_LOCK_KEY) is True
        monkeypatch.setenv("NARXNOMA_DSN", dsn)
        assert main(["cycle"]) == 1
    finally:
        holder.close()

class _FakeSource:
    slug = "fake"
    can_sweep = True

    def __init__(self):
        self.calls = []

    def sweep(self, category="smartphones"):
        from narxnoma.sources.base import Listing
        self.calls.append(("sweep", category))
        for i in range(3):
            yield Listing(store_slug="fake", source_key=f"k{i}", name_raw=f"Phone {i}",
                          price=1_000_000 + i, url=f"https://fake/{i}", category=category)

    def search(self, query):
        from narxnoma.sources.base import Listing
        self.calls.append(("search", query))
        yield Listing(store_slug="fake", source_key="q", name_raw=query,
                      price=2_000_000, url="https://fake/q")


def test_fetch_sweeps_without_a_database(monkeypatch, capsys):
    """`fetch` must never touch connect(): it is the path someone without
    Postgres uses to get prices out of a source in one command."""
    import json
    from narxnoma import cli

    fake = _FakeSource()
    monkeypatch.setattr(cli, "SOURCES", {"fake": fake})
    monkeypatch.setattr(cli, "connect", lambda: (_ for _ in ()).throw(AssertionError("db touched")))

    code = cli.main(["fetch", "--source", "fake", "--category", "laptops"])

    assert code == 0
    assert fake.calls == [("sweep", "laptops")]
    rows = [json.loads(line) for line in capsys.readouterr().out.splitlines()]
    assert [r["source_key"] for r in rows] == ["k0", "k1", "k2"]
    assert rows[0]["price"] == 1_000_000 and rows[0]["category"] == "laptops"
    assert "raw" not in rows[0], "raw payload stays out unless --raw is asked for"

"""Offline tests for narxnoma.daily: catalogue paging, field mapping, token reading, the lock."""

import json
import os
import time

import pytest

from narxnoma import daily


class FakeResp:
    def __init__(self, payload, status=200):
        self._p, self.status_code = payload, status

    def json(self):
        return self._p

    def raise_for_status(self):
        if self.status_code >= 400:
            raise RuntimeError(self.status_code)


class FakeSession:
    def __init__(self, pages, status=200):
        self.pages, self.status, self.calls = pages, status, []

    def get(self, url, params=None, headers=None, timeout=None):
        self.calls.append((params["page"], headers["Authorization"]))
        if self.status != 200:
            return FakeResp({}, self.status)
        i = params["page"] - 1
        return FakeResp(self.pages[i] if i < len(self.pages) else {"items": []})


CFG = {
    "ECOM_PRODUCTS_URL": "https://example.test/api/products",
    "ECOM_TOKEN": "Bearer tkn",
    "ECOM_PAGE_SIZE": "2",
    "ECOM_PAUSE_S": "0",
}


def test_paginates_until_short_page_and_sends_bearer():
    pages = [{"items": [{"name": "a"}, {"name": "b"}]}, {"items": [{"name": "c"}]}]
    s = FakeSession(pages)
    got = daily.fetch_catalogue(CFG, s)
    assert [x["name"] for x in got] == ["a", "b", "c"]
    assert s.calls == [(1, "Bearer tkn"), (2, "Bearer tkn")]


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "payload",
    [
        [{"name": "a"}],
        {"data": [{"name": "a"}]},
        {"data": {"items": [{"name": "a"}]}},
        {"results": [{"name": "a"}], "total": 1},
    ],
)
def test_envelopes(payload):
    assert daily.extract_items(payload) == [{"name": "a"}]


def test_server_ignoring_page_does_not_loop():
    same = {"items": [{"name": "a"}, {"name": "b"}]}
    got = daily.fetch_catalogue(CFG, FakeSession([same] * 600))
    assert len(got) == 2  # stops on the repeated first item


def test_expired_token_is_a_clear_error():
    with pytest.raises(PermissionError, match="expired"):
        daily.fetch_catalogue(CFG, FakeSession([], status=401))


def test_targets_mapping_and_stats():
    items = [
        {
            "name": "Phone X 8/256",
            "price": "5 990 000",
            "category": {"name": "Смартфоны"},
            "is_active": True,
        },
        {"title": "TV", "sale_price": 3000000.0, "category_name": "Телевизоры", "active": 1},
        {"name": "Hidden", "price": 1, "is_active": False},
        {"name": "No price", "price": 0},
        {"price": 5},
        {"name": "Loose", "price": 100},
    ]
    rows, st = daily.to_targets(items, {})
    assert [r["name"] for r in rows] == ["Phone X 8/256", "TV", "Loose"]
    assert rows[0]["our price"] == 5990000.0 and rows[0]["category"] == "Смартфоны"
    assert st == {
        "seen": 6,
        "inactive": 1,
        "no_name": 1,
        "no_price": 1,
        "no_category": 1,
        "kept": 3,
    }

        [{"name": "H", "price": 1, "is_active": False}], {"ECOM_ONLY_ACTIVE": "0"}

def test_shape_hides_values():

    assert s == {"name": "str", "price": "int", "category.name": "str"}

@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "content,expect",
    [
        ("Bearer abc\n", "abc"),
        ('{"access_token": "abc"}', "abc"),
        ("OTHER=1\nECOM_TOKEN='abc'\n", "abc"),
    ],
)
def test_token_file_formats(tmp_path, content, expect):
    f = tmp_path / "tok"
    f.write_text(content, encoding="utf-8")
    assert daily.read_token({"ECOM_TOKEN_FILE": str(f)}) == expect


def test_token_is_reread_each_call(tmp_path):
    f = tmp_path / "tok"
    f.write_text("one")
    assert daily.read_token({"ECOM_TOKEN_FILE": str(f)}) == "one"
    f.write_text("two")
    assert daily.read_token({"ECOM_TOKEN_FILE": str(f)}) == "two"


def test_lock_excludes_and_recovers_stale(tmp_path):
    a, b = daily.Lock(tmp_path / "l"), daily.Lock(tmp_path / "l", stale_h=0.001)
    assert a.acquire()
    assert not daily.Lock(tmp_path / "l").acquire(wait_s=0)
    old = time.time() - 3600
    os.utime(tmp_path / "l", (old, old))
    assert b.acquire()  # stale -> taken over
    b.release()
    assert a.acquire()

def test_report_refuses_to_start_when_telegram_cannot_send(tmp_path, monkeypatch):

def test_report_end_to_end_offline(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    """Catalogue -> csv -> research on the cache -> workbook -> one send, no network."""
    from narxnoma.research import collect
    from narxnoma.sources import SOURCES

    def sweep(slug, category, cache_dir, max_age_h, force):
        rows = [
            {
                "store_slug": slug,
                "source_key": "k",
                "price": 4_990_000,
                "name_raw": "Samsung Galaxy A55 8/256GB Black",
                "url": f"https://x/{slug}",
                "availability": "IN_STOCK",
                "image_url": None,
                "category": category,
            }
        ]
        return (rows if category == "smartphones" else []), time.time()

    monkeypatch.setattr(collect, "_sweep_cached", sweep)
    for s in SOURCES.values():
        if not s.can_sweep:
            monkeypatch.setattr(s, "search", lambda q: [], raising=False)
    items = [
        {
            "name": "Samsung Galaxy A55 8/256GB Black",
            "price": "5 100 000",
            "category": {"name": "Smartphones"},
            "is_active": True,
        },
        {"name": "Old phone", "price": 1, "category": "Smartphones", "is_active": False},
    ]
    monkeypatch.setattr(daily, "fetch_catalogue", lambda *a, **k: items)
    monkeypatch.setattr(daily, "telegram_problem", lambda cfg: None)
    sent = []
    monkeypatch.setattr(daily, "send_telegram", lambda cfg, p, c: sent.append((p, c)))
    assert daily.job_report({"NARXNOMA_DAILY_DIR": str(tmp_path)}) == 0
    ((path, caption),) = sent
    assert path.name.startswith("market_analysis_") and path.exists()
    assert caption.startswith("Market analysis") and "1 products" in caption
    assert not (tmp_path / "daily.lock").exists()

FILE: narxnoma-crawler/tests/db/test_advisory_lock.py
================================================
"""One cycle at a time. A second overlapping run doubles our request rate at
every retailer at once, which is how an IP gets blocked."""
import psycopg
import pytest

from narxnoma.db.repository import try_advisory_lock

pytestmark = pytest.mark.db

KEY = 20260802


def test_the_lock_is_granted_when_free(db_conn):
    assert try_advisory_lock(db_conn, KEY) is True


def test_a_second_connection_is_refused_while_it_is_held(db_conn, dsn):
    assert try_advisory_lock(db_conn, KEY) is True
    with psycopg.connect(dsn) as other:
        assert try_advisory_lock(other, KEY) is False


def test_the_lock_is_released_when_the_session_ends(dsn):
    # Session-scoped, so a crashed cycle cannot wedge the crontab forever.
    # This is the property a lock TABLE would need explicit cleanup for.
    with psycopg.connect(dsn) as first:
        assert try_advisory_lock(first, KEY) is True
    with psycopg.connect(dsn) as second:
        assert try_advisory_lock(second, KEY) is True


def test_different_keys_do_not_block_each_other(db_conn, dsn):
    assert try_advisory_lock(db_conn, KEY) is True
    with psycopg.connect(dsn) as other:
        assert try_advisory_lock(other, KEY + 1) is True

import pytest

pytestmark = pytest.mark.db


def test_migrate_creates_tables_and_seeds_stores(db_conn):
    with db_conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute("SELECT slug FROM store ORDER BY slug")
        slugs = [r[0] for r in cur.fetchall()]
    # asaxiy arrives in migration 3 and radius in migration 4, not in the
    # migration-1 seed list -- see the comments there. Listed explicitly
    # rather than derived from SOURCES: a source registered with no store row
    # is precisely the bug this catches.
    assert slugs == ["alifshop", "asaxiy", "beemarket", "glotr", "idea", "mediapark",
                     "olcha", "openshop", "radius", "texnomart", "uzum"]


def test_migrate_is_idempotent(db_conn):
    from narxnoma.db.migrate import migrate

    migrate(db_conn)          # second run must not raise or duplicate
    with db_conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute("SELECT count(*) FROM store")
        assert cur.fetchone()[0] == 10


def test_price_check_constraint_rejects_bad_values(db_conn):
    import psycopg

    with db_conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute("SELECT id FROM store WHERE slug = 'olcha'")
        store_id = cur.fetchone()[0]
        with pytest.raises(psycopg.errors.CheckViolation):
            cur.execute(
                "INSERT INTO raw_offer (store_id, source_key, name_raw, price, url)"
                " VALUES (%s, 'k', 'X', 99, 'u')", (store_id,))


def test_connect_commits_on_clean_exit(dsn):
    """A write through connect() must survive the connection closing.

    This was a real, silent bug: psycopg opens an implicit transaction on the
    first statement -- including the plain read every pipeline stage starts
    with -- after which the repository's own `with conn.transaction()` blocks
    nest as savepoints that release without committing. Closing without a
    commit rolled back everything, while every log line still reported success.
    """
    import psycopg

    from narxnoma.db.connection import connect

    with connect(dsn) as conn:
        with conn.cursor() as cur:          # plain read: opens the implicit tx
            cur.execute("SELECT count(*) FROM store")
        with conn.transaction():            # nests as a savepoint
            with conn.cursor() as cur:
                cur.execute("INSERT INTO store (slug, name, website_url)"
                            " VALUES ('committest', 'Commit Test', 'https://x')")

    with psycopg.connect(dsn) as check, check.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute("SELECT count(*) FROM store WHERE slug = 'committest'")
        persisted = cur.fetchone()[0]
        cur.execute("DELETE FROM store WHERE slug = 'committest'")
        check.commit()
    assert persisted == 1, "the write was rolled back when the connection closed"


def test_connect_rolls_back_when_the_body_raises(dsn):
    import psycopg

    from narxnoma.db.connection import connect

    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError):
        with connect(dsn) as conn:
            with conn.cursor() as cur:
                cur.execute("INSERT INTO store (slug, name, website_url)"
                            " VALUES ('rollbacktest', 'X', 'https://x')")
            raise RuntimeError("something went wrong mid-cycle")

    with psycopg.connect(dsn) as check, check.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute("SELECT count(*) FROM store WHERE slug = 'rollbacktest'")
        assert cur.fetchone()[0] == 0

"""Variants that no offer references are re-keying residue, not products."""
import pytest

from narxnoma.db import repository as repo
from narxnoma.matching.keys import VariantKey
from narxnoma.sources.base import Listing

pytestmark = pytest.mark.db


def _tv_key(code="ue55du7100uxuz"):
    return VariantKey(brand="samsung", model_tokens=frozenset({code}),
                      ram_gb=None, storage_gb=None, color=None, sim_kind=None,
                      category="televisions")


def _listing(key="tv1"):
    return Listing(store_slug="olcha", source_key=key,
                   name_raw="Телевизор Samsung UE55DU7100UXUZ", price=6_599_000,
                   url=f"https://olcha.uz/{key}", availability="IN_STOCK",
                   category="televisions")


def test_a_variant_no_offer_references_is_deleted(db_conn):
    repo.upsert_variant(db_conn, _tv_key())
    assert repo.delete_orphan_variants(db_conn) == 1
    assert repo.load_variant_keys(db_conn) == {}


def test_a_variant_with_an_offer_is_kept(db_conn):
    sid = repo.store_ids(db_conn)["olcha"]
    repo.upsert_offers(db_conn, sid, [_listing()])
    variant_id = repo.upsert_variant(db_conn, _tv_key())
    with db_conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute("SELECT id FROM offer WHERE source_key = 'tv1'")
        offer_id = cur.fetchone()[0]
    repo.attach_offer_to_variant(db_conn, offer_id, variant_id)

    assert repo.delete_orphan_variants(db_conn) == 0
    assert _tv_key() in repo.load_variant_keys(db_conn)


def test_an_out_of_stock_variant_is_kept(db_conn):
    # The deliberate decision recorded in schema.sql: a real product whose
    # offers have all gone out of stock keeps its page and a NULL price. Its
    # offer rows still exist, so this rule never reaches it.
    sid = repo.store_ids(db_conn)["olcha"]
    gone = Listing(store_slug="olcha", source_key="tv2",
                   name_raw="Телевизор Samsung UE55DU7100UXUZ", price=6_599_000,
                   url="https://olcha.uz/tv2", availability="OUT_OF_STOCK",
                   category="televisions")
    repo.upsert_offers(db_conn, sid, [gone])
    variant_id = repo.upsert_variant(db_conn, _tv_key())
    with db_conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute("SELECT id FROM offer WHERE source_key = 'tv2'")
        repo.attach_offer_to_variant(db_conn, cur.fetchone()[0], variant_id)

    assert repo.delete_orphan_variants(db_conn) == 0


def test_variant_keys_are_read_back_with_their_category(db_conn):
    # load_variant_keys omitted `category`, so every stored variant claimed to
    # be a smartphone: display_name took the phone branch and dereferenced a
    # NULL colour, and a freshly-built non-phone key could never match the one
    # loaded from the database.
    repo.upsert_variant(db_conn, _tv_key())
    keys = list(repo.load_variant_keys(db_conn))
    assert len(keys) == 1
    assert keys[0].category == "televisions"
    assert keys[0] == _tv_key()

FILE: narxnoma-crawler/tests/db/test_repository.py

import pytest

from narxnoma.db import repository as repo
from narxnoma.sources.base import Listing

pytestmark = pytest.mark.db


def listing(key="k1", price=2_723_000, name="Смартфон Xiaomi Redmi Note 15 8/256 ГБ, Синий"):
    return Listing(store_slug="olcha", source_key=key, name_raw=name,
                   price=price, url=f"https://olcha.uz/{key}", availability="IN_STOCK")


def test_store_ids_returns_all_seeded_stores(db_conn):
    ids = repo.store_ids(db_conn)
    assert set(ids) == {"uzum", "alifshop", "beemarket", "idea", "mediapark",
                        "olcha", "texnomart", "asaxiy", "radius", "glotr", "openshop"}


def test_raw_offer_is_append_only(db_conn):
    sid = repo.store_ids(db_conn)["olcha"]
    repo.record_raw_offers(db_conn, sid, [listing(price=2_723_000)])
    repo.record_raw_offers(db_conn, sid, [listing(price=2_699_000)])
    with db_conn.cursor() as cur:
        # ORDER BY id, not observed_at: observed_at defaults to now(), which is the
        # transaction timestamp -- rows written in the same transaction share it, so
        # only id (true insertion order) disambiguates them.
        cur.execute("SELECT price FROM raw_offer WHERE source_key='k1' ORDER BY id")
        assert [r[0] for r in cur.fetchall()] == [2_723_000, 2_699_000]


def test_upsert_inserts_then_updates_keeping_first_seen(db_conn):
    sid = repo.store_ids(db_conn)["olcha"]
    assert repo.upsert_offers(db_conn, sid, [listing(price=2_723_000)]) == (1, 0)
    with db_conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute("SELECT first_seen FROM offer WHERE source_key='k1'")
        first = cur.fetchone()[0]

    assert repo.upsert_offers(db_conn, sid, [listing(price=2_699_000)]) == (0, 1)
    with db_conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute("SELECT price, first_seen, last_seen FROM offer WHERE source_key='k1'")
        price, first_seen, last_seen = cur.fetchone()
    assert price == 2_699_000
    assert first_seen == first          # first_seen must never move
    assert last_seen >= first_seen


def test_upsert_does_not_duplicate_on_rerun(db_conn):
    sid = repo.store_ids(db_conn)["olcha"]
    repo.upsert_offers(db_conn, sid, [listing()])
    repo.upsert_offers(db_conn, sid, [listing()])
    with db_conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute("SELECT count(*) FROM offer WHERE source_key='k1'")
        assert cur.fetchone()[0] == 1


def test_run_bookkeeping(db_conn):
    sid = repo.store_ids(db_conn)["olcha"]
    run_id = repo.start_run(db_conn, sid)
    repo.finish_run(db_conn, run_id, ok=True, seen=440, kept=438)
    with db_conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute("SELECT ok, listings_seen, listings_kept, finished_at IS NOT NULL"
                    " FROM harvest_run WHERE id=%s", (run_id,))
        assert cur.fetchone() == (True, 440, 438, True)

import uuid

import psycopg
import pytest

pytestmark = pytest.mark.db

INSERT_VARIANT = (

    " sim_kind, display_name, slug, category)"
    " VALUES (%s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, 'smartphones') RETURNING id"
)
HONOR = ("honor", ["x9d"], 12, 256, "black", "dual",
         "Смартфон Honor X9D 12/256 ГБ, Черный", "honor-x9d-12-256-black")


def test_variant_tables_exist(db_conn):
    with db_conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute("""
            SELECT table_name FROM information_schema.tables
             WHERE table_schema = 'public'
               AND table_name IN ('variant', 'variant_price', 'unresolved_offer')
             ORDER BY table_name
        """)
        assert [r[0] for r in cur.fetchall()] == ["unresolved_offer", "variant", "variant_price"]


def test_slug_is_unique_so_duplicates_are_structurally_impossible(db_conn):
    # The slug is a deterministic function of the identity, so uniqueness here
    # is what stops "Cosmic orange" and "Cosmic Orange" becoming two products.
    with db_conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute(INSERT_VARIANT, HONOR)
        with pytest.raises(psycopg.errors.UniqueViolation):
            cur.execute(INSERT_VARIANT, HONOR)


def test_apple_variant_may_have_no_ram(db_conn):
    # Apple publishes no RAM; requiring it would make every iPhone unkeyable.
    with db_conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute(INSERT_VARIANT, ("apple", ["17", "pro"], None, 256, "silver",
                                     "dual", "Смартфон Apple iPhone 17 Pro 256 ГБ, Серебристый",
                                     "apple-17-pro-256-silver"))
        assert cur.fetchone()[0]


def test_non_phone_variant_may_omit_colour_and_sim(db_conn):
    # Plan 5 (categories): TVs, laptops, ACs, fridges, washers, ovens carry
    # no colour/SIM identity, so both hard phone-identity fields are now
    # nullable at the schema level. The smartphone rule (colour is required)
    # is enforced by the matching layer, not the schema.
    with db_conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute(
            "INSERT INTO variant (brand, model_tokens, ram_gb, storage_gb, color,"
            " sim_kind, display_name, slug, category)"
            " VALUES (%s, %s, NULL, 55, NULL, NULL, %s, %s, 'televisions') RETURNING id",
            ("samsung", ["ue55"], "Телевизор Samsung UE55", "samsung-ue55"),
        )
        assert cur.fetchone()[0]


def test_sim_kind_rejects_unknown(db_conn):
    # variant_key() normalises "unknown" to "dual", so only two values can ever
    # reach a canonical variant. The CHECK pins that.
    with db_conn.cursor() as cur, pytest.raises(psycopg.errors.CheckViolation):
        cur.execute(INSERT_VARIANT, ("honor", ["x9d"], 12, 256, "black", "unknown",
                                     "x", "honor-x9d-12-256-black-unknown"))


def test_offer_variant_id_must_reference_a_real_variant(db_conn):
    with db_conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute("SELECT id FROM store WHERE slug = 'olcha'")
        store_id = cur.fetchone()[0]
        cur.execute(
            "INSERT INTO offer (store_id, source_key, name_raw, price, url)"
            " VALUES (%s, 'k1', 'X', 1000000, 'u') RETURNING id", (store_id,))
        offer_id = cur.fetchone()[0]
        with pytest.raises(psycopg.errors.ForeignKeyViolation):
            cur.execute("UPDATE offer SET variant_id = %s WHERE id = %s",
                        (uuid.uuid4(), offer_id))


def test_unresolved_offer_requires_a_reason(db_conn):
    with db_conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute("SELECT id FROM store WHERE slug = 'olcha'")
        store_id = cur.fetchone()[0]
        cur.execute(
            "INSERT INTO offer (store_id, source_key, name_raw, price, url)"
            " VALUES (%s, 'k2', 'X', 1000000, 'u') RETURNING id", (store_id,))
        offer_id = cur.fetchone()[0]
        with pytest.raises(psycopg.errors.CheckViolation):
            cur.execute("INSERT INTO unresolved_offer (offer_id, reason)"
                        " VALUES (%s, '')", (offer_id,))

from narxnoma.matching.brands import (
    BRAND_ALIASES, BRAND_LABELS, BRANDS, BRANDS_WITHOUT_PUBLISHED_RAM, canonical_brand,
)


def test_aliases_collapse_sub_brands():
    assert canonical_brand("iphone") == "apple"
    assert canonical_brand("redmi") == "xiaomi"
    assert canonical_brand("poco") == "xiaomi"


def test_unaliased_brand_passes_through():
    assert canonical_brand("samsung") == "samsung"
    assert canonical_brand("honor") == "honor"


def test_apple_publishes_no_ram():
    # Apple never states RAM in consumer names. This drives both the
    # phantom-RAM guard (Task 4) and key completeness (Task 7).
    assert "apple" in BRANDS_WITHOUT_PUBLISHED_RAM
    assert "samsung" not in BRANDS_WITHOUT_PUBLISHED_RAM


def test_apple_label_includes_iphone():
    # "iphone" is a NON_MODEL_TOKEN, so it never survives into model_tokens.
    # Without it in the label, display names read "Смартфон Apple 17 Pro Max".
    assert BRAND_LABELS["apple"] == "Apple iPhone"
    assert BRAND_LABELS["samsung"] == "Samsung"


def test_every_alias_target_is_a_known_brand():
    # An alias resolving to a brand no vocabulary contains is a silent dead
    # end: the token matches, canonical_brand rewrites it, and the result
    # keys nothing. APPLIANCE_BRANDS is a second recognition vocabulary --
    # kept out of BRANDS because BRANDS doubles as the PHONE crawl frontier --
    # so a target may legitimately live in either.
    from narxnoma.matching.brands import APPLIANCE_BRANDS

    from narxnoma.matching.brands import NON_PHONE_ALIASES

    known = set(BRANDS) | set(APPLIANCE_BRANDS)
    for target in {**BRAND_ALIASES, **NON_PHONE_ALIASES}.values():
        assert target in known, target


def test_every_brand_has_a_label():
    for b in BRANDS:
        assert canonical_brand(b) in BRAND_LABELS


def test_every_appliance_brand_has_a_label():
    # display_name renders brand_label(); a brand without one falls back to
    # .capitalize(), which turns "7tech" into "7Tech" by luck and "aux" into
    # "Aux" wrongly. Every entry is spelled deliberately.
    from narxnoma.matching.brands import APPLIANCE_BRAND_LABELS, APPLIANCE_BRANDS

    missing = [b for b in APPLIANCE_BRANDS if b not in APPLIANCE_BRAND_LABELS]
    assert not missing, f"appliance brands with no display label: {missing}"


def test_new_brands_are_recognised_in_real_listing_shapes():
    from narxnoma.matching import extract_features
    assert extract_features("itel A70 4/128 GB Black").brand == "itel"
    assert extract_features("Nokia 110 4G Dual SIM Blue").brand == "nokia"
    assert extract_features("OnePlus Nord 4 12/256 Green").brand == "oneplus"


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The appliance-only alias map. Separate from BRAND_ALIASES because that dict
# is probed first in the phone path's SUBSTRING scan and also feeds the phone
# crawl frontier -- see brands.py.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def test_appliance_aliases_do_not_leak_into_the_phone_path():
    """The one property that makes a second alias map worth having.

    An appliance alias in BRAND_ALIASES would be probed as a substring against
    every phone name (14,860 golden rows pin that scan) AND would spend a real
    query per cycle at three retailers, asking for a phone brand that does not
    exist.
    """
    from narxnoma.matching.brands import APPLIANCE_BRAND_ALIASES
    from narxnoma.sources.brand_queries import BRAND_QUERIES

    for alias in APPLIANCE_BRAND_ALIASES:
        assert alias not in BRAND_ALIASES, alias
        assert alias not in BRAND_QUERIES, alias
        assert canonical_brand(alias) == alias, f"{alias} resolved on the phone path"


def test_appliance_aliases_resolve_outside_smartphones():
    from narxnoma.matching.brands import canonical_non_phone_brand

    assert canonical_non_phone_brand("prm") == "premier"
    assert canonical_non_phone_brand("shiv") == "shivaki"
    assert canonical_non_phone_brand("zifler") == "ziffler"
    assert canonical_non_phone_brand("бирюса") == "biryusa"
    assert canonical_non_phone_brand("können") == "konnen"
    # The phone aliases still apply outside phones: a MacBook is an Apple.
    assert canonical_non_phone_brand("macbook") == "apple"
    assert canonical_non_phone_brand("bosch") == "bosch"


def test_the_cyrillic_spelling_of_biryusa_keys_the_same_product():
    """The bug the third brand pass found.

    "biryusa" was in the vocabulary in the LATIN spelling and its display
    label was already "Бирюса" -- but every listing writes it in Cyrillic, and
    normalize() correctly leaves an all-Cyrillic token alone. The two
    spellings never met, and 20 offers were unkeyable.
    """
    from narxnoma.matching import extract_features

    cyrillic = extract_features("Холодильник Бирюса M6133", category="fridges")
    assert cyrillic.brand == "biryusa"
    assert cyrillic.model_tokens


def test_third_pass_brands_are_recognised_in_real_listing_shapes():
    from narxnoma.matching import extract_features

    for name, category, brand in (
        ("Кондиционер Gree Clivia Inverter 24 Gold", "acs", "gree"),
        ("Холодильник-морозильник ATLANT ХМ-4621-109-ND", "fridges", "atlant"),
        ("Ноутбук CHUWI GemiBook XPro 8GB", "laptops", "chuwi"),
        ("Телевизор KÖNNEN KN100HS", "televisions", "konnen"),
        ("Konnen KN-BFNF317/SI Sovutgichi", "fridges", "konnen"),
        ("Комбинированная плита Magna FS-M604BB(I)", "ovens", "magna"),
        ("Стиральная машина SHIV-WM 1106 Sentaku - (6 кг) Серый", "washers", "shivaki"),
        ("PRM-350TFNFID/DI", "fridges", "premier"),
        ("Газовые плиты Zifler Breeze Series BGS-6031BE", "ovens", "ziffler"),
    ):
        assert extract_features(name, category=category).brand == brand, name


def test_magna_does_not_swallow_premiers_magnate_line():
    """"Кондиционер Premier PRM-12MGSPA-INV/W Magnate" is a Premier, not a
    Magna. The non-phone probe's word boundary is what keeps them apart -- a
    substring scan would read "magna" inside "Magnate"."""
    from narxnoma.matching import extract_features

    f = extract_features(
        "Кондиционер Premier PRM-12MGSPA-INV/W Magnate GMCC DC inverter", category="acs")
    assert f.brand == "premier"


def test_rivacase_stays_unrecognised_on_purpose():
    """Its listings are laptop BAGS. Leaving the brand out of the vocabulary
    is what keeps them from forming laptop variants."""
    from narxnoma.matching import extract_features

    f = extract_features("Rivacase 7531 Black Eco 15.6 Noutbuk sumkasi", category="laptops")
    assert f.brand is None

"""Category-aware identity (Plan 5): non-phone products key on
brand + model alone; phones keep the full colour/SIM/memory signature.
"""
import pytest

from narxnoma.matching.features import extract_features
from narxnoma.matching.keys import (
    CATEGORY_PREFIX,
    NON_PHONE_CATEGORIES,
    display_name,
    slug,
    variant_key,
)


def _tv_key():
    return variant_key(extract_features("Телевизор Samsung UE55 55\" Black"), "dual", "televisions")


def test_non_phone_keys_on_brand_and_model_alone():
    # A TV's colour and diagonal are not identity: two titles that differ only
    # in colour/capacity must produce the SAME key (one product, many offers).
    k1 = variant_key(extract_features("Телевизор Samsung UE55 55\" Black"), "dual", "televisions")
    k2 = variant_key(extract_features("Телевизор Samsung UE55 55\" Silver"), "dual", "televisions")
    assert k1 is not None and k2 is not None
    assert k1 == k2
    assert k1.color is None and k1.sim_kind is None
    assert k1.category == "televisions"


def test_non_phone_does_not_require_ram_or_storage():
    # A fridge has no RAM and no storage; it must still be keyable.
    k = variant_key(
        extract_features("Холодильник Samsung RB34T 300 лт"), "dual", "fridges"
    )
    assert k is not None
    assert k.ram_gb is None and k.storage_gb is None


def test_non_phone_requires_brand_and_model():
    assert variant_key(extract_features("Телевизор 55\" 4K"), "dual", "televisions") is None


def test_all_non_phone_categories_have_a_display_prefix():
    assert set(CATEGORY_PREFIX) == NON_PHONE_CATEGORIES | {"smartphones"}
    for c in NON_PHONE_CATEGORIES:
        assert CATEGORY_PREFIX[c]


def test_non_phone_display_name_and_slug():
    k = _tv_key()
    assert k is not None
    assert display_name(k).startswith("Телевизор")
    assert slug(k).startswith("televisions-")


def test_phone_key_and_slug_unchanged():
    k = variant_key(extract_features("Смартфон Honor X9D 12/256 ГБ, Черный"), "dual")
    assert k is not None
    assert k.category == "smartphones"
    assert display_name(k) == "Смартфон Honor X9D 12/256 ГБ, Черный"
    assert slug(k) == "honor-x9d-12-256-black"


def test_invalid_category_rejected():
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        variant_key(extract_features("X Y"), "dual", "toasters")

"""Category flows from an offer row through identification (Plan 5)."""
from narxnoma.pipeline.extract import identify


def test_identify_uses_offer_category_for_non_phone():
    idn = identify(
        {
            "id": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001",
            "name_raw": 'Телевизор Samsung UE55 55" Black',
            "category": "televisions",
        }
    )
    assert idn.key is not None
    assert idn.key.category == "televisions"
    assert idn.key.color is None and idn.key.sim_kind is None


def test_identify_defaults_to_smartphones():
    # Offers written before the category column existed carry no category.
    idn = identify(
        {
            "id": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000002",
            "name_raw": "Смартфон Honor X9D 12/256 ГБ, Черный",
        }
    )
    assert idn.key is not None
    assert idn.key.category == "smartphones"
    assert idn.key.color == "black"

FILE: narxnoma-crawler/tests/matching/test_colors.py
