from narxnoma.matching.colors import COLOR_MAP, QUALIFIERS, colors_in_order, primary_color


def test_english_base_words():
    assert colors_in_order(["midnight", "black"]) == ["black", "black"]
    assert primary_color(["glacier", "blue"]) == "blue"


def test_primary_colour_is_the_last_mapped_token():
    # "Space Black" -> {gray, black}; the base colour is the final word.
    assert primary_color(["space", "black"]) == "black"
    assert primary_color(["desert", "gold"]) == "gold"


def test_russian_vocabulary():
    assert primary_color(["темно", "серый"]) == "gray"
    assert primary_color(["серебряный"]) == "silver"


def test_uzbek_vocabulary():
    # uzum serves uz-language card/model strings; unresolvable colours reject,
    # so every missing word here was a silent miss. See parsers/uzum.md section 8.
    assert primary_color(["kumush"]) == "silver"
    assert primary_color(["tilla"]) == "gold"
    assert primary_color(["yashil"]) == "green"
    assert primary_color(["muz"]) == "blue"
    assert primary_color(["qora"]) == "black"


def test_qualifiers_are_never_colours():
    # "Velvet Grey" -> {black, gray} would pool Black sellers into a Grey median.
    for q in ["velvet", "light", "dark", "golden", "темно", "светло", "меланж"]:
        assert q not in COLOR_MAP, f"{q} must not map to a colour"
        assert q in QUALIFIERS


def test_rang_is_not_a_colour():
    # Uzbek "Kumush rang" = "silver colour"; 'rang' is the word "colour".
    assert "rang" not in COLOR_MAP


def test_no_colour_returns_none():
    assert primary_color(["samsung", "galaxy"]) is None
    assert colors_in_order(["samsung"]) == []


def test_graphite_is_gray_not_black():
    # Corpus: "Redmi Pad Pro 6/128 Graphite Gray", "Galaxy A56 5G 8/256 GB
    # Graphite". While graphite mapped to black, "Graphite Gray" produced
    # {black, gray} and falsely intersected genuine Black listings.
    resolved = set(colors_in_order(["graphite", "gray"]))
    assert "black" not in resolved
    assert resolved == {"gray"}
    assert primary_color(["graphite", "gray"]) == "gray"


def test_cobalt_is_a_qualifier_not_blue_or_purple():
    # Corpus: all 17 occurrences are the compound "Cobalt Violet" (Galaxy
    # S26 family); cobalt never appears standalone. Remapping it to blue
    # (as one review suggested) would yield {blue, purple} and false-match
    # Blue listings, so it must be a qualifier, not a colour.
    resolved = set(colors_in_order(["cobalt", "violet"]))
    assert "blue" not in resolved
    assert resolved == {"purple"}
    assert "cobalt" in QUALIFIERS
    assert "cobalt" not in COLOR_MAP


def test_zolotistiy_maps_but_golden_does_not():
    # Corpus: all 10 occurrences of "золотистый" are standalone ("Honor X9D
    # 12/256 GB, золотистый"), while all 7 occurrences of "golden" are
    # compounds ("Golden White", "Golden Black"). The two are deliberately
    # classified differently: золотистый is a base colour, golden is a
    # shading qualifier.
    assert COLOR_MAP["золотистый"] == "gold"
    assert "golden" not in COLOR_MAP
    assert "golden" in QUALIFIERS


def test_qualifiers_and_color_map_are_disjoint():
    # Invariant, not a spot check. A word in both would be mapped to a colour
    # by colors_in_order AND skipped as a qualifier by feature extraction, so
    # "Velvet Grey"-style compounds would resolve to two colours and falsely
    # intersect a listing of the shading word's colour.
    overlap = set(QUALIFIERS) & set(COLOR_MAP)
    assert not overlap, f"words classified both ways: {sorted(overlap)}"

from narxnoma.matching import features as features_module
from narxnoma.matching.features import Features, extract_features


def test_brand_aliases():
    assert extract_features("iPhone 17 Pro 256GB").brand == "apple"
    assert extract_features("Redmi Note 15 8/256").brand == "xiaomi"
    assert extract_features("POCO X8 Pro 8/256").brand == "xiaomi"
    assert extract_features("Honor X9d 12/256").brand == "honor"


def test_model_tokens_keep_model_numbers():
    f = extract_features("Смартфон Samsung Galaxy A17 6/128 ГБ, чёрный")
    assert "a17" in f.model_tokens
    assert f.ram_gb == 6 and f.storage_gb == 128
    assert f.primary_color == "black"


def test_air_fe_se_are_model_modifiers():
    # Without "air", an iPhone Air target carries NO model token at all,
    # and matches every other iPhone.
    assert "air" in extract_features("Apple iPhone Air 256 ГБ, Space Black").model_tokens
    assert "fe" in extract_features("Samsung Galaxy S25 FE 8/128 Navy").model_tokens


def test_pro_and_max_are_both_kept():
    f = extract_features("iPhone 17 Pro Max 256 ГБ, Silver")
    assert {"pro", "max"} <= f.model_tokens


def test_sku_codes_are_not_model_tokens():
    # idea appends part numbers ("SM-A376EZADSOZ"); mediapark lists
    # "SAMSUNG SM-A075F A07". Real designators are <= 4 chars.
    f = extract_features("SAMSUNG SM-A075F A07 4/64")
    assert "a07" in f.model_tokens
    assert not any(len(t) >= 5 and any(c.isdigit() for c in t) for t in f.model_tokens)


def test_sku_min_len_is_measured_not_guessed():
    """Pin the threshold at 5, because raising it measurably hurts.

    Across all 14,860 golden rows, accept/reject agreement is 99.993% at 5 and
    99.987% at 6, 7, 8 and with the rule disabled entirely. Raising it is
    strictly worse, and the reason is visible in the two assertions below: at 6,
    five-character spec fragments survive as model tokens and then reject
    otherwise-valid candidates that simply do not repeat the marketing blurb.

    If you are here because you want to rescue "reno15" or "magic8", changing
    this number is not the fix -- see test_known_gap_real_designators_of_five_plus.
    """
    assert features_module._SKU_MIN_LEN == 5


def test_spec_blurb_fragments_never_become_model_tokens():
    # uzum card titles are marketing copy: '6.7" AMOLED 120Hz, 200Мп, 6500 мАч'.
    # If any of these became a model token, every candidate that omitted the
    # blurb -- which is most of them -- would be rejected for "missing" it.
    f = extract_features("Смартфон Xiaomi Redmi Note 15 Pro 8/256 120Hz 200MP 6500mAh, чёрный")
    for junk in ("120hz", "200mp", "6500mah"):
        assert junk not in f.model_tokens
    assert {"15", "note", "pro", "redmi"} <= f.model_tokens


def test_short_designators_still_survive():
    # The rule must not become so aggressive that it eats identity. These are
    # the tokens the whole matcher keys on.
    for name, token in [
        ("Samsung Galaxy A17 6/128 Black", "a17"),
        ("Honor X9d 12/256 Black", "x9d"),
        ("Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra 12/256 Black", "s26"),
        ("Vivo Y31d 4/128 Black", "y31d"),
    ]:
        assert token in extract_features(name).model_tokens, name


def test_known_gap_real_designators_of_five_plus():
    """Document, rather than hide, what this rule costs.

    Length cannot separate real designators from catalogue codes -- they
    overlap. In the corpus, length 5 holds both 'fold4'/'pro12' and
    '120hz'/'200mp'; length 6 holds both 'magic8' and 'mg3730'/'bt7510'.

    So these products are currently unkeyable, and that is a real gap, not a
    detail. Fixing it needs a targeted designator allowlist applied BEFORE the
    SKU rule, plus OPPO and Honor fixtures to measure against -- the golden
    corpus contains zero 'reno*' tokens and only 26 OPPO rows, so there is
    nothing here to tune with. This test exists so the gap fails loudly the day
    someone adds that allowlist, rather than lingering undocumented.
    """
    for name, lost in [
        ("OPPO Reno15 5G 12/512GB Aurora White", "reno15"),
        ("Honor Magic8 Pro 12/512 Black", "magic8"),
    ]:
        assert lost not in extract_features(name).model_tokens, (
            f"{lost!r} is now kept -- if that was deliberate, update this test "
            f"and re-measure agreement across the golden corpus"
        )


def test_galaxy_is_not_required():
    # mediapark lists the A07 with no "Galaxy" at all.
    assert "galaxy" not in extract_features("Samsung Galaxy A17 6/128").model_tokens


def test_memory_figures_never_become_model_tokens():
    f = extract_features("Honor X9d 12/256 GB Black")
    assert "12" not in f.model_tokens
    assert "256" not in f.model_tokens


def test_bands_are_reserved_not_model_tokens():
    f = extract_features("Samsung Galaxy A27 5G 8/256 ГБ, Черный")
    assert "5g" not in f.model_tokens


def test_unmappable_colour_yields_no_colour():
    # "Конфетный" is not in COLOR_MAP, so no colour resolves. score_match
    # then hard-rejects it for any colour-bearing target rather than letting
    # it act as a wildcard.
    f = extract_features("Смартфон Redmi 15 8/256 Конфетный")
    assert f.primary_color is None
    assert f.colors == frozenset()


def test_qualifier_does_not_hide_the_base_colour():
    # "Velvet Grey": 'velvet' is a QUALIFIER and must not map, but 'grey' must.
    g = extract_features("Смартфон Honor X8D 8/256 Velvet Grey")
    assert g.primary_color == "gray"


def test_features_are_hashable_and_frozen():
    f = extract_features("Honor X9d 12/256 GB Black")
    assert isinstance(f, Features)
    hash(f)

FILE: narxnoma-crawler/tests/matching/test_golden.py
================================================
import json
import pathlib


from narxnoma.matching import ACCEPT_THRESHOLD, extract_features, score_match

GOLDEN = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "fixtures" / "golden"

# Agreement floor. The corpus was generated by the same algorithm, so a
# correct implementation reproduces it almost exactly; the small allowance
# absorbs deliberate improvements (e.g. a widened colour vocabulary that
# ACCEPTS rows previously rejected).
MIN_AGREEMENT = 0.99

# A ratio floor this loose cannot see a real regression. Raising _SKU_MIN_LEN
# from 5 to 6 doubled the disagreements (1 -> 2) and still cleared 0.99 easily,
# so this suite would have waved through a change measured to make matching
# worse. The count is the sensitive instrument; pin it.
#
# Raise this ONLY alongside a measurement showing the new disagreements are
# deliberate improvements, and say which rows they are. Never raise it to make
# a failing run pass.
MAX_DISAGREEMENTS = 1


def _rows():
    for path in sorted(GOLDEN.glob("audit_*.json")):
        target_name = json.loads(
            (GOLDEN / "targets.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        )[int(path.stem.split("_")[1]) - 1]["name"]
        for row in json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")):
            yield target_name, row


def test_corpus_is_present_and_large():
    rows = list(_rows())
    assert len(rows) > 14000, f"expected the full corpus, got {len(rows)}"


def test_accept_reject_agreement_against_golden():
    disagreements = []
    total = 0
    for target_name, row in _rows():
        total += 1
        t = extract_features(target_name)
        c = extract_features(row["name"])
        ours_accepts = score_match(t, c) >= ACCEPT_THRESHOLD
        theirs_accepts = row["score"] >= ACCEPT_THRESHOLD
        if ours_accepts != theirs_accepts:
            disagreements.append((target_name, row["name"], row["why"], ours_accepts))

    agreement = 1 - len(disagreements) / total
    sample = "\n".join(
        f"  target={t[:44]!r} cand={c[:44]!r} golden_why={w!r} ours_accepts={o}"
        for t, c, w, o in disagreements[:15]
    )
    assert agreement >= MIN_AGREEMENT, (
        f"agreement {agreement:.4f} < {MIN_AGREEMENT} "
        f"({len(disagreements)} of {total} disagree)\n{sample}"
    )
    # The count catches what the ratio cannot: see MAX_DISAGREEMENTS above.
    assert len(disagreements) <= MAX_DISAGREEMENTS, (
        f"{len(disagreements)} disagreements, expected at most "
        f"{MAX_DISAGREEMENTS}. Agreement is still {agreement:.5f}, which is why "
        f"the ratio floor did not catch this.\n{sample}"
    )


def test_no_accepted_row_has_wrong_storage():
    """An accepted match must never disagree on storage. Invariant, not a ratio."""
    for target_name, row in _rows():
        t = extract_features(target_name)
        c = extract_features(row["name"])
        if score_match(t, c) >= ACCEPT_THRESHOLD:
            if t.storage_gb and c.storage_gb:
                assert t.storage_gb == c.storage_gb, (
                    f"accepted {row['name']!r} for {target_name!r} "
                    f"with storage {c.storage_gb} != {t.storage_gb}"
                )


def test_no_accepted_row_has_wrong_colour():
    """Colour is a hard identity field. Invariant."""
    for target_name, row in _rows():
        t = extract_features(target_name)
        c = extract_features(row["name"])
        if score_match(t, c) >= ACCEPT_THRESHOLD and t.colors:
            assert t.colors & c.colors, (
                f"accepted {row['name']!r} for {target_name!r} "
                f"with colours {sorted(c.colors)} vs {sorted(t.colors)}"
            )

from dataclasses import replace

from narxnoma.matching import VariantKey
from narxnoma.matching.features import extract_features as F
from narxnoma.matching.keys import (
    display_name, partial_key, resolve_partial, slug, variant_key,
)


def k(name, sim_kind="dual"):
    return variant_key(F(name), sim_kind)


def test_full_key_from_complete_listing():
    key = k("Смартфон Honor X9d 12/256 ГБ, черный")
    assert key.brand == "honor"
    assert key.ram_gb == 12 and key.storage_gb == 256
    assert key.color == "black"
    assert key.sim_kind == "dual"


def test_key_is_none_when_identity_incomplete():
    # No storage at all -> cannot be a canonical variant.
    assert variant_key(F("Чехол для Honor X9d"), "dual") is None
    # No colour -> colour is a hard identity field.
    assert variant_key(F("Honor X9d 12/256 GB"), "dual") is None


def test_apple_key_is_complete_without_ram():
    # Apple never publishes RAM and extract_memory refuses to infer it.
    # If RAM were required, NO iPhone could ever be keyed.
    key = k("Смартфон Apple iPhone 17 Pro Max 256 ГБ, Silver")
    assert key is not None
    assert key.ram_gb is None
    assert key.storage_gb == 256


def test_non_apple_key_still_requires_ram():
    assert variant_key(F("Samsung Galaxy A17 128GB Blue"), "dual") is None


def test_equal_keys_for_differently_worded_same_phone():
    a = k("Смартфон Honor X9d 12/256 ГБ, черный")
    b = k("Honor X9d 12/256 GB Midnight Black")
    assert a == b
    assert hash(a) == hash(b)


def test_case_and_punctuation_do_not_create_duplicates():
    # uzprice has "Cosmic orange" and "Cosmic Orange" as two products.
    a = k("Смартфон Apple iPhone 17 Pro Max 256 ГБ, Cosmic orange")
    b = k("Смартфон Apple iPhone 17 Pro Max 256 ГБ, Cosmic Orange")
    assert a == b


def test_esim_only_is_a_different_variant():
    dual = k("Смартфон Apple iPhone 17 Pro Max 256 ГБ, Silver", "dual")
    esim = k("Смартфон Apple iPhone 17 Pro Max 256 ГБ, Silver", "esim_only")
    assert dual != esim


def test_partial_key_resolves_when_exactly_one_candidate_matches():
    full = [k("Redmi Note 15 8/256 ГБ, черный")]
    p = partial_key(F("Redmi Note 15 256GB Black"), "dual")
    assert p.ram_gb is None
    assert resolve_partial(p, full) == full[0]


def test_partial_key_REFUSES_when_ambiguous():
    # THE RULE: both 8/256 and 12/256 exist, so a listing with no RAM is
    # genuinely ambiguous. uzprice attaches it anyway and lets it set the
    # headline price. We refuse.
    full = [
        k("Redmi Note 15 8/256 ГБ, черный"),
        k("Redmi Note 15 12/256 ГБ, черный"),
    ]
    p = partial_key(F("Redmi Note 15 256GB Black"), "dual")
    assert resolve_partial(p, full) is None


def test_partial_key_refuses_when_nothing_matches():
    full = [k("Redmi Note 15 8/256 ГБ, черный")]
    p = partial_key(F("Galaxy A17 128GB Blue"), "dual")
    assert resolve_partial(p, full) is None


def test_display_name_is_generated_not_copied():
    key = k("HONOR   x9d 12/256gb   midnight black")
    assert display_name(key) == "Смартфон Honor X9D 12/256 ГБ, Черный"


def test_display_name_orders_modifiers_not_alphabetically():
    # sorted() would give "17 Max Pro". Pro precedes Max in every real name.
    key = k("Смартфон Apple iPhone 17 Pro Max 256 ГБ, Silver")
    assert display_name(key) == "Смартфон Apple iPhone 17 Pro Max 256 ГБ, Серебристый"


def test_display_name_puts_family_prefix_first():
    # sorted() would give "15 Note Redmi".
    key = k("Смартфон Xiaomi Redmi Note 15 8/256 ГБ, чёрный")
    assert display_name(key) == "Смартфон Xiaomi Redmi Note 15 8/256 ГБ, Черный"


def test_display_name_uppercases_initialisms():
    # sorted() would give "Fe S25".
    key = k("Samsung Galaxy S25 FE 8/128 Navy")
    assert display_name(key) == "Смартфон Samsung S25 FE 8/128 ГБ, Синий"


def test_slug_is_deterministic_and_url_safe():
    a = k("Смартфон Honor X9d 12/256 ГБ, черный")
    b = k("Honor X9d 12/256 GB Midnight Black")
    assert slug(a) == slug(b)
    assert slug(a) == "honor-x9d-12-256-black"


def test_slug_omits_ram_when_the_brand_has_none():
    assert slug(k("Смартфон Apple iPhone 17 Pro Max 256 ГБ, Silver")) == \
        "apple-17-pro-max-256-silver"


def test_esim_only_slug_is_distinct():
    dual = slug(k("Смартфон Apple iPhone 17 Pro 256 ГБ, Silver", "dual"))
    esim = slug(k("Смартфон Apple iPhone 17 Pro 256 ГБ, Silver", "esim_only"))
    assert dual != esim
    assert esim.endswith("-esim")


def test_fold_and_flip_are_different_products():
    # THE MERGE: "fold"/"flip" were neither digit-bearing nor in
    # MODEL_MODIFIERS, so both names reduced to model_tokens={'7'} and
    # collapsed onto the identical key samsung-7-12-256-black, scoring 60
    # with why() == "OK". A Fold costs roughly twice a Flip.
    fold = k("Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 7 Black 12/256")
    flip = k("Samsung Galaxy Z Flip 7 Black 12/256")
    assert fold is not None and flip is not None
    assert fold != flip
    assert slug(fold) != slug(flip)


def test_unknown_sim_normalises_to_dual():
    # slug() was not injective: sim_kind "unknown" and "dual" built different
    # VariantKeys but identical slugs, so two keys claimed one URL.
    # uzum.md §6 documents eSIM-only variants as ALWAYS explicitly marked (in
    # three encodings), so an unmarked phone is the ordinary dual-SIM one.
    f = F("Смартфон Apple iPhone 17 Pro Max 256 ГБ, Silver")
    assert variant_key(f, "unknown") == variant_key(f, "dual")
    assert variant_key(f, "unknown").sim_kind == "dual"
    # esim_only stays distinct, and keeps its slug suffix.
    assert variant_key(f, "esim_only") != variant_key(f, "dual")
    assert slug(variant_key(f, "esim_only")).endswith("-esim")


def test_invalid_sim_kind_is_rejected():
    # SIM_KINDS was declared but never enforced, so any string became part of
    # a canonical identity -- a typo ("Dual", "dual_sim") would silently mint
    # a second canonical product for a phone that already had one.
    f = F("Смартфон Honor X9d 12/256 ГБ, черный")
    for bad in ["Dual", "dual_sim", "", "esim"]:
        try:
            variant_key(f, bad)
        except ValueError:
            continue
        raise AssertionError(f"variant_key accepted invalid sim_kind {bad!r}")


def test_display_name_distinguishes_an_esim_only_variant():
    """sim_kind is part of the key, so it must be part of the NAME.

    slug() appends "esim" and display_name() did not, so an eSIM-only phone
    and its dual-SIM sibling -- genuinely different products at genuinely
    different prices -- rendered byte-identical. Live, that produced 42 pairs
    of variants a user could not tell apart, including
    'Смартфон Apple iPhone 17 Pro 256 ГБ, Оранжевый' twice at 16,985,000 and
    17,690,000.

    Generated names are supposed to make duplicates structurally impossible;
    a generator that drops a key field reintroduces exactly the confusion it
    exists to prevent.
    """
    dual = VariantKey(brand="apple", model_tokens=frozenset({"17", "pro"}),
                      ram_gb=None, storage_gb=256, color="orange", sim_kind="dual")
    esim = replace(dual, sim_kind="esim_only")

    assert display_name(dual) == "Смартфон Apple iPhone 17 Pro 256 ГБ, Оранжевый"
    assert display_name(esim) != display_name(dual)
    assert "eSIM" in display_name(esim)


def test_no_two_distinct_keys_share_a_display_name():
    """The invariant behind the test above, stated directly: if two keys
    differ at all, their generated names must differ too.
    """
    base = VariantKey(brand="apple", model_tokens=frozenset({"17", "pro"}),
                      ram_gb=None, storage_gb=256, color="orange", sim_kind="dual")
    variations = [
        base,
        replace(base, sim_kind="esim_only"),
        replace(base, storage_gb=512),
        replace(base, color="blue"),
        replace(base, model_tokens=frozenset({"17", "pro", "max"})),
        replace(base, ram_gb=12),
    ]
    names = [display_name(k) for k in variations]
    assert len(set(names)) == len(names), f"collision among {names}"

from narxnoma.matching.memory import extract_memory
from narxnoma.matching.normalize import normalize


def mem(raw, brand=None):
    return extract_memory(raw, normalize(raw), brand)


def test_collects_all_unit_bearing_figures():
    # A re.search for the FIRST unit match returns 8 -> storage=8 -> every
    # such listing rejected. This killed all Honor 600 matches on uzum.
    assert mem("Honor 600 8ГБ/256ГБ") == (8, 256)
    assert mem("Xiaomi 12GB+512GB") == (12, 512)


def test_terabytes_convert_to_gb():
    assert mem("iPhone 17 Pro Max 1 ТБ", brand="apple") == (None, 1024)


def test_lookbehind_stops_model_being_read_as_memory():
    # Without the lookbehind, "Samsung Galaxy A17 128GB" parses the pair
    # "17 128" and yields ram=17.
    ram, storage = mem("Samsung Galaxy A17 128GB", brand="samsung")
    assert storage == 128
    assert ram != 17


def test_bare_pair_is_ram_and_storage_for_non_apple():
    assert mem("Samsung Galaxy A17 6 128", brand="samsung") == (6, 128)


def test_slash_pair_is_ram_and_storage():
    assert mem("Honor X9d 12/256 GB", brand="honor") == (12, 256)


def test_apple_bare_pair_is_NOT_ram():
    # THE BUG: "iPhone 16 256 GB" has the same shape as "12/256 GB".
    # Reading 16 as RAM moved it into reserved_nums, deleting the model
    # number from model_tokens, so iPhone 16 / 17 / Air all matched.
    # Apple never publishes RAM in consumer names.
    assert mem("Apple iPhone 16 256 GB Black", brand="apple") == (None, 256)
    assert mem("Apple iPhone 17 256 ГБ", brand="apple") == (None, 256)


def test_apple_WITH_separator_STILL_yields_no_ram():
    # SUPERSEDED behaviour. This test previously asserted (12, 256): an
    # explicit separator was taken as proof that a figure really was RAM,
    # even for Apple. That exemption is exactly what split one phone into two
    # canonical products, so Apple RAM suppression is now global and this
    # listing must yield no RAM at all. The storage reading is unchanged.
    assert mem("Iphone Air Space Black 12/256 GB", brand="apple") == (None, 256)


def test_single_unit_figure_classified_by_size():
    assert mem("Redmi A5 64GB") == (None, 64)
    assert mem("некий товар 8 GB") == (8, None)


def test_no_memory_at_all():
    assert mem("Чехол для iPhone 17", brand="apple") == (None, None)


def test_samsung_model_number_is_not_read_as_ram_fold():
    # Real listing: "Смартфон Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 7 512 ГБ Jet Black".
    # The model number 7 has the same "small int + big int" shape as a
    # bare RAM/storage pair. Samsung publishes RAM, so it isn't covered by
    # BRANDS_WITHOUT_PUBLISHED_RAM -- the plausibility set is what stops it.
    assert mem("Смартфон Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 7 512 ГБ Jet Black", brand="samsung") == (
        None,
        512,
    )


def test_samsung_model_number_is_not_read_as_ram_flip():
    # Real listing: "Смартфон Samsung Galaxy Z Flip 7 256 ГБ Jet Black".
    assert mem("Смартфон Samsung Galaxy Z Flip 7 256 ГБ Jet Black", brand="samsung") == (
        None,
        256,
    )


def test_scans_past_implausible_pair_to_find_real_memory():
    # Real listing: "Redmi A7 Pro smartfoni 6.9\" 120Hz 6000 mAh 13MP AI
    # 4/128 Qora". The marketing blurb contains "9 120" (from 6.9" and
    # 120Hz), which has the shape of a memory pair but isn't one; scanning
    # must skip it and find the real "4/128" pair.
    assert mem(
        'Redmi A7 Pro smartfoni 6.9" 120Hz 6000 mAh 13MP AI 4/128 Qora',
        brand="xiaomi",
    ) == (4, 128)


def test_watch_size_is_not_plausible_storage():
    # Real listing: "Samsung Galaxy Watch 5 44mm Graphite". 44 is not a
    # plausible storage size, so neither RAM nor storage should be read.
    assert mem("Samsung Galaxy Watch 5 44mm Graphite", brand="samsung") == (None, None)


def test_explicit_unit_case_still_works():
    assert mem("Honor 600 8ГБ/256ГБ") == (8, 256)


def test_two_digit_ram_after_two_digit_model_number():
    # Real listing: "Redmi Note 15 12/256 ГБ, черный". normalize() turns
    # this into "redmi note 15 12 256 гб черный" -- the model number "15"
    # sits directly before the RAM "12", so a non-overlapping scan finds
    # only ("15", "12"), which is correctly rejected as implausible
    # storage, and never backtracks to see the real ("12", "256") pair.
    assert mem("Redmi Note 15 12/256 ГБ, черный", brand="xiaomi") == (12, 256)


def test_two_digit_ram_after_two_digit_model_number_16():
    # Real listing: "Redmi Note 15 16/512 ГБ". Same trap as above with a
    # different RAM size, confirming the fix isn't specific to "12".
    assert mem("Redmi Note 15 16/512 ГБ", brand="xiaomi") == (16, 512)


def test_single_digit_ram_after_model_number_still_works():
    # Real listing: "Redmi Note 15 8/256 ГБ, черный". The single-digit RAM
    # case always worked (a 1-digit run can't be misread as a 2-4 digit
    # storage figure), so this pins the pre-fix behaviour against regression.
    assert mem("Redmi Note 15 8/256 ГБ, черный", brand="xiaomi") == (8, 256)


def test_apple_unit_bearing_pair_yields_no_ram():
    # THE SPLIT: the BRANDS_WITHOUT_PUBLISHED_RAM guard used to sit only on
    # the bare-pair fallback, so "12/256GB" reached the unit-bearing pass
    # untouched and returned ram=12, while "iPhone 17 Pro 256 ГБ" returned
    # None. One phone, two canonical products (apple-17-pro-12-256-silver and
    # apple-17-pro-256-silver): a split offer pool and two displayed prices.
    # Apple publishes no RAM, so any such figure is a reseller's own wording.
    assert mem("iPhone 17 Pro 12/256GB Silver", brand="apple") == (None, 256)


def test_non_apple_unit_bearing_pair_still_reads_ram():
    # The suppression must be brand-scoped, not blanket: brands that DO
    # publish RAM keep it as identity, or 8/256 and 12/256 would merge.
    assert mem("Honor X9d 12/256GB Black", brand="honor") == (12, 256)


def test_a_lone_bare_figure_is_read_as_storage():
    # THE GAP: every rule above needs either a UNIT ("256 GB") or a second
    # adjacent figure ("12 256"). A storage figure standing alone with
    # neither was read as nothing at all, so the listing became unkeyable.
    #
    # That is not a rare shape. uzum states memory in a per-SKU
    # characteristic whose value is frequently the bare figure -- Память:
    # "128" -- and the resulting name "Apple iPhone 12 pro 128 Синий" has no
    # unit and no adjacent number. It yielded storage=None while
    # 'Apple iPhone 12 128 Алый' yielded 128, purely because the model
    # number happened to sit next to the memory figure in the second one.
    assert mem("Apple iPhone 12 pro 128 Синий", brand="apple") == (None, 128)
    assert mem("IPhone 17 Pro Max 512 Серебряный", brand="apple") == (None, 512)


def test_a_lone_bare_figure_must_be_a_plausible_storage_size():
    # A lone figure is far weaker evidence than a pair, so it is admitted
    # only from the plausible-storage set. A model number ("Honor 200",
    # "Nokia 105") must never be mistaken for a capacity.
    assert mem("Honor 200 Pro", brand="honor") == (None, None)
    assert mem("Смартфон Nokia 105", brand=None) == (None, None)


def test_a_lone_bare_figure_followed_by_another_unit_is_not_storage():
    # "64 МП" is a camera, "120 Гц" a refresh rate. Both are plausible
    # storage NUMBERS sitting in a marketing blurb, and the lone-figure rule
    # is the one rule loose enough to swallow them.
    assert mem("Redmi Note 14 Pro 64 МП камера", brand="xiaomi") == (None, None)
    assert mem("Realme C75 128 mp AI", brand="realme") == (None, None)


def test_a_real_pair_still_wins_over_a_lone_figure():
    # The lone-figure rule is a LAST resort: it may only run when every
    # stronger rule has already declined. "8/256" must not be overridden by
    # the bare "64" that follows it.
    assert mem("Poco X7 8/256 ГБ 64 МП", brand="xiaomi") == (8, 256)

FILE: narxnoma-crawler/tests/matching/test_non_phone_identity.py

"""Non-phone identity: the rules a television needs and a phone must not get.

Every listing quoted here is REAL -- taken from the live catalogue during the
measurement that motivated this module. Under the phone-only extractor, 75% of
2,076 harvested non-phone offers produced no key at all and never reached the
site; the cases below are the mechanisms behind that.
"""
import pytest

from narxnoma.matching.brands import brand_label
from narxnoma.matching.categories import (
    is_accessory,
    is_model_token,
    ordered_non_phone_tokens,
)
from narxnoma.matching.features import extract_features
from narxnoma.matching.keys import display_name, variant_key
from narxnoma.matching.normalize import normalize
from narxnoma.pipeline.cluster import is_wellformed


# --- the catalogue code IS the identity -------------------------------------

@pytest.mark.parametrize("name,category", [
    ("Телевизор Samsung UE55DU7100UXUZ", "televisions"),
    ("Холодильник Samsung RT47CG6442B1WT", "fridges"),
    ("Духовой шкаф Samsung NV68A1145RS/WT", "ovens"),
    ("Стиральная машина Samsung WW60AG4S00CELD, белый", "washers"),
    ("Кондиционер TCL TAC-CT12INV/RIF, белый", "acs"),
])
def test_appliance_model_code_survives_as_identity(name, category):
    # The phone extractor discards mixed letter+digit tokens of 5+ characters
    # as catalogue noise. For an appliance that token is the whole name, and
    # discarding it made 100% of ovens unkeyable.
    f = extract_features(name, category)
    assert f.brand == "samsung" if "Samsung" in name else f.brand is not None
    assert f.model_tokens, f"{name} yielded no model tokens"
    assert variant_key(f, "dual", category) is not None


def test_phone_still_discards_sku_codes():
    # The same input under the phone rules must be unchanged: "a075f" is a
    # catalogue code and "a07" is the identity.
    f = extract_features("SAMSUNG SM-A075F A07 4/64 Black")
    assert "a075f" not in f.model_tokens
    assert "a07" in f.model_tokens


# --- brand vocabulary --------------------------------------------------------

@pytest.mark.parametrize("name,category,brand", [
    ("Телевизор Artel SMART A32PHCH010 Google tv HD", "televisions", "artel"),
    ("Ноутбук Lenovo ThinkPad T14 Gen 4 21HD0077US", "laptops", "lenovo"),
    ("Ноутбук HP EliteBook 14", "laptops", "hp"),
    ("Ноутбук Hp15-fd0043nq i3-1315U", "laptops", "hp"),
    ("Холодильник Bosch KGN56CX30U", "fridges", "bosch"),
    ("Кондиционер LG Dual Cool Inverter I24CGH", "acs", "lg"),
    ("Газовая плита PRЕMIER Eco BT60F-40VW", "ovens", "premier"),
    ("MacBook Air 13-inch M4 16/256GB Silver", "laptops", "apple"),
])
def test_appliance_brands_are_recognised(name, category, brand):
    assert extract_features(name, category).brand == brand


@pytest.mark.parametrize("name", [
    "Ноутбук Acer Aspire зарядное устройство charger",   # "arg" inside "charger"
    "Телевизор большой large screen",                     # "arg" inside "large"
])
def test_short_brand_names_are_not_matched_as_substrings(name):
    # The appliance vocabulary contains "arg", "lg" and "hp". A substring scan
    # -- which is what the phone path does -- finds "arg" inside "charger" and
    # "large", inventing a manufacturer out of an adjective.
    assert extract_features(name, "laptops").brand != "arg"


# --- vocabulary is the precision instrument ---------------------------------

def test_marketing_words_never_split_one_product_in_two():
    a = extract_features("Телевизор Artel UA43H3502 Android TV", "televisions")
    b = extract_features("Телевизор Artel UA43H3502", "televisions")
    assert a.model_tokens == b.model_tokens
    assert variant_key(a, "dual", "televisions") == variant_key(b, "dual", "televisions")


def test_descriptors_never_split_one_product_in_two():
    a = extract_features("Двухкамерный холодильник Artel HD455", "fridges")
    b = extract_features("Холодильник Artel HD455", "fridges")
    assert variant_key(a, "dual", "fridges") == variant_key(b, "dual", "fridges")


def test_a_cpu_word_is_a_spec_on_a_laptop_and_a_name_on_an_air_conditioner():
    """Measured across all 5,132 non-laptop non-phone offers: 8 carry a
    PROCESSORS word, and every one is an air conditioner whose product LINE
    collides with a chip. cut_at_processor truncates positionally, so
    "Rulls ARC 12" lost its capacity as well as its name and could form no
    key at all -- 6 offers across uzum and alifshop, all unresolved."""
    ac = extract_features("Кондиционер Rulls ARC 12 Inverter", category="acs")
    assert ac.brand == "rulls"
    assert "arc" in ac.model_tokens and "12" in ac.model_tokens

    sitronic = extract_features("Кондиционер Sitronic Vega Inverter 18", category="acs")
    assert sitronic.brand == "sitronic"
    assert "vega" in sitronic.model_tokens

    # And the laptop rule is untouched: a CPU still ends the name there.
    laptop = extract_features(
        "Ноутбук Acer Aspire Snapdragon X1 26100", category="laptops")
    assert laptop.model_tokens == frozenset({"aspire"})


def test_two_air_conditioners_of_one_line_do_not_merge():
    """Why the CPU stoplist could not simply be dropped for acs: with "vega"
    stripped but the capacity kept, every Sitronic 18 would key alike."""
    vega = variant_key(
        extract_features("Кондиционер Sitronic Vega Inverter 18", "acs"), "dual", "acs")
    other = variant_key(
        extract_features("Кондиционер Sitronic Alba Inverter 18", "acs"), "dual", "acs")
    assert vega is not None and other is not None
    assert vega != other


def test_bq_is_a_brand_despite_being_two_characters():
    """Short tokens are a blind spot in head-token counting, not in reality.
    BQ's 55FU32B is carried by asaxiy, uzum and alifshop."""
    f = extract_features("Телевизор BQ 55FU32B 4K UHD webOS", category="televisions")
    assert f.brand == "bq"
    assert "55fu32b" in f.model_tokens


@pytest.mark.parametrize("name", [
    "Ноутбук ASUS VivoBook X1502VA-BQ827 / i7-13620H / DDR4 16GB / SSD 512GB / 15.6\"",
    "ASUS Vivobook 15 X1502VA-BQ982 i7-13620H/16/512GB Cool Silver Noutbuki",
])
def test_bq_does_not_read_itself_out_of_an_asus_sku(name):
    """The regression adding BQ caused, and the reason short brands opt out of
    the trailing-digit boundary.

    "-BQ827" is ASUS's own suffix. normalize() splits the hyphen to "bq827",
    the digit counted as a word boundary, and both machines were relabelled BQ
    -- and merged with each other. Nothing aggregate could see it: it looked
    exactly like a healthy two-store match.
    """
    assert extract_features(name, category="laptops").brand == "asus"


@pytest.mark.parametrize("word", ["pro", "air", "max", "plus", "neo"])
def test_designators_are_kept_because_they_name_the_product(word):
    # A MacBook Air is not a MacBook Pro. These read as marketing on a phone,
    # so the temptation is to strip them everywhere -- which would merge two
    # genuinely different products, the one failure this module must not have.
    assert is_model_token(word)


def test_macbook_air_and_pro_are_different_products():
    air = variant_key(extract_features("MacBook Air 13 M4 256GB", "laptops"), "dual", "laptops")
    pro = variant_key(extract_features("MacBook Pro 13 M4 256GB", "laptops"), "dual", "laptops")
    assert air is not None and pro is not None
    assert air != pro


# --- a laptop's identity ends where its specification begins ----------------

def test_laptop_spec_after_the_delimiter_is_not_identity():
    f = extract_features(
        "Ноутбук Acer Predator Helios Neo 16S AI / U9-275HX / DDR5 32GB / RTX 5060",
        "laptops",
    )
    assert {"predator", "helios", "neo"} <= f.model_tokens
    assert "rtx" not in f.model_tokens and "5060" not in f.model_tokens


def test_storage_is_still_read_from_the_whole_laptop_title():
    # Truncation is for model tokens only: memory must survive it, or an
    # Aspire 512 and an Aspire 256 become one product.
    small = extract_features("Ноутбук Acer Aspire 8/256", "laptops")
    large = extract_features("Ноутбук Acer Aspire 8/512", "laptops")
    assert small.storage_gb == 256 and large.storage_gb == 512
    assert variant_key(small, "dual", "laptops") != variant_key(large, "dual", "laptops")


# --- a television has no RAM -------------------------------------------------

@pytest.mark.parametrize("category", ["televisions", "fridges", "acs", "washers", "ovens"])
def test_memory_is_absent_outside_phones_and_laptops(category):
    # The plausible-storage set (32, 64, ...) overlaps exactly with television
    # diagonals. "Телевизор Premier 32PRM840FSV" was keyed with storage 32 and
    # rendered as "... 32 ГБ" -- a spec the product does not have.
    f = extract_features("Телевизор Premier 32PRM840FSV 32", category)
    assert f.ram_gb is None and f.storage_gb is None


def test_television_diagonal_is_legitimate_identity():
    # "Телевизор MoonX 32" is a real product whose diagonal is the only thing
    # distinguishing it. The phone capacity guard refused exactly these.
    k = variant_key(extract_features('Телевизор MoonX 32" Черный', "televisions"),
                    "dual", "televisions")
    assert k is not None
    assert is_wellformed(k)


def test_capacity_guard_still_protects_phones():
    from narxnoma.matching.keys import VariantKey
    bad = VariantKey("apple", frozenset({"17", "256"}), None, 512, "black", "dual")
    assert not is_wellformed(bad)


# --- mixed-script titles -----------------------------------------------------

@pytest.mark.parametrize("raw,expected", [
    ("Tелевизор Artel", "телевизор artel"),        # Latin T in a Russian word
    ("Cтиральная машина", "стиральная машина"),    # Latin C
    ("Стиральная машинa", "стиральная машина"),    # Latin a
])
def test_latin_letters_inside_russian_words_are_folded(raw, expected):
    assert normalize(raw) == expected


def test_cyrillic_letters_inside_a_model_code_are_folded_to_latin():
    # "Автохолодильник Alpicool С20" -- a CYRILLIC С inside a code every other
    # listing writes with a Latin C. Two spellings, one product.
    assert normalize("Alpicool С20") == normalize("Alpicool C20")


def test_a_latin_brand_with_one_cyrillic_letter_keeps_its_brand():
    # "PRЕMIER" is Latin with a single Cyrillic Е. Folding toward Cyrillic
    # produced the unmatchable "рrемiеr" and lost the brand entirely.
    assert normalize("PRЕMIER") == "premier"


def test_single_script_tokens_are_left_alone():
    assert normalize("Vivobook") == "vivobook"
    assert normalize("телевизор") == "телевизор"


# --- accessories -------------------------------------------------------------

def test_a_laptop_bag_is_not_a_laptop():
    assert is_accessory("Rivacase 7531 Black Eco 15.6 Noutbuk sumkasi", "laptops")


def test_a_product_that_names_its_own_category_first_is_the_product():
    # An accessory word inside such a title describes what is in the box.
    assert not is_accessory("Телевизор Samsung UE55 с пультом", "televisions")
    assert not is_accessory("Ноутбук Acer Aspire в сумке", "laptops")


def test_accessory_rule_never_applies_to_phones():
    # Phones have their own denylist (sources/not_a_phone.py); running both
    # would drop the real phones its regression tests exist to protect.
    assert not is_accessory("Чехол для Samsung Galaxy", "smartphones")


# --- one product, however the retailer decorates it -------------------------

def _key(name, category):
    return variant_key(extract_features(name, category), "dual", category)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("category,a,b", [
    # Finish, capacity and internal code fragments, all around ONE code.
    ("fridges", "Холодильник Samsung RB29FERNDSA",
     "SAMSUNG RB29FERNDSA 290L Sovutgichi"),
    ("fridges", "Холодильник Samsung RT62K7110SL",
     "Холодильник Samsung Inox RT62K7110SL"),
    ("fridges", "Холодильник LG GN-B392SMBB Inverter",
     "LG GN-B392SMBB.APZQCIS Muzlatgichi"),
    ("acs", "Кондиционер Artel Everest 12 Inverter ARTSID3AW12BE",
     "Кондиционер Artel Everest ARTSID3AW12BE Inverter"),
    ("acs", "Artel 12HS S SIR1W12BE Konditsioneri",
     "Настенный кондиционер Artel S Inverter SIR1W12BE"),
    ("televisions", "Телевизор Artel SMART A32PHCH010 Google tv HD",
     "Телевизор Artel A32PHCH010 32\", чёрный"),
    ("televisions", "Samsung UE55DU7100UXUZ Smart Televizori",
     "Телевизор Samsung UE55DU7100UXUZ Smart, черный"),
])
def test_one_catalogue_code_is_one_product(category, a, b):
    ka, kb = _key(a, category), _key(b, category)
    assert ka is not None and kb is not None
    assert ka == kb, f"{a!r} and {b!r} should be one product"


def test_a_title_without_a_code_keeps_its_distinguishing_figure():
    # Nothing else identifies these, so the figure must survive.
    assert _key("Кондиционер Midea Naomi PRO AI Inverter 09", "acs") != \
           _key("Кондиционер Midea Naomi PRO AI Inverter 24", "acs")
    assert _key('Телевизор MoonX 32"', "televisions") is not None


def test_unknown_colour_words_never_become_identity():
    # Colour is deliberately not identity outside phones. A finish word the
    # palette does not know must be dropped, not promoted to a model token --
    # these three split one fridge into three products at three prices.
    base = _key("Холодильник Artel Frost HD276FND", "fridges")
    assert base == _key("Холодильник Artel Frost Матовый HD276FND", "fridges")
    assert base == _key("Холодильник Artel Frost Асфальт Мокрый HD276FND", "fridges")


def test_a_laptop_cpu_is_not_its_name():
    # Only bites when the retailer omits the "/" that usually fences the spec.
    assert _key("Ноутбук Acer Aspire Snapdragon X1 26100", "laptops") == \
           _key("Ноутбук Acer Aspire", "laptops")


def test_macbook_generations_stay_apart():
    # "m4" looks like a spec token and is not: it is the identity of the
    # machine, so PROCESSORS must not contain it.
    assert _key("MacBook Air 13 M4 256GB", "laptops") != \
           _key("MacBook Air 13 M2 256GB", "laptops")


# --- display -----------------------------------------------------------------

def test_family_name_leads_the_model_string():
    # A frozenset has no order, and alphabetical order puts the screen size
    # first on almost every laptop: "ASUS 15 Go Vivobook".
    assert ordered_non_phone_tokens({"15", "go", "vivobook"}) == ["vivobook", "go", "15"]


def test_codes_come_before_bare_figures():
    assert ordered_non_phone_tokens({"55", "ue55du7100uxuz"}) == ["ue55du7100uxuz", "55"]


def test_apple_label_is_not_iphone_outside_phones():
    # BRAND_LABELS maps apple -> "Apple iPhone" because the word iPhone is
    # stripped from phone names and has to be put back. A MacBook is also
    # brand apple, so the phone label renders "Ноутбук Apple iPhone MacBook".
    assert brand_label("apple", "laptops") == "Apple"
    assert brand_label("apple", "smartphones") == "Apple iPhone"


def test_non_phone_display_name_reads_naturally():
    k = variant_key(
        extract_features("Телевизор Samsung UE55DU7100UXUZ", "televisions"),
        "dual", "televisions",
    )
    assert display_name(k) == "Телевизор Samsung UE55DU7100UXUZ"

from narxnoma.matching.normalize import normalize


def test_lowercases_and_collapses_whitespace():
    assert normalize("  Samsung   Galaxy  A17 ") == "samsung galaxy a17"


def test_none_and_empty():
    assert normalize(None) == ""
    assert normalize("") == ""


def test_folds_yo_to_ye():
    # uzum ships both "Тёмно-зелёный" and "Темно-зеленый" for the same colour
    assert normalize("Тёмно-зелёный") == "темно зеленый"


def test_separators_become_spaces():
    assert normalize("8ГБ/256ГБ") == "8гб 256гб"
    assert normalize("Honor X9d, Midnight Black, 12/256 GB") == \
        "honor x9d midnight black 12 256 gb"


def test_trailing_plus_becomes_plus_word():
    # "Pro+" is a real model modifier
    assert normalize("Honor X5d Pro+") == "honor x5d pro plus"


def test_inner_plus_becomes_space_not_plus_word():
    # THE BUG: mapping every '+' to 'plus' injected a phantom model token
    # that rejected every iPhone on BeeMarket.
    assert normalize("SIM+eSIM") == "sim esim"
    assert "plus" not in normalize("nanoSim+eSim")

FILE: narxnoma-crawler/tests/matching/test_purity.py
================================================
import ast
import pathlib

STDLIB_OK = {
    "re", "unicodedata", "dataclasses", "typing", "statistics",
    "functools", "itertools", "collections", "enum", "math",
}
MATCHING_DIR = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "narxnoma" / "matching"


def _imported_roots(path):
    tree = ast.parse(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    roots = set()
    for node in ast.walk(tree):
        if isinstance(node, ast.Import):
            for a in node.names:
                roots.add(a.name.split(".")[0])
        elif isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom):
            if node.level == 0 and node.module:
                roots.add(node.module.split(".")[0])
    return roots


def test_matching_modules_exist():
    """Guard against the guard passing vacuously over an empty directory."""
    modules = {p.name for p in MATCHING_DIR.glob("*.py")}
    assert {"brands.py", "normalize.py"} <= modules


def test_matching_imports_stdlib_only():
    offenders = {}
    for path in MATCHING_DIR.glob("*.py"):
        bad = _imported_roots(path) - STDLIB_OK - {"narxnoma"}
        if bad:
            offenders[path.name] = sorted(bad)
    assert offenders == {}, f"non-stdlib imports in matching: {offenders}"

from narxnoma.matching.sim import is_esim_only, sim_kind


def test_explicit_dual_markers_are_not_esim_only():
    # Checked FIRST: "SIM+eSIM" contains "esim" but is the physical variant.
    for s in ["SIM+eSIM", "nanoSim+eSim", "2 SIM", "dualSIM", "две сим"]:
        assert is_esim_only(s) is False


def test_esim_only_forms():
    # uzum encodes it three ways; all must be screened. Price gap is real:
    # 20,789,010 dual vs 18,099,000 eSIM-only for the same nominal phone.
    for s in ["17 Pro Max 256 (e-Sim)", "iPhone 17 Pro Max 256GB (eSIM)",
              "Apple iPhone 17 Air 256GB, eSIM"]:
        assert is_esim_only(s) is True


def test_no_sim_information():
    assert is_esim_only("Honor X9d 12/256 GB Black") is False


def test_sim_kind_labels():
    assert sim_kind("iPhone 17 Pro 256GB (eSIM)") == "esim_only"
    assert sim_kind("iPhone 17 Pro 256GB nanoSIM+eSIM") == "dual"
    assert sim_kind("Honor X9d 12/256 GB Black") == "unknown"


def test_slash_separated_dual_marker_is_not_esim_only():
    # docs/parsers/uzum.md §6: the rendered spec sheet for the dual variant
    # shows "Тип SIM карты : nano-SIM/eSIM" -- a slash, not a plus. Before the
    # fix this collapsed to "...nanosim/esim" with no "+", so _DUAL missed it
    # and _ESIM matched the trailing "esim", misclassifying a dual phone as
    # eSIM-only.
    s = "Тип SIM карты : nano-SIM/eSIM"
    assert is_esim_only(s) is False
    assert sim_kind(s) == "dual"


def test_sim_word_boundary_before_cyrillic():
    # "SIM карта" (uzum.md §6, the SIM characteristic key/value form).
    # Separator-stripping turns it into "simкарта"; Cyrillic "к" is a \w
    # character under Python's Unicode-aware \b, so \bsim\b never matched
    # and sim_kind fell through to "unknown" instead of "dual".
    assert sim_kind("SIM карта") == "dual"


def test_slash_separated_dual_marker_esim_only_false():
    # Same slash-separated marker as above, in its shorter raw form.
    assert is_esim_only("nanoSIM/eSIM") is False


def test_genuine_esim_only_still_detected():
    # Pins that widening separator stripping does not over-correct and start
    # calling genuine eSIM-only phones dual.
    s = "iPhone 17 Pro Max 256GB (eSIM)"
    assert is_esim_only(s) is True
    assert sim_kind(s) == "esim_only"


def test_no_sim_information_with_a_slash_in_the_name():
    # A name with no SIM information at all, that also contains a slash in
    # the memory figure -- proves widened separator stripping ("/" now
    # stripped too) does not create a spurious "simesim"/"esim" match.
    assert sim_kind("Honor X9d 12/256 GB Black") == "unknown"


def test_bare_dual_marker_is_recognised():
    # uzum.md §6 lists a bare "dual" among the explicit dual markers, but
    # _DUAL only matched "dualsim", so sim_kind("dual") fell through to
    # "unknown" and a phone documented as dual got no SIM classification.
    assert sim_kind("dual") == "dual"
    assert is_esim_only("dual") is False
    # The bare alternative must not cost us the compound spelling.
    assert sim_kind("dualSIM") == "dual"

from narxnoma.matching.stats import robust_median


def test_empty():
    assert robust_median([]) == (None, [])


def test_small_sample_is_not_stripped():
    median, kept = robust_median([100, 200, 300])
    assert median == 200
    assert kept == [100, 200, 300]


def test_iqr_strips_an_outlier():
    prices = [1000, 1010, 1020, 1030, 50000]
    median, kept = robust_median(prices)
    assert 50000 not in kept
    assert median == 1015


def test_never_returns_empty_kept():
    median, kept = robust_median([5, 5, 5, 5])
    assert kept
    assert median == 5

FILE: narxnoma-crawler/tests/pipeline/test_aggregate.py

"""Aggregation: which number a page shows, and which listing it came from."""
import pytest

from narxnoma.db import repository as repo
from narxnoma.pipeline.aggregate import recompute_variant_prices, uzum_spread
from narxnoma.pipeline.cluster import cluster_offers
from narxnoma.pipeline.extract import identify
from narxnoma.sources.base import Listing

pytestmark = pytest.mark.db


def seed(conn, name, key, store="olcha", price=2_723_000, availability="IN_STOCK"):
    ids = repo.store_ids(conn)
    repo.upsert_offers(conn, ids[store], [Listing(
        store_slug=store, source_key=key, name_raw=name, price=price,
        url=f"https://{store}.uz/{key}", availability=availability)])
    with conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute("SELECT id FROM offer WHERE source_key = %s AND store_id = %s",
                    (key, ids[store]))
        return cur.fetchone()[0]


def cluster(conn):
    cluster_offers(conn, (identify(r) for r in repo.load_unattached_offers(conn)))


def price_row(conn):
    with conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute("""
            SELECT min_price, median_price, max_price, offer_count,
                   in_stock_offer_count, store_count, min_store_id, min_offer_id
              FROM variant_price
        """)
        return cur.fetchone()


HONOR = "Смартфон Honor X9d 12/256 ГБ, черный"


def test_single_offer_variant_has_min_equal_median_equal_max(db_conn):
    seed(db_conn, HONOR, "a", price=4_839_000)
    cluster(db_conn)
    recompute_variant_prices(db_conn)

    lo, med, hi, offers, in_stock, stores, *_ = price_row(db_conn)
    assert lo == med == hi == 4_839_000
    assert offers == in_stock == stores == 1


def test_out_of_stock_offer_never_becomes_the_headline_price(db_conn):
    # A cheaper listing nobody can buy must not be advertised as the price.
    seed(db_conn, HONOR, "cheap", price=3_000_000, availability="OUT_OF_STOCK")
    seed(db_conn, HONOR, "real", store="idea", price=4_839_000)
    cluster(db_conn)
    recompute_variant_prices(db_conn)

    lo, _, _, offers, in_stock, _, _, _ = price_row(db_conn)
    assert lo == 4_839_000, "the out-of-stock 3,000,000 must not win"
    assert offers == 2, "but it is still counted as an observation"
    assert in_stock == 1


def test_headline_price_records_which_listing_it_came_from(db_conn):
    # The provenance IS the feature: it lets a page quote the retailer's own
    # wording beside the number so a shopper can check the match themselves.
    seed(db_conn, HONOR, "dear", price=5_500_000)
    cheapest = seed(db_conn, HONOR, "cheap", store="idea", price=4_839_000)
    cluster(db_conn)
    recompute_variant_prices(db_conn)

    lo, _, _, _, _, _, min_store, min_offer = price_row(db_conn)
    assert lo == 4_839_000
    assert min_offer == cheapest
    with db_conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute("SELECT slug FROM store WHERE id = %s", (min_store,))
        assert cur.fetchone()[0] == "idea"


def test_a_variant_with_no_in_stock_offers_has_no_headline_price(db_conn):
    # min_price is nullable precisely so this case does not force us to either
    # publish an unbuyable price or delete the variant's row.
    seed(db_conn, HONOR, "gone", price=4_839_000, availability="OUT_OF_STOCK")
    cluster(db_conn)
    recompute_variant_prices(db_conn)

    lo, _, _, offers, in_stock, _, _, _ = price_row(db_conn)
    assert lo is None
    assert offers == 1 and in_stock == 0


def test_recompute_is_idempotent_and_reflects_stock_changes(db_conn):
    offer_id = seed(db_conn, HONOR, "a", price=4_839_000)
    cluster(db_conn)
    recompute_variant_prices(db_conn)
    assert price_row(db_conn)[0] == 4_839_000

    # The offer goes out of stock; the stale headline must not survive.
    with db_conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute("UPDATE offer SET availability = 'OUT_OF_STOCK' WHERE id = %s",
                    (offer_id,))
    recompute_variant_prices(db_conn)
    assert price_row(db_conn)[0] is None

    with db_conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute("SELECT count(*) FROM variant_price")
        assert cur.fetchone()[0] == 1, "recompute must not duplicate rows"


def test_uzum_spread_strips_an_outlier_from_the_median(db_conn):
    # A marketplace carries mis-listed items priced like phones. One of them
    # must not drag the median off the real market price.
    for i, price in enumerate([4_800_000, 4_850_000, 4_900_000, 4_950_000, 40_000_000]):
        seed(db_conn, HONOR, f"u{i}", store="uzum", price=price)
    cluster(db_conn)

    with db_conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute("SELECT id FROM variant")
        variant_id = cur.fetchone()[0]

    spread = uzum_spread(db_conn, variant_id)
    assert spread.seller_count == 5
    assert spread.min_price == 4_800_000
    assert spread.max_price == 40_000_000, "the outlier is still reported as the max"
    assert spread.median_price < 5_000_000, "but it must not drag the median"


def test_uzum_spread_is_none_when_there_is_no_spread_to_report(db_conn):
    seed(db_conn, HONOR, "solo", store="uzum", price=4_839_000)
    cluster(db_conn)
    with db_conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute("SELECT id FROM variant")
        variant_id = cur.fetchone()[0]
    assert uzum_spread(db_conn, variant_id) is None


def test_spread_ignores_other_stores(db_conn):
    seed(db_conn, HONOR, "u1", store="uzum", price=4_800_000)
    seed(db_conn, HONOR, "u2", store="uzum", price=4_900_000)
    seed(db_conn, HONOR, "other", store="olcha", price=9_000_000)
    cluster(db_conn)
    with db_conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute("SELECT id FROM variant")
        variant_id = cur.fetchone()[0]

    spread = uzum_spread(db_conn, variant_id)
    assert spread.seller_count == 2
    assert spread.max_price == 4_900_000, "olcha's 9,000,000 is not a uzum seller"

"""Pass B: reaching the source that cannot be swept. No network here."""
import pytest

from narxnoma.pipeline.backfill import (
    BackfillResult,
    backfill_search_only_sources,
    build_query,
)
from narxnoma.sources.base import Listing


class FakeMediapark:
    slug = "mediapark"
    can_sweep = False

    def __init__(self, results=None, boom_on=None):
        self.results = results or {}
        self.boom_on = boom_on
        self.queries = []

    def sweep(self):
        raise NotImplementedError("mediapark is search-only")

    def search(self, query):
        self.queries.append(query)
        if self.boom_on and self.boom_on in query:
            raise RuntimeError("upstream 500")
        return iter(self.results.get(query, []))


class FakeRepo:
    def __init__(self):
        self.raw = []
        self.upserts = []

    def record_raw_offers(self, conn, store_id, listings):
        listings = list(listings)
        self.raw.extend(listings)
        return len(listings)

    def upsert_offers(self, conn, store_id, listings):
        listings = list(listings)
        self.upserts.extend(listings)
        return len(listings), 0


def listing(key="m1", price=4_839_000):
    return Listing(store_slug="mediapark", source_key=key,
                   name_raw="Смартфон Honor X9D 12/256", price=price,
                   url=f"https://mediapark.uz/{key}")


HONOR = "Смартфон Honor X9D 12/256 ГБ, Черный"


def test_query_drops_our_own_prefix_but_keeps_memory_and_colour():
    # mediapark RANKS rather than filtering with strict AND, so stripping the
    # memory figure or the colour measurably worsens recall. Only our own
    # generated "Смартфон" prefix goes -- no retailer indexes that.
    query = build_query(HONOR)
    assert not query.startswith("Смартфон")
    assert "Honor X9D" in query
    assert "12/256" in query, "memory must survive: it is what ranks the right variant"
    assert "Черный" in query, "colour must survive for the same reason"


def test_query_is_stable_for_an_apple_variant_without_ram():
    assert build_query("Смартфон Apple iPhone 17 Pro 256 ГБ, Серебристый") == \
        "Apple iPhone 17 Pro 256 Серебристый"


def test_results_are_written_as_offers():
    source = FakeMediapark({build_query(HONOR): [listing()]})
    repo = FakeRepo()

    result = backfill_search_only_sources(
        None, source, "store-1", [("v1", HONOR)], repo=repo)

    assert result.queried == 1
    assert result.variants_matched == 1
    assert result.offers_written == 1
    assert len(repo.raw) == 1 and len(repo.upserts) == 1


def test_a_variant_with_no_match_records_nothing_and_does_not_raise():
    source = FakeMediapark({})
    repo = FakeRepo()

    result = backfill_search_only_sources(
        None, source, "store-1", [("v1", HONOR)], repo=repo)

    assert result.misses == 1
    assert result.variants_matched == 0
    assert repo.raw == [] and repo.upserts == []


def test_one_failing_query_does_not_end_the_pass():
    # A single bad response must not cost us the rest of the catalogue.
    good = build_query("Смартфон Honor X9D 12/256 ГБ, Черный")
    source = FakeMediapark({good: [listing()]}, boom_on="Pixel")
    repo = FakeRepo()

    result = backfill_search_only_sources(
        None, source, "store-1",
        [("v1", "Смартфон Google Pixel 10 12/256 ГБ, Черный"), ("v2", HONOR)],
        repo=repo)

    assert result.queried == 2
    assert result.misses == 1
    assert result.variants_matched == 1, "the good query still ran and wrote"


def test_the_pass_is_bounded_so_one_cycle_cannot_run_away():
    # The catalogue grows without limit; a backfill that scaled with it would
    # eventually outlast the four-hour window and collide with the next run.
    source = FakeMediapark({})
    repo = FakeRepo()
    variants = [(f"v{i}", f"Смартфон Honor X{i} 12/256 ГБ, Черный") for i in range(50)]

    result = backfill_search_only_sources(
        None, source, "store-1", variants, repo=repo, max_queries=10)

    assert result.queried == 10
    assert len(source.queries) == 10


def test_backfill_never_calls_sweep():
    # sweep() raises for this source by design; the whole point of Pass B is
    # that it reaches mediapark another way.
    source = FakeMediapark({})
    backfill_search_only_sources(None, source, "store-1", [("v1", HONOR)],
                                 repo=FakeRepo())
    with pytest.raises(NotImplementedError):
        source.sweep()


def test_backfill_does_not_attach_anything_itself():
    # A search hit is a suggestion, not evidence. Clustering decides on the
    # next run whether the listing really is that variant.
    import inspect

    import narxnoma.pipeline.backfill as mod

    source = inspect.getsource(mod)
    assert "attach_offer_to_variant" not in source
    assert "upsert_variant" not in source


def test_result_starts_empty():
    assert BackfillResult() == BackfillResult(0, 0, 0, 0)

FILE: narxnoma-crawler/tests/pipeline/test_cluster.py

"""Clustering: attach only when exactly one product can be the right one."""
import pytest

from narxnoma.db import repository as repo
from narxnoma.pipeline.cluster import (
    REASON_AMBIGUOUS,
    REASON_NO_CANDIDATE,
    REASON_MEMORY_IN_MODEL,
    REASON_NO_IDENTITY,
    cluster_offers,
    detach_drifted_offers,
)
from narxnoma.pipeline.extract import identify
from narxnoma.sources.base import Listing

pytestmark = pytest.mark.db


def seed_offer(conn, name, key="k1", store="olcha", price=2_723_000):
    """Put one real offer row in the database and return its id."""
    ids = repo.store_ids(conn)
    repo.upsert_offers(conn, ids[store], [Listing(
        store_slug=store, source_key=key, name_raw=name, price=price,
        url=f"https://{store}.uz/{key}", availability="IN_STOCK")])
    with conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute("SELECT id FROM offer WHERE source_key = %s AND store_id = %s",
                    (key, ids[store]))
        return cur.fetchone()[0]


def identities_for(conn):
    return [identify(row) for row in repo.load_unattached_offers(conn)]


def variant_count(conn):
    with conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute("SELECT count(*) FROM variant")
        return cur.fetchone()[0]


def unresolved_reason(conn, offer_id):
    with conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute("SELECT reason FROM unresolved_offer WHERE offer_id = %s", (offer_id,))
        row = cur.fetchone()
        return row[0] if row else None


def attached_variant(conn, offer_id):
    with conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute("SELECT variant_id FROM offer WHERE id = %s", (offer_id,))
        return cur.fetchone()[0]


def test_differing_case_and_wording_collapse_to_one_variant(db_conn):
    # "Cosmic orange" and "Cosmic Orange" are two separate products on a
    # competitor's site, splitting the offer pool so BOTH pages show a wrong
    # minimum. The canonical key is case- and wording-insensitive by
    # construction, so this must be impossible here.
    a = seed_offer(db_conn, "Смартфон Apple iPhone 17 Pro Max 256 ГБ, Cosmic orange", "a1")
    b = seed_offer(db_conn, "iPhone 17 Pro Max 256GB Cosmic Orange", "b1", store="idea")

    result = cluster_offers(db_conn, identities_for(db_conn))

    assert result.attached == 2
    assert variant_count(db_conn) == 1
    assert attached_variant(db_conn, a) == attached_variant(db_conn, b)


def test_ambiguous_partial_is_parked_not_guessed(db_conn):
    # Both 8/256 and 12/256 exist. An offer stating only 256 is compatible with
    # both, so no evidence picks one. Attaching it anyway -- which produces a
    # fuller-looking catalogue -- is the exact defect this platform exists to
    # avoid, because the price would then be shown against a phone it is not for.
    seed_offer(db_conn, "Смартфон Xiaomi Redmi Note 15 8/256 ГБ, чёрный", "full8")
    seed_offer(db_conn, "Смартфон Xiaomi Redmi Note 15 12/256 ГБ, чёрный", "full12")
    ambiguous = seed_offer(db_conn, "Смартфон Xiaomi Redmi Note 15 256 ГБ, чёрный", "amb")

    result = cluster_offers(db_conn, identities_for(db_conn))

    assert attached_variant(db_conn, ambiguous) is None
    assert unresolved_reason(db_conn, ambiguous) == REASON_AMBIGUOUS
    assert result.unresolved == 1
    with db_conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute("SELECT candidate_ids FROM unresolved_offer WHERE offer_id = %s",
                    (ambiguous,))
        assert len(cur.fetchone()[0]) == 2, "both candidates must be recorded"


def test_partial_with_exactly_one_candidate_attaches(db_conn):
    # Only 8/256 exists, so "256" can only mean that one. Evidence, not a guess.
    full = seed_offer(db_conn, "Смартфон Xiaomi Redmi Note 15 8/256 ГБ, чёрный", "full8")
    partial = seed_offer(db_conn, "Смартфон Xiaomi Redmi Note 15 256 ГБ, чёрный", "part")

    cluster_offers(db_conn, identities_for(db_conn))

    assert attached_variant(db_conn, partial) is not None
    assert attached_variant(db_conn, partial) == attached_variant(db_conn, full)
    assert unresolved_reason(db_conn, partial) is None


def test_partial_with_no_candidate_is_parked_distinctly(db_conn):
    # Nothing to attach to. Different from ambiguity, and the report must be
    # able to tell them apart: this is a catalogue gap, not a vague listing.
    orphan = seed_offer(db_conn, "Смартфон Vivo Y31d 256 ГБ, чёрный", "orph")

    cluster_offers(db_conn, identities_for(db_conn))

    assert attached_variant(db_conn, orphan) is None
    assert unresolved_reason(db_conn, orphan) == REASON_NO_CANDIDATE


def test_no_identity_at_all_is_parked(db_conn):
    # A catalogue parent with no variant spec: real, and common.
    vague = seed_offer(db_conn, "Смартфон Honor X5d Plus", "vague")

    cluster_offers(db_conn, identities_for(db_conn))

    assert attached_variant(db_conn, vague) is None
    assert unresolved_reason(db_conn, vague) == REASON_NO_IDENTITY


def test_esim_only_and_dual_are_different_variants(db_conn):
    # An eSIM-only iPhone is a different product at a materially different
    # price -- one marketplace lists them side by side at 18.1M and 20.8M.
    seed_offer(db_conn, "Смартфон Apple iPhone 17 Pro 256 ГБ (nanoSim+eSim), Silver", "dual")
    seed_offer(db_conn, "Смартфон Apple iPhone 17 Pro 256 ГБ (eSIM), Silver", "esim")

    cluster_offers(db_conn, identities_for(db_conn))

    assert variant_count(db_conn) == 2


def test_clustering_is_idempotent(db_conn):
    seed_offer(db_conn, "Смартфон Honor X9d 12/256 ГБ, черный", "h1")
    seed_offer(db_conn, "Honor X9d 12/256 GB Midnight Black", "h2", store="idea")

    first = cluster_offers(db_conn, identities_for(db_conn))
    after_first = variant_count(db_conn)
    second = cluster_offers(db_conn, identities_for(db_conn))

    assert first.attached == 2
    assert after_first == 1
    assert variant_count(db_conn) == 1, "a second run must not duplicate variants"
    assert second.attached == 0, "already-attached offers are not reconsidered"


def test_a_parked_offer_is_retried_and_attaches_once_its_variant_exists(db_conn):
    # THE RETRY RULE, in the shape it actually takes in production. A vague
    # listing arrives before any retailer has published a fully-specified one,
    # so there is nothing to attach it to. Cycles later another retailer lists
    # the same phone properly, and the earlier offer becomes resolvable.
    #
    # Without the retry, that offer is dead the moment it is first parked, and
    # the unresolved count becomes a permanently rising number nobody can act
    # on -- when it is supposed to be the signal that the matcher needs work.
    partial = seed_offer(db_conn, "Смартфон Xiaomi Redmi Note 15 256 ГБ, чёрный", "part")

    cluster_offers(db_conn, identities_for(db_conn))
    assert unresolved_reason(db_conn, partial) == REASON_NO_CANDIDATE
    assert variant_count(db_conn) == 0

    # A later cycle: another retailer publishes the full specification.
    seed_offer(db_conn, "Смартфон Xiaomi Redmi Note 15 8/256 ГБ, чёрный",
               "full8", store="idea")

    cluster_offers(db_conn, identities_for(db_conn))

    assert attached_variant(db_conn, partial) is not None
    assert unresolved_reason(db_conn, partial) is None, \
        "the refusal must be cleared once the offer attaches"


def test_a_parked_offer_stays_parked_while_it_remains_ambiguous(db_conn):
    # The retry must not become a slow leak into guessing: reconsidering an
    # offer every cycle is only safe because the answer is still "refuse" until
    # the evidence actually changes.
    seed_offer(db_conn, "Смартфон Xiaomi Redmi Note 15 8/256 ГБ, чёрный", "full8")
    seed_offer(db_conn, "Смартфон Xiaomi Redmi Note 15 12/256 ГБ, чёрный", "full12")
    ambiguous = seed_offer(db_conn, "Смартфон Xiaomi Redmi Note 15 256 ГБ, чёрный", "amb")

    for _ in range(3):
        cluster_offers(db_conn, identities_for(db_conn))
        assert attached_variant(db_conn, ambiguous) is None
        assert unresolved_reason(db_conn, ambiguous) == REASON_AMBIGUOUS


def test_display_name_is_generated_not_copied(db_conn):
    # Copying a retailer's wording is how a competitor ended up with two
    # products for one phone. The name is a function of the key.
    seed_offer(db_conn, "HONOR   x9d  12/256gb   midnight black", "h1")

    cluster_offers(db_conn, identities_for(db_conn))

    with db_conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute("SELECT display_name, slug FROM variant")
        name, slug_value = cur.fetchone()
    assert name == "Смартфон Honor X9D 12/256 ГБ, Черный"
    assert slug_value == "honor-x9d-12-256-black"


def test_a_memory_figure_in_the_model_tokens_is_refused_not_catalogued(db_conn):
    """No phone is named "256". A capacity that reached the model tokens is
    always a parsing failure, so the variant it would mint is a product that
    does not exist -- and minting it pools genuinely different SKUs behind
    one headline price, which is the exact defect this platform exists to
    avoid, reproduced in our own data.

    This is a backstop, not the repair. The uzum card-range leak that made
    it necessary is fixed at source; the guard stays because the failure is
    silent by construction -- a wrong variant looks exactly like a right one
    -- and any source can reintroduce it.
    """
    offer_id = seed_offer(
        db_conn, "Смартфон Apple iPhone 17 256 Pro Max 512 ГБ, Оранжевый", "leak")

    result = cluster_offers(db_conn, identities_for(db_conn))

    assert result.attached == 0
    assert variant_count(db_conn) == 0
    assert unresolved_reason(db_conn, offer_id) == REASON_MEMORY_IN_MODEL


def test_a_real_model_number_is_not_mistaken_for_a_capacity(db_conn):
    """The guard keys on capacities only. Model numbers that merely look
    numeric -- 12, 15, 17, 200 -- must still catalogue normally.
    """
    seed_offer(db_conn, "Смартфон Apple iPhone 12 Pro 256 ГБ, Черный", "ok1")
    seed_offer(db_conn, "Смартфон Honor 200 Pro 12/512 ГБ, Черный", "ok2", store="idea")

    result = cluster_offers(db_conn, identities_for(db_conn))

    assert result.attached == 2
    assert variant_count(db_conn) == 2


def test_an_offer_whose_name_now_says_something_else_is_re_examined(db_conn):
    """A parser fix must be able to heal the catalogue it already wrote.

    Clustering only ever loads offers with variant_id IS NULL, so an offer
    attached in an earlier cycle is never reconsidered. That is right while
    name_raw is stable -- and wrong the moment a source fix changes it,
    which is exactly when the catalogue is most likely to be wrong. The
    uzum card-range repair rewrote 217 stored names; without this the
    offers behind them would have sat on their old, incorrect variants
    indefinitely, and no report would have said so.
    """
    offer_id = seed_offer(db_conn, "Смартфон Honor X9d 12/256 ГБ, черный", "drift")
    cluster_offers(db_conn, identities_for(db_conn))
    original = attached_variant(db_conn, offer_id)
    assert original is not None

    # The source is corrected and the next harvest stores a different name.
    with db_conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute("UPDATE offer SET name_raw = %s WHERE id = %s",
                    ("Смартфон Honor X9d 12/512 ГБ, черный", offer_id))

    detached = detach_drifted_offers(db_conn)
    assert detached == 1
    cluster_offers(db_conn, identities_for(db_conn))

    moved = attached_variant(db_conn, offer_id)
    assert moved is not None and moved != original
    with db_conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute("SELECT storage_gb FROM variant WHERE id = %s", (moved,))
        assert cur.fetchone()[0] == 512


def test_an_unchanged_catalogue_detaches_nothing(db_conn):
    """Reconciliation runs every cycle, so a steady state must be a no-op --
    otherwise it churns every offer through detach and re-attach each run.
    """
    seed_offer(db_conn, "Смартфон Honor X9d 12/256 ГБ, черный", "a")
    seed_offer(db_conn, "Смартфон Apple iPhone 17 Pro 256 ГБ, Синий", "b", store="idea")
    cluster_offers(db_conn, identities_for(db_conn))

    assert detach_drifted_offers(db_conn) == 0
    assert detach_drifted_offers(db_conn) == 0


def test_a_partial_attachment_compatible_with_its_variant_is_left_alone(db_conn):
    """An offer attached by partial resolution has no full key of its own, so
    "re-derive and compare" cannot judge it. It is kept while it remains
    COMPATIBLE with the variant it sits on, and only detached when the name
    now contradicts it -- otherwise every cycle would tear down and rebuild
    every partial attachment.
    """
    seed_offer(db_conn, "Смартфон Honor X9d 12/256 ГБ, черный", "full")
    partial = seed_offer(db_conn, "Honor X9d 256 ГБ черный", "part", store="idea")
    cluster_offers(db_conn, identities_for(db_conn))
    assert attached_variant(db_conn, partial) is not None

    assert detach_drifted_offers(db_conn) == 0


def test_display_names_are_regenerated_not_frozen_at_creation(db_conn):
    """upsert_variant uses ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, so a variant's name is
    written once and never revisited. A correction to the generator would
    then apply only to products first seen afterwards and leave the existing
    catalogue on the old wording -- the same shape as the schema.sql header
    rule, where a change silently applies to fresh data but not production.
    """
    seed_offer(db_conn, "Смартфон Honor X9d 12/256 ГБ, черный", "n1")
    cluster_offers(db_conn, identities_for(db_conn))

    with db_conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute("UPDATE variant SET display_name = 'stale wording'")
    assert repo.refresh_display_names(db_conn) == 1

    with db_conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute("SELECT display_name FROM variant")
        assert cur.fetchone()[0] == "Смартфон Honor X9D 12/256 ГБ, Черный"

    # Idempotent: a catalogue already correct must report no changes.
    assert repo.refresh_display_names(db_conn) == 0


def test_an_offer_already_sitting_on_a_malformed_variant_is_evicted(db_conn):
    """The refusal must hold for a variant that predates it.

    An offer whose name still produces the malformed key AGREES with its
    stored variant, so the drift check saw no contradiction and kept it
    there. Live, that left one artefact variant --
    'Смартфон Apple iPhone 128 13 256 ГБ, Черный' -- still holding an offer
    after every other one had been repaired, because uzum's relevance sweep
    had not returned that SKU again and its old name_raw survived.
    """
    offer_id = seed_offer(db_conn, "Смартфон Apple iPhone 13 128 128/256 ГБ Черный", "old")
    # Build the malformed variant the way an earlier cycle would have.
    identity = identities_for(db_conn)[0]
    assert identity.key is not None and "128" in identity.key.model_tokens
    variant_id = repo.upsert_variant(db_conn, identity.key)
    repo.attach_offer_to_variant(db_conn, offer_id, variant_id)

    assert detach_drifted_offers(db_conn) == 1
    assert attached_variant(db_conn, offer_id) is None

    cluster_offers(db_conn, identities_for(db_conn))
    assert attached_variant(db_conn, offer_id) is None
    assert unresolved_reason(db_conn, offer_id) == REASON_MEMORY_IN_MODEL


def test_a_partial_key_cannot_resolve_onto_a_malformed_variant(db_conn):
    """The other way in. Refusing only at creation leaves partial resolution
    free to attach offers to a malformed variant that already exists.
    """
    bad = seed_offer(db_conn, "Смартфон Apple iPhone 13 128 128/256 ГБ Черный", "bad")
    identity = identities_for(db_conn)[0]
    variant_id = repo.upsert_variant(db_conn, identity.key)
    repo.attach_offer_to_variant(db_conn, bad, variant_id)

    # A vague listing whose partial key is compatible with that variant.
    vague = seed_offer(db_conn, "Apple iPhone 13 128 256 ГБ Черный", "vague", store="idea")
    cluster_offers(db_conn, [identify(r) for r in repo.load_unattached_offers(db_conn)])

    assert attached_variant(db_conn, vague) is None
