"""Offline parse tests for the radius client.

Fixture recorded live on 2026-08-11 with:
    POST https://new.api.radius.uz/graphql/
    {"query": CATEGORY_QUERY, "operationName": "CategoryProducts",
     "variables": {"slug": "konditsionery", "first": 100, "after": null}}
    Headers: Accept: application/json, Content-Type: application/json,
             Accept-Language: ru, Origin: https://radius.uz,
             Referer: https://radius.uz/,
             User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64)
             AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/150.0.0.0 Safari/537.36
"""
import json
import pathlib

import pytest

from narxnoma.sources.base import PRICE_MAX, PRICE_MIN
from narxnoma.sources.radius import _image, next_cursor, numeric_id, parse

FIXTURES = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "fixtures" / "sources"
FIXTURE = FIXTURES / "radius.json"

# A SECOND fixture, and it earns its place. `konditsionery` happens to have
# exactly one variant per product, so it cannot tell a per-product parser from
# a per-variant one -- the counts are identical. `smartfony` is where the
# distinction is real (20 products, 41 variants) and where getting it wrong
# cost 79 of 80 phone attachments. Recorded the same way with
# {"slug": "smartfony", "first": 20}.
PHONES = FIXTURES / "radius_phones.json"

# Copied from the first real node in the recorded file. The source key is the
# VARIANT id (8046), not the product id (5195) -- see radius.py.
KNOWN_SOURCE_KEY = "8046"
KNOWN_NAME = "Кондиционер Artel ARTSID2CW12BE Iceberg 12 Inv"
KNOWN_PRICE = 5_388_000
KNOWN_URL = ("https://radius.uz/ru/product/8046-"
             "konditsioner-artel-artsid2cw12be-iceberg-inv")


def payload():
    return json.loads(FIXTURE.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))


def phones():
    return json.loads(PHONES.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))


def nodes(doc):
    return [e["node"] for e in doc["data"]["category"]["products"]["edges"]]


def test_fixtures_exist_and_are_not_empty():
    """Guards against every test below passing vacuously over an empty file."""
    for path in (FIXTURE, PHONES):
        assert path.exists(), f"record the fixture first: {path}"
    assert nodes(payload())
    assert nodes(phones())


def test_parse_returns_listings():
    assert parse(payload()), "parse() found nothing in a real recorded response"


def test_one_listing_per_variant_not_per_product():
    """The measured decision this client turns on.

    Emitting one listing per Product attached 1 of 80 phones (1.3%): radius
    keeps the memory pair and the colour on the variant, and a phone key
    needs both. Asserted on the PHONES fixture, because `konditsionery` has
    one variant per product and cannot tell the two parsers apart.
    """
    doc = phones()
    variants = sum(len(n["variants"]) for n in nodes(doc))
    assert variants > len(nodes(doc)), (
        "this fixture must contain multi-variant products, or the test "
        "cannot tell products from variants")
    assert len(parse(doc)) == variants == 41
    assert len(nodes(doc)) == 20


def test_the_product_name_alone_could_not_key_a_phone():
    """Why the variant is the unit, stated as a property of the data.

    Every phone product whose variants differ has a name with no memory pair;
    the variant names carry one.
    """
    import re

    memory = re.compile(r"\d+\s*/\s*\d+\s*(?:GB|ГБ)", re.I)
    multi = [n for n in nodes(phones()) if len(n["variants"]) > 1]
    assert multi
    for node in multi:
        assert not memory.search(node["name"]), node["name"]
        for variant in node["variants"]:
            assert memory.search(variant["name"]), variant["name"]


def test_the_variants_of_one_phone_keep_their_own_prices():
    """"HUAWEI Nova Y61" spans 1,397,000 to 1,959,000 across its variants. A
    per-product parser would publish one of those as the price of all three."""
    doc = phones()
    node = next(n for n in nodes(doc) if len(n["variants"]) > 1)
    listings = {x.source_key: x for x in parse(doc)}
    prices = {listings[numeric_id(v["id"])].price for v in node["variants"]}
    assert len(prices) > 1, "pick a node whose variants differ in price"


def test_every_listing_has_provenance():
    for lst in parse(payload()):
        assert lst.store_slug == "radius"
        assert lst.source_key and lst.source_key.isdigit()
        assert lst.name_raw
        assert lst.url.startswith("https://radius.uz/ru/product/")


def test_every_price_is_an_integer_inside_the_fences():
    for lst in parse(payload()):
        assert isinstance(lst.price, int)
        assert PRICE_MIN <= lst.price <= PRICE_MAX


def test_source_keys_are_unique_within_one_response():
    keys = [lst.source_key for lst in parse(payload())]
    assert len(keys) == len(set(keys))


def test_a_known_product_parses_exactly():
    lst = next(x for x in parse(payload()) if x.source_key == KNOWN_SOURCE_KEY)
    assert lst.name_raw == KNOWN_NAME
    assert lst.price == KNOWN_PRICE
    assert lst.url == KNOWN_URL
    assert lst.availability == "IN_STOCK"


def test_the_name_comes_from_the_variant_not_the_product():
    doc = payload()
    node = nodes(doc)[0]
    assert node["name"] != node["variants"][0]["name"], (
        "pick a fixture node whose variant name differs, or this proves nothing")
    lst = next(x for x in parse(doc) if x.source_key == KNOWN_SOURCE_KEY)
    assert lst.name_raw == node["variants"][0]["name"]


def test_each_variant_gets_its_own_url_and_price():
    """Verified live: /ru/product/<non-default variant id>-<slug> returns 200
    and renders that colour."""
    doc = payload()
    for node in nodes(doc):
        for variant in node["variants"]:
            vid = numeric_id(variant["id"])
            lst = next(x for x in parse(doc) if x.source_key == vid)
            assert lst.url == f"https://radius.uz/ru/product/{vid}-{node['slug']}"
            assert lst.price == int(variant["priceAmount"])


def test_the_url_never_uses_the_product_id():
    """Building it from Product.id is a clean 404 on the live site -- checked
    on six products, all 404. See radius.py's module docstring."""
    doc = payload()
    for node in nodes(doc):
        pid = numeric_id(node["id"])
        for lst in parse({"data": {"category": {"products": {
                "edges": [{"node": node}]}}}}):
            assert f"/product/{pid}-" not in lst.url


def test_a_variant_without_its_own_price_falls_back_to_the_product():
    doc = payload()
    node = nodes(doc)[0]
    node["variants"][0]["priceAmount"] = None
    lst = next(x for x in parse(doc) if x.source_key == KNOWN_SOURCE_KEY)
    assert lst.price == int(
        node["pricing"]["priceRange"]["start"]["amount"])


def test_a_product_with_no_variants_yields_nothing():
    doc = payload()
    node = nodes(doc)[0]
    before = len(parse(doc))
    dropped = len(node["variants"])
    node["variants"] = []
    assert len(parse(doc)) == before - dropped
    assert KNOWN_SOURCE_KEY not in {x.source_key for x in parse(doc)}

def test_numeric_id_decodes_saleor_global_ids():
    assert numeric_id("UHJvZHVjdDo1MTk1") == "5195"              # Product:5195
    assert numeric_id("UHJvZHVjdFZhcmlhbnQ6ODA0Ng==") == "8046"  # ProductVariant:8046


def test_numeric_id_returns_none_rather_than_raising():
    """One malformed id must cost one listing, not the whole sweep."""
    for bad in (None, "", "not-base64!!", "aGVsbG8=", "UHJvZHVjdDo="):
        assert numeric_id(bad) is None

def test_availability_comes_from_the_variant_and_falls_back_to_the_product():
    doc = payload()
    ns = nodes(doc)
    ns[0]["variants"][0]["isAvailable"] = False
    ns[1]["variants"][0]["isAvailable"] = None
    ns[1]["isAvailable"] = True
    out = {x.source_key: x.availability for x in parse(doc)}
    assert out[KNOWN_SOURCE_KEY] == "OUT_OF_STOCK"
    assert out[numeric_id(ns[1]["variants"][0]["id"])] == "IN_STOCK"


def test_an_unset_flag_everywhere_is_unknown_not_out_of_stock():
    doc = payload()
    node = nodes(doc)[0]
    node["isAvailable"] = None
    node["variants"][0]["isAvailable"] = None
    lst = next(x for x in parse(doc) if x.source_key == KNOWN_SOURCE_KEY)
    assert lst.availability == "UNKNOWN", (
        "an unset field is not evidence of a sold-out product")


def test_next_cursor_ends_the_sweep_when_there_is_no_next_page():
    doc = payload()
    assert doc["data"]["category"]["products"]["pageInfo"]["hasNextPage"] is False
    assert next_cursor(doc) is None


def test_next_cursor_returns_the_cursor_when_there_is_a_next_page():
    doc = payload()
    page_info = doc["data"]["category"]["products"]["pageInfo"]
    page_info["hasNextPage"] = True
    page_info["endCursor"] = "YXJyYXljb25uZWN0aW9uOjk5"
    assert next_cursor(doc) == "YXJyYXljb25uZWN0aW9uOjk5"


def test_parse_reads_the_search_connection_too():
    """search() and sweep() share parse(); the two queries differ only in
    whether the connection hangs off `category` or off the root."""
    doc = payload()
    node = nodes(doc)[0]
    search_shaped = {"data": {"products": {"edges": [{"node": node}]}}}
    assert [x.source_key for x in parse(search_shaped)] == [
        numeric_id(v["id"]) for v in node["variants"]]


def test_parse_survives_an_empty_or_missing_payload():
    assert parse({"data": {"category": None}}) == []
    assert parse({}) == []
    assert parse(None) == []


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

#
# Saleor returns a thumbnail URL for every image, but radius's thumbnailer
# does not render .avif sources: the URL is well-formed, non-null, and 404s.
# Measured over all 274 live radius offers -- 272 thumbnails load, the 2 avif

def test_avif_thumbnails_are_replaced_by_the_original_that_exists():
    avif = ("https://new.api.radius.uz/thumbnails/200/images/product/"
            "31101cec018f49b29871c665b6aa7fde.avif")
    assert _image({"url": avif}) == (
        "https://new.api.radius.uz/media/images/product/"
        "31101cec018f49b29871c665b6aa7fde.avif")


@pytest.mark.parametrize("url", [
    "https://new.api.radius.uz/thumbnails/200/images/product/abc.webp",
    "https://new.api.radius.uz/thumbnails/512/images/product/abc.jpg",
    "https://new.api.radius.uz/thumbnails/200/images/product/abc.png",
])
def test_every_other_format_keeps_its_thumbnail(url):
    """272 of 274 work; only avif is swapped, so a grid keeps loading renders."""
    assert _image({"url": url}) == url


def test_a_missing_thumbnail_is_none_not_a_crash():
    assert _image(None) is None
    assert _image({}) is None
    assert _image({"url": ""}) is None


def test_the_fixtures_still_parse_to_reachable_looking_images():
    for path in (FIXTURE, PHONES):
        listings = parse(json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")))
        assert listings
        for l in listings:
            if l.image_url:
                assert l.image_url.startswith("https://new.api.radius.uz/")
                assert not (l.image_url.endswith(".avif")
                            and "/thumbnails/" in l.image_url)

"""radius's category map, its registration, and the GraphQL failure modes."""
import pytest

from narxnoma.matching.keys import CATEGORIES
from narxnoma.pipeline.report import EXPECTED_MIN_OFFERS
from narxnoma.sources import SOURCES
from narxnoma.sources.base import Listing, Source
from narxnoma.sources.radius import CATEGORY_SLUGS, RadiusSource


def test_category_slugs_cover_all_supported_categories():
    # Verified live 2026-08-11 by walking radius's whole tree through
    # `categories(level: 0)` and reading every totalCount.
    assert CATEGORY_SLUGS == {
        "smartphones": ("smartfony", "iphone-17-17-pro-17-pro-max-air", "iphone-air-3"),
        "televisions": ("televizory",),
        "laptops": ("noutbuki", "noutbuki-apple"),
        "acs": ("konditsionery",),
        "fridges": ("kholodilniki",),
        "washers": ("stiralnye-mashiny",),
        "ovens": ("gazovye-plity", "dukhovoi-shkaf"),
    }
    assert set(CATEGORY_SLUGS) == set(CATEGORIES)


def test_apple_products_are_swept_separately():
    """The trap this map exists for.

    radius files MacBooks and iPhones under a top-level "Apple" category, not
    under `noutbuki`/`smartfony`. Sweeping the obvious slug alone silently
    loses every Apple product -- including the iPhones, which are the
    most-compared phones in the catalogue, and whose absence looks exactly
    like a retailer that stopped selling them.
    """
    assert "noutbuki-apple" in CATEGORY_SLUGS["laptops"]
    assert any("iphone" in s for s in CATEGORY_SLUGS["smartphones"])


def test_radius_is_registered_and_satisfies_the_source_protocol():
    assert "radius" in SOURCES
    assert isinstance(SOURCES["radius"], Source)
    assert SOURCES["radius"].can_sweep is True


def test_radius_has_a_coverage_floor():
    assert EXPECTED_MIN_OFFERS["radius"] > 0


def test_every_registered_source_has_a_coverage_floor():
    assert set(SOURCES) <= set(EXPECTED_MIN_OFFERS)


def test_radius_is_seeded_in_the_schema():
    """harvest_all reports "store not seeded" for a source with no store row,
    and the migration-1 seed INSERT will never run again in production."""
    import pathlib

    schema = (pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
              / "narxnoma" / "db" / "schema.sql").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    _, _, appended = schema.partition(
        "INSERT INTO schema_version (version) VALUES (2)")
    assert "'radius'" in appended


def test_sweep_rejects_unknown_category():
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        list(RadiusSource().sweep(category="toasters"))


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# GraphQL reports failure with HTTP 200 and an `errors` key -- the uzum trap.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _node(pid_b64: str, name: str, variant_b64: str, price: int = 3_000_000):
    return {"node": {
        "id": pid_b64, "name": name, "slug": "x", "isAvailable": True,
        "brand": {"name": "Artel"}, "category": {"slug": "konditsionery"},
        "defaultVariant": {"id": variant_b64},
        "variants": [{"id": variant_b64, "name": name, "sku": "X",
                      "priceAmount": price, "currency": "UZS",
                      "isAvailable": True, "quantityAvailable": 5,
                      "thumbnail": {"url": "https://new.api.radius.uz/t.webp"}}],
        "pricing": {"priceRange": {"start": {"amount": price, "currency": "UZS"}}},
        "thumbnail": {"url": "https://new.api.radius.uz/t.webp"},
    }}


def _page(edges, has_next=False, cursor=None):
    return {"data": {"category": {"slug": "konditsionery", "products": {
        "totalCount": len(edges),
        "pageInfo": {"hasNextPage": has_next, "endCursor": cursor},
        "edges": edges}}}}


def test_a_graphql_errors_key_raises_rather_than_yielding_nothing(monkeypatch):
    """HTTP 200 with an `errors` key is how GraphQL reports failure. Swallowing
    it would record a half-swept category as a successful harvest of nothing --
    the one failure mode EXPECTED_MIN_OFFERS and harvest_run.ok exist to catch.
    """
    import narxnoma.sources.radius as mod

    monkeypatch.setattr(mod, "post_json", lambda *a, **k: {
        "errors": [{"message": "Cannot query field \"gross\" on type \"Money\"."}]})
    src = RadiusSource()
    src._get_session = lambda: None
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="GraphQL errors"):
        list(src.sweep(category="acs"))


def test_an_unknown_slug_raises_rather_than_yielding_nothing(monkeypatch):
    import narxnoma.sources.radius as mod

    monkeypatch.setattr(mod, "post_json", lambda *a, **k: {"data": {"category": None}})
    src = RadiusSource()
    src._get_session = lambda: None
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="no such category"):
        list(src.sweep(category="acs"))


def test_sweep_walks_the_cursor_to_the_end(monkeypatch):
    import narxnoma.sources.radius as mod

    pages = [
        _page([_node("UHJvZHVjdDox", "A", "UHJvZHVjdFZhcmlhbnQ6MTE=")],
              has_next=True, cursor="c1"),
        _page([_node("UHJvZHVjdDoy", "B", "UHJvZHVjdFZhcmlhbnQ6MjI=")]),
    ]
    seen_cursors = []

    def fake_post(session, url, json=None, **kw):
        seen_cursors.append(json["variables"]["after"])
        return pages[len(seen_cursors) - 1]

    monkeypatch.setattr(mod, "post_json", fake_post)
    src = RadiusSource()
    src._get_session = lambda: None

    out = list(src.sweep(category="acs"))
    # source_key is the VARIANT id: ProductVariant:11 and ProductVariant:22.
    assert [x.source_key for x in out] == ["11", "22"]
    assert seen_cursors == [None, "c1"], "the endCursor must be carried forward"
    assert all(x.category == "acs" for x in out)


def test_sweep_deduplicates_a_product_reached_through_two_slugs(monkeypatch):
    """`ovens` and `laptops` sweep two slugs each, and Saleor's
    Category.products includes descendants -- so the same product can arrive
    twice. source_key is the upsert key, so a duplicate would inflate
    HarvestResult.seen while writing one row."""
    import narxnoma.sources.radius as mod

    same = _node("UHJvZHVjdDo5", "Duxovka", "UHJvZHVjdFZhcmlhbnQ6OTk=")
    monkeypatch.setattr(mod, "post_json", lambda *a, **k: _page([same]))
    src = RadiusSource()
    src._get_session = lambda: None

    out = list(src.sweep(category="ovens"))     # two slugs, one product each
    assert [x.source_key for x in out] == ["99"]


def test_sweep_tags_listings_with_our_category(monkeypatch):
    import narxnoma.sources.radius as mod

    def fake_paginate(fetch, parse_page, following):
        yield Listing(store_slug="radius", source_key="1",
                      name_raw="Телевизор Artel UA43H3502",
                      price=4_000_000, url="https://radius.uz/ru/product/1-x",
                      category="smartphones")

    monkeypatch.setattr(mod, "paginate", fake_paginate)
    src = RadiusSource()
    src._get_session = lambda: None
    out = list(src.sweep(category="televisions"))
    assert len(out) == 1 and out[0].category == "televisions"

"""Offline parse tests for the texnomart client.

Fixture recorded live on 2026-07-31 with:
    GET https://gw.texnomart.uz/api/common/v1/search/result?q=smartfon&page=1&limit=20
    Headers: Accept: application/json, text/plain, */*, accept-device: web,
             accept-language: uz, accept-region: 2,
             Origin: https://texnomart.uz, Referer: https://texnomart.uz/,
             User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36
             (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/150.0.0.0 Safari/537.36
"""
import json
import pathlib

from narxnoma.matching.features import extract_features
from narxnoma.matching.keys import variant_key
from narxnoma.matching.sim import sim_kind
from narxnoma.sources.texnomart import parse
from narxnoma.sources.base import PRICE_MAX, PRICE_MIN

FIXTURE = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "fixtures" / "sources" / "texnomart.json"

# FIXTURE: copy these three from one real item in the recorded file.
KNOWN_SOURCE_KEY = "354792"
KNOWN_PRICE = 1727000            # in SUM, after any unit conversion
KNOWN_URL = "https://texnomart.uz/product/detail/354792/"


def payload():
    return json.loads(FIXTURE.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))


def test_fixture_exists_and_is_not_empty():
    """Guards against the parse tests passing vacuously over an empty file."""
    assert FIXTURE.exists(), f"record the fixture first: {FIXTURE}"
    assert payload()


def test_parse_returns_listings():
    listings = parse(payload())
    assert listings, "parse() found nothing in a real recorded response"


def test_every_listing_has_provenance():
    # A price we cannot attribute to a specific retailer listing is worthless.
    for lst in parse(payload()):
        assert lst.store_slug == "texnomart"
        assert lst.source_key
        assert lst.name_raw
        assert lst.url.startswith("http")


def test_every_price_is_an_integer_inside_the_fences():
    for lst in parse(payload()):
        assert isinstance(lst.price, int)
        assert PRICE_MIN <= lst.price <= PRICE_MAX


def test_source_keys_are_unique_within_one_response():
    # source_key is the upsert key; duplicates would silently collapse offers.
    keys = [lst.source_key for lst in parse(payload())]
    assert len(keys) == len(set(keys))


def test_known_product_parses_exactly():
    by_key = {lst.source_key: lst for lst in parse(payload())}
    assert KNOWN_SOURCE_KEY in by_key
    assert by_key[KNOWN_SOURCE_KEY].price == KNOWN_PRICE
    assert by_key[KNOWN_SOURCE_KEY].url == KNOWN_URL


def test_malformed_items_are_dropped_not_raised():
    # One bad item must never kill a sweep of several hundred.
    broken = payload()
    broken["data"]["products"].append({
        "id": 999999001,
        "name": None,
        "sale_price": 1500000,
        "old_price": 0,
    })
    broken["data"]["products"].append({
        "id": 999999002,
        "name": "Junk item with null price",
        "sale_price": None,
        "old_price": 0,
    })
    good_listings = parse(payload())
    good_keys = {lst.source_key for lst in good_listings}
    result_listings = parse(broken)   # must not raise even with the junk items above
    result_keys = {lst.source_key for lst in result_listings}
    assert good_keys <= result_keys
    assert "999999001" not in result_keys
    assert "999999002" not in result_keys
    # Neither junk item may leak through under some other key either -- pin the
    # count so a leak can't pass by coincidentally matching an existing key.
    assert len(result_listings) == len(good_listings)


def test_price_fence_drops_the_recorded_accessory():
    """Pin the one real drop in the recorded fixture, not just its count.

    The fixture holds 20 raw items but parse() yields 19. The missing one is
    id 88473, "Keramik himoya oynasi Redmi Note 9S" -- a ceramic screen
    protector priced at 4,000 SUM, well below the 100,000 SUM price fence.
    It's an accessory, not a phone, and the fence is correctly rejecting it.
    Asserting the specific key (not just a count) means this test still
    means something if the fixture is ever re-recorded and its size changes.
    """
    raw_items = payload()["data"]["products"]
    assert len(raw_items) == 20

    listings = parse(payload())
    assert len(listings) == 19

    parsed_keys = {lst.source_key for lst in listings}
    assert "88473" not in parsed_keys


def test_every_listing_yields_a_usable_identity():
    """name_raw is the clustering stage's ONLY handle on what a product is.

    See the uzum module's version of this test for why: a name that yields no
    identity is a product lost from the catalogue, silently and with every
    other test still green.

    BRAND is the non-negotiable part and texnomart meets it on all 19
    listings -- its titles lead with the brand ("OPPO Reno15 5G 12/512GB
    Aurora White Smartfoni").

    FULLY KEYABLE: 17 of 19. The two that fall short, both investigated
    rather than assumed:
      - "Vivo Y11d 4/256GB Platinum" -- "platinum" is not in COLOR_MAP, so no
        colour resolves and colour is a hard identity field. A vocabulary
        gap, not a texnomart defect: the name is well formed and every other
        field extracts.
      - "OPPO Reno15 5G 12/512GB Aurora White Smartfoni" -- brand, RAM,
        storage and colour all extract, but `model_tokens` comes out EMPTY,
        because "reno15" is 7 characters of mixed letters and digits and
        `extract_features` treats any such token of length >= 5 as an SKU
        code ("sm-a175f", "a075f") rather than a designator. Written as
        "Reno 15" the same listing keys fine. That is a matching-engine
        limitation rather than a data limitation, and it is reported as such
        -- deliberately NOT fixed here, since changing the SKU heuristic
        touches every source's identity at once.
    """
    features = [(lst, extract_features(lst.name_raw)) for lst in parse(payload())]

    brandless = [lst.name_raw for lst, f in features if not f.brand]
    assert not brandless, f"no brand recoverable, so unclusterable: {brandless}"

    keyable = [lst for lst, f in features if variant_key(f, sim_kind(lst.name_raw))]
    # Pinned to the measured value so any regression fails rather than drifts.
    assert len(keyable) == 17, [
        lst.name_raw for lst, f in features if not variant_key(f, sim_kind(lst.name_raw))
    ]

"""Texnomart category-aware sweep (Plan 5): query + allow-list mapping."""
from narxnoma.sources.base import Listing
from narxnoma.sources.texnomart import CATEGORY_KEEP_WORD, CATEGORY_QUERY, TexnomartSource


def test_category_maps_cover_all_supported_categories():
    # texnomart names its results in Uzbek (Latin): Televizori, Noutbuki,
    # Konditsioneri, Muzlatgichi, "Kir yuvish mashinasi", Duxovkasi.
    assert CATEGORY_QUERY == {
        "smartphones": "smartfon",
        "televisions": "televizor",
        "laptops": "noutbuk",
        "acs": "konditsioner",
        "fridges": "xolodilnik",
        "washers": "stiraln",
        "ovens": "duxovka",
    }
    assert CATEGORY_KEEP_WORD["televisions"] == "televizor"
    assert CATEGORY_KEEP_WORD["fridges"] == "muzlatgich"  # Uzbek, not Russian
    assert CATEGORY_KEEP_WORD["washers"] == "kir yuvish"


def test_sweep_allow_lists_by_category_word_and_tags():
    src = TexnomartSource()
    src._paginate = lambda q: [
        Listing(store_slug="texnomart", source_key="1", name_raw="Televizor Premier 43PRM700S",
                price=4_000_000, url="https://texnomart.uz/x", category="smartphones"),
        Listing(store_slug="texnomart", source_key="2", name_raw="Samsung Galaxy A26",
                price=3_000_000, url="https://texnomart.uz/x", category="smartphones"),
    ]
    out = list(src.sweep(category="televisions"))
    assert [l.source_key for l in out] == ["1"]
    assert out[0].category == "televisions"


def test_sweep_rejects_unknown_category():
    src = TexnomartSource()
    try:
        list(src.sweep(category="toasters"))
        assert False, "expected ValueError"
    except ValueError:
        pass

"""Offline parse tests for the uzum client.

Fixture recorded live on 2026-08-01 with:
    Step 1a - mint an anonymous token:
        POST https://id.uzum.uz/api/auth/token
        Headers: Accept: */*, Accept-Language: ru-RU (required),
                 Content-Type: application/json,
                 Referer: https://uzum.uz/ (required),
                 User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36
                 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/150.0.0.0 Safari/537.36,
                 x-iid: <uuid4>
        Body: {}
        Response: 204 No Content; token read from the Set-Cookie: access_token=<JWT> header.

    Step 1b - the makeSearch query itself:
        POST https://graphql.uzum.uz/
        Headers: Authorization: Bearer <token>, Content-Type: application/json,
                 apollographql-client-name: web-customers,
                 apollographql-client-version: 1.63.2, x-iid: <same uuid4>,
                 city-id: 1, Origin: https://uzum.uz, Referer: https://uzum.uz/,
                 User-Agent: <as above>
        Body: {"query": "<getMakeSearch, see docs/parsers/uzum.md section 3>",
               "variables": {"q": {"text": "Samsung", "showAdultContent": "TRUE",
                                    "filters": [], "sort": "BY_RELEVANCE_DESC",
                                    "pagination": {"offset": 0, "limit": 72}}}}

The live call reported total=565 for "Samsung" and returned 72 items on this
page; saved verbatim except trimmed to the first 20 items (26 SKUs across
them) so the fixture stays readable. No Accept-Language was sent on the
graphql call itself (not in the required-header set -- see
docs/parsers/uzum.md section 2), so the recorded card titles and
characteristic keys came back in Uzbek ("Smartfonlar Android", "Xotira",
"Rang") rather than the Russian shown in the doc's examples -- category
FILTERING still works because it keys on category.id (15271), not the
locale-dependent title text.
"""
import json
import pathlib

import pytest
import requests

from narxnoma.matching import extract_features, variant_key
from narxnoma.sources import uzum
from narxnoma.sources.base import PRICE_MAX, PRICE_MIN
from narxnoma.sources.uzum import _build_name_raw, _card_image, _char_kind, _items, parse

FIXTURE = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "fixtures" / "sources" / "uzum.json"

# FIXTURE: copy these three from one real item in the recorded file.
# productId 1978967, skuId 6998861 -- the SKU whose characteristicValues state
# its own memory ("Xotira": "8/256GB") while the card TITLE also lists both
# "6/128" and "8/256" for the sibling SKU -- i.e. the live instance of the
# exact card-range-vs-SKU trap docs/parsers/uzum.md section 5b warns about.
KNOWN_SOURCE_KEY = "6998861"
KNOWN_PRICE = 3068010            # sellPrice, in SUM -- NOT fullPrice (10000000)
KNOWN_URL = "https://uzum.uz/ru/product/1978967"
KNOWN_NAME_RAW = "Smartfon Samsung Galaxy A17 4G 8/256GB Qora"


def payload():
    return json.loads(FIXTURE.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))


def test_fixture_exists_and_is_not_empty():
    """Guards against the parse tests passing vacuously over an empty file."""
    assert FIXTURE.exists(), f"record the fixture first: {FIXTURE}"
    assert payload()


def test_parse_returns_listings():
    listings = parse(payload())
    assert listings, "parse() found nothing in a real recorded response"


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Product photos.
#
# uzum published none at all -- 5,461 offers, the largest source in the
# catalogue, every one imageless -- because SEARCH_QUERY never asked for
# `photos`. Recorded separately from uzum.json rather than by re-recording it,
# because that file pins the SKU-memory-vs-card-title trap on specific ids and
# re-recording would throw that evidence away to test something unrelated.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

PHOTOS_FIXTURE = FIXTURE.with_name("uzum_photos.json")


def photos_payload():
    return json.loads(PHOTOS_FIXTURE.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))


def test_every_uzum_listing_carries_a_photo():
    listings = parse(photos_payload())
    assert len(listings) > 50, "fixture too small to be evidence"
    missing = [l.source_key for l in listings if not l.image_url]
    assert not missing, f"{len(missing)} listings with no image_url"


def test_photo_urls_are_uzum_cdn_renders_not_originals():
    """PRODUCT_540 is a card-sized render; ORIGINAL would be a full-res file.

    Also pins that `high` is a plain URL string. Both facts come from the live
    schema: `photos.link` requires a `trans:` argument, so getting this wrong
    is a 400 at query time rather than a null at read time.
    """
    for l in parse(photos_payload()):
        assert l.image_url.startswith("https://images.uzum.uz/")
        assert "t_product_540_high" in l.image_url


def test_each_listing_takes_the_photo_of_the_card_it_came_from():
    """Every SKU on a card shares that card's photo -- and no other card's.

    Written first as "all SKUs of one productId share one photo", which
    FAILED: makeSearch returns one card per COLOUR, so a productId arrives as
    several cards with different pictures. That is the stronger, better
    property (see _card_image) and this is the version that states it.
    """
    items = _items(photos_payload())
    assert len(items) > 50
    for item in items:
        expected = _card_image(item["catalogCard"])
        single = {"data": {"makeSearch": {"items": [item]}}}
        built = parse(single)
        for l in built:
            assert l.image_url == expected, l.source_key


def test_uzum_splits_one_product_into_a_card_per_colour():
    """The reason a photo is colour-accurate rather than merely model-accurate.

    Pinned because it is the assumption _card_image rests on: if uzum ever
    collapses colours onto one card, the picture stops matching the variant
    and this test is where that shows up.
    """
    items = _items(photos_payload())
    by_product: dict[int, list[dict]] = {}
    for item in items:
        card = item["catalogCard"]
        by_product.setdefault(card["productId"], []).append(card)
    multi = {p: cards for p, cards in by_product.items() if len(cards) > 1}
    assert multi, "fixture no longer has a product split across cards"
    for cards in multi.values():
        images = {_card_image(c) for c in cards}
        assert len(images) == len(cards), (
            "two cards of the same product share a photo, so the split is no "
            "longer by colour")


def test_a_card_without_photos_yields_no_image_rather_than_raising():
    """The old fixture predates the field; parse must survive its absence."""
    listings = parse(payload())
    assert listings
    assert all(l.image_url is None for l in listings)

def test_known_product_parses_exactly():

def test_url_never_carries_skuid():
    """The outbound-link bug (2026-08-10): uzum's 302 meta-refresh builds
    id.uzum.uz/api/auth/redirect?redirectUrl=<product>?skuId=<id> with the
    nested query raw, and the auth endpoint answers that malformed parameter
    with a conflict JSON. The human-facing URL is the canonical product page;
    SKU identity stays in source_key.
    """
    for lst in parse(payload()):
        assert "?" not in lst.url, lst.url
        assert lst.url.startswith("https://uzum.uz/ru/product/"), lst.url
        assert lst.source_key in ("6998861", "6998862") or lst.source_key.isdigit()


def test_known_product_uses_sellprice_not_fullprice():
    """The headline trap: fullPrice (10,000,000 for this SKU) is a
    struck-through fantasy figure -- sellPrice (3,068,010) is the real one.
    Read the raw integer straight out of the fixture, not a synthetic number.
    """
    raw_item = next(
        it for it in payload()["data"]["makeSearch"]["items"]
        if it["catalogCard"]["productId"] == 1978967
    )
    raw_sku = next(
        s for s in raw_item["catalogCard"]["skuList"] if s["id"] == 6998861
    )
    assert raw_sku["sellPrice"] == 3068010
    assert raw_sku["fullPrice"] == 10000000
    by_key = {lst.source_key: lst for lst in parse(payload())}
    assert by_key[KNOWN_SOURCE_KEY].price == raw_sku["sellPrice"]


def test_known_product_name_raw_strips_the_cards_other_memory_tiers():
    """docs/parsers/uzum.md section 5b: the card title for productId 1978967
    lists BOTH "6/128" and "8/256" ("...Galaxy A17 4G, 6/128, 8/256,..."),
    but this SKU (skuId 6998861) states its own memory ("8/256GB" via the
    "Xotira" characteristic). name_raw must reflect the SKU's own spec, not
    let the card's overall range leak in -- this is the exact bug that once
    reported 2,672,010 for a phone whose true price was 3,068,010.
    """
    by_key = {lst.source_key: lst for lst in parse(payload())}
    name = by_key[KNOWN_SOURCE_KEY].name_raw
    assert name == KNOWN_NAME_RAW
    assert "6/128" not in name
    assert "8/256GB" in name


def test_raw_carries_untouched_card_title_and_characteristic_values():
    """The clustering stage must be able to redo name-building without
    re-crawling -- so the untouched card title and the SKU's full
    characteristicValues list must survive into Listing.raw verbatim.
    """
    by_key = {lst.source_key: lst for lst in parse(payload())}
    lst = by_key[KNOWN_SOURCE_KEY]
    assert lst.raw["card_title"] == (
        "Smartfon Samsung Galaxy A17 4G, 6/128, 8/256, sAMOLED 90 Hz, 50 Mp, 5000 mA/h, 25 Вт"
    )
    assert lst.raw["characteristic_values"] == [
        {"title": "8/256GB", "characteristic": {"title": "Xotira"}},
        {"title": "Qora", "characteristic": {"title": "Rang"}},
    ]


def test_malformed_items_are_dropped_not_raised():
    # One bad item must never kill a sweep of several hundred.
    broken = payload()
    items = broken["data"]["makeSearch"]["items"]
    items.append({
        "catalogCard": {
            "__typename": "SkuGroupCard",
            "productId": 9999901,
            "title": "Junk item with null price",
            "category": {"id": 15271, "title": "Smartfonlar Android"},
            "skuList": [
                {"id": 99999011, "sellPrice": None, "fullPrice": None,
                 "availableAmount": 5, "characteristicValues": []},
            ],
        }
    })
    items.append({

            "__typename": "SkuGroupCard",
            "productId": 9999902,

            "category": {"id": 15272, "title": "iOS"},
            "skuList": [
                {"id": 99999021, "sellPrice": 5000000, "fullPrice": 5000000,
                 "availableAmount": 5, "characteristicValues": []},
            ],
        }
    })
    good_keys = {lst.source_key for lst in parse(payload())}
    result_keys = {lst.source_key for lst in parse(broken)}   # must not raise
    assert good_keys <= result_keys
    assert "99999011" not in result_keys
    assert "99999021" not in result_keys


def test_errors_key_returns_empty_list_not_raise():
    """GraphQL signals failure as HTTP 200 with an `errors` key, not an HTTP
    error status (docs/parsers/uzum.md section 2). parse() must recognise
    that shape and return [] rather than raising or returning garbage --
    the live client (UzumSource._fetch_payload) is what raises on this, so a broken
    sweep call is loud instead of silently looking like an empty brand.
    """
    broken_response = {
        "data": None,
        "errors": [{"message": "HTTP fetch failed from 'search-gateway': 4.."}],
    }
    assert parse(broken_response) == []


def test_off_category_items_are_dropped():

def test_zero_stock_sku_is_kept_as_out_of_stock():
    """Deliberate inversion of docs/parsers/uzum.md section 4 ("filter to
    availableAmount > 0; zero-stock SKUs are phantom listings"): that
    instruction was written for a target-driven matcher hunting one phone.
    This is an aggregator cataloguing everything -- a zero-stock SKU is a
    real observation (this seller is out of this variant right now), so it
    is kept with availability="OUT_OF_STOCK" rather than dropped. None of
    this recording's real SKUs happen to be zero-stock, so covered
    synthetically.
    """
    broken = payload()
    items = broken["data"]["makeSearch"]["items"]
    items.append({
        "catalogCard": {
            "__typename": "SkuGroupCard",
            "productId": 7777701,
            "title": "Smartfon Samsung Galaxy Zero Stock Test",
            "category": {"id": 15271, "title": "Smartfonlar Android"},
            "skuList": [
                {"id": 77777011, "sellPrice": 2500000, "fullPrice": 2500000,
                 "availableAmount": 0, "characteristicValues": []},
            ],
        }
    })
    by_key = {lst.source_key: lst for lst in parse(broken)}
    assert "77777011" in by_key
    assert by_key["77777011"].availability == "OUT_OF_STOCK"


def test_esim_only_variant_is_kept():
    """Deliberate inversion of docs/parsers/uzum.md section 6: that section
    screens eSIM-only variants OUT because they were the wrong answer to a
    specific target query. Here an eSIM-only iPhone is a legitimate, separate
    offer at a genuinely different price, so it must be recorded, not
    dropped -- with whatever SIM information exists surviving into raw for
    the clustering stage to use later. None of this recording's real items
    are iPhones with SIM characteristics, so covered synthetically.
    """
    broken = payload()
    items = broken["data"]["makeSearch"]["items"]
    items.append({
        "catalogCard": {
            "__typename": "SkuGroupCard",
            "productId": 6666601,
            "title": "Apple smartfon iPhone 17 Air 256GB, 512GB, 1TB, eSIM",
            "category": {"id": 15272, "title": "iOS"},
            "skuList": [
                {"id": 66666011, "sellPrice": 18099000, "fullPrice": 18099000,
                 "availableAmount": 4,
                 "characteristicValues": [
                     {"title": "17 Air 256GB (eSIM)", "characteristic": {"title": "Модель"}},
                     {"title": "e-SIM", "characteristic": {"title": "Сим-карта"}},
                 ]},
            ],
        }
    })
    by_key = {lst.source_key: lst for lst in parse(broken)}
    assert "66666011" in by_key
    lst = by_key["66666011"]
    sim_values = [
        cv["title"] for cv in lst.raw["characteristic_values"]
        if "sim" in cv["characteristic"]["title"].lower() or "сим" in cv["characteristic"]["title"].lower()
    ]
    assert sim_values == ["e-SIM"]


def test_parsed_count_is_pinned_to_the_recording():
    """Pin how many of the recorded items survive parsing.

    Retailer responses mix phones with accessories, and the price fence
    silently drops the accessories -- correctly, but silently. Without this
    assertion a change to PRICE_MIN or coerce_price could turn a 4,000 SUM
    screen protector into a catalogue entry and no test would fail.

    This recording is 20 catalogCards / 26 SKUs total (some cards carry more
    than one SKU -- see docs/parsers/uzum.md section 5). All 20 cards are
    category 15271 (Android); every SKU has a positive sellPrice well inside
    [PRICE_MIN, PRICE_MAX] (1,490,000-13,000,000 SUM), a non-empty
    characteristicValues-or-title-derived name, and a valid id. Nothing in
    this recording trips a fence or a required-field check, so all 26 SKUs
    survive try_build_listing -- 0 dropped.
    """
    raw_items = payload()["data"]["makeSearch"]["items"]
    raw_sku_count = sum(len(it["catalogCard"].get("skuList") or []) for it in raw_items)
    parsed = parse(payload())
    assert len(raw_items) == 20
    assert raw_sku_count == 26
    assert len(parsed) == 26   # nothing dropped in this recording


def test_every_listing_yields_a_usable_identity():
    """name_raw is the clustering stage's ONLY handle on what a product is.

    Nothing downstream re-reads the retailer's response: clustering is
    handed `name_raw` and must recover, at minimum, the brand and the
    storage tier from it. A name that cannot yield both is not a slightly
    worse name -- it is a product that silently drops out of the catalogue,
    because there is no key to file it under and no error to notice.

    The whole test suite passed while two of these 26 listings parsed to
    "Smartfon Samsung Galaxy A16 <colour>" -- brand-only, no memory at all
    -- because every other test asserted that name_raw was *non-empty*, not
    that it was *usable*. This asserts usable.

    RAM is deliberately not asserted: `scan_memory` suppresses RAM for Apple
    on purpose (Apple publishes none, so any figure came from a reseller's
    wording), so a correct iPhone name legitimately yields ram_gb=None.
    Brand and storage have no such exemption.
    """
    unkeyable = []
    for lst in parse(payload()):
        features = extract_features(lst.name_raw)
        if not (features.brand and features.storage_gb):
            unkeyable.append((lst.source_key, lst.name_raw, lst.raw["card_title"]))
    assert not unkeyable, (
        "these listings cannot be keyed by the clustering stage and would be "
        f"lost from the catalogue: {unkeyable}"
    )


def test_char_kind_classifies_every_observed_key():
    """docs/parsers/uzum.md section 7's observed-key list, exercised.

    `RAM/ROM` was named in that list from the start and still classified as
    "other" -- `normalize` folds it to "ram rom", which no prefix test
    recognised -- so every SKU keyed that way lost its memory value in
    silence. Listing the key in the doc is not the same as handling it; this
    is the test that makes the two agree.
    """
    expected = {
        "memory": [
            "Память", "память", "ПАМЯТЬ", "Памят:", "Память:", "Памяьт:",
            "памяять", "Память ", "Объем памяти", "Xotirasi", "RAM/ROM",
            # from the 2026-08-01 live recording
            "Xotira", "Xotira:", "XOTIRA", "xotra",
        ],
        "model": ["Модель", "модел"],
        "sim": ["Сим-карта", "SIM карта", " SIM карта"],
        "color": ["Цвет", "Rang"],
        # `Тип` is genuinely ambiguous and `16 PRO MAX` is a value being used
        # as a key -- neither identifies a field we read, so "other" is the
        # correct answer, not a miss.
        "other": ["Тип", "16 PRO MAX"],
    }
    for kind, keys in expected.items():
        for key in keys:
            assert _char_kind(key) == kind, f"{key!r} classified as {_char_kind(key)!r}"


def test_ram_rom_key_memory_value_reaches_name_raw():
    """The end-to-end consequence of the _char_kind gap above: a `RAM/ROM`
    key classified as "other" means the memory never reaches name_raw.
    """
    broken = payload()
    broken["data"]["makeSearch"]["items"].append({
        "catalogCard": {
            "__typename": "SkuGroupCard",
            "productId": 5555501,
            "title": "Smartfon Xiaomi Redmi Note 14, 6.7 AMOLED, 50Mp",
            "category": {"id": 15271, "title": "Smartfonlar Android"},
            "skuList": [
                {"id": 55555011, "sellPrice": 2900000, "fullPrice": 2900000,
                 "availableAmount": 3,
                 "characteristicValues": [
                     {"title": "8/256GB", "characteristic": {"title": "RAM/ROM"}},
                     {"title": "Qora", "characteristic": {"title": "Rang"}},
                 ]},
            ],
        }
    })
    by_key = {lst.source_key: lst for lst in parse(broken)}
    assert by_key["55555011"].name_raw == "Smartfon Xiaomi Redmi Note 14 8/256GB Qora"


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# _build_name_raw unit tests. Arguments are (card_title, model_v, mem_v,
# color_v) exactly as _parse_sku passes them.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def test_name_raw_model_override_keeps_the_brand_not_the_noun():
    """The Critical: a `Модель` override used to destroy the name.

    Only the card head's FIRST WORD was kept as a prefix, and on uzum that
    word is very often the product-type noun "Smartfon"/"Смартфон" -- 10 of
    this recording's 20 cards lead that way. The brand was thrown away and a
    meaningless noun kept in its place. Compounding it, the section 5b
    memory strip was applied to the Модель value itself, deleting the SKU's
    own storage tier -- the one figure section 5b exists to protect. The
    pair produced "Smartfon A16 Qora": brand, RAM and storage all gone.
    """
    name = _build_name_raw(
        "Smartfon Samsung Galaxy A16, 4/128 GB, 2 SIM", "A16 8/256", "", "Qora"
    )
    assert name == "Samsung Galaxy A16 8/256 Qora"
    features = extract_features(name)
    assert features.brand == "samsung"
    assert features.ram_gb == 8
    assert features.storage_gb == 256
    # The card's own 4/128 range must not follow the SKU's 8/256 in.
    assert "4/128" not in name


def test_name_raw_iphone_card_keeps_the_brand_word_without_repeating_the_model():
    """An `IPhone`-prefixed card: the head supplies the brand the bare
    Модель value lacks, and the head words the Модель already states
    ("17", "Pro/Pro", "Max") are dropped rather than duplicated.
    """
    name = _build_name_raw(
        "IPhone 17 Pro/Pro Max, 256, 512, 1 ТБ, 2 ТБ", "17 Pro Max 256 GB", "", ""
    )
    assert name == "IPhone 17 Pro Max 256 GB"
    features = extract_features(name)
    assert features.brand == "apple"
    assert features.storage_gb == 256


def test_name_raw_recovers_memory_stated_after_the_first_comma():
    """Section 5a truncates the card title at the first comma, but two of
    this recording's 26 listings state their memory just AFTER that comma
    and carry no memory characteristic -- so both parsed to a name with no
    RAM and no storage, unkeyable, while the figure sat untouched in
    raw["card_title"]. When neither the SKU nor the truncated head yields
    memory, the full title is searched and the match appended.
    """
    name = _build_name_raw(
        "Smartfon Samsung Galaxy A16, 4/128 GB, 2 SIM, Super AMOLED, kamera 50 Mp",
        "", "", "Qora",
    )
    assert name == "Smartfon Samsung Galaxy A16 4/128 GB Qora"
    features = extract_features(name)
    assert (features.ram_gb, features.storage_gb) == (4, 128)


def test_name_raw_sku_memory_wins_over_the_cards_range():
    """docs/parsers/uzum.md section 5b, the trap that once reported
    2,672,010 for a phone whose true price was 3,068,010: the card head
    lists the range "(8+8)/128 GB", this SKU states "8/128". The card's
    figures are stripped from the head; the SKU's own value stands. The
    strip must not leave "( )/" residue behind either -- SKU 6931382 in the
    fixture parsed to "Smartfon Oppo A5i Pro ( )/ 8/128 Binafsha".
    """
    name = _build_name_raw(
        "Smartfon Oppo A5i Pro (8+8)/128 GB, oq/binafsha, IP65", "", "8/128", "Binafsha"
    )
    assert name == "Smartfon Oppo A5i Pro 8/128 Binafsha"
    assert "(" not in name and ")" not in name


def test_name_raw_keeps_a_trailing_plus_model_marker():
    """The residue cleanup strips orphaned separators, but "Pro+" is a real
    designator, not residue -- dropping the "+" merges the Pro+ into the Pro.
    """
    name = _build_name_raw(
        "Telefon Xiaomi Redmi Note 14 Pro+, 8/256GB", "Note 14 Pro+", "12/512", ""
    )
    assert name == "Xiaomi Redmi Note 14 Pro+ 12/512"


def test_name_raw_bare_sku_memory_blocks_the_card_title_recovery():
    """A bare memory figure IS a stated memory, and must switch off the
    last-resort recovery just as "8/256" does.

    _has_memory only ever recognised a slash-separated pair or a
    unit-bearing figure, so `Память: "128"` looked like NO memory at all --
    and the recovery then reached past the first comma and appended the
    card's whole RANGE beside the SKU's own correct figure. Live: card
    'Смартфон "Apple iPhone" 12, 64/128/256 ГБ, SIM' with Память "128"
    became 'Смартфон "Apple iPhone" 12 128 64/128 Алый', whose storage read
    128 while "64" became a MODEL token -- a product that does not exist.
    """
    name = _build_name_raw(
        'Смартфон "Apple iPhone" 12, 64/128/256 ГБ, SIM, чехол в подарок',
        "", "128", "Алый",
    )
    assert "64/128" not in name
    assert name == 'Смартфон "Apple iPhone" 12 128 Алый'
    features = extract_features(name)
    assert features.storage_gb == 128
    assert "64" not in features.model_tokens


def test_name_raw_bare_memory_inside_a_model_value_strips_the_card_range():
    """The same blindness on section 5b's own gate rather than the recovery.

    The strip of the card-derived prefix is gated on the SKU having stated
    memory; with `Модель: "17 Pro 256"` the figure is bare, so the gate
    never fired and the card's range survived in the prefix. Live, that
    produced 'IPhone / Max 256/512 GB 17 Pro 256 Оранжевый' -- storage 512
    from the card, "256" demoted to a model token, and three different SKUs
    (Pro 256, Pro Max 256, Pro 512) merged onto one variant.
    """
    name = _build_name_raw(
        "IPhone 17 Pro / Max 256/512 GB, E-Sim только,  Apple", "17 Pro 256", "", "Оранжевый"
    )
    assert "256/512" not in name
    features = extract_features(name)
    assert features.storage_gb == 256
    assert features.model_tokens == frozenset({"17", "pro"})


def test_name_raw_does_not_inherit_the_cards_other_bundled_model():
    """A card bundling two models must not lend the SKU the one it is not.

    'IPhone 17 Pro / Max' bundles the Pro and the Pro Max. _prefix_for_model
    dropped only the head words the Модель value already contained, so for
    the plain '17 Pro 256' SKU the word "Max" survived into the prefix and
    the offer keyed as a Pro MAX. Once a head word belongs to the model, the
    Модель value owns the rest of the head.
    """
    name = _build_name_raw(
        "IPhone 17 Pro / Max 256/512 GB, E-Sim только,  Apple", "17 Pro 256", "", "Оранжевый"
    )
    assert "Max" not in name
    assert extract_features(name).model_tokens == frozenset({"17", "pro"})

    # ...and the Pro Max SKU on the very same card still keeps its Max.
    sibling = _build_name_raw(
        "IPhone 17 Pro / Max 256/512 GB, E-Sim только,  Apple",
        "17 Pro Max 512", "", "Оранжевый",
    )
    assert extract_features(sibling).model_tokens == frozenset({"17", "pro", "max"})
    assert extract_features(sibling).storage_gb == 512


def test_name_raw_strips_a_chained_memory_range_whole():
    """A card listing three tiers leaves the last one behind.

    The strip consumed exactly two figures, so "12/256/512" lost "12/256"
    and left "512" standing in the head. Live, that made
    'Samsung Galaxy S25 Edge 512 12/256 Голубой' -- the bare-pair scan then
    read the card's 512 as the capacity and demoted the SKU's own 256 to a
    model token, which is the leak inverted rather than fixed.
    """
    name = _build_name_raw(
        "Samsung Galaxy S25 Edge 12/256/512, гарантия 1 год, зарегистрирован в IMIE",
        "", "12/256", "Голубой",
    )
    assert name == "Samsung Galaxy S25 Edge 12/256 Голубой"
    features = extract_features(name)
    assert (features.ram_gb, features.storage_gb) == (12, 256)
    assert "512" not in features.model_tokens


def test_name_raw_strips_a_hyphen_separated_memory_range():
    """uzum sellers also write the RAM-ROM pair with a hyphen.

    "(4-64/4-128)" matched no memory pattern at all, so the strip chewed out
    the middle and left "POCO C81 Pro (4- -128) 4/64" -- the card's 128 then
    beat the SKU's own 64 as the capacity.
    """
    name = _build_name_raw("POCO C81 Pro (4-64/4-128)", "4/64", "", "Черный")
    assert name == "POCO C81 Pro 4/64 Черный"
    features = extract_features(name)
    assert (features.ram_gb, features.storage_gb) == (4, 64)


def test_name_raw_refuses_to_recover_a_range_from_the_card_title():
    """The recovery may only take a SPEC, never a RANGE.

    A pair is a RAM/storage spec when its smaller figure is a plausible RAM
    size ("4/128", "12/256"); when both figures are capacities ("128/256",
    "256/512") it is the card's range across the SKUs it bundles, and it
    identifies nothing. This SKU states no memory of its own and the card
    offers only a range, so the honest result is a name with no capacity --
    which the clustering stage then refuses, rather than publishing a price
    under a product picked by coin toss.
    """
    name = _build_name_raw(
        "Смартфон Apple iPhone 13, 128/256GB, SIM+eSIM, чехол в подарок", "", "", "Синий"
    )
    assert "128/256" not in name
    assert extract_features(name).storage_gb is None
    assert variant_key(extract_features(name), "dual") is None


def test_name_raw_recovery_still_fires_when_the_sku_states_nothing():
    """The recovery is switched off by a STATED memory, not disabled.

    A SKU with no memory characteristic and no figure in its Модель value
    still has nothing but the card title to go on, which is the case the
    recovery was built for.
    """
    name = _build_name_raw(
        "Smartfon Samsung Galaxy A16, 4/128 GB, 2 SIM, Super AMOLED", "", "", "Qora"
    )
    assert name == "Smartfon Samsung Galaxy A16 4/128 GB Qora"

def test_undecodable_token_cookie_does_not_raise():
    """The JWT `exp` only decides WHEN to refresh. If uzum ever hands back an
    opaque or reformatted access_token cookie, a decode crash would kill the
    whole sweep over a token that may well still work.
    """
    exp = uzum._decode_jwt_exp("not-a-jwt")
    assert exp > 0
    assert uzum._decode_jwt_exp("") > 0


def test_401_mid_sweep_remints_once_and_retries(monkeypatch):
    """A server-side revocation is invisible to the cache, which refreshes
    only on the locally decoded `exp`. Before this, the resulting 401
    propagated an HTTPError straight out of sweep() and ended the run.
    """
    monkeypatch.setattr(uzum, "_token_cache", {"token": None, "iid": None, "exp": 0})
    mints = []

    def fake_mint():
        mints.append(1)
        return f"token-{len(mints)}", "iid"

    monkeypatch.setattr(uzum, "_mint_token", fake_mint)
    monkeypatch.setattr(uzum, "_decode_jwt_exp", lambda token: 2 ** 31)

    calls = []

    def fake_post_json(session, url, **kwargs):
        calls.append(kwargs["headers"]["Authorization"])
        if len(calls) == 1:
            response = requests.Response()
            response.status_code = 401
            raise requests.HTTPError("401 Unauthorized", response=response)
        return {"data": {"makeSearch": {"total": 0, "items": []}}}

    monkeypatch.setattr(uzum, "post_json", fake_post_json)
    source = uzum.UzumSource()
    monkeypatch.setattr(source, "_get_session", lambda: None)

    assert source._fetch_payload("Samsung", 0) == {
        "data": {"makeSearch": {"total": 0, "items": []}}
    }
    assert calls == ["Bearer token-1", "Bearer token-2"]   # re-minted, not reused


def test_second_401_is_left_to_raise(monkeypatch):
    """One retry, not a loop: a persistent 401 is a real auth failure and
    must surface rather than being swallowed into an empty sweep.
    """
    monkeypatch.setattr(uzum, "_token_cache", {"token": None, "iid": None, "exp": 0})
    monkeypatch.setattr(uzum, "_mint_token", lambda: ("token", "iid"))
    monkeypatch.setattr(uzum, "_decode_jwt_exp", lambda token: 2 ** 31)

    def always_401(session, url, **kwargs):
        response = requests.Response()
        response.status_code = 401
        raise requests.HTTPError("401 Unauthorized", response=response)

    monkeypatch.setattr(uzum, "post_json", always_401)
    source = uzum.UzumSource()
    monkeypatch.setattr(source, "_get_session", lambda: None)

    with pytest.raises(requests.HTTPError):
        source._fetch_payload("Samsung", 0)


def test_non_401_http_error_is_not_retried(monkeypatch):
    """Only 401 means "token"; a 500 must not trigger a pointless re-mint."""
    monkeypatch.setattr(uzum, "_token_cache", {"token": None, "iid": None, "exp": 0})
    mints = []

    def fake_mint():
        mints.append(1)
        return "token", "iid"

    monkeypatch.setattr(uzum, "_mint_token", fake_mint)
    monkeypatch.setattr(uzum, "_decode_jwt_exp", lambda token: 2 ** 31)

    def always_500(session, url, **kwargs):
        response = requests.Response()
        response.status_code = 500
        raise requests.HTTPError("500 Server Error", response=response)

    monkeypatch.setattr(uzum, "post_json", always_500)
    source = uzum.UzumSource()
    monkeypatch.setattr(source, "_get_session", lambda: None)

    with pytest.raises(requests.HTTPError):
        source._fetch_payload("Samsung", 0)
    assert len(mints) == 1


def test_a_spaced_hyphen_is_prose_not_a_memory_separator():
    """The hyphen separator must be TIGHT, or it eats the model number.

    Found in branch review. Widening the separator class to catch uzum's
    "(4-64/4-128)" also matched "70 - 2" in
    "REALME NOTE 70 - 2 дня работы от одной зарядки", so the strip deleted
    the model number and left the battery figure behind: the offer keyed as
    'realme note 6300 /128', with 6300 мАч standing in for the model. Two
    live offers were affected, and the capacity guard cannot catch it --
    6300 is not a capacity, so the variant looks perfectly well-formed.

    Worse than a lost offer: another retailer's Realme Note 70 keys
    correctly, so the two never merge and the offer pool splits.
    """
    card = "Новый Смартфон REALME NOTE 70 - 2 дня работы от одной зарядки, 6300 мАч"
    name = _build_name_raw(card, "", "4/128", "Черный")
    assert "70" in extract_features(name).model_tokens
    assert extract_features(name).storage_gb == 128


def test_a_tight_hyphen_is_still_a_memory_separator():
    """The case the widening was for must keep working."""
    name = _build_name_raw("POCO C81 Pro (4-64/4-128)", "4/64", "", "Черный")
    assert name == "POCO C81 Pro 4/64 Черный"
    assert extract_features("Samsung Galaxy A17 4GB-128GB Qora").storage_gb == 128

"""Uzum category-aware parse/sweep (Plan 5): id mapping + tagging."""
from narxnoma.sources.base import Listing
from narxnoma.sources.uzum import CATEGORY_IDS, parse


def test_category_ids_cover_all_supported_categories():
    # Verified live 2026-08-10 via makeSearch per product type, then RE-verified
    # the same day while fixing the category crawl frontier. Two ids were
    # missing, both confirmed by reading catalogCard.category off a live
    # response:
    #   13 Газовые плиты  -- "газовая плита" returns 72/72 under id 13, not 11,
    #      so every gas cooker uzum sells was fetched and then filtered out.
    #   83 Морозильники   -- the Uzbek "muzlatgich" resolves to FREEZERS here
    #      ("холодильник"/"sovutgich" reach id 82), and freezers belong with
    #      fridges for the same reason cookers belong with ovens.
    assert CATEGORY_IDS == {
        "smartphones": {15271, 15272},
        "televisions": {12601},
        "laptops": {12520},
        "acs": {14373},
        "fridges": {82, 83},
        "washers": {15291, 15296},
        "ovens": {11, 13},
    }


def _payload_with(category_id):
    return {
        "data": {
            "makeSearch": {
                "items": [
                    {
                        "catalogCard": {
                            "category": {"id": category_id, "title": "X"},
                            "productId": 1,
                            "title": "Телевизор Samsung",
                            "skuList": [
                                {"id": 10, "sellPrice": 4000000, "fullPrice": 5000000,
                                 "availableAmount": 1, "characteristicValues": []}
                            ],
                        }
                    }
                ]
            }
        }
    }


def test_parse_filters_and_tags_by_category():
    out = parse(_payload_with(12601), category="televisions")
    assert len(out) == 1 and out[0].category == "televisions"
    # A smartphone in the same payload is dropped for the televisions sweep.
    assert len(parse(_payload_with(15271), category="televisions")) == 0


def test_parse_defaults_to_smartphones():
    out = parse(_payload_with(15271))
    assert len(out) == 1 and out[0].category == "smartphones"


def test_parse_rejects_unknown_category():
    try:
        parse(_payload_with(1), category="toasters")
        assert False, "expected ValueError"
    except ValueError:
        pass

"""Head-to-head: uzprice's headline price vs our variant-exact price.

For each of the 20 target pages we independently query all 7 sources, score every
candidate with our matcher, and keep only exact variant matches (brand + model +
RAM + storage + colour, with the reverse model-token check and eSIM screening).
"""
import json, os, sys, time, traceback

import requests

S = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
sys.path.insert(0, S)
sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8")

from matcher import ACCEPT_THRESHOLD, extract_features, robust_median, score_match, why
import sources

targets = json.load(open(os.path.join(S, "targets.json"), encoding="utf-8"))
session = requests.Session()
results = []

for idx, t in enumerate(targets, 1):
    name = t["name"]
    tf = extract_features(name)
    print("[%2d/20] %s" % (idx, name[:70]))
    print("        target: brand=%s ram=%s storage=%s colors=%s model=%s"
          % (tf["brand"], tf["ram"], tf["storage"], sorted(tf["colors"]), sorted(tf["model_tokens"])))

    per_store, audit = {}, []
    for store, fn in sources.CLIENTS.items():
        try:
            cands = fn(session, name)
        except Exception as e:
            print("        %-10s ERROR %s" % (store, str(e)[:90]))
            continue
        kept = []
        for c in cands:
            cf = extract_features(c["name"])
            sc = score_match(tf, cf)
            if sc >= ACCEPT_THRESHOLD:
                kept.append(dict(c, score=sc))
            audit.append({"store": store, "name": c["name"], "price": c["price"],
                          "score": sc, "why": why(tf, cf) if sc < ACCEPT_THRESHOLD else "OK"})
        if kept:
            best = min(kept, key=lambda x: x["price"])
            per_store[store] = {"min": best["price"], "url": best["url"],
                                "matched_name": best["name"], "n": len(kept),
                                "all": sorted(x["price"] for x in kept)}
        print("        %-10s %3d cand -> %2d exact %s"
              % (store, len(cands), len(kept),
                 "min {:,}".format(per_store[store]["min"]) if store in per_store else ""))
        time.sleep(0.2)

    shared = {k: v for k, v in per_store.items() if k in
              {"alifshop", "idea", "olcha", "texnomart", "mediapark"}}
    extra = {k: v for k, v in per_store.items() if k in {"uzum", "beemarket"}}

    uz_med = None
    if "uzum" in per_store:
        uz_med, _ = robust_median(per_store["uzum"]["all"])

    row = {
        "name": name, "slug": t["slug"], "storeCount": t["storeCount"],
        "uzprice_headline": t["headline"], "uzprice_headline_from": t["headline_from"],
        "uzprice_headline_store": t["headline_store"],
        "uzprice_colour_exact": t["exact_min"],
        "ours_shared_min": min((v["min"] for v in shared.values()), default=None),
        "ours_shared_store": min(shared, key=lambda k: shared[k]["min"]) if shared else None,
        "ours_all_min": min((v["min"] for v in per_store.values()), default=None),
        "ours_all_store": min(per_store, key=lambda k: per_store[k]["min"]) if per_store else None,
        "ours_all_url": (per_store[min(per_store, key=lambda k: per_store[k]["min"])]["url"]
                         if per_store else None),
        "uzum_min": extra.get("uzum", {}).get("min"),
        "uzum_median": uz_med,
        "uzum_url": extra.get("uzum", {}).get("url"),
        "beemarket_min": extra.get("beemarket", {}).get("min"),
        "per_store": {k: v["min"] for k, v in per_store.items()},
    }
    results.append(row)
    json.dump(audit, open(os.path.join(S, "audit_%02d.json" % idx), "w", encoding="utf-8"),
              ensure_ascii=False)
    print("        => ours(shared)={} ours(all)={} uzprice={}\n".format(
        "{:,}".format(row["ours_shared_min"]) if row["ours_shared_min"] else "-",
        "{:,}".format(row["ours_all_min"]) if row["ours_all_min"] else "-",
        "{:,}".format(row["uzprice_headline"])))

json.dump(results, open(os.path.join(S, "results.json"), "w", encoding="utf-8"),
          ensure_ascii=False, indent=1)
print("wrote results.json")

"""Scan uzprice's own API for pages where the headline price comes from a
different colour variant than the page's own title.

Selection rule fixed in advance (no cherry-picking): among ALL multi-store
smartphone products, keep those where the offers pool >=2 resolvable colours AND
the cheapest offer's colour differs from the page's colour. Then take the 20 with
the highest storeCount -- i.e. their most comparison-rich, most visible pages.
"""
import json, os, sys, time, urllib.request

S = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
sys.path.insert(0, S)
sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8")
from matcher import extract_features

UA = "Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/150.0.0.0 Safari/537.36"


def get(path):
    req = urllib.request.Request("https://uzprice.uz" + path, headers={"User-Agent": UA})
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=60) as r:
        return json.load(r)


items = json.load(open(os.path.join(S, "smartphones.json"), encoding="utf-8"))
seen, uniq = set(), []
for i in items:
    if i["id"] not in seen:
        seen.add(i["id"]); uniq.append(i)

multi = [i for i in uniq if (i.get("storeCount") or 0) >= 2]
multi.sort(key=lambda i: -(i.get("storeCount") or 0))
print("scanning %d multi-store products..." % len(multi))

defects = []
for k, p in enumerate(multi):
    try:
        offs = get("/api/v1/products/%s/offers" % p["slug"])
    except Exception as e:
        print("  skip", p["slug"], e); continue
    if not offs:
        continue
    page_col = extract_features(p["canonicalName"])["colors"]
    cols = set()
    for o in offs:
        cols |= extract_features(o.get("variantCanonicalName") or "")["colors"]
    cheapest = min(offs, key=lambda o: o["price"])
    ch_col = extract_features(cheapest.get("variantCanonicalName") or "")["colors"]

    if len(cols) >= 2 and page_col and ch_col and not (page_col & ch_col):
        exact = [o for o in offs
                 if extract_features(o.get("variantCanonicalName") or "")["colors"] & page_col]
        defects.append({
            "slug": p["slug"], "name": p["canonicalName"], "brand": p.get("brand"),
            "storeCount": p.get("storeCount"), "headline": p["minPrice"],
            "headline_from": cheapest.get("variantCanonicalName"),
            "headline_store": cheapest["store"]["slug"],
            "colors_pooled": sorted(cols), "page_color": sorted(page_col),
            "n_offers": len(offs),
            "exact_min": min((o["price"] for o in exact), default=None),
            "exact_store": (min(exact, key=lambda o: o["price"])["store"]["slug"] if exact else None),
            "n_exact": len(exact),
        })
    time.sleep(0.28)
    if (k + 1) % 40 == 0:
        print("  ...%d scanned, %d defects" % (k + 1, len(defects)))

print("\n%d of %d multi-store pages show the defect (%.0f%%)"
      % (len(defects), len(multi), len(defects) / len(multi) * 100))

json.dump(defects, open(os.path.join(S, "defects_all.json"), "w", encoding="utf-8"), ensure_ascii=False, indent=1)
top = defects[:20]
json.dump(top, open(os.path.join(S, "targets.json"), "w", encoding="utf-8"), ensure_ascii=False, indent=1)
print("\n=== 20 selected (highest storeCount) ===")
for d in top:
    err = ""
    if d["exact_min"]:
        diff = d["exact_min"] - d["headline"]
        err = "  understates by {:+,} ({:.1f}%)".format(diff, diff / d["headline"] * 100)
    print("%-58s st=%d off=%2d  headline=%9s from %-22s %s"
          % (d["name"][:56], d["storeCount"], d["n_offers"], "{:,}".format(d["headline"]),
             (d["headline_from"] or "")[:22], err))
