FILE: narxnoma-web/components/SearchBox.tsx
================================================
"use client";

import { useRouter } from "next/navigation";
import { useCallback, useEffect, useRef, useState } from "react";
import { useLang } from "./LangProvider";
import { price, t } from "@/lib/i18n";

interface Suggestion {
  slug: string;
  display_name: string;
  min_price: number | null;
  store_count: number;
}

/** How long to wait after the last keystroke before asking the server. */
const DEBOUNCE_MS = 220;

/**
 * The search box.
 *
 * TWO THINGS THIS GOT WRONG, both worth stating because neither is visible
 * from reading the component alone.
 *
 * 1. THE DROPDOWN USED TO OPEN BY ITSELF. Its effect ran on mount, and on
 *    /search the box is pre-filled with the current query, so the effect
 *    fetched suggestions and called setOpen(true) with `document.activeElement`
 *    still BODY -- nobody had focused, clicked or typed anything. The panel is
 *    640x374 and sits directly over the sort bar, so `elementFromPoint` at the
 *    sort buttons returned a suggestion link. Every click meant to change the
 *    sort order landed on a product instead. That is the entire "sort and the
 *    sidebar filters do not work" report: the handlers were always fine, the
 *    clicks never reached them.
 *
 *    So the panel now opens only after a real interaction (`touched`), and
 *    closes on Escape, on pick, and on a click outside.
 *
 * 2. THE URL ONLY CHANGED ON SUBMIT. Typing narrowed nothing until Enter, and
 *    the address bar never reflected what was on screen, so a result could not
 *    be linked or reloaded. `onQuery` now fires on every (debounced) keystroke;
 *    the search page uses it to rewrite ?q= and refetch in place. Without that
 *    prop -- the home page -- the box still navigates on submit, because there
 *    is nothing on the home page to update live.
 */
export default function SearchBox({
  initial = "",
  big = false,
  onQuery,
  resumeTyping = false,
}: {
  initial?: string;
  big?: boolean;
  /** Called with the typed text, debounced. Present only where the page can
   *  re-render results in place. */
  onQuery?: (q: string) => void;
  /** The reader was mid-word on another page; take the caret back. */
  resumeTyping?: boolean;
}) {
  const router = useRouter();
  const lang = useLang();
  const [q, setQ] = useState(initial);
  const [sugg, setSugg] = useState<Suggestion[]>([]);
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
  const [brands, setBrands] = useState<string[]>([]);
  const timer = useRef<ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | null>(null);
  const wrap = useRef<HTMLDivElement | null>(null);
  const input = useRef<HTMLInputElement | null>(null);
  /** False until the user focuses or types. Nothing may open before it. */
  const touched = useRef(false);
  /** Latest onQuery, so the debounce effect need not depend on its identity. */
  const emit = useRef(onQuery);
  emit.current = onQuery;

  // Follow the query when the page itself changes it (back/forward, or a
  // fresh server render). Skipped while the user is typing, so their caret is
  // never yanked out from under them.
  useEffect(() => {
    if (!touched.current) setQ(initial);
  }, [initial]);

  useEffect(() => {
    if (timer.current) clearTimeout(timer.current);
    if (!touched.current) return; // never act on the value we were handed
    const query = q.trim();

    timer.current = setTimeout(async () => {
      if (emit.current) {
        emit.current(query);
      } else if (query.length >= 2) {
        // No results on this page to update in place (the home page), so the
        // only way for the address bar to follow the typing is to go where
        // the results are. Done once, on the way to /search; from there the
        // page updates itself and the URL never navigates again.
        //
        // `?typing=1` asks the search page to focus its box and put the caret
        // at the end, so a word begun here can be finished there. Without it
        // the hop lands on a fresh input and swallows the rest of the word.
        router.push(`/search?q=${encodeURIComponent(query)}&typing=1`);
        return;
      }
      if (query.length < 2) {
        setSugg([]);
        setBrands([]);
        setOpen(false);
        return;
      }
      try {
        const r = await fetch(`/api/suggest?q=${encodeURIComponent(query)}`);
        if (!r.ok) return;
        const j = await r.json();
        setSugg(j.variants ?? []);
        setBrands(j.brands ?? []);
        setOpen((j.variants ?? []).length > 0 || (j.brands ?? []).length > 0);
      } catch {
        /* offline: suggestions are a nicety */
      }
    }, DEBOUNCE_MS);

    return () => {
      if (timer.current) clearTimeout(timer.current);
    };
  }, [q, router]);

  // Arriving from the home page mid-word: take the caret back so the rest of
  // the word lands in the box rather than nowhere.
  useEffect(() => {
    if (!resumeTyping) return;
    const el = input.current;
    if (!el) return;
    touched.current = true;
    el.focus();
    const end = el.value.length;
    try {
      el.setSelectionRange(end, end);
    } catch {
      /* type=search does not always allow selection ranges */
    }
  }, [resumeTyping]);

  // Close when the click lands anywhere else. `onBlur` alone was not enough:
  // it never fires for a panel that was opened without focus.
  useEffect(() => {
    if (!open) return;
    const onDown = (e: MouseEvent) => {
      if (!wrap.current?.contains(e.target as Node)) setOpen(false);
    };
    document.addEventListener("mousedown", onDown);
    return () => document.removeEventListener("mousedown", onDown);
  }, [open]);

  const submit = useCallback(
    (e?: React.FormEvent) => {
      e?.preventDefault();
      const query = q.trim();
      setOpen(false);
      if (onQuery) {
        // The page updates in place; do not navigate out from under it.
        if (timer.current) clearTimeout(timer.current);
        onQuery(query);
        return;
      }
      router.push(query ? `/search?q=${encodeURIComponent(query)}` : "/search");
    },
    [q, router, onQuery]
  );

  return (
    <div className="searchbox-wrap" ref={wrap}>
      <form className="searchbox" onSubmit={submit} role="search">
        <input
          ref={input}
          type="search"
          value={q}
          onChange={(e) => {
            touched.current = true;
            setQ(e.target.value);
          }}
          onFocus={() => {
            touched.current = true;
          }}
          onKeyDown={(e) => {
            if (e.key === "Escape") setOpen(false);
          }}
          placeholder={
            lang === "uz"
              ? "Smartfon, model yoki brend — masalan, iPhone 17"
              : "Смартфон, модель или бренд — например, iPhone 17"
          }
          aria-label={t(lang, "search.ph")}
          autoFocus={big}
        />
        <button type="submit">{t(lang, "search.go")}</button>
      </form>
      {open && (sugg.length > 0 || brands.length > 0) && (
        <div className="suggest">
          {brands.length > 0 && (
            <>
              <div className="s-brand">{lang === "uz" ? "Brendlar" : "Бренды"}</div>
              {brands.map((b) => (
                <a key={b} href={`/search?q=${encodeURIComponent(b)}`}>
                  <span className="s-name">{b}</span>
                </a>
              ))}
            </>
          )}
          {sugg.map((s) => (
            <a key={s.slug} href={`/p/${s.slug}`}>
              <span className="s-name">{s.display_name}</span>
              <span className="s-meta">
                {" "}
                · {lang === "uz" ? "dan" : "от"} {price(lang, s.min_price)} ·{" "}
                {s.store_count} {lang === "uz" ? "do'kon" : "магазинов"}
              </span>
            </a>
          ))}
        </div>
      )}
    </div>
  );
}

FILE: narxnoma-web/components/SearchClient.tsx
================================================
"use client";

import { useCallback, useEffect, useRef, useState } from "react";
import Facets from "./Facets";
import InfiniteGrid from "./InfiniteGrid";
import SearchBox from "./SearchBox";
import { useLang } from "./LangProvider";
import { plural, t } from "@/lib/i18n";
import type { SearchResult } from "@/lib/queries";

const SORTS = ["relevance", "price_asc", "price_desc", "stores"] as const;

/**
 * SSR-first search: the server renders `initialResult` (SEO + first paint),
 * then this component takes over. A query, facet or sort change fetches
 * /api/search and swaps the results without a full navigation; the URL is
 * updated in place so the view stays shareable.
 */
export default function SearchClient({
  initialResult,
  initialQs,
  initialRawQ,
  resumeTyping = false,
}: {
  initialResult: SearchResult;
  initialQs: string;
  initialRawQ: string;
  resumeTyping?: boolean;
}) {
  const lang = useLang();
  const [res, setRes] = useState<SearchResult>(initialResult);
  const [qs, setQs] = useState(initialQs);
  const [rawQ, setRawQ] = useState(initialRawQ);
  const [loading, setLoading] = useState(false);
  const [error, setError] = useState<string | null>(null);
  const seq = useRef(0); // drop out-of-order responses

  // A server render for a NEW url must win over whatever we are holding.
  // useState only reads its argument on mount, so without this a soft
  // navigation to /search?q=… re-renders the server component and leaves this
  // component showing the previous query's results.
  useEffect(() => {
    setRes(initialResult);
    setQs(initialQs);
    setRawQ(initialRawQ);
    seq.current += 1; // cancel anything in flight for the old url
  }, [initialResult, initialQs, initialRawQ]);

  const apply = useCallback(async (nextQs: string) => {
    const id = ++seq.current;
    // history.replaceState (not router.replace): a client navigation from
    // router.replace suspends the route transition and leaves the fetch and
    // this component stuck (observed: loading never clears, URL never
    // updates, despite the server returning both 200s). replaceState keeps
    // the URL shareable with zero navigation; results update in place.
    window.history.replaceState(null, "", `/search?${nextQs}`);
    setQs(nextQs);
    setLoading(true);
    setError(null);
    try {
      const r = await fetch(`/api/search?${nextQs}`);
      if (!r.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${r.status}`);
      const j = (await r.json()) as SearchResult;
      if (seq.current === id) setRes(j);
    } catch (e) {
      if (seq.current === id)
        setError(e instanceof Error ? e.message : "не удалось обновить выдачу");
    } finally {
      if (seq.current === id) setLoading(false);
    }
  }, []);

  // Re-sync if the user navigates (back/forward) to a different query string.
  useEffect(() => {
    const sync = () => {
      const q = window.location.search.replace(/^\?/, "");
      if (q !== qs) {
        setQs(q);
        setRawQ(new URLSearchParams(q).get("q") ?? "");
        fetch(`/api/search?${q}`)
          .then((r) => r.json())
          .then((j) => setRes(j as SearchResult))
          .catch(() => {});
      }
    };
    window.addEventListener("popstate", sync);
    return () => window.removeEventListener("popstate", sync);
  }, [qs]);

  const qsFor = useCallback(
    (patch: Record<string, string | null>) => {
      const sp = new URLSearchParams(qs);
      for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(patch)) {
        if (v == null || v === "") sp.delete(k);
        else sp.set(k, v);
      }
      sp.delete("page"); // any change resets paging
      return sp.toString();
    },
    [qs]
  );

  // Every keystroke (debounced inside SearchBox) rewrites ?q= and refetches,
  // so the address bar always describes what is on screen.
  const onQuery = useCallback(
    (typed: string) => {
      if (typed === rawQ) return;
      setRawQ(typed);
      apply(qsFor({ q: typed || null }));
    },
    [apply, qsFor, rawQ]
  );

  // The grid drives its own paging, so it gets the filters without `page`.
  const gridQs = (() => {
    const sp = new URLSearchParams(qs);
    sp.delete("page");
    return sp.toString();
  })();

  const pager =
    res.pages > 1 ? (
      <div className="pager">
        {Array.from({ length: res.pages }, (_, i) => i + 1)
          .slice(Math.max(0, res.page - 3), Math.min(res.pages, res.page + 2))
          .map((p) => (
            <button
              key={p}
              className={p === res.page ? "cur" : ""}
              onClick={() => apply(qsFor({ page: String(p) }))}
              type="button"
            >
              {p}
            </button>
          ))}
      </div>
    ) : null;

  return (
    <>
      <div style={{ padding: "18px 0 4px" }}>
        <SearchBox initial={rawQ} onQuery={onQuery} resumeTyping={resumeTyping} />
      </div>
      <div className="search-layout">
        <details className="facets-mobile">
          <summary>{t(lang, "facet.filters")}</summary>
          <Facets f={res.facets} applied={res.applied} q={qs} onApply={apply} />
        </details>
        <Facets
          f={res.facets}
          applied={res.applied}
          q={qs}
          onApply={apply}
          className="facets-desktop"
        />
        <section>
          <div className="result-head">
            <h2>
              {res.applied.q
                ? `«${rawQ}» — ${plural(lang, res.total, "natija", "результат", "результата", "результатов")}`
                : plural(lang, res.total, "model", "модель", "модели", "моделей")}
              {loading && <span className="count"> · {t(lang, "res.updating")}</span>}
            </h2>
            <span className="count">{t(lang, "stat.updated")}</span>
          </div>
          <div className="sort-bar">
            {SORTS.map((key) => (
              <button
                key={key}
                className={res.applied.sort === key ? "on" : ""}
                onClick={() =>
                  apply(qsFor({ sort: key === "relevance" ? null : key }) || "")
                }
                type="button"
              >
                {t(lang, `sort.${key}`)}
              </button>
            ))}
          </div>

          {error && <div className="banner">Не удалось обновить выдачу: {error}</div>}

          {res.hits.length === 0 ? (
            <div className="empty">
              <p>{t(lang, "res.empty", { q: rawQ })}</p>
              <p style={{ marginTop: 8 }}>{t(lang, "res.emptyHint")}</p>
            </div>
          ) : (
            <InfiniteGrid
              initialHits={res.hits}
              initialPage={res.page}
              pages={res.pages}
              total={res.total}
              qs={gridQs}
              pagerFallback={pager}
            />
          )}
        </section>
      </div>
    </>
  );
}

import { Pool } from "pg";

declare global {
  // eslint-disable-next-line no-var
  var __narxnomaPool: Pool | undefined;
}

// One pool per process; Next dev hot-reloads modules, so guard against leaks.
export const pool: Pool =
  global.__narxnomaPool ??
  new Pool({
    connectionString:
      process.env.DATABASE_URL ??
      "postgresql://narxnoma@127.0.0.1:55432/narxnoma",
    max: 10,
    connectionTimeoutMillis: 5000,
    statement_timeout: 10_000,
  });

if (process.env.NODE_ENV !== "production") global.__narxnomaPool = pool;

export async function query<T extends object>(
  text: string,
  params: unknown[] = []
): Promise<T[]> {
  const res = await pool.query(text, params);
  return res.rows as T[];
}

/** Idempotent schema bits the web owns (click log for /api/out). */
export async function ensureWebSchema(): Promise<void> {
  await query(`
    CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS outbound_click (
      id          bigint GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
      offer_id    uuid NOT NULL,
      variant_id  uuid,
      store_id    uuid,
      referer     text,
      clicked_at  timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
    )
  `);
}

// RU formatting helpers: prices, plurals, relative time. Every number rendered
// on a page goes through here so JetBrains Mono + narrow-NBSP grouping is
// applied in exactly one place.

const NBSP = "\u202F"; // narrow no-break space for digit grouping

export function formatPrice(sum: number | null | undefined): string {
  if (sum == null) return "—";
  const digits = Math.abs(sum)
    .toString()
    .replace(/\B(?=(\d{3})+(?!\d))/g, NBSP);
  return `${digits}\u00A0сум`;
}

/** Pluralisation: pluralRu(3, "магазин", "магазина", "магазинов") -> "3 магазина" */
export function pluralRu(
  n: number,
  one: string,
  few: string,
  many: string
): string {
  const abs = Math.abs(n) % 100;
  const d = abs % 10;
  if (abs >= 11 && abs <= 19) return `${n}\u00A0${many}`;
  if (d === 1) return `${n}\u00A0${one}`;
  if (d >= 2 && d <= 4) return `${n}\u00A0${few}`;
  return `${n}\u00A0${many}`;
}

export function timeAgoRu(ts: string | Date | null | undefined): string {
  if (!ts) return "никогда";
  const then = new Date(ts).getTime();
  const diffMs = Date.now() - then;
  if (diffMs < 0) return "только что";
  const min = Math.floor(diffMs / 60_000);
  if (min < 1) return "только что";
  if (min < 60) return pluralRu(min, "мин назад", "мин назад", "мин назад");
  const h = Math.floor(min / 60);
  if (h < 24) return pluralRu(h, "час назад", "часа назад", "часов назад");
  const d = Math.floor(h / 24);
  if (d === 1) return "вчера";
  return pluralRu(d, "день назад", "дня назад", "дней назад");
}

export function formatDateRu(ts: string | Date | null | undefined): string {
  if (!ts) return "—";
  return new Date(ts).toLocaleString("ru-RU", {
    day: "numeric",
    month: "long",
    hour: "2-digit",
    minute: "2-digit",
  });
}

/** Availability strings used by the crawler (offer.availability). */
export type Availability = "IN_STOCK" | "OUT_OF_STOCK" | "UNKNOWN";

export function availabilityRu(a: string | null | undefined): {
  label: string;
  cls: string;
} {
  switch (a) {
    case "IN_STOCK":
      return { label: "в наличии", cls: "in-stock" };
    case "OUT_OF_STOCK":
      return { label: "нет в наличии", cls: "out-of-stock" };
    case "UNKNOWN":
      return { label: "наличие не указано", cls: "unknown" };
    default:
      return { label: "—", cls: "unknown" };
  }
}

import { query } from "./db";

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Types
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

export interface VariantHit {
  id: string;
  slug: string;
  brand: string;
  display_name: string;
  ram_gb: number | null;
  // Nullable outside smartphones by design: a television has no storage, no
  // colour identity and no SIM. The columns were relaxed to NULL when
  // categories landed; these types still claimed non-null, which is how a
  // refrigerator card came to print "eSIM".
  storage_gb: number | null;
  color: string | null;
  sim_kind: string | null;
  category: string;
  min_price: number | null;
  median_price: number | null;
  max_price: number | null;
  offer_count: number;
  in_stock_offer_count: number;
  store_count: number;
  computed_at: string;
  latest_offer_at: string | null;
  image_url: string | null;
  brand_rank: number;
  pos: number;
}

export interface FacetValue {
  value: string | number;
  count: number;
  min_price?: number | null;
}

export interface SearchResult {
  hits: VariantHit[];
  total: number;
  page: number;
  pages: number;
  facets: {
    brands: FacetValue[];
    colors: FacetValue[];
    rams: (number | null)[];
    ramCounts: Record<string, number>;
    priceBands: { lo: number; hi: number; count: number }[];
    priceMin: number | null;
    priceMax: number | null;
  };
  applied: {
    q: string | null;
    brands: string[];
    colors: string[];
    rams: number[];
    priceLo: number | null;
    priceHi: number | null;
    multiStore: boolean;
    sort: string;
  };
}

export type SortKey = "relevance" | "price_asc" | "price_desc" | "stores";

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Query normalisation: brand synonyms (UZ/RU colloquial -> catalogue brand)
// and noise words. Users type "айфон 17", "реди ноут 15", "смартфон".
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

// Synonym targets MUST be the words that actually appear in display_name
// ("Apple iPhone 17 Pro"), because search is a substring match over it.
// Mapping "айфон" -> "apple" silently returned 0 results for "айфон 17".
const BRAND_SYNONYMS: Record<string, string> = {
  айфон: "iphone",
  iphone: "iphone",
  редми: "redmi",
  реди: "redmi",
  рилми: "realme",
  самсунг: "samsung",
  хуавей: "huawei",
  хонор: "honor",
  виво: "vivo",
  инфеникс: "infinix",
  инфиникс: "infinix",
  оппо: "oppo",
  моторола: "motorola",
  техно: "tecno",
  тecno: "tecno",
  асус: "asus",
  гугл: "google",
  галакси: "galaxy",
  галакcи: "galaxy",
  // Category nouns. display_name is generated in Russian and ALWAYS opens
  // with one ("Телевизор 7Tech 7TV4G55QLEDKS1"), so these are the most
  // searchable words in the catalogue -- they used to be discarded as noise,
  // which is why "смартфон" matched nothing while every phone was named one.
  телефон: "смартфон",
  смартфон: "смартфон",
  smartfon: "смартфон",
  telefon: "смартфон",
  televizor: "телевизор",
  noutbuk: "ноутбук",
  laptop: "ноутбук",
  konditsioner: "кондиционер",
  muzlatgich: "холодильник",
  duxovka: "духовой",
  pechka: "духовой",
};

/**
 * The query, split into the tokens a row must ALL contain.
 *
 * Search used to match `display_name LIKE '%<the whole query>%'`, which made
 * word order and adjacency mandatory: "iphone 256" found 0 of the 186 rows
 * that hold both words, and "asus vivobook 15" found 5 of 26. Users do not
 * type catalogue names in catalogue order.
 */
export function queryTokens(raw: string): string[] {
  const q = raw
    .toLowerCase()
    .replace(/[^\p{L}\p{N}\s-]/gu, " ")
    .replace(/\s+/g, " ")
    .trim();
  if (!q) return [];
  return q
    .split(" ")
    .map((w) => (w in BRAND_SYNONYMS ? BRAND_SYNONYMS[w] : w))
    .filter(Boolean);
}

export function normalizeQuery(raw: string): string {
  return queryTokens(raw).join(" ");
}

/**
 * Case-folded display_name, explicitly under ICU.
 *
 * THE DATABASE IS LC_COLLATE=C / LC_CTYPE=C, so Postgres' own `lower()` folds
 * ASCII and leaves everything else alone: `lower('Телевизор Samsung')` is
 * `'Телевизор samsung'`. Every one of the catalogue's display names opens
 * with a Cyrillic capital, so before this every Cyrillic search in the site
 * returned exactly nothing -- "телевизор", "холодильник", "ноутбук",
 * "кондиционер", all zero, on a catalogue where those words name thousands of
 * rows. ILIKE and citext read the same ctype and are no help; pg_trgm is not
 * installed. ICU is compiled in (784 collations), and `lower(x COLLATE
 * "und-x-icu")` folds Cyrillic correctly, so the fix is per-expression and
 * needs neither an extension nor a database rebuild.
 *
 * Use this ANYWHERE a user's typed text is compared to catalogue text. A bare
 * lower() will appear to work in every English test and silently fail for the
 * language the site is actually written in.
 */
const FOLDED_NAME = `lower(v.display_name COLLATE "und-x-icu")`;
const FOLDED_BRAND = `lower(v.brand COLLATE "und-x-icu")`;

/**
 * The picture for one grid card, as `v.id`'s cheapest available image.
 *
 * Restricted to IN_STOCK offers this returned nothing for 1,936 of 11,150
 * listed products, because whether a picture exists and whether the cheapest
 * seller happens to have stock are unrelated facts. The out-of-stock tier is
 * a fallback only, so a card still shows the in-stock seller's picture
 * whenever there is one.
 */
const CARD_IMAGE = `COALESCE(
              (SELECT o.image_url FROM offer o
                WHERE o.variant_id = v.id AND o.image_url IS NOT NULL
                  AND o.availability = 'IN_STOCK'
                ORDER BY o.price LIMIT 1),
              (SELECT o.image_url FROM offer o
                WHERE o.variant_id = v.id AND o.image_url IS NOT NULL
                ORDER BY o.price LIMIT 1)
            )`;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Base WHERE builder shared by results + facet queries.
// "excludeFacet" lets each facet's counts ignore its own selection, so the
// sidebar shows what is *available*, not what is already checked.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

interface SearchParams {
  qNorm: string;
  /** Every token the row must contain; see queryTokens. */
  qTokens: string[];
  brands: string[];
  colors: string[];
  rams: number[];
  priceLo: number | null;
  priceHi: number | null;
  multiStore: boolean;
  category: string | null;
  /** Drop variants with no buyable price. The category page has always done
   *  this (getCategoryProducts required min_price NOT NULL); search and the
   *  catalogue never have, and this keeps that difference explicit rather
   *  than letting one page quietly change behaviour when it switched query. */
  priced?: boolean;
}

function baseWhere(p: SearchParams, excludeFacet?: "brands" | "colors" | "rams") {
  const clauses: string[] = [];
  const params: unknown[] = [];
  let i = 1;
  // Every token must appear, in any order, in the catalogue name OR in what
  // some retailer calls the same product.
  //
  // display_name is GENERATED from the variant key, so it carries only what
  // the matcher treats as identity -- and the matcher drops marketing words.
  // "Galaxy" is one of them: 1,730 offers say Galaxy, 9 display names do, so
  // "samsung galaxy a26" -- the ordinary way to name that phone -- matched
  // nothing while the phone sat in the catalogue as "Смартфон Samsung A26
  // 8/256 ГБ, Чёрный". Searching the offers as well costs about 100ms over
  // 8,600 variants and needs no change to identity, which is the one thing
  // that must not move to make a search box work.
  for (const token of p.qTokens) {
    clauses.push(
      `(${FOLDED_NAME} LIKE '%' || $${i} || '%'
        OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM offer o
                    WHERE o.variant_id = v.id
                      AND lower(o.name_raw COLLATE "und-x-icu") LIKE '%' || $${i} || '%'))`
    );
    params.push(token);
    i += 1;
  }
  if (excludeFacet !== "brands" && p.brands.length) {
    clauses.push(`v.brand = ANY($${i}::text[])`);
    params.push(p.brands);
    i += 1;
  }
  if (excludeFacet !== "colors" && p.colors.length) {
    clauses.push(`v.color = ANY($${i}::text[])`);
    params.push(p.colors);
    i += 1;
  }
  if (excludeFacet !== "rams" && p.rams.length) {
    clauses.push(`v.ram_gb = ANY($${i}::int[])`);
    params.push(p.rams);
    i += 1;
  }
  if (p.priceLo != null) {
    clauses.push(`vp.min_price >= $${i}`);
    params.push(p.priceLo);
    i += 1;
  }
  if (p.priceHi != null) {
    clauses.push(`vp.min_price <= $${i}`);
    params.push(p.priceHi);
    i += 1;
  }
  if (p.multiStore) {
    clauses.push("vp.store_count >= 2");
  }
  if (p.category) {
    clauses.push(`v.category = $${i}`);
    params.push(p.category);
    i += 1;
  }
  if (p.priced) {
    clauses.push("vp.min_price IS NOT NULL");
  }
  return { where: clauses.length ? `WHERE ${clauses.join(" AND ")}` : "", params };
}

const PAGE_SIZE = 24;

export async function searchVariants(
  raw: SearchParams & { sort: SortKey; page: number }
): Promise<SearchResult> {
  const p: SearchParams = {
    qNorm: raw.qNorm,
    qTokens: raw.qTokens,
    brands: raw.brands,
    colors: raw.colors,
    rams: raw.rams,
    priceLo: raw.priceLo,
    priceHi: raw.priceHi,
    multiStore: raw.multiStore,
    category: raw.category,
    priced: raw.priced,
  };
  const { where, params } = baseWhere(p);
  // The SELECT's brand-rank/pos expressions need a query term as a parameter.
  // It must go in a COPY: `params` is reused by the count and facet queries,
  // which do not declare it. The FIRST token is the ranking term -- with
  // token matching there is no single "the query" string to position, and the
  // leading word is what a user is anchoring on ("samsung a26" -> samsung).
  const qIdx = params.length + 1;
  const rankTerm = p.qTokens[0] ?? "";
  const resParams = [...params, rankTerm];

  // --- results ------------------------------------------------------------
  const orderBy = {
    relevance: `brand_rank, pos, vp.store_count DESC, vp.min_price ASC NULLS LAST`,
    price_asc: `vp.min_price ASC NULLS LAST, vp.store_count DESC`,
    price_desc: `vp.min_price DESC NULLS LAST`,
    stores: `vp.store_count DESC, vp.min_price ASC NULLS LAST`,
  }[raw.sort];

  const res = await query(
    `SELECT v.id, v.slug, v.brand, v.display_name, v.ram_gb, v.storage_gb,
            v.color, v.sim_kind, v.category,
            vp.min_price, vp.median_price, vp.max_price,
            vp.offer_count, vp.in_stock_offer_count, vp.store_count, vp.computed_at,
            (SELECT max(o.last_seen) FROM offer o WHERE o.variant_id = v.id) AS latest_offer_at,
            ${CARD_IMAGE} AS image_url,
            CASE WHEN ${FOLDED_BRAND} = $${qIdx} THEN 0
                 WHEN ${FOLDED_BRAND} LIKE $${qIdx} || '%' THEN 1 ELSE 2 END AS brand_rank,
            -- strpos returns 0 when the term is absent, which would sort
            -- those rows FIRST. Push them last instead.
            CASE WHEN strpos(${FOLDED_NAME}, $${qIdx}) = 0 THEN 2147483647
                 ELSE strpos(${FOLDED_NAME}, $${qIdx}) END AS pos
       FROM variant v
       JOIN variant_price vp ON vp.variant_id = v.id
       ${where}
      ORDER BY ${orderBy}
      LIMIT ${PAGE_SIZE} OFFSET ${(raw.page - 1) * PAGE_SIZE}`,
    resParams
  );
  const totalRes = await query<{ n: string }>(
    `SELECT count(*) AS n FROM variant v JOIN variant_price vp ON vp.variant_id = v.id ${where}`,
    params
  );
  const total = Number(totalRes[0]?.n ?? 0);

  // --- facets --------------------------------------------------------------
  const brands = await query<FacetValue>(
    `SELECT v.brand AS value, count(*) AS count, min(vp.min_price) AS min_price
       FROM variant v JOIN variant_price vp ON vp.variant_id = v.id
       ${baseWhere(p, "brands").where}
      GROUP BY v.brand ORDER BY count DESC, min_price ASC`,
    baseWhere(p, "brands").params
  );
  const colors = await query<FacetValue>(
    `SELECT v.color AS value, count(*) AS count
       FROM variant v JOIN variant_price vp ON vp.variant_id = v.id
       ${baseWhere(p, "colors").where}
      GROUP BY v.color ORDER BY count DESC`,
    baseWhere(p, "colors").params
  );
  const rams = await query<{ value: number | null; count: string }>(
    `SELECT v.ram_gb AS value, count(*) AS count
       FROM variant v JOIN variant_price vp ON vp.variant_id = v.id
       ${baseWhere(p, "rams").where}
      GROUP BY v.ram_gb ORDER BY v.ram_gb ASC NULLS FIRST`,
    baseWhere(p, "rams").params
  );
  const priceRes = await query<{ lo: number | null; hi: number | null }>(
    `SELECT min(vp.min_price) AS lo, max(vp.min_price) AS hi
       FROM variant v JOIN variant_price vp ON vp.variant_id = v.id
       ${baseWhere(p).where}`,
    baseWhere(p).params
  );
  // node-pg returns bigint as string; coerce before ANY comparison or math.
  const priceLo = priceRes[0]?.lo != null ? Number(priceRes[0].lo) : null;
  const priceHi = priceRes[0]?.hi != null ? Number(priceRes[0].hi) : null;

  // Price bands of ~2.5M SUM for the facet (fits the 1.6–34M observed range).
  // One query: width_bucket over the base set, mapped back to band edges.
  const bands: { lo: number; hi: number; count: number }[] = [];
  if (priceLo != null && priceHi != null && priceHi > priceLo) {
    const STEP = 2_500_000;
    const lo = priceLo - (priceLo % STEP);
    const hi = Math.ceil(priceHi / STEP) * STEP;
    const nb = Math.max(1, Math.ceil((hi - lo) / STEP));
    // width_bucket's parameters come AFTER the WHERE clause's, so their
    // placeholders must be offset by the where-param count.
    const bw = baseWhere(p);
    const w3 = bw.params.length + 1;
    const w4 = w3 + 1;
    const w5 = w4 + 1;
    const bandRes = await query<{ bucket: number; n: string }>(
      `SELECT width_bucket(vp.min_price, $${w3}, $${w4}, $${w5}) AS bucket, count(*) AS n
         FROM variant v JOIN variant_price vp ON vp.variant_id = v.id
         ${bw.where}
        GROUP BY bucket ORDER BY bucket`,
      [...bw.params, lo, hi + STEP, nb]
    );
    for (const r of bandRes) {
      // width_bucket yields NULL for variants whose min_price is NULL
      // (out-of-stock-only); they have no price and must not appear in a
      // price band as garbage (measured: "2 500 000сум — 1сум", 303 rows).
      if (r.bucket == null) continue;
      const bLo = lo + (Number(r.bucket) - 1) * STEP;
      bands.push({ lo: bLo, hi: bLo + STEP - 1, count: Number(r.n) });
    }
    // Keep the eight bands that hold the most products, then restore price
    // order. This used to be `splice(0, bands.length - 8)`, which drops from
    // the FRONT and so kept the eight most EXPENSIVE bands: searching
    // "samsung" offered 35M–47.5M with 2, 2, 1 and 1 products in them, while
    // the several hundred phones between 1M and 10M had no band at all. A
    // price filter whose every option matches almost nothing is worse than no
    // price filter.
    if (bands.length > 8) {
      const keep = [...bands].sort((a, b) => b.count - a.count).slice(0, 8);
      const kept = new Set(keep.map((b) => b.lo));
      bands.splice(0, bands.length, ...bands.filter((b) => kept.has(b.lo)));
    }
  }

  return {
    hits: res as unknown as VariantHit[],
    total,
    page: raw.page,
    pages: Math.max(1, Math.ceil(total / PAGE_SIZE)),
    facets: {
      brands,
      // Colour and RAM are PHONE facets. Outside smartphones both columns are
      // NULL by design, so an unfiltered GROUP BY yields a single null bucket
      // that renders as an empty, unclickable chip on every television and
      // fridge result page. Dropping the null bucket makes the facet list
      // category-aware without needing to know the category: a result set with
      // no colours simply offers no colour filter.
      colors: colors.filter((c) => c.value != null),
      rams: rams.map((r) => r.value).filter((v) => v != null),
      // Plain object, NOT a Map: SearchResult crosses both RSC (initial SSR)
      // and the /api/search JSON endpoint, and Maps serialize to {} in JSON,
      // which then throws on .get() client-side (the facet-click bug
      // 2026-08-10).
      ramCounts: Object.fromEntries(
        rams
          .filter((r) => r.value != null)
          .map((r) => [String(r.value), Number(r.count)])
      ),
      priceBands: bands,
      priceMin: priceLo,
      priceMax: priceHi,
    },
    applied: {
      q: raw.qNorm || null,
      brands: p.brands,
      colors: p.colors,
      rams: p.rams,
      priceLo: p.priceLo,
      priceHi: p.priceHi,
      multiStore: p.multiStore,
      sort: raw.sort,
    },
  };
}

export interface OfferRow {
  id: string;
  name_raw: string;
  price: number;
  availability: string;
  last_seen: string;
  url: string | null;
  image_url: string | null;
  store_name: string;
  store_slug: string;
}

export interface StoreRollup {
  store_name: string;
  store_slug: string;
  offers: number;
  in_stock: number;
  min_p: number | null;
  max_p: number | null;
  median_p: number | null;
  last_seen: string | null;
}

export interface SiblingRow {
  id: string;
  slug: string;
  color: string;
  display_name: string;
  min_price: number | null;
  in_stock_offer_count: number;
  store_count: number;
}

export interface VariantRow {
  id: string;
  slug: string;
  brand: string;
  display_name: string;
  ram_gb: number | null;
  // Nullable outside smartphones by design: a television has no storage, no
  // colour identity and no SIM. The columns were relaxed to NULL when
  // categories landed; these types still claimed non-null, which is how a
  // refrigerator card came to print "eSIM".
  storage_gb: number | null;
  color: string | null;
  sim_kind: string | null;
  category: string;
}

export interface PriceRow {
  min_price: number | null;
  median_price: number | null;
  max_price: number | null;
  offer_count: number;
  in_stock_offer_count: number;
  store_count: number;
  computed_at: string;
  min_offer_id: string | null;
  min_offer_name: string | null;
  min_offer_url: string | null;
  min_store_name: string | null;
  hero_image_url: string | null;
}

export interface VariantPage {
  variant: VariantRow | null;
  price: PriceRow | null;
  offers: OfferRow[];
  stores: StoreRollup[];
  siblings: SiblingRow[];
}

export async function getVariantPage(slug: string): Promise<VariantPage> {
  const variants = await query<VariantRow>(
    `SELECT id, slug, brand, display_name, ram_gb, storage_gb, color, sim_kind, category
       FROM variant WHERE slug = $1`,
    [slug]
  );
  if (!variants.length) return { variant: null, price: null, offers: [], stores: [], siblings: [] };
  const v = variants[0];

  const price = await query<PriceRow>(
    `SELECT vp.min_price, vp.median_price, vp.max_price, vp.offer_count,
 vp.in_stock_offer_count, vp.store_count, vp.computed_at,
 vp.min_offer_id,
 (SELECT o.name_raw FROM offer o WHERE o.id = vp.min_offer_id) AS min_offer_name,
            (SELECT o.url FROM offer o WHERE o.id = vp.min_offer_id) AS min_offer_url,
            (SELECT s.name FROM store s WHERE s.id = vp.min_store_id) AS min_store_name,
            -- The hero picture used to be the CHEAPEST offer's picture and
            -- nothing else, so a variant whose cheapest seller publishes no
            -- image showed no image at all -- while the grid card for the
            -- same product, which already picked the cheapest offer that HAS
            -- one, showed it. Clicking a product made its picture disappear.
            -- uzum alone accounts for 5,461 imageless offers, and 302
            -- variants had a picture available and rendered none.
            --
            -- Preference order, cheapest first within each tier: the min
            -- offer, then any in-stock offer, then any offer at all. A
            -- picture from a second retailer of the same product is right;
            -- an empty frame is not.
            COALESCE(
              (SELECT o.image_url FROM offer o
                WHERE o.id = vp.min_offer_id AND o.image_url IS NOT NULL),
              (SELECT o.image_url FROM offer o
                WHERE o.variant_id = vp.variant_id AND o.image_url IS NOT NULL
                  AND o.availability = 'IN_STOCK'
                ORDER BY o.price LIMIT 1),
              (SELECT o.image_url FROM offer o
                WHERE o.variant_id = vp.variant_id AND o.image_url IS NOT NULL
                ORDER BY o.price LIMIT 1)
            ) AS hero_image_url
       FROM variant_price vp WHERE vp.variant_id = $1`,
    [v.id]
  );

  const offers = await query<OfferRow>(
    `SELECT o.id, o.name_raw, o.price, o.availability, o.last_seen, o.url, o.image_url,
            s.name AS store_name, s.slug AS store_slug
       FROM offer o JOIN store s ON s.id = o.store_id
      WHERE o.variant_id = $1 AND o.availability <> 'OUT_OF_STOCK'
      ORDER BY (o.availability = 'IN_STOCK') DESC, o.price ASC`,
    [v.id]
  );

  const stores = await query<StoreRollup>(
    `SELECT s.name AS store_name, s.slug AS store_slug,
            count(*) AS offers,
            count(*) FILTER (WHERE o.availability = 'IN_STOCK') AS in_stock,
            min(o.price) AS min_p, max(o.price) AS max_p,
            percentile_disc(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY o.price) AS median_p,
            max(o.last_seen) AS last_seen
       FROM offer o JOIN store s ON s.id = o.store_id
      WHERE o.variant_id = $1
      GROUP BY s.id, s.name, s.slug
      ORDER BY min_p ASC NULLS LAST, s.name`,
    [v.id]
  );

  // Colour siblings = same model, only colour differs. The catalogue can
  // hold SEVERAL models per (brand, storage, ram, sim) -- e.g. Samsung A26
  // vs A26 5G split into separate canonicals -- so (brand, storage, ram,
  // sim) alone over-groups and the picker would compare different phones
  // ("Черный", "Черный" ×4 with −1.4M deltas). The display_name stem
  // (everything before the colour) is the same-model identity here.
  const stem = v.display_name.split(",")[0]!.trim();
  const siblings = await query<SiblingRow>(
    `SELECT v.id, v.slug, v.color, v.display_name,
            vp.min_price, vp.in_stock_offer_count, vp.store_count
       FROM variant v JOIN variant_price vp ON vp.variant_id = v.id
      WHERE v.brand = $1 AND v.storage_gb = $2
        AND v.ram_gb IS NOT DISTINCT FROM $3 AND v.sim_kind = $4
        AND split_part(v.display_name, ',', 1) = $5
      ORDER BY vp.min_price ASC NULLS LAST`,
    [v.brand, v.storage_gb, v.ram_gb, v.sim_kind, stem]
  );

  return {
    variant: v,
    price: price[0] ?? null,
    offers,
    stores,
    siblings,
  };
}

// Browse / home

export async function getBrandsByCategory(): Promise<
  { category: string; brand: string; count: number; min_price: number | null; stores: number }[]
> {
  // ::int on both aggregates, deliberately. node-pg returns bigint as a
  // STRING, and the home page SUMS these per category to size its category
  // tiles -- so `cur.count += b.count` concatenated "12" and "5" into "125"
  // instead of adding them, and the min_price comparison compared strings.
  // Same trap the price-band code already hit; casting in SQL fixes it at the
  // source rather than at each call site. Every value here fits in int4:
  // prices are fenced at 100,000,000.
  return query(
    `SELECT v.category, v.brand, count(*)::int AS count,
            min(vp.min_price)::int AS min_price, max(vp.store_count)::int AS stores
       FROM variant v JOIN variant_price vp ON vp.variant_id = v.id
      GROUP BY v.category, v.brand
      ORDER BY v.category, count DESC`
  );
}

export async function getHomeStats(): Promise<{
  variants_priced: number;
  stores: number;
  unresolved: number;
  last_updated: string | null;
  variants_total: number;
}> {
  const r = await query<{
    variants_priced: string;
    variants_total: string;
    stores: string;
    unresolved: string;
    last_updated: string | null;
  }>(
    `SELECT (SELECT count(*) FROM variant_price WHERE min_price IS NOT NULL) AS variants_priced,
            (SELECT count(*) FROM variant) AS variants_total,
            (SELECT count(*) FROM store WHERE is_active) AS stores,
            (SELECT count(*) FROM unresolved_offer) AS unresolved,
            (SELECT max(last_seen) FROM offer) AS last_updated`
  );
  const row = r[0]!;
  return {
    variants_priced: Number(row.variants_priced),
    stores: Number(row.stores),
    unresolved: Number(row.unresolved),
    last_updated: row.last_updated,
    variants_total: Number(row.variants_total),
  };
}

export async function getFeatured(): Promise<VariantHit[]> {
  return query(
    `SELECT v.id, v.slug, v.brand, v.display_name, v.ram_gb, v.storage_gb,
            v.color, v.sim_kind, v.category,
            vp.min_price, vp.median_price, vp.max_price,
            vp.offer_count, vp.in_stock_offer_count, vp.store_count, vp.computed_at,
            (SELECT max(o.last_seen) FROM offer o WHERE o.variant_id = v.id) AS latest_offer_at,
            ${CARD_IMAGE} AS image_url,
            0 AS brand_rank, 0 AS pos
       FROM variant v JOIN variant_price vp ON vp.variant_id = v.id
      WHERE vp.store_count >= 2 AND vp.min_price IS NOT NULL
      ORDER BY vp.store_count DESC, vp.min_price ASC
      LIMIT 10`
  );
}

/** Top `per` products from EACH category (by store count, then price). Lets
 *  the home page show a slice of every category, not just phones. */
export async function getFeaturedPerCategory(
  per: number = 4
): Promise<{ category: string; hits: VariantHit[] }[]> {
  const rows = await query<{ category: string; rn: number } & VariantHit>(
    `WITH ranked AS (
        SELECT v.id, v.slug, v.brand, v.display_name, v.ram_gb, v.storage_gb,
               v.color, v.sim_kind, v.category,
               vp.min_price, vp.median_price, vp.max_price,
               vp.offer_count, vp.in_stock_offer_count, vp.store_count, vp.computed_at,
               (SELECT max(o.last_seen) FROM offer o WHERE o.variant_id = v.id) AS latest_offer_at,
               ${CARD_IMAGE} AS image_url,
               -- Carried by most retailers first, then most widely stocked,
               -- and only then cheapest. Ordering by price alone fills an
               -- appliance row with the cheapest no-name units in the
               -- catalogue, which is the opposite of a shop window.
               ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
                 PARTITION BY v.category
                 ORDER BY vp.store_count DESC,
                          vp.in_stock_offer_count DESC,
                          vp.min_price ASC
               ) AS rn
          FROM variant v JOIN variant_price vp ON vp.variant_id = v.id
         WHERE vp.min_price IS NOT NULL
    )
    SELECT * FROM ranked WHERE rn <= $1 ORDER BY category, rn`,
    [per]
  );
  const groups = new Map<string, VariantHit[]>();
  for (const r of rows) {
    // `category` stays ON the hit as well as keying the group: VariantHit
    // declares it, and a card that needs to know what it is showing (spec
    // chips, links) would otherwise read undefined.
    const { rn: _rn, ...hit } = r;
    const arr = groups.get(r.category) ?? [];
    arr.push(hit as VariantHit);
    groups.set(r.category, arr);
  }
  return [...groups.entries()].map(([category, hits]) => ({ category, hits }));
}

export async function getSearchSuggestions(q: string) {
  // Same token rule and same ICU fold as the results page. When the two
  // disagree the dropdown offers products the search page then cannot find,
  // which reads as the search box being broken even when it is not.
  const tokens = queryTokens(q);
  if (!tokens.length) return { variants: [], brands: [] };
  const clauses = tokens
    .map(
      (_, n) =>
        `(${FOLDED_NAME} LIKE '%' || $${n + 1} || '%'
          OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM offer o
                      WHERE o.variant_id = v.id
                        AND lower(o.name_raw COLLATE "und-x-icu") LIKE '%' || $${n + 1} || '%'))`
    )
    .join(" AND ");
  const variants = await query(
    `SELECT v.slug, v.display_name, vp.min_price, vp.store_count
       FROM variant v JOIN variant_price vp ON vp.variant_id = v.id
      WHERE ${clauses}
      ORDER BY vp.store_count DESC, vp.min_price ASC NULLS LAST LIMIT 6`,
    tokens
  );
  const brands = await query<{ brand: string }>(
    `SELECT DISTINCT v.brand FROM variant v
      WHERE ${FOLDED_BRAND} LIKE $1 || '%' ORDER BY v.brand LIMIT 5`,
    [tokens[0]]
  );
  return { variants, brands: brands.map((b) => b.brand) };
}

export interface StoreHealth {
  name: string;
  slug: string;
  website_url: string;
  is_active: boolean;
  offers: number;
  fresh_24h: number;
  newest_offer: string | null;
  last_ok: string | null;
  last_try: string | null;
  last_error: string | null;
}

export async function getStoresHealth(): Promise<StoreHealth[]> {
  return query(
    `SELECT s.name, s.slug, s.website_url, s.is_active,
            (SELECT count(*) FROM offer o WHERE o.store_id = s.id) AS offers,
            (SELECT count(*) FROM offer o WHERE o.store_id = s.id
               AND o.last_seen > now() - interval '24 hours') AS fresh_24h,
            (SELECT max(o.last_seen) FROM offer o WHERE o.store_id = s.id) AS newest_offer,
            (SELECT max(h.finished_at) FROM harvest_run h
               WHERE h.store_id = s.id AND h.ok) AS last_ok,
            (SELECT max(h.started_at) FROM harvest_run h WHERE h.store_id = s.id) AS last_try,
            (SELECT h.error FROM harvest_run h
               WHERE h.store_id = s.id AND NOT h.ok
               ORDER BY h.started_at DESC LIMIT 1) AS last_error
       FROM store s ORDER BY s.name`
  );
}

    [offerId, variantId, storeId, referer]
  );
}

FILE: narxnoma-web/lib/searchParams.ts

import { normalizeQuery, queryTokens } from "./queries";
import type { SortKey } from "./queries";

export interface ParsedSearch {
  rawQ: string;
  qNorm: string;
  /** The tokens a row must all contain; see queryTokens. */
  qTokens: string[];
  brands: string[];
  colors: string[];
  rams: number[];
  priceLo: number | null;
  priceHi: number | null;
  multiStore: boolean;
  category: string | null;
  /** `priced=1` — only variants with a buyable price. Used by the category
   *  page, whose grid has always excluded them. */
  priced: boolean;
  sort: SortKey;
  page: number;
  /** URLSearchParams string carrying every applied filter (for /api/search). */
  qs: string;
}

const SORTS: SortKey[] = ["relevance", "price_asc", "price_desc", "stores"];

/**
 * Shared by the SSR search page and /api/search so a facet toggle refetches
 * EXACTLY what the server rendered for the same URL.
 */
export function parseSearchParams(
  sp: Record<string, string | string[] | undefined>
): ParsedSearch {
  const get = (k: string): string => {
    const v = sp[k];
    return Array.isArray(v) ? (v[0] ?? "") : (v ?? "");
  };
  const list = (k: string): string[] =>
    get(k)
      .split(",")
      .map((s) => s.trim())
      .filter(Boolean);

  const rawQ = get("q");
  const qTokens = queryTokens(rawQ);
  const qNorm = normalizeQuery(rawQ);
  const brands = list("brand");
  const colors = list("color");
  const rams = list("ram")
    .map((r) => (r === "none" ? NaN : Number(r)))
    .filter((r) => !Number.isNaN(r) && Number.isFinite(r));
  const priceBand = get("price");
  const priceLo = priceBand ? Number(priceBand) : null;
  const priceHi =
    priceLo != null && !Number.isNaN(priceLo) ? priceLo + 2_499_999 : null;
  const multiStore = get("multi") === "1";
  const category = get("category") || null;
  const priced = get("priced") === "1";
  const sortRaw = get("sort") as SortKey;
  const sort: SortKey = SORTS.includes(sortRaw) ? sortRaw : "relevance";
  const page = Math.max(1, Number(get("page")) || 1);

  const qs = new URLSearchParams();
  if (rawQ) qs.set("q", rawQ);
  if (brands.length) qs.set("brand", brands.join(","));
  if (colors.length) qs.set("color", colors.join(","));
  if (rams.length) qs.set("ram", rams.join(","));
  if (priceLo != null) qs.set("price", String(priceLo));
  if (multiStore) qs.set("multi", "1");
  if (category) qs.set("category", category);
  if (priced) qs.set("priced", "1");
  qs.set("sort", sort);
  if (page > 1) qs.set("page", String(page));

  return {
    rawQ,
    qNorm,
    qTokens,
    brands,
    colors,
    rams,
    priceLo,
    priceHi,
    multiStore,
    category,
    priced,
    sort,
    page,
    qs: qs.toString(),
  };
}

---
name: adding-a-narxnoma-source
description: Use when adding a new retailer or marketplace to the narxnoma engine, when a site seems unscrapable because its HTML is an empty shell, or when deciding whether a store is worth adding.
---

# Adding a source

## Overview

A source is one file implementing `Source` (`narxnoma/sources/base.py`),
one recorded fixture, one test module, one doc, and four registrations.
Everything the client claims must be asserted against the fixture; the doc
is written so the client could be rebuilt from it alone.

## 1. Find the durable path

```dot
digraph find_path {
    "Open site, DevTools > Network > Fetch/XHR, type a search" [shape=box];
    "Response with prices?" [shape=diamond];
    "Copy as cURL; that JSON API is the source" [shape=box];
    "Site server-rendered? (view-source shows priced cards)" [shape=diamond];
    "Parse HTML from machine attributes (data-*, ids), never prose" [shape=box];
    "Read the JS bundles for an API host (radius: new.api.)" [shape=box];
    "Open site, DevTools > Network > Fetch/XHR, type a search" -> "Response with prices?";
    "Response with prices?" -> "Copy as cURL; that JSON API is the source" [label="yes"];
    "Response with prices?" -> "Site server-rendered? (view-source shows priced cards)" [label="no"];
    "Site server-rendered? (view-source shows priced cards)" -> "Parse HTML from machine attributes (data-*, ids), never prose" [label="yes"];
    "Site server-rendered? (view-source shows priced cards)" -> "Read the JS bundles for an API host (radius: new.api.)" [label="no"];
}
```

Check `robots.txt` first. If it disallows the browse surface, you need
written permission from the site (see skill `fetch-glotr`) or you stop.

Prefer, in order: category/catalogue endpoint (olcha, beemarket) → broad
query walk (texnomart) → brand-query list (idea, alifshop, share
`brand_queries.py`) → search-only with `can_sweep = False` (mediapark).

## 2. Write the client

```python
# narxnoma/sources/<slug>.py
API_URL = "https://..."
PRODUCT_URL = "https://.../{id}"          # verified in a browser, not guessed

def _parse_item(item: dict) -> Listing | None:
    price = coerce_price(item.get("<the one current-price field>"))
    return try_build_listing(store_slug="<slug>", source_key=str(item["id"]),
                             name_raw=item["name"], price=price,
                             url=PRODUCT_URL.format(id=item["id"]),
                             image_url=item.get("image"), raw=item)

def parse(payload: dict) -> list[Listing]:     # pure function of one response
    ...

class <Slug>Source:
    slug = "<slug>"
    can_sweep = True
    def sweep(self, category="smartphones") -> Iterator[Listing]:  # uses base.paginate
    def search(self, query) -> Iterator[Listing]:
```

Invariants the base layer enforces or expects:

- `parse()` never filters by category; crawl policy lives in `sweep()`.
- Use `base.paginate(fetch, parse, next_page)`: retries one bad page, raises
  when a page fails outright, and only `next_page` ends the sweep — never
  an empty page.
- Multi-seller site: one listing per seller offer, `source_key` = offer id.
- Variant-level site (radius): one listing per variant, name from the variant.
- Price unit checked against the rendered page; `PRICE_MIN..PRICE_MAX` fence.
- GraphQL: inspect `errors` under HTTP 200.
- HTML: read the product id from two places and drop the card when they disagree.

## 3. Record a fixture and test

Save one real response to `tests/fixtures/sources/<slug>.json|html` (redact
nothing; it is public catalogue data). Tests in `tests/sources/test_<slug>.py`
assert, from the fixture: count parsed, one exact price and URL, the
end-of-pagination signal, and the trap you found. Add a `@pytest.mark.live`
case to `test_contract_live.py` asserting the endpoint shape.

## 4. Register

| where | what |
|---|---|
| `narxnoma/sources/__init__.py` | add to `SOURCES` |
| `narxnoma/pipeline/report.py` | `EXPECTED_MIN_OFFERS["<slug>"]` — measured floor; a source below it is flagged SUSPICIOUS |
| `narxnoma/db/schema.sql` | new migration inserting the `store` row (slug, name, url) |
| `narxnoma/matching/brands.py` | any new brands the source introduces |
| `docs/parsers/<slug>.md` + `README.md` table | canonical notes |
| `skills/fetch-<slug>/SKILL.md` | operational card |

## 5. Measure before calling it done

Run `python -m narxnoma.cli fetch --source <slug>`, open three built URLs
in a browser, compare three prices to the page. Then, with Postgres,
`cycle` and read the coverage report: the number that matters is how many
products got a **second** price, not how many rows arrived (radius: 2.2% of
offers, 4.8% of comparisons).

## Common mistakes

| Mistake | Fix |
|---|---|
| Stop paging on an empty page | Stop on the site's own pager / total count; empty pages are filtered pages |
| Build the slug yourself | Take it verbatim; open it |
| Trust `status_code` | GraphQL and some REST return 200 with an error body |
| One code path divides by 100, another does not | Single price coercion function per client |
| Doc written after the fact | Rebuild the client from the doc; if you cannot, the doc is incomplete |

# alifshop.uz — REST POST, multi-seller, price in tiyin

Notes: `docs/parsers/alifshop.md`. Client: `narxnoma-crawler/narxnoma/sources/alifshop.py`.

## Run

```bash
cd narxnoma-crawler   # pip install -e . once
python -m narxnoma.cli fetch --source alifshop --limit 60
python -m narxnoma.cli fetch --source alifshop --query "honor x9d"
```

## Endpoint

```
POST https://gw.alifshop.uz/web/client/search/full-text
Content-Type: application/json
Accept-Language: ru
service-token: service-token-alifshop     # fixed public string, not a secret
Origin: https://alifshop.uz
Referer: https://alifshop.uz/
Body: {"query": "Honor X9d", "page": 0, "size": 20}
```

- `page` is **0-based** (beemarket/texnomart are 1-based).
- `size` capped at **20** server-side; 3 pages per brand is enough for a median.
- No catalogue browse: `sweep()` loops the shared brand list
  (`sources/brand_queries.py`), one search per brand.

## Price — tiyin

`items[].price` is in **tiyin (1/100 UZS)**. Divide by 100 once, in one place
(`_coerce_tiyin_price`). A partial divisor bug yields 100x prices that still
pass plausibility fences on some rows.

## Category

Items carry no category field. `aggregations.category` is a histogram whose
bucket names (`"Смартфоны Samsung"`) the endpoint accepts back as a `category`
filter and honours server-side. Discover the bucket per brand, then re-request
filtered; fall back to unfiltered with a warning if none matches.

## URL

`https://alifshop.uz/moderated-offer/<slug>` — the obvious `/product/<slug>` **404s**.
Use the API's slug verbatim.

## Traps

- Multi-seller: `source_key` is the listing UUID, one row per partner offer.
  Never collapse sellers; price = IQR-trimmed median.
- Query is strict AND; two-shot: colour-stripped first, then verbatim.
- `+` only means `plus` when trailing a word (`Pro+`); `nanoSim+eSim` must not
  mint a `plus` model token.
- Sellers omit RAM: missing RAM on a candidate = unknown, not reject.

Fixture: `tests/fixtures/sources/alifshop.json`. Tests: `tests/sources/test_alifshop*.py`.

FILE: skills/fetch-asaxiy/SKILL.md
================================================
---
name: fetch-asaxiy
description: Use when fetching prices or listings from asaxiy.uz, when looking for an asaxiy JSON API, when asaxiy titles come back in Uzbek, or when an asaxiy sweep loops re-ingesting the same products.
---

# asaxiy.uz — server-rendered HTML, no JSON API at all

The exception to "call the SPA's API": asaxiy's only `/ajax/*` routes are
login and filter plumbing. Category pages ship a complete, priced product
grid in the initial HTML. Notes: `docs/parsers/asaxiy.md`.
Client: `narxnoma-crawler/narxnoma/sources/asaxiy.py`.

## Run

```bash
cd narxnoma-crawler   # pip install -e . once
python -m narxnoma.cli fetch --source asaxiy --limit 50
python -m narxnoma.cli fetch --source asaxiy --category washers
```

No `search()`.

## Request

```
GET https://asaxiy.uz/ru/product/<category-path>            # page 1
GET https://asaxiy.uz/ru/product/<category-path>/page=<N>   # page N >= 2
Accept: text/html
Accept-Language: ru-RU,ru;q=0.9
```

- Page number is a **path segment**; `?page=2` is ignored.
- Russian by `/ru/` path. `Accept-Language` and the `_language` cookie are
  ignored; `?language=ru` only works via a 301 that `X-Requested-With:
  XMLHttpRequest` suppresses.
- Do **not** send `X-Requested-With`: the lighter fragment drops the
  `totalPages` script, the only end-of-catalogue signal.
- Category paths in `CATEGORY_PATHS`.

## Read machine attributes, not prose

Each card carries a hidden `<span id="product_cart_data_<id>" data-id
data-name data-name-ru data-price data-old-price data-img data-brand-name>`
— the values asaxiy's own cart uses. Read `data-price` (integer UZS, no
separators) and `data-name-ru`. Never parse `6 719 000 so'm`.

## URL — tied to the id, twice

Anchor: `<a href="/ru/product/<slug>" onclick="sendSelectItemEvent(<id>, this)">`.
Require that id to equal the cart block's id; drop the card otherwise. A
markup shift must cost a listing, never mint one with a neighbour's URL.

## Availability

CSS class `js-buy-guest` present = IN_STOCK, absent = OUT_OF_STOCK. Do not read
the buy href (localised: scored every Russian card out-of-stock) or the
`Нет в наличии` text (Russian-only).

## Pagination trap

An out-of-range page **301s to page 1 and serves 24 real products again**.
Stop on `let totalPages = parseInt('6', 10)` from the page's inline script
AND on the first page adding no unseen id.

## Category leaves are broader than the category

A leaf holds neighbours (e.g. freezers under fridges). Filter by the
category noun; see doc §6.

Fixtures: `tests/fixtures/sources/asaxiy_ru.html`, `asaxiy_uz.html`. Tests: `tests/sources/test_asaxiy*.py`.

# market.beeline.uz — REST GET, single seller, category endpoint

Notes: `docs/parsers/beemarket.md`. Client: `narxnoma-crawler/narxnoma/sources/beemarket.py`.

## Run

python -m narxnoma.cli fetch --source beemarket --limit 50

## Endpoints

Sweep — category-scoped, the request the site's own category page makes:

```
GET https://market.beeline.uz/api/web/categories/<slug>/products?page=<1-based>&is_bshop=1
```

Search — generic, honours `q`:

```
GET https://market.beeline.uz/api/web/search?q=<text>&is_bshop=1&page=<1-based>
```

Headers: `Accept-Language: ru`, `Referer: https://market.beeline.uz/`. No auth.
Both return the doubly-nested `data.data[]` list with `data.last_page`. Stop
on `last_page`.

Category slugs: `CATEGORY_SLUGS` in the client (`smartfony` = smartphones).
Adding `category=`/`category_id=` to the generic search is silently ignored —

Integer UZS.

## URL

## Traps

- Search is strict AND on product names: `q=smartfon` returns one accessory.
  Broad query, strict match.
- `SIM+eSIM` in names: only a trailing `+` is `plus`.
- Colour sits mid-name (`Honor X9d, Midnight Black, 12/256 GB`): parse by

- Accessories carry no storage; the storage rule drops them.

FILE: skills/fetch-glotr/SKILL.md
================================================
---
name: fetch-glotr
description: Use when asked to fetch listings from glotr.uz (robots.txt forbids it; only with the site's written permission), when every glotr picture belongs to the neighbouring product, or when a glotr sweep ingests far more rows than the category holds.
---

# glotr.uz — server-rendered classifieds board

**Access first.** glotr's `robots.txt` disallows the browse surface
(`/search`, `/*?catid=`, `/*?page=`, `Crawl-delay: 10`) for every user agent
and names `ClaudeBot`/`GPTBot`/`CCBot` with `Disallow: /`. The original
operator swept it under an **explicit written grant from glotr**. That grant
does not travel with this code. Do not run this client against glotr.uz
without your own permission from them, and do not copy the approach to
another site whose robots.txt says the same.

Notes: `docs/parsers/glotr.md`. Client: `narxnoma-crawler/narxnoma/sources/glotr.py`.

## Run (with permission)

```bash
cd narxnoma-crawler   # pip install -e . once
python -m narxnoma.cli fetch --source glotr --category ovens --limit 50
```

No `search()`.

## Request

```
GET https://glotr.uz/<category-path>/            # page 1
GET https://glotr.uz/<category-path>/?page=N
Accept-Language: ru-RU,ru;q=0.9
```

No auth. Yii-rendered, UTF-8. 56 cards per page. `--category` maps to the
path via `CATEGORY_PATHS`:

| `--category` | path |
|---|---|
| smartphones | `telefoni-i-plansheti` |
| televisions | `televizori` |
| laptops | `noutbuki` |
| acs | `konditsioneri` |
| fridges | `xolodilniki` |
| washers | `stiralnie-mashini` |
| ovens | `duxovie-shkafi` |

robots.txt states `Crawl-delay: 10`. Honour it even under a grant:
`NARXNOMA_MIN_DELAY=10 NARXNOMA_MAX_DELAY=12`.

## A classifieds board, not a shop

Sellers post into any category they like. Every category page is noisy:
filter with **positive keeps** (title must carry the category noun) plus an
accessory drop — never a denylist alone. See doc §6.

## Card — the photos come before the name

```
<div class='product-card '>
  header:  <a href="/<slug>-p-<id>/"> <img data-src=... alt=...>   (photos)
  content: <a href='/<slug>-p-<id>/' class='product-card__link'>name</a>
           <span class='text-stock text-success'>В наличии</span>
           <div class="price-retail proposal-price"> 2 610 800 <span>сум</span></div>
```

Cut cards at `<div class='product-card '` (encloses both halves). Read the
`-p-<id>` **twice** — photo anchor and name anchor — and drop the card when
they disagree. Cutting at the name anchor gave 55/55 listings their
neighbour's picture while every count stayed green.

## Price and availability

Price text `7 579 000` — strip spaces, `coerce_price`. Cards with no price
("цена по запросу") are dropped with a warning.
`text-success` = IN_STOCK; `text-warning` (под заказ), `text-secondary`
(уточнить), absent = UNKNOWN. **Nothing maps to OUT_OF_STOCK**: sellers
delist rather than mark.

## Pagination trap — filler past the end

Beyond the last page glotr serves **21 unrelated products, a different set
every time**, under the category's own heading. "No new ids" never fires; a
240-oven category ingested 2,739. Stop when the pager's `<li class="next">`
has no `<a>` (last page is `next disabled`; past the end there is no
`pagination-list` at all). The pager is windowed (page 1 links 2–5 only);
never size the catalogue from it. Keep no-new-ids as a backstop.

Fixtures: `tests/fixtures/sources/glotr*.html`. Tests: `tests/sources/test_glotr.py`.

# mediapark.uz — autocomplete only, no sweep

There is no catalogue endpoint and no pagination; a sweep is structurally
impossible. Reach it per known variant (`pipeline/backfill.py` does this after
clustering).

## Endpoint

```
GET https://api.v2.mediapark.uz/v1/diginetica/autocomplete?st=<text>&lang=ru
Accept-Language: ru
Origin: https://mediapark.uz
Referer: https://mediapark.uz/

```

Parameter is `st`, not `q`. Returns top ~5–10 ranked hits in one call.

- `products[].price` (string) — run through `coerce_price`. `oldPrice` unused.
- `linkUrl` verbatim, prefixed with `https://mediapark.uz`. Route resolves by

  phone). Never parse or rebuild it.

Ranking engine, not a filter: keep the query near-verbatim, including the
`6/128` form and colour, so the exact variant ranks into the short list.
Strip only the `Смартфон` prefix and `GB`. Aggressive stripping measurably
worsens recall here.

- `SAMSUNG SM-A075F A07`: skip mixed alphanumeric tokens ≥ 5 chars; never
  require the word `galaxy`.
- No per-item category; the `categories` key is suggestion links, unrelated to items.
- Headless browsers hit bot detection; JSON is the only route.

---
name: fetch-openshop
description: Use when fetching prices or listings from openshop.uz (web.openshop.uz API), when an openshop sweep stops at ~2,400 products or 48 per page, when an openshop link opens the API or an Uzbek page, or when matching a whole assortment against openshop's catalogue.
---

# openshop.uz — REST POST, full-catalogue sweep

Single-seller shop; the whole catalogue (~5,700 products) is ~120 requests.
Notes: `docs/parsers/openshop.md`. Client: `narxnoma-crawler/narxnoma/sources/openshop.py`.

## Run

```bash
cd narxnoma-crawler   # pip install -e . once
python -m narxnoma.cli fetch --source openshop --limit 50
python -m narxnoma.cli fetch --source openshop --category ovens
python -m narxnoma.cli fetch --source openshop --query "honor x9d"    # fuzzy: pick by name_raw
```

Whole catalogue, every product type, no price fence (Python):

```python
from narxnoma.sources.openshop import OpenshopSource
items = list(OpenshopSource().iter_catalogue())   # raw dicts, walked per top category
```

## Endpoint

```
POST https://web.openshop.uz/api/v1/shop/product/get_products
     ?category_id=<top id>&page=<n>&per_page=48&sort_by=latest     # filters in the QUERY STRING
Accept-Language: ru
language: ru                 # custom header; without it names are Uzbek
Origin: https://openshop.uz
Referer: https://openshop.uz/
```

- Response `{data:[items], meta:{current_page,last_page,per_page,total}}`. Stop on
  `meta.last_page`, never on an empty page.
- Also accepts `subcategory_id`, `subsubcategory_id`, `brand_id`, `search`.
- Tree: `POST /shop/category/categories_tree` body `{}` — 3 levels, the **third is
  the product type** (and the brand for phones/tablets).
- Detail: `POST /shop/product/get_product?slug=<slug>` body `{"with_variants": true}`.
- Rate limit 120/min; the client self-throttles at 0.55 s/request.

## Price

`price.total` — integer UZS, already discounted. `price.old_price` is the
struck-through figure. One field, through `coerce_price`.

## URL

`https://openshop.uz/shop/product/<slug>?lang=ru`, built from `slug`. **Never the
item's `link`** — it points at `web.openshop.uz`, the API host. Without `?lang=ru`
the page is Uzbek. The page `<title>` states the price (`… | Цена: 4 899 000 сум`);
`page_title(slug)` returns `(title, price)` for verification.

## Traps (each returns HTTP 200)

- `per_page` **capped at 48**, silently.
- **Deep paging caps at ~2,400**: an unfiltered walk said 5,731 and repeated
  products after page 50. Walk per top-level category (`iter_catalogue`).
- `/shop/category/<slug>` in the JS bundle is a front-end route; on the API host it
  returns an empty list.
- `search_product?q=` (header search) is fuzzy over SEO tags and capped at 60 —
  useless for identity.
- Every colour × memory is its own product (`group.id` ties them). iPhones come as
  `(SIM + eSIM)`, `(eSIM + eSIM)`, `(SIM + SIM)` at different prices, plus
  `Certified Refurbished`.
- Only in-stock goods are listed; "not found" can mean sold out.
- Product pages answer the odd 502 — retry before calling a link dead.
- Matching openshop names hit eight matcher gaps (`SIM + eSIM` → phantom `plus`,
  one-digit models dropped off-phone, `/` cuts appliance codes, Uzbek `қ`…): see
  `docs/parsers/openshop.md` §8 before matching outside phones.

Fixture: `tests/fixtures/sources/openshop.json`. Tests: `tests/sources/test_openshop.py`.

# radius.uz — Saleor GraphQL, one row per variant

Cleanest source, smallest catalogue (~274 offers) and 4.8% of all
comparisons: judge a source by the second prices it creates. Notes:
`docs/parsers/radius.md`. Client: `narxnoma-crawler/narxnoma/sources/radius.py`.

## Run

```bash
cd narxnoma-crawler   # pip install -e . once

```

## Endpoint

```
POST https://new.api.radius.uz/graphql/
Content-Type: application/json
Accept-Language: ru
Origin: https://radius.uz
Referer: https://radius.uz/
```

No auth. `api.radius.uz` does not resolve; `new.api.` is live. Found in the

Galaxy A26 5G 8/256GB Black (Черный)`. Identity lives on the variant: emit

`https://radius.uz/ru/product/<variant-id>-<product-slug>`. Product-id URLs
**404 on every product**; both ids sit beside the slug and both look right.
A non-default variant id also resolves and renders that colour.

## Category slugs — the Apple trap

`noutbuki` holds 9 laptops, none Apple; MacBooks and iPhones live under a
top-level `apple` category, absent from `smartfony`. Slugs are tuples per
category in the client so Apple is swept.

## Traps

- GraphQL failure is **HTTP 200** with `errors` and null `data`; raise on it
  and on a null `category`.
- `thumbnail(size:N).url` is non-null even when the file was never rendered:
  `.avif` sources 404. For avif only, swap `/thumbnails/<N>/` for `/media/`.

FILE: skills/fetch-texnomart/SKILL.md

---
name: fetch-texnomart
description: Use when fetching prices or listings from texnomart.uz, or when a texnomart sweep contains cases, tablets and chargers alongside phones.
---

# texnomart.uz — REST GET, single seller, broad-query sweep

Notes: `docs/parsers/texnomart.md`. Client: `narxnoma-crawler/narxnoma/sources/texnomart.py`.

## Run

```bash
cd narxnoma-crawler   # pip install -e . once
python -m narxnoma.cli fetch --source texnomart --limit 50
python -m narxnoma.cli fetch --source texnomart --category laptops
python -m narxnoma.cli fetch --source texnomart --query "iphone 16 pro"
```

## Endpoint

```
GET https://gw.texnomart.uz/api/common/v1/search/result?q=<text>&page=<1-based>&limit=20
accept-device: web
accept-region: 2
Accept-Language: uz
Origin: https://texnomart.uz
Referer: https://texnomart.uz/
```

No auth. Paginate until `data.pagination.total_page`. No catalogue browse:
`sweep()` sends one broad category word (`CATEGORY_QUERY`: `smartfon`,
`televizor`, `noutbuk`, `konditsioner`, `xolodilnik`, `stiraln`, `duxovka`)
and walks the result.

## Price

`sale_price` only. `old_price` is frequently `0` and must never be a fallback.
Integer UZS.

## URL

`https://texnomart.uz/product/detail/<id>/` from `id`. `image` is the picture.

## Category — a denylist, not an allowlist

Items carry **no category field**. On a 467-offer phone sweep, 30% were not
phones, and 15 of those formed full product keys (a tablet has brand, memory
and colour). Phones use `sources/not_a_phone.py`, a denylist of product-type
nouns: an allowlist would drop any phone whose title lacks the expected noun,
and losing a real phone is worse than admitting an accessory the matcher can
still reject. Non-phone categories keep only titles carrying the category
noun (`CATEGORY_KEEP_WORD`).

Two false positives already handled: `Черное стекло` (protector vs colour —
only the qualified protector sense counts) and `USB-адаптер` in a phone's
marketing title (charger in the box, so `adapter` is not denied).

Fixture: `tests/fixtures/sources/texnomart.json`. Tests: `tests/sources/test_texnomart*.py`, `test_not_a_phone.py`.

---
name: fetch-uzum
description: Use when fetching prices or listings from uzum.uz (Uzum Market), minting its anonymous GraphQL token, or when an uzum request returns 401, HTTP 200 with an errors key, or prices that do not match the product page.
---

# uzum.uz — GraphQL, anonymous token, multi-seller

Largest source (5,000+ offers). Only source with auth, per-SKU pricing, and a
failure mode that looks like success. Full notes: `docs/parsers/uzum.md`.
Client: `narxnoma-crawler/narxnoma/sources/uzum.py`.

## Run

```bash
cd narxnoma-crawler   # pip install -e . once
python -m narxnoma.cli fetch --source uzum --category smartphones --limit 50
python -m narxnoma.cli fetch --source uzum --query "galaxy a56"
```

## Auth — mint, no account

```
POST https://id.uzum.uz/api/auth/token   body {}
Accept-Language: ru-RU        # required (any value)
Referer: https://uzum.uz/     # required (uzum.uz origin)
```

Response **204 No Content**; token is in `Set-Cookie: access_token=<JWT>`, not
the body. `Origin` is NOT required. TTL 6 h (`exp` claim); refresh ~5 min early.
A bare 401 mid-run means server-side revocation: re-mint once, retry once.

## Endpoint

```
POST https://graphql.uzum.uz/
Authorization: Bearer <token>
Content-Type: application/json
apollographql-client-name: web-customers
x-iid: <any UUID>
```

All four required. Drop `apollographql-client-name` or `x-iid` and you get
**HTTP 200, `data: null`, `errors: [...]`**. Always inspect `errors`.
Introspection is on; persisted queries not enforced. Query text: `SEARCH_QUERY`
in the client; pagination `offset`/`limit` (72 per page, offset cap 1000, so the
frontier is per category, not per brand).

## Price — SKU, never card

| field | meaning | use |
|---|---|---|
| `skuList[].sellPrice` | this variant's price, integer UZS | **yes** |
| `minSellPrice` | card minimum across every model and tier | no |
| `fullPrice` | struck-through pre-discount | no |

One listing per SKU. Card titles are marketing blurbs bundling several models;
memory and colour come from SKU `characteristics`, whose keys are typo-ridden
(`Объем встроенной памяти` vs `Объём ...`) — match by token `ram`/`rom`, not by
exact key. Category filter client-side on `catalogCard.category.id`
(15271 Android, 15272 iPhone; other categories in `CATEGORY_IDS`).

## URL

`https://uzum.uz/ru/product/<productId>?skuId=<skuId>` — 302s to the slug URL;
never build a slug. `?skuId=` preselects the exact variant.

## Images

Request `photos` explicitly; it is not in the default selection. Missing it
published 5,461 offers with no picture while every count stayed green.

## Traps

- eSIM-only variants carry a marker; an unmarked phone is dual-SIM, not unknown.
- Colours in characteristics are Russian; in card/model strings often Uzbek
  (`Kumush`, `Tilla`, `Yashil`, `Muz`). Both vocabularies in the matcher.
- Search is strict AND: drop colour words and `5G`/`4G` from the query.
- Multi-seller: many partners per SKU. Price = IQR-trimmed median; uzum also
  reports a min.

Fixture: `tests/fixtures/sources/uzum.json`, `uzum_photos.json`. Tests: `tests/sources/test_uzum*.py`.
